title: Constitution Day 2026: Why India celebrates Samvidhan Divas on November 26
description: India celebrates Constitution Day on November 26 to mark the adoption of the Constitution in 1949, honoring Dr BR Ambedkar and constitutional values.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Constitution Day 2026: Why India celebrates Samvidhan Divas on November 26
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 09:29 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 09:29 IST
Nationwide events mark Samvidhan Divas to honour the framers and promote democratic values, with the historic text releasing in multiple regional languages.
India celebrates Constitution Day, also known as Samvidhan Divas, on November 26 every year to mark the adoption of the country's Constitution by the Constituent Assembly in 1949.
The occasion honours the contributions of the Constitution's framers, particularly Dr BR Ambedkar, who chaired the Drafting Committee. It also serves as a reminder of the constitutional principles of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity that underpin India's democratic framework.
The theme of this year's celebration by the Dr Ambedkar Foundation in New Delhi is "The Constitution @76: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's Constitutional Vision and the Future of Indian Democracy".
Why is Constitution Day celebrated on November 26?
The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on November 26, 1949, following nearly three years of deliberations and discussions.
However, the Constitution came into force on January 26, 1950, marking India's transition into a sovereign democratic republic. The date was chosen to commemorate the Purna Swaraj declaration made by the Indian National Congress in 1930.
While January 26 is celebrated as Republic Day, November 26 commemorates the adoption of the Constitution.
The government officially designated November 26 as Constitution Day in 2015 to promote awareness of constitutional values and recognise Dr BR Ambedkar's contribution to the making of the Constitution. Before that, the day was observed as National Law Day.
Constitution Day 2026: Theme
The theme for the Dr Ambedkar Foundation's 2026 celebrations is "The Constitution @76: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's Constitutional Vision and the Future of Indian Democracy".
The theme highlights the relevance of Ambedkar's constitutional vision in strengthening democratic institutions and promoting justice, liberty, equality, fraternity, constitutional morality and accountable governance.
How is Constitution Day celebrated?
Constitution Day is marked across educational institutions, government offices and other organisations through activities aimed at spreading awareness about the Constitution.
These include readings of the Preamble, debates, quizzes, lectures, essay competitions and discussions on Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties.
In New Delhi, the Dr Ambedkar Foundation is scheduled to organise a programme at the Dr Ambedkar International Centre on November 26. Former Chief Justice of India Justice UU Lalit is slated to read the Preamble and deliver a lecture on constitutional governance and Ambedkar's legacy.
A national programme at Vigyan Bhavan will also mark the 77th Constitution Day, with the Constitution set to be released in 22 regional languages.
What is the significance of Constitution Day?
Constitution Day goes beyond commemorating the adoption of a historic document. It reinforces the importance of constitutional values, democratic accountability, equality before the law, and individual freedoms.
The Preamble lays down the foundational ideals of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity. These principles continue to guide India's democratic institutions and governance framework.
The occasion also encourages citizens to understand their constitutional rights and duties and reflect on the responsibilities that come with being part of a democratic society.
Constitution Day vs Republic Day: What is the difference?
Although both occasions are closely linked to India's constitutional journey, they mark two distinct milestones.
Constitution Day – November 26: Marks the adoption of the Indian Constitution by the Constituent Assembly in 1949. Republic Day – January 26: Marks the day the Constitution came into effect in 1950, establishing India as a republic.
Both dates hold historical significance, with Constitution Day recognising the making and adoption of the Constitution and Republic Day celebrating its implementation.

title: Watch | Indian Army aircraft use highway as runway in first-of-its-kind exercise in Gujarat
description: Four Indian Army aircraft land, refuel and take off from the Amritsar–Jamnagar Economic Corridor in Gujarat, demonstrating how national highways could serve as emergency landing strips.
author: Vivek Dubey
content:
Watch | Indian Army aircraft use highway as runway in first-of-its-kind exercise in Gujarat
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 09:02 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 09:02 IST
An elite military aviation team successfully landed and refueled four aircraft on a national highway stretch in Gujarat, marking a strategic milestone in testing civil infrastructure for emergency defense operations.
Four aircraft belonging to the Indian Army’s ‘Team Mountain Eagles’ landed and took off from the Amritsar–Jamnagar Economic Corridor in Gujarat as part of an exercise demonstrating the potential use of national highways as emergency landing grounds.
The operation was conducted on a stretch of NH-754A between Chainage Km 946 and Km 949 as part of the ongoing ‘Wings of Valour and Unity Expedition’.
The formation consisted of two fixed-wing microlight aircraft and two flexible-wing powered hang gliders. The aircraft took off from Kandla Airport and landed near Bakutra Toll Plaza in Santalpur taluka of Gujarat’s Patan district.
In a historic demonstration of synergy between the Indian Army and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), 4️⃣ microlight aircraft of the Indian Army’s ‘Team Mountain Eagles’, participating in the Wings of Valour and Unity Expedition, successfully landed and took off from the Amritsar–Jamnagar Economic Corridor (NH-754A), between Chainage Km 946 and Km 949 in Gujarat.
This remarkable feat underscores the commitment of the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways and NHAI to developing world-class highway infrastructure that strengthens connectivity, drives economic growth and meets the strategic and operational needs of our Armed Forces. It also highlights the potential of National Highways to facilitate aero-adventure, tourism and other emerging activities, wherever feasible, with appropriate safety measures and coordination. I congratulate the Indian Army’s ‘Team Mountain Eagles’, NHAI and all the concerned authorities for their exemplary coordination and successful execution of this historic endeavour. Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi Ji, we remain committed to building a robust, resilient and future-ready National Highway network that goes beyond connectivity to serve the nation’s developmental, strategic and emergency-response needs. #PragatiKaHighway #AmritsarJamnagarEconomicCorridor
#TeamMountainEagles — Nitin Gadkari (@nitin_gadkari) November 26, 2026
The team belongs to the Army Adventure Nodal Centre at the Military College of Telecommunication Engineering (MCTE), Mhow, Madhya Pradesh. The aircraft landed on the highway, underwent ground refuelling and subsequently took off to continue the expedition.
According to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, the exercise was the first successful landing and refuelling operation involving this four-aircraft formation on a national highway.
Highway as runway
The demonstration highlighted the possibility of using suitable sections of national highways as alternative landing grounds for small aircraft during emergencies and other operational requirements.
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) worked with the Army, local administration and police to prepare the stretch for the operation. Its teams managed safety arrangements, temporary traffic diversions and the restoration of normal traffic movement after the exercise.
The selected highway section was assessed for surface conditions, road geometry and safety requirements before the aircraft landed.
Gadkari on dual use
Reacting to the development, Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari described the operation as “a historic demonstration of synergy between the Indian Army and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)”.
He said the exercise demonstrated how highway infrastructure could serve the strategic and operational requirements of the Armed Forces, apart from improving connectivity and supporting economic growth.
Gadkari also highlighted the potential of national highways to support aero-adventure and tourism activities, subject to feasibility, safety arrangements and coordination.
Expedition details
The ‘Wings of Valour and Unity Expedition’ was flagged off from Mhow on November 14, 2026, and is scheduled to conclude at the same location on November 28. The expedition covers Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Rajasthan.
The operation on the Amritsar–Jamnagar Expressway marks a milestone for Team Mountain Eagles and highlights the potential of India's highway infrastructure to support defence preparedness and emergency operations alongside regular road transportation.

उन्होंने पत्रकारों से बात करते हुए कहा कि पूरा विधेयक हमारे हाथ में आने दीजिए. एक बार जब यह हमारे पास आ जाएगा, तो हम इस पर चर्चा कर सकते हैं और हो सकता है कि यह एक अच्छा विधेयक साबित हो. सुले ने आगे कहा कि देश में ऐसे कई मौके आए हैं जब विपक्ष और सत्ता पक्ष ने राष्ट्रीय हित में कानून पास करने के लिए मिलकर काम किया है. सुले के इस बयान को परिसीमन बिल के समर्थन का संकेत माना जा रहा है. वहीं, उनके इस बयान पर उद्धव ठाकरे की पार्टी और कांग्रेस ने सवाल खड़े किए हैं.

title: सत्र की सुगबुगाहट, दिल्ली में बढ़ी आहट: मंत्रियों को विदेशी दौरे रद्द करने का फरमान, क्या है मोदी सरकार का 'दिसंबर प्लान'?
description: प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने अपने मंत्रिमंडल के सदस्यों से कहा कि वे आगामी शीतकालीन सत्र के लिए तैयार रहें. माना जा रहा है कि शीतकालीन सत्र 15 दिसंबर से पहले बुलाया जा सकता है. सूत्रों ने यहां तक कहा कि सरकार सत्र बुलाने के लिए दो तारीखों पर विचार कर रही है.
author: अभिनव त्रिपाठी
content:
संसद का शीतकालीन सत्र 15 दिसंबर के पहले बुलाया जा सकता है. इस बात के संकेत खुद पीएम नरेंद्र मोदी ने दिए. बुधवार (25 नवंबर) को पीएम की अध्यक्षता में हुई कैबिनेट बैठक में आगामी सत्र के मुद्दों पर भी चर्चा हुई. बताया जाता है कि पीएम मोदी ने अपने मंत्रिमंडल के सहयोगियों से कहा है शीतकालीन सत्र से पहले अपनी तैयारियों को दुरुस्त कर लें और किसी विदेश यात्रा पर जाने से बचें.
पीएम मोदी की सलाह से संकेत मिलते हैं, सरकार का मानना है कि सत्र की शुरुआत होने से पहले सभी मंत्री मौजूद रहें. बताया जाता है कि बुधवार को हुई मंत्रिमंडल की बैठक में पीएम मोदी ने सुझाव दिया कि संसद का शीतकालीन सत्र 15 दिसंबर से पहले बुलाया जाए और मंत्रियों से यह भी कहा कि ने सुनिश्चित करें कि उनके संबंधित मंत्रालय पूरी तरीके से तैयार रहें.
सूत्रों की मानें, तो संसद के शीतकालीन सत्र के लिए सरकार दो तारीखों पर विचार कर रही है. बताया जाता है कि या तो 29 नवंबर से सत्र बुलाया जा सकता है या फिर 6 दिसंबर के बाद सत्र को बुलाया जा सकता है. सूत्रों के मुताबिक, 15 दिसंबर से पहले सरकार किसी भी डेट पर सत्र बुलाने की तैयारी में है.
सूत्रों ने दावा किया कि संसदीय मामलों की कैबिनेट समिति सत्र शुरू होने की तारीख और इसकी अवधि के बारे में अंतिम फैसला लेगी. बता दें कि केंद्र सरकार की ये तैयारियां ऐसे समय पर की जा रही हैं, जब विपक्षी दल शीतकालीन सत्र बुलाने में हो रही देरी पर सवाल खड़ा कर रहा है.
बता दें कि शीतकालीन सत्र की घोषणा न होने के कारण संसद का एक विशेष सत्र बुलाए जाने की अटकलें भी तेज हो गई हैं. हालांकि, इसको लेकर भी पुष्टि नहीं हो सकी है. माना जा रहा था कि लोकसभा और विधानसभा क्षेत्रों के प्रस्तावित परिसीमन विधेयक को लेकर ये विशेष सत्र बुलाया जा सकता है.
अब संसद का शीतकलीन सत्र 15 दिसंबर से पहले शुरू होने की उम्मीद है. ऐसे में सबकी नजरें इस बात पर टिकी हैं कि क्या केंद्र सरकार परिसीमन और महिला आरक्षण से जुड़ा प्रस्तावित विधेयक पेश करेगी या नहीं. बता दें कि फिलहाल एनडीए के पास 320 सदस्य हैं. विधेयक को पास कराने के लिए दो-तिहाई बहुमत चाहिए. ऐसे में इस आंकड़े तक पहुंचने के लिए उन्हें विपक्षी दलों के समर्थन की जरूरत होगी.
गौरतलब है कि इसी साल 17 अप्रैल को सरकार ने एक विशेष सत्र बुलाया था और इस दौरान विधेयक को पेश किया गया था. लंबी चर्चा के बाद भी इस विधेयक पारित नहीं कराया जा सका, क्योंकि सरकार के पास जरूरी संख्या बल नहीं था. विधेयक के पारित कराने के लिए 543 सदस्यों वाले मौजूदा लोकसभा में 361 वोटों की आवश्यकता होगी. फिलहाल तीन सीटें खाली हैं, इसलिए सदन में अभी 540 सदस्य हैं.
संसद के अगले सत्र की घोषणा में हो रही देरी पर विपक्ष ने सवाल खड़े किए हैं. कांग्रेस ने केंद्र सरकार के इरादों पर सवाल खड़ा किया और परिसीमन को लेकर उसकी योजनाओं पर स्पष्टीकरण भी मांगा है. कांग्रेस के राष्ट्रीय प्रवक्ता जयराम रमेश ने कहा था कि अब तक देश को शीतकालीन सत्र या किसी संभावित विशेष सत्र की तारीखों के बारे में बता दिया जाना चाहिए था.
इसके साथ ही प्रधानमंत्री मोदी और केंद्रीय गृह मंत्री अमित शाह की जोड़ी का जिक्र करते हुए रमेश ने पूछा कि PM-HM की जोड़ी क्या खेल खेल रही है. अगर मान लिया जाए कि यह जोड़ी अभी भी साथ है? इसके अलावा उन्होंने परिसीमन पर प्रस्तावित कानून के लिए जरूरी संख्या जुटाने की सरकार की रणनीति पर भी सवाल भी उठाए.

title: तिरुपति बालाजी के दरबार में गोल्ड का महासमर्पण: 45 आभूषण, 9 सेट में 121 किलो सोना... CM नायडू की मौजूदगी में चढ़ेगी करीब 160 करोड़ की भेंट
description: तिरुमला तिरुपति देवस्थानम में विराजमान वेंकटेश्वर स्वामी के दरबार से आस्था और समर्पण की दिव्य मिसाल देखने को मिली है. यहां गुरुवार को एक भक्त 121 किलो सोने से तैयार आभूषण मंदिर को अर्पित करने जा रहा है. करीब 150 से 160 करोड़ रुपये कीमत वाली इस भेंट में 45 आभूषण नौ सेट में हैं. दानदाता ने अपनी पहचान गुप्त रखने की इच्छा जताई है.
author: श्वेतांक रत्नाम्बर
content:
भारत के सबसे समृद्ध मंदिरों में शुमार तिरुपति बालाजी के दरबार में आस्था और वैभव का एक अनोखा संगम देखने को मिलने वाला है. भगवान वेंकटेश्वर स्वामी यानी तिरुपति बालाजी के चरणों में उनका एक भक्त ऐसी भेंट चढ़ाने जा रहा है, जिसकी चर्चा देशभर में रही है. इस गुप्त महादान में एक-दो किलो नहीं, बल्कि पूरे 121 किलो सोने के आभूषणों की भेंट शामिल हैं. भगवान को समर्पित इस बेशकीमती चढ़ावे में 45 आभूषणों के नौ सेट बताए जा रहे हैं, जिनकी अनुमानित कीमत करीब 150 से 160 करोड़ रुपये बताई जा रही है. खास बात यह है कि इतना बड़ा दान करने वाले इस भक्त ने अपनी पहचान सार्वजनिक न करने की अपील की है. ये भेंट मुख्यमंत्री चंद्रबाबू नायडू की मौजूदगी में TTD को सौंपी जाएगी.
भगवान दिव्य हैं तो भक्त भी निराले हैं. इस असाधारण दान को TTD के इतिहास में किसी एक व्यक्ति द्वारा दिए गए सबसे बड़े स्वर्ण दान में से एक माना जा रहा है. आंध्र प्रदेश के मुख्यमंत्री एन चंद्रबाबू नायजू की मौजूदगी में ये आभूषण औपचारिक रूप से तिरुमाला तिरुपति देवस्थानम (TTD) को सौंपे जाएंगे. मुख्यमंत्री नायडू सुबह 10 बजे तिरुपति के SV एग्रीकल्चर कॉलेज हेलीपैड पहुंचेंगे. चंद्रबाबू सुबह 10:45 बजे तिरुमाला के गायत्री निलयम पहुंचेंगे. सुबह 11:10 बजे वैकुंठम कतार परिसर (क्यू कॉम्प्लेक्स) के जरिए श्रीवारी के दर्शन करेंगे. तिरुमाला दौरे के बाद, मुख्यमंत्री चंद्रबाबू नायडू तेलंगाना के भद्राद्री कोठागुडेम के लिए रवाना होंगे.
सोने के आभूषण भेंट करने का कार्यक्रम सुबह 11:35 बजे तय है. इन सोने के आभूषणों में श्रीवारी का मुकुट और 'पद्म पादालु' (चरण) शामिल हैं. TTD के अधिकारी भक्त से औपचारिक रूप से ये आभूषण प्राप्त करेंगे. इस खास शुभ अवसर पर टीटीडी के मैनेजमेंट के सभी प्रमुख लोग भी मौजूद रहेंगे.
मां महालक्ष्मी अगर धनाध्यक्षा हैं, तो भगवान विष्णु श्रीनिवास हैं. तिरुपति बालाजी मंदिर में स्वर्ण दान की परंपरा बेहद प्राचीन है. रिपोर्ट्स के मुताबिक इस मंदिर में हर महीने औसतन लगभग 100 किलोग्राम सोना चढ़ाया जाता है. टीटीडी के पास कई टन सोना है.
खबरों के मुताबिक दानदाता ने कई साल पहले अमेरिका जाने से पहले अपने बेहतर भविष्य के लिए भगवान वेंकटेश्वर स्वामी से प्रार्थना की थी. आगे चलकर उन्होंने एक आईटी कंपनी शुरू की और एक सफल बिजनेसमैन बने. हाल ही में, अपनी कंपनी में 60% हिस्सेदारी बेचने के बाद उन्हें 6,000 करोड़ रुपये से अधिक की राशि मिली थी. इसके बाद, अपनी संपत्ति का एक हिस्सा उन्होंने सामाजिक कार्यों के लिए समर्पित करने और भगवान वेंकटेश्वर के प्रति अपना पुराना संकल्प पूरा करने के लिए इस भेंट को देने का फैसला लिया.

title: India Rejects US 'Excess Capacity' Charge, Pushes Back Against Proposed 25% Tariff On Exports  72-character headline:
description: India has rejected US allegations of structural excess manufacturing capacity as the USTR proposes tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, with a lower 17% rate linked to a trade deal.
author: Shruti Sneha
content:
India Rejects US 'Excess Capacity' Charge, Pushes Back Against Proposed 25% Tariff On Exports 72-character headline:
India has rejected US allegations of structural excess manufacturing capacity as the USTR proposes tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, with a lower 17% rate linked to a trade deal.
- India News
- 4 min read
New Delhi: India has pushed back against allegations by the United States that its manufacturing policies are creating structural excess capacity, as Washington moves ahead with a proposal to impose tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods following an investigation under Section 301 of the US Trade Act.
The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said on Wednesday that the government was examining a notice issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) and maintained that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector.
“The Notice is currently under examination,” the ministry said, adding that India had engaged constructively throughout the investigation.
The government also pointed out that the Department of Commerce had rejected the allegations in its submissions during the investigation. India has maintained that its manufacturing expansion is driven by domestic demand and the need to reduce dependence on other countries for critical inputs.
Advertisement
New Delhi has also called for trade-related concerns to be addressed through ongoing negotiations for the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA). It reiterated its commitment to concluding the agreement at the earliest, referring to the framework announced on February 2 and the joint statement issued on February 7.
Why has the US questioned India's manufacturing push?
The 189-page report from the USTR, which was published on Wednesday, looks at manufacturing policies in 14 economies, including India. It contends that India's key programs, like Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat, and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) plan, are pushing production over what the market can sustain.
Advertisement
According to the analysis, India would need to produce an extra $500 billion at 2025 levels in order to expand manufacturing's contribution to 25% of its GDP under the Make in India strategy.
According to the USTR, India's "acts, policies, and practices" pertaining to manufacturing are irrational and impede US trade.
However, over the course of the eight-month probe, India has continuously contested this finding. Its stance is that manufacturing production is not dictated by government directives, but rather is dependent on market conditions and actual orders.
Additionally, New Delhi has maintained that initiatives like PLI and Make in India are meant to boost local output and shouldn't be seen as attempts to build manufacturing capacity without matching demand.
At the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee in October, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal voiced India's concerns, stating that the country "does not have structural excess capacity" in the areas that Washington has highlighted.
During the probe, India also took part in private meetings with the USTR.
How much tariff is the US proposing on Indian goods?
In light of the Section 301 inquiry, the USTR proposed a 25% tariff on Indian goods. However, if India and the US reach a trade deal, the suggested rate might drop to 17%.
Steel, solar, healthcare, and information and communications technology (ICT) are among the industries that the inquiry has highlighted. Concerns about India's labor rules, limitations on market access, and rising imports of Chinese industrial inputs have also been brought up.
The proposed tariffs do not apply to certain medicinal products. These include patented medications, hundreds of drug components utilized in pharmaceuticals, and generic medications in dosage form.
The USTR links lower tariff rates for certain nations to the potential for trade deals. The suggested tariff rates for other economies also differ.
Proposed USTR Section 301 tariff rates:
Written comments on the proposed tariffs can be submitted until January 5, 2027, while hearings are scheduled to begin on January 25.
Can the India-US trade deal change the tariff outcome?
The current trade talks are especially crucial because of the proposed tariff cut for India. Since February 2025, the US and India have been discussing a bilateral trade deal.
Washington outlined an 18% reciprocal tax on a variety of Indian commodities as part of the framework for an interim trade agreement that the two nations unveiled in February.
The most recent USTR proposal adds another level of complexity to the negotiations; Indian exporters may be impacted by the gap between the conditional 17% rate and the proposed 25% tariff.
While claiming that its manufacturing policies are intended to suit domestic requirements and develop production capacities, the Indian government is currently reviewing Washington's most recent notification. New Delhi has reaffirmed its desire to reach an early bilateral deal and settle trade-related disputes through negotiations.

title: Ankita Bhandari Case: Zero FIR Against Pulkit Arya’s Father Vinod Arya For Leaking Her Private Chats
description: Dehradun police filed a Zero FIR against Vinod Arya and advocate Anuj Pundir for allegedly releasing Ankita Bhandari’s private WhatsApp chats after a press conference, on her mother Soni Devi’s complaint.
author: Asian News International
content:
Ankita Bhandari Case: Zero FIR Against Pulkit Arya’s Father Vinod Arya For Leaking Her Private Chats
Dehradun police filed a Zero FIR against Vinod Arya and advocate Anuj Pundir for allegedly releasing Ankita Bhandari’s private WhatsApp chats after a press conference, on her mother Soni Devi’s complaint.
- India News
- 2 min read
Dehradun: Police officials at the Rajpur police station in Uttarakhand's Dehradun have registered a Zero FIR against Vinod Arya, father of Pulkit Arya, the prime accused in the Ankita Bhandari murder case and his advocate, Anuj Pundir, following a written complaint by Ankita’s mother, Soni Devi.
The case is regarding the public release of her late daughter’s private WhatsApp chats after a press conference in Haridwar.
The FIR has been filed under Sections 66C and 66D of the Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008, along with Sections 356(2) and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.
Nineteen-year-old Ankita was employed as a receptionist at Rishikesh’s Vanantra Resort, overseen by Pulkit Arya, whose father, Vinod Arya, is a former BJP leader. Less than four weeks into the role, she vanished on September 18, 2022, and authorities found her body in the Chilla canal six days afterwards.
Advertisement
Prosecutors argued during court proceedings that Pulkit coerced Ankita into offering sexual favours to visitors, a demand she turned down. A Pauri Garhwal court found Pulkit, along with co-accused Saurabh Bhaskar and Ankit Gupta, guilty of murder on May 30, 2025, handing down rigorous life sentences to all three.
Text exchanges on WhatsApp between Ankita and her acquaintances proved central to the case, with prosecutors citing them to demonstrate that the alleged pressure upset her and prompted her wish to quit the property.
Advertisement
The killing triggered major demonstrations throughout Uttarakhand, casting a spotlight on how revenue police initially handled the probe and why part of the resort was razed shortly after the death.
Despite the sentencing, questions have continued over the family’s push to investigate an unnamed "VIP" purportedly tied to the case. In January 2026, after fresh demonstrations and appeals from Ankita’s relatives, state authorities asked the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to step in, leading the agency to open a case into the suspected VIP connection. Her family has kept up pressure for inquiries into whether additional individuals played a role in the events leading to her murder.
At a November 16 press briefing, Vinod Arya distributed over 4,000 pages of alleged chat logs involving Ankita and a male acquaintance to contend that his son had done no wrong. A day later, at an All India Students’ Association gathering in Dehradun, Soni Devi claimed that people were still trying to tarnish her late daughter’s reputation.

title: Delhi to Get Two New Hospitals with 1,815 Beds in 2027; 40 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs to Open in December
description: According to the CM's Office, the govt is also planning to open 40 new Ayushman Arogya Mandirs next month, coinciding with the 102nd birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, to strengthen primary healthcare services and provide treatment facilities closer to people's homes.
author: Asian News International
content:
Delhi to Get Two New Hospitals with 1,815 Beds in 2027; 40 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs to Open in December
According to the CM's Office, the govt is also planning to open 40 new Ayushman Arogya Mandirs next month, coinciding with the 102nd birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, to strengthen primary healthcare services and provide treatment facilities closer to people's homes.
- India News
- 4 min read
New Delhi: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Wednesday said two major hospitals in Siraspur and Hastal, together offering 1,815 beds, will become operational next year as the government steps up efforts to expand healthcare infrastructure and improve access to medical services across the capital.
According to the Chief Minister's Office, the government is also planning to open 40 new Ayushman Arogya Mandirs next month, coinciding with the 102nd birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, to strengthen primary healthcare services and provide treatment facilities closer to people's homes.
Gupta made the announcements while reviewing the progress of various Health Department projects at the Delhi Secretariat. She directed officials to ensure that all hospital and healthcare infrastructure projects are completed within their stipulated timelines, making it clear that negligence or unnecessary delays would not be tolerated.
Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh and senior officials from the Health Department and the Public Works Department (PWD) attended the meeting.
Advertisement
The Chief Minister said the government's focus was on providing accessible, quality and timely healthcare to every citizen. She said expanding healthcare infrastructure involved not only constructing new hospitals but also ensuring the availability of modern medical equipment, doctors and other healthcare personnel to improve patient care.
She also stressed the need to strengthen primary healthcare facilities so that residents would not have to travel long distances for treatment of common ailments. Officials were directed to ensure that public welfare projects were implemented with responsibility, promptness and sensitivity.
Advertisement
Providing an update on the two major hospital projects, CM Gupta said the 1,164-bed hospital in Siraspur was ready, with the procurement of medical equipment underway and targeted for completion by the end of January. Construction of the 651-bed hospital in Hastal is also nearing completion, and the facility is expected to become operational next year.
The two hospitals are expected to improve access to medical services in their respective areas and ease the patient load on existing healthcare facilities.
On primary healthcare expansion, Gupta said 1,139 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs were being developed across Delhi, of which 415 were already operational. The government aims to open 40 more centres next month. She added that facilities receiving a higher number of patients were being considered for two-shift operations to ensure timely treatment at the local level.
The government is also developing two hospitals with 691 beds each in Madipur and Jwalapuri, both scheduled for completion by 2028. The Madipur hospital is being constructed at an estimated cost of Rs 466.50 crore, while the Jwalapuri project has been pegged at Rs 484.04 crore.
Alongside new hospitals, the government is expanding maternal and child healthcare facilities at existing institutions. A 463-bed maternal and child healthcare block is being developed at Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hospital in Rohini, while its OPD block is ready for inauguration.
A 270-bed maternal and child healthcare block at Rao Tula Ram Memorial Hospital and a 460-bed block at Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital in Khichripur are also nearing completion. Efforts are underway to make these facilities operational shortly.
The review also covered the proposed integrated redevelopment of Lok Nayak Hospital and the Maulana Azad Medical College campus. The project has an estimated timeline of around 30 months, covering both planning and construction.
The government is also working towards bringing Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital, Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital, Delhi State Cancer Institute and the Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Sciences (IHBAS), all located in the Trans-Yamuna region, under a common institutional framework. The move is aimed at strengthening specialised medical services and improving coordination among these institutions.
In another major initiative, the government plans to establish medical colleges at Indira Gandhi Hospital in Dwarka and Guru Gobind Singh Government Hospital, with 150 MBBS seats proposed at each institution.
The government is also working to increase the number of seats at Baba Saheb Ambedkar Medical College from 125 to 200 and at the Maulana Azad Institute of Dental Sciences from 50 to 70. These measures are aimed at expanding medical education capacity while increasing the availability of trained and specialist doctors.
Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh said the government was working to strengthen hospital infrastructure, medical facilities, equipment and human resources as part of a coordinated effort to improve Delhi's healthcare system.
He said the Health Department was regularly monitoring projects and coordinating with the departments concerned to ensure the timely completion of construction work, procurement of medical equipment and other necessary arrangements. Along with building new hospitals and expanding existing facilities, the government was focused on improving treatment infrastructure and ensuring adequate support for medical services.

title: Trump's new tariff threat puts India's manufacturing ambitions under pressure
description: The US flags pharma, steel, solar and IT in its investigation into excess industrial capacity, while offering India a lower tariff ceiling if a trade deal is reached
author: Dheeraj Kumar
content:
Trump's new tariff threat puts India's manufacturing ambitions under pressure
The US flags pharma, steel, solar and IT in its investigation into excess industrial capacity, while offering India a lower tariff ceiling if a trade deal is reached
India is seeking to emerge as a global manufacturing hub and an alternative to China, but US President Donald Trump's latest tariff offensive could complicate that ambition. Washington has proposed duties of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, accusing New Delhi of following industrial policies that contribute to excess manufacturing capacity.
The proposed tariffs could be capped at 17 per cent if India concludes a trade agreement with the US, but rise to 25 per cent if negotiations fail, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Wednesday. The proposal comes as the two countries continue negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement, with market access and tariffs remaining key points of discussion.
India has rejected the US allegations, maintaining that it does not have structural excess manufacturing capacity in any sector. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said it was examining the determination issued by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) and reiterated that trade-related concerns should be addressed through ongoing negotiations.
The latest action is part of a broader US investigation into alleged excess industrial capacity across 16 economies. Washington has issued determinations against 14 trading partners, including India, China, Japan, South Korea and the European Union.
Why is the US questioning India's manufacturing policies?
In its investigation under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, the USTR identified several Indian government policies and industrial practices that it considers unreasonable and harmful to American commercial interests.
These include India's industrial expansion policies, inadequate labour protections, financial repression, barriers to market access and its alleged failure to address global excess manufacturing capacity.
Washington argues that these practices hurt American producers, exports, jobs and investment while creating economic security risks through dependence on inputs from non-market economies.
The investigation has identified pharmaceuticals and medical devices, steel, solar products and information and communications technology (ICT) as sectors of particular concern.
The US has also raised concerns about India's reliance on manufacturing inputs and foreign investment from non-market economies, particularly in strategically important industries.
The findings put India's industrial expansion strategy under scrutiny. New Delhi has been seeking to strengthen domestic production, reduce import dependence and attract companies looking to diversify their manufacturing operations beyond China.
However, Washington argues that industrial expansion supported by government policies, financial assistance and other market-distorting practices can create production capacity beyond what domestic and global markets can absorb.
India has disputed this assessment. The Commerce Ministry said the country had engaged constructively throughout the investigation and had told Washington that it did not have structural excess capacity in any sector.
17% or 25%: What is Trump's tariff proposal for India?
Under the latest proposal, the US is considering a tariff ceiling of 25 per cent on Indian goods if the two countries fail to reach a trade agreement.
However, the rate could be capped at 17 per cent if India concludes a reciprocal trade agreement that addresses Washington's concerns, Greer said.
The proposed rate is part of a wider effort by the Trump administration to use trade measures against what it considers unfair industrial practices among major trading partners.
In February 2026, New Delhi and Washington agreed on a framework for a trade deal. The understanding brought down the punitive tariff on most Indian goods, imposed in August 2025 after an earlier round of negotiations collapsed, from 50 per cent to 18 per cent.
The US Supreme Court subsequently struck down Trump's use of emergency powers to impose sweeping global tariffs, prompting his administration to pursue alternative legal mechanisms.
The latest Section 301 investigation is part of Washington's effort to rebuild its tariff framework following the court ruling.
The USTR has also proposed tariff caps for other trading partners. China faces a proposed capped rate of 20 per cent if its trade truce with Washington remains in place, but the rate could rise to 40 per cent if the arrangement breaks down. Vietnam faces a proposed rate of 20 per cent under a trade agreement and 35 per cent if negotiations fail.
Which Indian industries could face scrutiny?
The sectors identified by Washington are important to India's manufacturing and export ambitions.
India is a major supplier of pharmaceutical products and has been seeking to strengthen domestic production of medicines, medical devices and other critical healthcare products.
The US investigation has raised concerns about manufacturing practices in these sectors, particularly the role of industrial policies and dependence on inputs from non-market economies.
Steel and solar products are also under scrutiny. Both industries have been central to India's efforts to expand domestic manufacturing capacity and strengthen supply chains.
In information and communications technology, Washington has flagged concerns over industrial expansion and dependence on manufacturing inputs from non-market economies.
The investigation is not limited to individual companies or products. It examines government policies and practices that the US believes contribute to structural excess capacity and distort global manufacturing and trade.
When will the proposed US tariffs take effect?
The proposed tariffs are not final and will go through a public consultation process before a decision is taken.
Interested parties have until January 5, 2027, to submit written comments and requests to participate in the hearings. Public hearings are scheduled to begin on January 25.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the proposed duties would not take effect until after the January 25 hearing.
India's Commerce Ministry has said New Delhi remains committed to working closely with Washington towards an early conclusion of the bilateral trade agreement.
I am a Business Correspondent at Firstpost (Network18). I am particularly interested in covering the AI revolution and how it is changing businesses, industries and the way we live and work. I also follow developments in energy, defence and aerospace, especially as technology, geopolitics and changing global priorities reshape these sectors. My broader reporting interests include the Indian economy, macroeconomics, financial markets, corporate affairs, international trade and geopolitics. I enjoy reporting on stories that help explain what is changing in the business world, why it matters and what it means for India and the global economy. Before joining Firstpost, I worked with Reuters News as an Associate Correspondent. title: 1,700 Indian nationals deported from US since start of 2026: MEA
description: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal says India verifies the nationality of individuals before accepting deportees, reiterating New Delhi’s cooperation with Washington on migration while opposing illegal immigration.
author: FP News Desk
content:
1,700 Indian nationals deported from US since start of 2026: MEA
MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal says India verifies the nationality of individuals before accepting deportees, reiterating New Delhi’s cooperation with Washington on migration while opposing illegal immigration.
As many as 1,700 Indian nationals have been deported from the United States since the beginning of 2026, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Wednesday, underlining that India follows a nationality verification process before accepting individuals facing deportation.
Addressing a question on the latest deportation figures during the ministry’s bi-weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India continues to cooperate with Washington on migration and mobility-related matters but remains firmly opposed to illegal immigration.
He said the two countries maintain cooperation on deportations and that Indian authorities verify the nationality of individuals before agreeing to take them back.
"Where and when we receive information about a person to be deported, we verify his or her nationality and thereafter we agree to take him back," Jaiswal said.
Providing the latest figures, he added that 1,700 Indian nationals had been deported from the US since the beginning of the year.
The latest figure marks an increase from 1,273 Indian nationals deported from the US between January 1 and July 31, 2026, as shared by Jaiswal in July. At the time, the MEA spokesperson had also highlighted India’s due diligence process before facilitating the return of individuals facing deportation from foreign countries.
”We continue to work with several foreign governments on deportation issues. We do conduct due diligence on our side to confirm the nationality of the person concerned,” Jaiswal had said.
He had further clarified that arrangements for facilitating travel or return to India are undertaken only after the government is satisfied with the nationality of the individual concerned.
Providing the figures for the previous year during the July briefing, Jaiswal had said that a total of 3,567 Indian nationals were deported from the United States in 2025.
With inputs from agencies

title: Tracks of trust: How India is using railways to bring its neighbours closer
description: From a 1927 narrow-gauge line in the Nepal Terai to the new Ayodhya-Janakpur Sarayu-Kamala Express, India’s rail diplomacy with Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Myanmar is a win-win wager on trade, pilgrims and people-to-people ties
author: Akhileshwar Sahay
content:
Tracks of trust: How India is using railways to bring its neighbours closer
From a 1927 narrow-gauge line in the Nepal Terai to the new Ayodhya-Janakpur Sarayu-Kamala Express, India’s rail diplomacy with Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Myanmar is a win-win wager on trade, pilgrims and people-to-people ties
On Monday (November 23), Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah flagged off the inaugural Sarayu-Kamala Express between Ayodhya and Janakpur. Named after the river of Ram's city and the river of Sita's Mithila, the weekly train covers 604 kilometres, stopping at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur and Basti, leaving Janakpur Dham on Saturdays and Ayodhya Cantt on Mondays.
It was Shah's first visit to India since he was sworn in as prime minister in March 2026. The joint press release records eight MoUs, Indian development assistance of Rs 15,000 crore, and a new route for Nepal's transit trade through Deendayal Port at Kandla, with access to Paradip to follow once the infrastructure is in place. On rail, they closed the survey stage of the Raxaul–Kathmandu line and agreed to collaborate on Nepal's East–West Railway.
Indian Railways pitches the train to pilgrims and to border families in Bihar and Nepal travelling for work, study, and kinship. Behind that sits a larger idea: India is using its railways, the subcontinent's oldest connective tissue, as an instrument of foreign policy.
The idea is not new; the speed and deliberateness are.
The roots: When railways ran before borders hardened
Railways reached the Himalayan kingdom long before diplomacy thought of them. In 1927, Nepal's first railway opened between Amlekhganj and Raxaul on the Indian frontier. It was a two-foot-six-inch narrow-gauge line that ran up from the border through Birgunj, and for years it was, in effect, Kathmandu's gateway to India. In 1937, a second line opened from Jaynagar in Bihar to Janakpur.
Both lines began on Indian soil, at Raxaul and Jaynagar, and fed into the railway network of British India, carrying timber, goods and passengers. They were built in the Rana era with British engineering and survey help, but they ran as Nepalese railways, not as part of British India's state railway system. Passenger service on the Raxaul–Amlekhganj line ended in 1965, and freight wound down later in the decade. The decisive blow came from the road: the Tribhuvan Rajpath, opened in 1956, shifted traffic to Kathmandu to buses and trucks, and air links further changed travel.
The Janakpur line survived as a rickety lifeline on ageing track. The stretch beyond Janakpur to Bijalpura was cut in 2001 after flood damage, and the rest closed in early 2014 for conversion to broad gauge, reopening in phases.
To the east, history was crueller. Undivided Bengal had an integrated rail network. The 1947 Partition split it across a new border, though cross-border trains kept running until the 1965 India–Pakistan war halted passenger services. Partition also severed Assam's rail route through East Pakistan; India answered with the Assam Rail Link through North Bengal, begun in January 1948 and built in two years, opening to goods in December 1949 and to passengers on January 26, 1950. When the Maitree Express rolled into Dhaka on Pohela Boishakh, April 14, 2008, it restored the Kolkata–Dhaka passenger link after 43 years.
South Asia's railways were built for one economic space that borders fragmented and wars severed. Rail diplomacy today is largely an effort to repair what geography intended and politics undid.
Nepal: From survey files to running trains
For a long time, India-Nepal rail cooperation was more promise than performance. That has changed in the last four years.
On April 2, 2022, Modi and then Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba launched the 35-km Jaynagar-Kurtha cross-border rail link, the first broad-gauge passenger link between two countries and the converted descendant of the 1937 Janakpur line. Modi said the two leaders had agreed to give priority to trade and cross-border connectivity "in all respects", and that the Jayanagar–Kurtha line was part of this. On June 1, 2023, the two prime ministers inaugurated the Jogbani–Biratnagar link in eastern Nepal, built with Indian grant assistance.
The real breakthrough was in freight. On November 13, 2025, the two countries exchanged a Letter of Exchange amending the Protocol to the Treaty of Transit.
It permits rail freight between Jogbani and Biratnagar, including bulk cargo; liberalises Kolkata-Jogbani, Kolkata-Nautanwa, and Visakhapatnam-Nautanwa corridors; and allows containerised and bulk cargo to move by rail directly from Kolkata and Visakhapatnam ports to the Nepal Customs Yard near Biratnagar.
In July 2026, the first direct commercial container train, carrying 40 containers of canola, ran from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar with no transhipment at the border. Until then, Nepal's rail cargo had been funnelled through Birgunj; the transit rights it rides on go back to the Treaty of Trade and Transit of 1960.
Then there is Kathmandu. On April 7, 2018, PMs Modi and Oli agreed to build a new electrified rail line, with India's financial support, from Raxaul to Kathmandu, with India to complete the preparatory survey within a year and its implementation and funding to be settled on the basis of a Detailed Project Report. An MoU for the survey was signed that August on the margins of the Bimstec summit in Kathmandu, with Konkan Railway entrusted with the work. The Final Location Survey report was handed over to Nepal in June 2023, and on November 23 Modi and Shah announced its finalisation. Construction across the Mahabharat and Chure ranges will be a true test of engineering and political will.
East–West Railway adds a second axis. Nepal has long wanted a line running the length of its Terai, from Mechi in the east to Mahakali in the west. At the June 2026 meetings of the bilateral Project Steering Committee and Joint Working Group, two sides discussed Indian technical support, the Raxaul–Kathmandu survey report, and operating procedures for the Janakpur–Ayodhya service. Joined up, a Terai trunk line with spurs to Jaynagar, Raxaul, Jogbani and Nautanwa, plus a climb to Kathmandu, would put every major Nepali town a single journey from an Indian port, pilgrimage centre or city. The Sarayu-Kamala Express is the first visible thread of that network.
Bhutan: The kingdom without a railway gets two
Bhutan has never had a railway. On September 29, 2025, India and Bhutan signed an intergovernmental MoU to establish railway links: Kokrajhar–Gelephu (69 km) and Banarhat–Samtse (20 km), at an estimated cost of Rs 4,033 crore. The first runs from Assam to Gelephu, the site of King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck's Gelephu Mindfulness City, a service-sector special administrative region that India has pledged to support fully. The second runs from West Bengal's Jalpaiguri district to Samtse, Bhutan's industrial town. India will fund both: the Ministry of Railways will pay for the Indian sections, and the Ministry of External Affairs will pay for the Bhutanese sections under India's assistance to Bhutan's 13th Five-Year Plan. The Kokrajhar–Gelephu line has been declared a Special Railway Project to speed up land acquisition.
At the special MEA briefing announcing the lines, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw put the logic plainly: by building about 70 km, Bhutan gains access to a 150,000-km network. India accounts for nearly 80 per cent of Bhutan's total trade. For a landlocked kingdom, a railhead at its own border cuts the cost of everything from cement to fuel; for Assam's Bodoland region, it turns a peripheral district into a gateway.
Bangladesh: The network built, the trains stopped
Bangladesh is where India's rail diplomacy has gone furthest, and where it has stumbled hardest.
After Maitree, came the Kolkata–Khulna Bandhan Express, flagged off in November 2017, and the Mitali Express to New Jalpaiguri in 2022. In all, six pre-1965 rail links between the two countries have been restored. On November 1, 2023, Modi and Sheikh Hasina inaugurated the Akhaura–Agartala link, the first rail link between Bangladesh and India's Northeast, built with an Indian grant of Rs 392.52 crore, together with the 65-km Khulna–Mongla port rail line, also built with Indian assistance. The Railway Ministry told the Lok Sabha in December 2015 that the Akhaura link would cut the Kolkata–Agartala rail distance from 1,581 km via Guwahati to about 460 km via Dhaka.
Then came July 2024. Amid the upheaval in Bangladesh, the Maitree, Bandhan and Mitali passenger services were suspended "due to security considerations"; goods trains continue to run. The Maitree had been popular, especially with Bangladeshi travellers coming to India for medical treatment and tourism.
Candour requires saying that this is a setback. Hope allows us to say it is not the end. Bangladesh's BNP won the general election of February 12, 2026, and Modi was among the first leaders to call Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. In September 2026, the two railway administrations met in Dhaka to discuss restoring all three passenger trains, with Dhaka proposing a faster Maitree route over the Padma Bridge. By early October, no resumption date had been announced.
The tracks, the interchange yards and the bridges are still there. That is the quiet virtue of rail diplomacy: physical connectivity outlasts political weather. When governments are ready to talk, the infrastructure is waiting.
Sri Lanka: Rebuilding the line the war destroyed
Sri Lanka's link with India's railways once ran through the sea. The Indo-Ceylon Boat Mail carried passengers from Madras Egmore over the Pamban Bridge to Dhanushkodi, across the Palk Strait by ferry to Talaimannar, and on by train to Colombo, until the December 1964 cyclone destroyed the Dhanushkodi line.
Modern rail diplomacy with Colombo has been about rebuilding. The Northern line to Jaffna, Kankesanthurai and Talaimannar was destroyed in the civil war. IRCON rebuilt it under a concessional Indian line of credit of about $800 million, and Modi flagged off the restored service at Talaimannar Pier in March 2015. On April 6, 2025, he and President Anura Kumara Dissanayake inaugurated the 128-km Maho–Omanthai line, refurbished with $91.27 million of Indian assistance, and launched a Maho–Anuradhapura signalling system funded by a $14.89 million Indian grant. The same day, Modi opened the new Pamban Bridge in Tamil Nadu.
Trains now run to Talaimannar on one side of the strait and to Rameswaram on the other, but no rail-and-ferry service yet joins them.
Myanmar: The gateway still to be built
Myanmar is India's land gateway to Southeast Asia and the Trans-Asian Railway. The Railway Ministry told the Lok Sabha in 2016 that the missing link is about 360 km, from Jiribam in India to Kalay in Myanmar, via Moreh and Tamu; Imphal-Moreh accounts for 111 km and Tamu-Kalay for 128 km. A final location survey for the Imphal-Moreh section was sanctioned in January 2022. In Mizoram, the 223-km Sairang–Hbicchhuah line aims to take tracks to the state's southern border, opening trade routes to Myanmar and Southeast Asia via Sittwe port.
Since the 2021 coup and civil war, neither side has been able to build across the frontier. Myanmar is rail diplomacy in waiting. India is wise to keep laying track towards the border, so that when Myanmar is ready, the line ends at Moreh rather than in Imphal.
Why it is a win-win
Critics see only a contest of influence with China; that reading is incomplete. Rail diplomacy works because each side gains something real.
For Nepal and Bhutan, it corrects geography. Being landlocked is a tax on every import and export. A direct container train from Kolkata, port access at Kandla and Paradip, and railheads at Biratnagar, Gelephu, and Samtse lower that tax. Cheaper inputs make Nepali and Bhutanese manufacturing more competitive, and a reliable outlet to the sea gives them leverage in third-country markets.
For India, it is a stable and prosperous periphery. Every container that moves by rail to Biratnagar is cargo for Indian ports, Indian Railways and Indian logistics firms. The Northeast, long a cul-de-sac reached only through the narrow Siliguri corridor, gains alternative routes through Bangladesh.
For land trade, rail is the efficient mode. Trucks queuing for days at border points such as Raxaul-Birgunj and Petrapole-Benapole are among South Asia's most familiar images of lost money. A rake of 40 containers replaces dozens of trucks, cuts handling and spoilage, and simplifies customs. The November 2025 transit amendment and the July 2026 Kolkata–Biratnagar run show what happens when procedure catches up with infrastructure.
For people-to-people ties, it is the cheapest bridge there is. The Ayodhya–Janakpur train is a Ramayana pilgrimage circuit, but it is also a family train. The roti-beti relationship of the Terai and Mithila, with marriages, festivals and shared kin on both sides of the open border, runs on affordable, predictable travel. The same was true of the Maitree Express, whose passengers were overwhelmingly ordinary Bangladeshi travellers, patients and tourists. Air travel is for the few; trains are for the many.
For the region, it is integration by stealth. The Bhutan lines plug into the same Indian grid that carries Nepal's freight and once carried Bangladesh's passengers; a line to Moreh would one day carry it towards Southeast Asia. That is regionalism built from the ground up rather than declared at summits.
The caveats India must heed
Rail diplomacy will be judged by trains that run, not by MoUs signed. The remaining sections of the Jaynagar-Bijalpura-Bardibas and Jogbani-Biratnagar links, both funded by Indian grants, were still under implementation in June 2026. The Raxaul–Kathmandu line, announced in 2018, has only now finished its survey. The Imphal–Moreh line is still under survey, and Bangladesh's passenger trains have been idle for more than two years.
Three things would help: published, deadline-bound joint monitoring; customs, immigration and visa regimes reformed alongside the tracks, since a train held a day at the border loses its advantage; and insulating passenger services from political turbulence, so that people with no stake in a diplomatic quarrel do not lose their train home.
The track ahead
Nearly a century after a narrow-gauge steam train first puffed out of Raxaul towards Amlekhganj, India and Nepal are planning a broad-gauge electric line to Kathmandu. Bhutan is about to hear its first train whistle. Bangladesh and India are working out how to bring passengers back, Sri Lanka's war-torn Northern line is running again on Indian credit, and the track to Myanmar waits at the edge of Manipur.
The rail lines of South Asia were laid for one economic space. Politics divided it; diplomacy, patiently, is sewing it back together. If India keeps its timelines and its neighbours keep the trains running, the Sarayu-Kamala Express will be remembered not as a ceremonial flag-off but as one more stitch in a subcontinent learning, once again, to travel together.
(Akhileshwar Sahay is a Multidisciplinary Thought Leader with Action Bias, a Bharat-based Impact Consultant and a keen watcher of the changing national and international scenario. Views are personal.)

title: Delhi's poor air streak continues, AQI at 226; no immediate relief in sight
description: Delhi AQI today: The capital recorded an AQI of 226 at 7 am on Thursday, with three locations in the very poor category; Sirsa in Haryana reported the highest city-level reading nationally at 368
author: Barkha Mathur
content:
Delhi's poor air streak continues, AQI at 226; no immediate relief in sight
The capital recorded an AQI of 226 at 7 am on Thursday, with three locations in the very poor category; Sirsa in Haryana reported the highest city-level reading nationally at 368
Listen to This Article
Delhi's air quality remained firmly in the poor category on Thursday, with the city-wide AQI at 226 at 7 am, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data. While the reading was marginally lower than Wednesday's 228, pollution levels remained elevated across several parts of the capital, with three locations recording air quality in the very poor category.
Of the 59 monitoring stations in the capital, 56 had valid readings. Thirty-seven recorded AQI levels above 200, while three crossed 300 and entered the 'very poor' category. PM2.5 was the prominent pollutant in the city's average reading.
Anand Vihar recorded the highest AQI at 327, followed by Delhi Technological University (DTU) at 308 and North Campus, Delhi University, at 302. Pusa recorded 298, while ITO reported 296 and Burari Crossing 289.
At the other end, Sri Aurobindo Marg recorded the lowest AQI at 139, followed by Jharoda Kalan at 146 and Pusa (DPCC) at 147. IMD Lodhi Road reported 148, while Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium recorded 153. These locations were in the 'moderate' category.
NCR cities continue to report poor air
Also Read
Air quality across the National Capital Region (NCR) remained uneven, with several cities reporting readings in the poor category. Meerut in Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest AQI in the region at 276, followed by Ghaziabad and Greater Noida at 264 each.
Panchgaon in Haryana reported an AQI of 261, while Bhiwadi in Rajasthan recorded 246. Dharuhera and Manesar in Haryana reported readings of 238 and 233, respectively. Gurugram also recorded 233, while Noida stood at 228 and Delhi at 226.
Bahadurgarh reported an AQI of 217, followed by Rohtak at 211. Baghpat recorded 193, Bharatpur 192 and Sonipat 184. Faridabad reported an AQI of 172, while Hapur stood at 162.
Among the better-performing cities in the region, Palwal recorded the lowest AQI at 87, followed by Alwar at 112 and Panipat at 142.
Sirsa records India's highest AQI
Among the 286 cities with valid readings in the CPCB's 7 am dataset, Sirsa in Haryana recorded the highest AQI at 368, placing it in the 'very poor' category. Anpara in Uttar Pradesh followed at 307, while Darbhanga in Bihar reported 290.
Ballabgarh in Haryana recorded an AQI of 289, followed by Gajraula in Uttar Pradesh at 287. Sri Ganganagar in Rajasthan and Meerut in Uttar Pradesh both reported 276, while Kaithal in Haryana recorded 273.
At the other end, Chikkaballapur in Karnataka recorded the lowest AQI at 19, followed by Cuddalore in Tamil Nadu at 25 and Ramanagara in Karnataka at 26. Gangtok in Sikkim reported 27, while Eloor in Kerala and Madikeri in Karnataka recorded 30 each.
Under the CPCB's National Air Quality Index classification, readings between 0 and 50 are categorised as 'good', 51 and 100 as 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 as 'moderate', 201 and 300 as 'poor', 301 and 400 as 'very poor', and 401 and 500 as 'severe'.
Grap Stage II remains in force
Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (Grap) remains in force across Delhi-NCR, according to the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM). The measures include intensified mechanised road sweeping, dust suppression and water sprinkling, stricter enforcement of dust-control norms at construction sites, and steps to encourage the use of public transport.
The CAQM dashboard lists Stage II as active, with the order effective from November 2. The measures are intended to prevent further deterioration in air quality across the region.

title: SC examines duty-free shops' regulatory exemption in nicotine pouch case
description: The Supreme Court issued notice on a plea challenging a Bombay High Court ruling that goods sold at duty-free shops are not exempt from domestic regulatory requirements
author: Bhavini Mishra
content:
SC examines duty-free shops' regulatory exemption in nicotine pouch case
The Supreme Court issued notice on a plea challenging a Bombay High Court ruling that goods sold at duty-free shops are not exempt from domestic regulatory requirements
Listen to This Article
The Supreme Court on Wednesday issued notice on a plea by Mumbai Travel Retail Private Limited challenging a Bombay High Court ruling that goods imported into India are not exempt from domestic regulatory laws merely because they are stored or sold at duty-free shops beyond the customs frontier.
A Bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice Vipul M Pancholi issued notice after hearing senior advocate Shyam Divan, appearing for the company.
The dispute concerns restrictions imposed by authorities on the sale of tobacco-free nicotine pouches, marketed under the brands ZYN and FOX, at international departure duty-free outlets at Mumbai airport.
Divan argued that the High Court’s findings had implications extending beyond the products in question and could affect the entire duty-free retail industry.
He submitted that the ruling was contrary to the Supreme Court’s earlier judgments on the customs frontier and the point at which imported goods become part of the domestic market.
Also Read
Challenging the restrictions on the nicotine pouches, Divan said the High Court had accepted the company’s contention that there was no material to establish that the products were drugs.
However, it had declined to quash the communications restricting their sale and instead directed the company to approach the authorities with a representation.
He explained that the pouches are placed inside the mouth, allowing nicotine to be absorbed by the body. The products, he said, were sold in several countries and were not imported for domestic consumption in India.
On the legal position governing duty-free outlets, Divan submitted that goods stored in bonded warehouses for sale at such shops did not enter the domestic tariff area until they crossed the customs barrier. Relying on the Supreme Court’s judgments in Garden Silk Mills and Kiran Spinning Mills, he argued that import for domestic consumption was complete only when goods crossed the customs frontier and a bill of entry for home consumption was filed.
The Bench sought clarification on the distinction between goods entering India’s territorial waters and those crossing the customs barrier. Divan maintained that the two were legally distinct stages.
He also cited the Supreme Court’s ruling concerning duty-free shops operated by the India Tourism Development Corporation at Bengaluru airport, submitting that goods kept in bonded warehouses could not be treated as having crossed the customs frontier.
Divan cautioned that the High Court’s observations could have wider consequences for duty-free retailers, including the applicability of domestic laws governing metrology, packaging, standardised weights and food safety.
He further told the Bench that imports were broadly classified as free, restricted or prohibited, and that the nicotine pouches fell within the category of freely importable goods.
Their presence within airport premises, he argued, did not make them subject to the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, while they remained in bonded warehouses outside the domestic tariff area.
The products are sold at duty-free outlets operated by Mumbai Travel Retail and Flemingo Dutyfree Shop Private Limited at Mumbai International Airport.
Authorities restricted their sale on the ground that they qualified as drugs under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and required an import licence and registration.
The Bombay High Court held that the exemption available to duty-free shops was confined to fiscal measures, such as customs duties and indirect taxes, and did not extend to regulatory requirements under public health and safety laws.
It held that goods entering India’s territorial waters remained subject to domestic regulatory laws even when stored or sold through duty-free shops.
However, it declined to determine conclusively whether the nicotine pouches qualified as drugs under Section 3(b) of the Act, observing that their classification would depend on their composition and intended use.

title: Centre plans time-bound disposal of arbitral challenges, decree execution
description: The proposed amendments to the existing legal framework seek to improve the enforceability and finality of arbitral awards and ensure the timely execution of decrees
author: Bhavini Mishra
content:
Centre plans time-bound disposal of arbitral challenges, decree execution
The proposed amendments to the existing legal framework seek to improve the enforceability and finality of arbitral awards and ensure the timely execution of decrees
Listen to This Article
The Centre is proposing further amendments to ensure that challenges to arbitral awards and execution of decrees are resolved within a stipulated timeframe, Rajiv Mani, secretary, legislative department and department of legal affairs, Ministry of Law and Justice, said on Wednesday. 
Speaking at the ICA-SCC Arbitration Institute Conclave in New Delhi, Mani said the proposed changes would build on the existing legal framework, including the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, and the Commercial Courts Act, 2015, to improve the enforceability and finality of arbitral awards. 
“Besides the enactment of the Commercial Courts Act of 2015, we are also proposing to introduce further amendments so that the finality of an arbitral award, when challenged under the applicable law and the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, is resolved within a time-bound manner, and the execution of the decree takes place, of course, in a time-bound manner,” he said. 
The remarks come as India and the European Union (EU) move towards operationalising their free trade agreement (FTA), which is expected to expand cross-border trade and investment.  
The India-EU Investment Protection Agreement is also under negotiation, with an early conclusion in view, Mani said. 
Also Read
He said a predictable dispute-resolution framework would be particularly important for smaller enterprises, exporters, and startups seeking to benefit from increased access to international markets. The government also wants arbitration to expand beyond metropolitan centres to Tier-II and Tier-III cities. 
Mani said arbitration and mediation should be viewed as complementary mechanisms rather than competing alternatives. While arbitration provides a binding adjudication of disputes, mediation allows parties to reach mutually acceptable settlements while preserving commercial relationships. 
He cited the Mediation Act, 2023, as an important addition to India's dispute-resolution framework and said multi-tiered dispute-resolution clauses combining negotiation, mediation, and arbitration could help parties resolve disagreements more efficiently. 
Pre-institution mediation under the Commercial Courts Act also provides an opportunity to settle disputes before approaching courts, he added. 
Welcoming the conclusion of negotiations on the India-EU FTA, Mani said the agreement could be signed soon, possibly within the year.  
He said stronger economic ties between the two sides would require a partnership built on trust and effective mechanisms to address commercial disputes. 
India and the EU recorded merchandise trade of approximately $136.5 billion in 2024-25. The FTA is expected to provide preferential market access for around 99.5 per cent of Indian exports by trade value once it comes into force. 
Arun Chawla, director general of the Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA), said the agreement could reduce the cost of doing business, while effective dispute-resolution mechanisms would help lower the risks associated with cross-border transactions.
He said arbitral institutions needed to focus on credibility, efficiency, and adaptability, particularly as commercial disputes increasingly involve emerging technologies, energy transition, infrastructure, and intellectual property (IP).
On the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in arbitration, he said technology should strengthen human judgment rather than compromise the independence and fairness of adjudication.
Petra Menander, Sweden's ambassador to India, said bilateral trade between the two countries had expanded significantly over the past decade, with Sweden doubling its exports to India and India tripling its exports to Sweden. The two countries aim to double their economic exchange by 2030.
Caroline Falconer, secretary general of the SCC Arbitration Institute, said parties from more than 90 countries had used the Stockholm-based institution over the past decade. Indian parties featured in its caseload almost every year, primarily in disputes involving European companies. Most arbitrations administered by the institution concluded in approximately a year, she said.
The conclave, organised by the ICA and SCC Arbitration Institute, also discussed the implications of changing trade, investment, and technology trends for India-EU dispute resolution.

title: Delhi AQI today: India’s capital suffers from severe air quality at 263 on November 26, faces high risk of asthma
description: Delhi’s AQI stood at 263 on the US scale Thursday morning, down from an overnight peak of 334 but still posing a high risk of asthma symptoms, according to AQI.in.
author: Sounak Mukhopadhyay
content:
Smoky haze covered Delhi on Thursday, November 26, as air quality reached the severe category. The Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 263 at 8:41 AM on the US scale. It fell 71 points from the overnight peak of 334. New Delhi ranked 60th among the world’s most polluted cities at the time. Delhi’s air quality improved through Wednesday afternoon before worsening again in the evening. The AQI fell to 165 at 5:01 PM, its lowest in the previous 24 hours. It rose above 300 before midnight, reaching 334 at 3:31 AM on Thursday. Readings remained above 300 until after 5 AM, then eased later in the morning. The November calendar shows a reading of 226 for Wednesday, down from 236 on Tuesday. Monday’s reading was higher at 311. The highest daily figure through November 25 was 666 on November 9. The next highest was 547 on November 12. All 14 days in the first fortnight had readings above 300. Delhi’s seven-day AQI peaked at 532 at 6 AM on November 19. That seven-day period ended on November 25. The lowest reading in that series was 186 at noon on November 25. Early morning readings were above 400 on several days during that stretch. The latest morning reading was roughly half the seven-day peak. Delhi’s PM10 level was 261 micrograms per cubic metre across the city at 8:41 am. The World Health Organization’s guideline is 45 micrograms per cubic metre. Delhi’s reading was about 5.8 times that level. The PM10 reading fell in the unhealthy category. The concentration of finer PM2.5 particles was 186 micrograms per cubic metre. Carbon monoxide stood at 2,214 parts per billion. Nitrogen dioxide measured 20 parts per billion while sulphur dioxide measured six. Ozone was recorded at one part per billion. The temperature was 17°C and humidity was 48%. The wind speed was 5.4 km/h, and the UV index was 0.5. New Delhi had the highest AQI among 8 Indian metros. It ranked 273rd in that comparison, followed by Kolkata at 256. Pune recorded 198, Mumbai 185 and Ahmedabad 175. Chennai stood at 125. Bengaluru had the lowest reading at 71, followed by Hyderabad at 92. AQI.in flagged a high risk of asthma symptoms at the reported pollution level. The symptoms listed include wheezing, breathlessness, chest tightness and a persistent cough. It advised people with asthma to stay indoors and keep windows closed to reduce exposure. It also advised against strenuous outdoor activity and exposure to secondhand smoke. title: Sri Lanka allows Indians to travel without ETA approval temporarily | What travellers should know
description: Sri Lanka has temporarily waived prior ETA approval for Indian travellers while its ETA system undergoes maintenance. The move aims to prevent travel disruptions.
author: Sanchari Ghosh
content:
Sri Lanka has temporarily waived prior Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) approval for Indian travellers due to maintenance of its ETA system. Hence, Indian travellers can now visit the island nation without obtaining ETA approval until further notice. Mahishini Colonné, High Commissioner of Sri Lanka to India, informed in a post, Important travel update for Indian travellers to Sri Lanka Due to temporary maintenance of Sri Lanka’s ETA system, Indian travellers may travel to Sri Lanka without prior ETA approval, until further notice. “We regret any inconvenience caused and appreciate your understanding,” she added The temporary relaxation is intended to ease travel disruptions while the system undergoes maintenance. Sri Lanka, earlier this year, announced launching a six-country tourism ‌promotion campaign to nearly double arrivals during its peak winter season and earn $4.2 billion. The largely digital promotions will focus on key source markets Australia, China, Germany, the UK, Russia and India ahead of Sri Lanka launching a long-delayed global promotion campaign in April 2027, said Roshan Ranasinghe, deputy minister of tourism, as reported by Reuters. "Tourism is crucial for our economy. After the delay of nearly a decade this global campaign is to take Sri Lanka to the world, to crucial markets, and to give a realistic idea of what is available in Sri Lanka," he told reporters at a briefing in Colombo. Tourism is the third-largest foreign exchange earner in the country of 22 million, famed for its pristine beaches, ancient temples and aromatic tea. Sri Lanka recorded 1.3 million arrivals in ‌the first seven months of this year after experiencing about a 20% decline in March and April due to the Gulf crisis. Tourism earnings were $1.5 billion at the end of July, latest government data showed. The island subsequently revised its initial target of 3 million arrivals to 2.7 million and is expecting $4.2 billion in revenue. Sri Lanka earned $3.2 billion from tourism in 2025. Sri Lanka, which imports all its fuel, has struggled with soaring energy costs from the Iran war, which have increased prices by about 35% since March, prompting fuel rationing and the declaration of Wednesdays as public holidays. Tourism dollars are also crucial for the island to boost its foreign exchange reserves, which stood at $6.6 billion at the end of last month. The Central Bank of Sri Lanka raised its key policy rate by 100 basis points to 8.75% in May, partly to reduce pressure on the rupee. title: Akshaya Patra pitches public-private model to tackle hunger at UN dialogue
description: The Akshaya Patra Foundation highlighted its school-meal model at a UN development dialogue in Geneva, arguing that feeding children can serve both as a social safety net and a long-term investment in nutrition and development. The foundation said its 26-year partnership with the government under the PM Poshan programme shows how public, private and non-profit sectors can work together to address hunger.
author: ET Bureau
content:
The foundation participated in a panel discussion on “Responsibility by Design: Promising Business Practices” at the Development Dialogues at the Palais des Nations on November 24.
The event, hosted by Prof Surya Deva, UN Special Rapporteur on the Right to Development, was held on the sidelines of the UN Forum on Business and Human Rights.
The discussion focused on ways businesses can integrate responsibility towards people and the environment into their business models, governance, incentives and day-to-day operations.
“Feeding schoolchildren is a systematic, strategic social intervention that can provide food and nutrition security and act as a social safety net through child development,” said Naveena Neerada Dasa, executive director for strategy and international affairs at Akshaya Patra.
The foundation has implemented the government’s flagship PM Poshan mid-day meal programme for the past 26 years, he said.
Dasa described Akshaya Patra as a “time-tested public-private partnership” bringing together the government and the for-profit and non-profit sectors to address hunger.
“Every meal for a child is an investment for a sustainable future,” he said.
Highlighting the scope for businesses and non-profits to learn from each other, Dasa said companies across sectors have demonstrated that human rights and environmental considerations can be integrated into their operations while remaining profitable.
Such successful models should be promoted as “proof-of-concept” case studies to help other organisations understand how human rights and environmental considerations can be incorporated into their business models, he added.
