title: Nepal flash floods: Kathmandu begins process to declare 213 missing Indians presumed dead
description: Nepal begins death declarations for 213 missing Indians from August flash floods; objections invited by December 2 via embassy contact details.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
The Nepal government has begun the process of presumption and declaration of death for 213 Indian nationals who remain missing since the flash floods in August this year, the Indian Embassy in Nepal said.
The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) has published a list of the 213 missing Indian nationals for presumption and declaration of death on its website, the Embassy said in a press release on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).
The NDRRMA has invited objections for additions, deletions or amendments in the details contained in the list.
In case the family members of persons who remain missing have any concerns, objections or proposed changes regarding this list, they can contact the Indian Embassy before December 2, it said. They could contact via the email address eoikathmandufloodsupport@gmail.com or mobile phone number +9779851316807.
The Nepal government will finalise the list and formally issue the declaration of death after completing the process of seeking comments or amendments.
The Embassy will then begin obtaining death certificates for these individuals from local authorities in Nepal.
Nepal’s flash floods: How can communities rebuild after a disaster?
During this process, the Embassy may seek additional details and documents from family members of the missing persons, and will provide a suitable update in the coming days, it said.
The August 26 flash floods that took place in the Trishuli-Bhote Koshi river system killed at least 1,453 people, and left more than 5,000 missing, according to the NDRRMA.
Flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal. Flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal.

title: Uttariya instead of robes: West Bengal Government suggests universities to adopt Indian attire in convocations
description: West Bengal urges universities to replace Western robes with Indian handloom attire like Uttariya for convocations to promote culture and sustainability.
author: Senjuti Sengupta
content:
West Bengal Higher Education Department has advised all the State-aided universities to adopt Indian attire such as Uttariya and clothes made of handloom fabric instead of Western robes during convocation or any academic ceremony.
“We are putting effort to follow our own Indian culture and tradition. Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies. Why do we have to wear robes? Many institutions, including the Indian Institute of Technology [IIT], have adopted only uttariya. Hence, we made the suggestion,” West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay told media persons on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).
The development also came days after Mr. Chattopadhyay praised the Jalpaiguri Government Engineering College for upholding Indian traditions by replacing the conventional academic gown with a traditional uttariya.
“As we strive to build a self-reliant Bharat, our education system must also reflect our civilisational values and cultural identity,” he wrote on X congratulating the students of the college.
In its notice sent to all the vice chancellors of the universities, the department has now said that the UGC had not prescribed any rigid uniform design for ceremonial robes.
Hence, the universities have the flexibility to incorporate traditional Indian attire, such as the uttariya, and to design distinct ceremonial attire for dignitaries and degree recipients.
Monday’s (November 23) notice to the V-Cs said that the ceremonial attire made from Indian handloom was more suited to India’s climate. Such a preference for handloom fabrics and traditional Indian attire also supports the rural handloom industry and weavers’ livelihoods, it said.
“In view of the above, you are requested to take necessary steps to consider adopting handloom fabrics and traditional attire for the academic robes worn during convocation in your esteemed university as well as affiliated colleges, wherever applicable,” the department stated in the advisory asking the universities to send to confirmation of the communication to the department.

title: Thirupparankundram Deepathoon row: What does John Doe order passed by Madras HC mean?
description: Thirupparankundram Deepathoon row: What is Madras HC's John Doe order?
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, on November 24, 2026, passed a ‘John Doe’ order in the Deepathoon case with regard to the lighting of the lamp at Thirupparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai for Karthigai Deepam. The High Court bench restrained anyone from violating the November 20 Supreme Court order which allowed the lighting of the lamp on the hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement” only.
Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row LIVE
What is a John Doe order?
A ‘John Doe’ order is an ex parte injuction ordered against unknown persons. Ex parte injunctions are injunctions that are granted even without hearing the other party. Issued against anonymous offenders, these are also called ‘Ashok Kumar’ orders in India and are equivalents of the place holder ‘John Doe’ used in the U.S.
Who are John Doe orders issued against?
Often used as a prohibitory measure by the courts, John Doe orders are issued against anonymous offenders or the world at large.
In the Thirupparankundram-Deepathoon case, the High Court restricted “members of the general public” from calling for violating the November 20 order issued by the Supreme Court on the issue.
What did the court say in the Deepathoon order?
“Article 144 of the Constitution mandates that all authorities, civil and judicial, in the territory of India shall act in aid of the Supreme Court. The District Collector is a civilian authority and Article 144 will squarely apply to him. Since officials brazenly defied judicial orders last year in connection with Karthigai Deepam, we deem it necessary to remind the District Collector that he is a public servant who is answerable only to the Supreme Court in this case. He shall ignore any contra advice given by any other authority,” the Bench said.
“We are sure that no law officer worth his salt will counsel him to act in contravention of the order dated November 20. No doubt, a review petition has been filed before the Supreme Court in respect of the order dated November 20. But no order has been passed in the review petition...The law that has been laid down is that pendency of a review petition is not a ground for non-compliance,” the court added.
Frequently used in intellectual property right cases
John Doe or Ashok Kumar orders are frequently used in intellectual property right cases.
A 2021 report published in The Hindu notes that there has been a rise in John Doe orders as a “pre-emptive measure against copyright infringement.”
A 2026 report in The Hindu notes that actor Salman Khan had “sought an injunction against unknown persons, joined as Defendant No. 1 (’John Doe’ or ‘Ashok Kumar’) in a case relating to a China-based AI voice generation platform seeking to vacate an interim injunction protecting Mr Khan’s personality rights.
What is the Thirupparankundram Deepathoon issue?
The controversy revolves around the Thirupparankanduram hillock in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai and the lighting of a ceremonial lamp on the day of Karthigai Deepam.
On November 20, the Supreme Court had ruled allowing the lighting of the lamp on the deepathoon atop the Thirupparankundram Hill as a “limited one-time arrangement.” The deepathoon, or stone lamp pillar, is around 50 metres from the Sikandar Badusha Dargah. While the dargah is on the hilltop, the Subramaniya Swamy Temple is at the base of the hillock. The court’s interim arrangement comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the dargah on the ownership of the hilltop and the deepathoon site.
However, the ruling TVK government on November 24, defied the Supreme Court order, and the festival lamp was lit only at its customary place at the Thirupparankundram hill.

title: CJP leader Ashutosh Ranka expresses solidarity with Indian student at Oxford alleging racism
description: Cockroach Janta Party leader Ashutosh Ranka on Thursday expressed solidarity with Indian PhD student Kamakshi. | India News
author: ANI
content:
CJP leader Ashutosh Ranka expresses solidarity with Indian student at Oxford alleging racism
Cockroach Janta Party leader Ashutosh Ranka on Thursday expressed solidarity with Indian PhD student Kamakshi.
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Ashutosh Ranka on Thursday expressed solidarity with Indian PhD student Kamakshi, who has alleged racial discrimination at the University of Oxford, and urged the Indian Embassy to raise the issue with the British government, saying that racism and casteism should "not be tolerated".
Reacting to a viral video in which Kamakshi alleged that she faced a racially charged encounter and was told, "You smell...", Ranka said he had witnessed instances of Indian students facing racism during his four years in London, including from other Indian students.
Also Read I CJP’s Saurav Das claims his passport leaked, blames ‘BJP-aligned’ social media handles
Deep Dive
"Look, regarding racism, I lived in London for four years myself. I have seen instances where Indian students face racism, sometimes even from other Indian students. This is completely unacceptable. I haven't seen the specific video you are referring to, but we stand firmly with such students. Racism should not happen, and neither should casteism. We will request and urge the Indian Embassy to raise this issue with the British government; however, I do not know the exact details yet," he told ANI.
PhD student shares racist encounter
Kamakshi, who is pursuing a PhD at the University of Oxford, shared a video on Instagram recounting a racially charged encounter she experienced while shopping in the city. She also spoke about broader experiences of racism faced by people of colour in Oxford and prestigious academic institutions.
Explaining why she decided to speak about such experiences, Kamakshi said that the support she received after a racist comment was posted on one of her earlier posts encouraged her to speak out.
"All of you were so angry on my behalf [that it] made me realise that I was doing a disservice to you by not talking to you about the negative experiences that people have in Oxford," she said.
On Congress-Meta meet
Ranka also reacted to the reported meeting between Congress leaders and Meta officials amid allegations of content restrictions on the social media platform, accusing the platform of digital censorship and questioning the deletion of 54 lakh posts in six months.
He alleged that Meta deleted 5.4 million posts between January and June 2026, with the reasons cited being government directions or compliance with government regulations.
"Between January and June 2026 - a span of six months - Meta deleted 5.4 million (54 lakh) posts. Each time, the only reason provided is that it was done at the behest of the government or in compliance with government regulations. What has transpired in this country that necessitated the deletion of 5.4 million posts in just six months?" he said.
Alleging that the platform's algorithm favoured content related to Prime Minister Narendra Modi while suppressing posts about Dr BR Ambedkar, Ranka said, "When photos or videos of Mr Modi are posted, the algorithm promotes them effectively. Conversely, if we post content about Babasaheb, the algorithm suppresses it. When we attempt to raise substantive issues, the algorithm ensures they are completely buried."
He further alleged that digital censorship was being carried out deliberately in the country and said the party would oppose it.
"Digital censorship is being enforced in this country in a very clear, deliberate manner—something we will absolutely not accept, and we will raise our voices against it, united," he added.
Ranka on Constitution Day
On Constitution Day, Ranka described the occasion as one of the most important days of the year, saying that the Constitution embodied the ideology and values of the nation.
"Constitution Day is one of the most important days of the year. Our Constitution embodies the ideology and values of our nation. In recent years, we have witnessed how protecting the Constitution itself has become a major challenge. The very values and ideals enshrined in our Constitution, the principles laid out in our Preamble, are currently under threat of destruction," he said.
Also Read I ‘CJP is not going to get into elections’: Abhijeet Dipke on upcoming UP polls
He said the occasion held greater significance in the present circumstances and appealed to people across the country to come forward to protect the Constitution.
"This is precisely why today holds even greater significance. We appeal to the people across the country to come forward and protect the Constitution. Only if the Constitution survives, will this nation survive," Ranka added.

title: 'I will handle them': The story of 26/11 hero Major Sandeep Unnikrishnan
description: Major Sandeep Unnikrishnan's actions during the operation would become one of the defining accounts of courage and sacrifice during the 26/11 attacks. | India News
author: Shubham Pandey
content:
Shubham Pandey works as Chief Content Producer at the Hindustan Times online desk, where he writes news articles, explainers, and features with a focus on audience engagement, traffic growth, and real-time storytelling. With over a decade of experience across journalism, digital newsrooms, and strategic communications, he brings a strong understanding of online journalism, particularly in leveraging SEO, search trends, and live blogs to drive sustained reader engagement. Previously, he led the sports team at Zee News English, strengthening editorial operations while delivering measurable growth in readership. His reporting experience includes assignments with Firstpost, where he covered sports with a strong narrative focus. Shubham has worked across both startups and large media organisations, including building a sports website from the ground up in a startup environment—demonstrating versatility and leadership. His stint as Senior Account Manager at Edelman India further expanded his expertise in strategic communications, brand storytelling, and reputation management. Across roles, he specialises in content planning, writing, and crafting credible narratives for diverse audiences. He has collaborated with former international cricketers Cheteshwar Pujara, Nick Knight, and Danny Morrison to create compelling, high-impact sports content, blending editorial depth with mass appeal. When he is not writing news or watching sports, he enjoys exploring films from around the world.
'I will handle them': The story of 26/11 hero Major Sandeep Unnikrishnan
Major Sandeep Unnikrishnan's actions during the operation would become one of the defining accounts of courage and sacrifice during the 26/11 attacks.
On the night of November 26, 2008, Mumbai came under attack. Ten heavily armed terrorists who arrived from Pakistan struck multiple locations across the city, including Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, the Oberoi Trident, Nariman House and the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel. Gunfire and explosions shattered the city's sense of security as people were killed, hostages were taken and several buildings turned into battlegrounds.
As the attacks unfolded, ordinary citizens and security personnel found themselves caught in an unprecedented crisis. Railway staff and police officers helped people escape danger, hotel employees risked their lives to guide guests to safety, and security forces moved in to confront the terrorists.
The rescue operations lasted three days, with the siege at the Taj Hotel emerging as one of the most intense and prolonged encounters.
Among those who entered the burning hotel to take on the terrorists was Major Sandeep Unnikrishnan of the National Security Guard (NSG). His actions during the operation would become one of the defining accounts of courage and sacrifice during the 26/11 attacks.
Major Unnikrishnan's heroics
As the Taj's interiors filled with smoke and terrorists unleashed grenades and gunfire, Major Unnikrishnan led his team through the hotel, clearing rooms and confronting the attackers. During the operation, a fellow commando, Sunil Yadav, was wounded. Unnikrishnan helped evacuate him from the hotel and get him to a medical team waiting outside.
But he did not retreat with his injured colleague. Instead, he returned to the building and continued the operation.
Before returning to the firefight, he spoke to the other commandos, delivering words that would later become synonymous with his courage: “Do not come up, I will handle them.”
Unnikrishnan went on to engage the terrorists alone. He was eventually shot in the back by the attackers and succumbed to his injuries on November 28, as commandos continued to search the hotel floor by floor. By then, the operation at the Taj had turned into a prolonged gun battle, with the siege lasting around 60 hours.
Looking back
For those who knew him, his decision to return to the fight was not entirely surprising. His childhood friends remembered him as someone who was fearless, decisive and always willing to take responsibility.
Known as “U Sandeep” in school, he studied at Frank Anthony Public School in Bengaluru. His classmate Sandeep Naidu, who spent nearly a decade with him, recalled him as bold and upfront, but never arrogant.
“He was bold, upfront and wanted to be in control. He had so much conviction but was never pompous. He made up his mind to join the army when he was in class eight,” Naidu told HT in an earlier interview.
The Unnikrishnan family had moved from Cheruvannur in Kerala's Kozhikode district to Bengaluru. His father, K Unnikrishnan, worked as an officer at the Indian Space Research Organisation before retiring in 2007. His parents initially hoped their son would become a doctor, but Sandeep had other plans.
His determination to join the armed forces was evident from an early age. As a teenager, he travelled alone from Bengaluru to Bhopal to pursue admission to the Indian Navy through the National Defence Academy (NDA). He informed his parents of his plans only after clearing the entrance examination and then insisted on making the journey on his own.
His mother, Dhanalakshmi, later recalled how other parents called to congratulate the family after learning that he had managed to reach Bhopal on his own.
Although he could not join the Navy because of a minor vision defect, the setback did not end his ambition. A few months later, he received a call from the Army and joined the 7 Bihar Regiment, based in Danapur, after completing his training at the Indian Military Academy in 1999.
At the NDA, Unnikrishnan earned a reputation for being selfless, generous and composed. His slim build concealed a formidable determination, which became evident during training camps and cross-country races. He also topped the Army's Ghatak Course, a demanding programme designed to prepare soldiers for combat operations.
A story from his days at the academy offered a glimpse of the person he was beyond the uniform.
During a trek up Sinhagad Fort near Pune, a group of cadets had run short of water. Unnikrishnan was the first to reach a well and began filling their canteens. But when a tourist approached him with a water bottle, he filled it first. More tourists followed, and he continued drawing water for them. By the time he was done, he had not managed to fill his own canteen.
His friend and fellow cadet, Prasenjit Mund, recalled the incident in an earlier interview with HT as an example of Unnikrishnan's instinctive generosity. Without complaining, he had put the needs of strangers ahead of his own.
In 2007, Unnikrishnan joined the National Security Guard and was assigned to its Special Action Group (SAG), the force's elite counter-terrorism unit. He was eventually entrusted with leading the 51 Special Action Group team deployed during the Mumbai attacks.

title: Former Karnataka minister Nagendra exonerated of misappropriation of funds
description: Karnataka’s CID named B Nagendra  a witnesses rather than accused in its final charge sheet filed in a special court | India News
author: Arun Dev
content:
Arun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.
Former Karnataka minister Nagendra exonerated of misappropriation of funds
Karnataka’s CID named B Nagendra a witnesses rather than accused in its final charge sheet filed in a special court
Karnataka’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has exonerated former minister B Nagendra of misappropriating funds from the Maharishi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation and named him and the corporation’s former chairman, Basavaraj Daddal, as key witnesses rather than as accused in its final charge sheet filed in the Lokayukta Special Court on Wednesday.
It said it found no evidence that Nagendra misappropriated the corporation’s funds or was aware of the alleged illegal transactions between officials and private intermediaries, according to an investigator familiar with the findings. The CID identified the corporation’s then managing director Parashuram, Nekkunti Nagaraj, and Hyderabad-based businessman Satyanarayana Varma as the principal accused, the investigator added.
Nagendra was forced to resign as the scheduled tribes welfare minister in 2024 when the alleged misappropriation first surfaced. The case involves the alleged diversion of ₹89.62 crore from the corporation, which implements welfare programmes for scheduled tribe communities. The money was transferred to accounts in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana through allegedly fraudulent transactions and forged documents.
The matter came to light in May 2024 after an accounts superintendent with the corporation died by suicide at his residence in Shivamogga. In a note, he alleged irregularities in the corporation’s financial transactions and pointed to the involvement of senior officials. A subsequent complaint led to a police investigation, which was later handed over to the CID.
The CID found the diversion was facilitated by an arrangement between the corporation’s then managing director and private intermediaries. Nagaraj allegedly persuaded Parashuram to transfer the corporation’s money by promising that it would be doubled through investments.
The CID concluded that the transactions were carried out without Nagendra’s knowledge. It examined the role of bank officials in facilitating the transfers and the use of forged documents to move the money.
The case became a major political embarrassment for the Congress government, with the Opposition Bharatiya Janata Party and Janata Dal (Secular) accusing it of failing to protect funds meant for scheduled tribe communities. Nagendra was re-inducted into the Cabinet in August but resigned days later following renewed Opposition pressure.
Central agencies, the Central Bureau of Investigation and the Enforcement Directorate, are also probing the diversion of the corporation’s funds.

title: Gandhi Family Legacy Vs SP's Numbers: Who Really Has The Stronger Claim To Amethi-Rae Bareli?
description: The Congress sees the region as central to its revival in Uttar Pradesha but the SP sees little reason to surrender constituencies where it has built a stronger electoral presence
author: News18
content:
Gandhi Family Legacy Vs SP's Numbers: Who Really Has The Stronger Claim To Amethi-Rae Bareli?
The Congress sees the region as central to its revival in Uttar Pradesha but the SP sees little reason to surrender constituencies where it has built a stronger electoral presence
Got Question about the News?
The Samajwadi Party’s decision to offer the Congress just one assembly seat across Amethi and Rae Bareli has struck a particularly sensitive nerve in the ongoing seat-sharing negotiations for Uttar Pradesh and it’s not difficult to guess why. These are not just two parliamentary constituencies for the Congress but the heart of the Gandhi family’s political legacy in the state, and the party’s claim to them is rooted in decades of electoral history.
However, the Samajwadi Party, led by Akhilesh Yadav, has a different argument—political legacy cannot be the only basis for deciding who contests a seat. The numbers on the ground, particularly in assembly elections, tell a very different story.
- Baat Jeet Ki Hai: Akhilesh Urges Congress To Focus On Winnability As SP Names First 5 UP Poll Picks
- UP Polls 2027: Akhilesh Forms Seat-Sharing Panel, Congress Demands Respectable Share | News18
- Rs 40,000 Pension For Women, Caste Census, Free Metro Rides For Students: SP To Unveil 'Jan-Man' Manifesto Today
- SP Sends Clear Message To Congress: No Bihar-Like Seat-Sharing Formula In Uttar Pradesh | Exclusive Details
That is what makes Amethi and Rae Bareli an important test of the Congress-SP alliance. The Congress sees the region as central to its revival in Uttar Pradesha but the SP sees little reason to surrender constituencies where it has built a stronger electoral presence.
ALSO READ | How Many UP Seats Does Congress ‘Deserve’ Based On Winnability? Depends On Who You Ask
So, why are these 10 assembly seats so important to both parties, what does their electoral history reveal, and why is the Gandhi family’s legacy not enough to settle the argument?
Why Amethi And Rae Bareli Matter So Much To Congress
The Congress’s emotional and political claim over the two parliamentary constituencies is difficult to dispute.
Amethi has been associated with the Gandhi family since Sanjay Gandhi won the Lok Sabha seat in 1980. After his death, Rajiv Gandhi represented it, followed by Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi. Rahul won Amethi in 2004, 2009 and 2014, before losing to the BJP’s Smriti Irani in 2019.
Rae Bareli has an even longer association with the family. Feroze Gandhi represented the constituency in the first two Lok Sabha elections, followed by Indira Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi and, most recently, Rahul Gandhi. Sonia won Rae Bareli four consecutive times before Rahul took over the seat in 2024.
ALSO READ | Not Just 2 Seats: Can Saharanpur Make Or Break Congress-SP Alliance Ahead Of UP Elections?
The 2024 Lok Sabha election also helped the Congress re-establish its presence in the region. Rahul Gandhi won Rae Bareli, while party candidate Kishori Lal Sharma defeated Smriti Irani in Amethi.
For the Congress, therefore, these constituencies are not simply seats where it wants to contest. They are central to its political identity in Uttar Pradesh. Being offered only one assembly seat across the two parliamentary constituencies is likely to be seen as a symbolic downgrade, particularly at a time when the party is trying to rebuild its organisation in the state.
But Lok Sabha victories and assembly-level strength are two different things.
What The 10 Assembly Seats Tell Us
The two parliamentary constituencies together comprise 10 assembly segments—five each in Amethi and Rae Bareli. And the 2022 assembly election results offer the clearest explanation for why the SP believes it has a stronger claim to most of them.
The Congress failed to win even one of these 10 seats in 2022. The SP won six, while the BJP took the remaining four. This is a significant shift from the region’s older political map, where the Congress had enjoyed a much stronger presence.
ALSO READ | ‘Are We Beggars?’ Imran Masood Sees Red As SP Stakes Claim To Saharanpur Amid UP Alliance Talks
In fact, 2007 was among the last major electoral highs for the Congress in this belt. Several constituencies that the party had won repeatedly, including Amethi, Bachhrawan and Sareni, had their last Congress victories in that election. The party briefly revived in 2017, winning Harchandpur and Rae Bareli, but could not hold on to that ground.
Amethi: Congress’s legacy, SP’s foothold
The five assembly constituencies under the Amethi Lok Sabha seat are Amethi, Gauriganj, Jagdishpur, Salon and Tiloi.
The SP won Amethi and Gauriganj in 2022, while the BJP secured Tiloi, Jagdishpur and Salon. The Congress did not win any of the five.
The Amethi assembly seat itself has changed hands between the SP and BJP over the past three elections. Congress’s Ameeta Singh last won it in 2007. The SP’s Gayatri Prajapati captured it in 2012, the BJP won it in 2017, and the SP returned in 2022 with Maharaji Prajapati as its candidate.
Gauriganj has also been an important constituency for the SP. Rakesh Pratap Singh won it three consecutive times from 2012, although his subsequent expulsion from the party and movement towards the BJP have complicated the local political picture.
Jagdishpur is particularly relevant to the current negotiations. The BJP won the seat in 2022, with the Congress finishing second. It is the one assembly seat from the Amethi-Rae Bareli belt included in the SP’s reported 26-seat offer to the Congress.
The Congress may see Jagdishpur as a starting point in a region it considers its own. But the SP’s larger argument is that the party’s historical association with Amethi has not translated into Assembly victories.
Rae Bareli: A Stronger Case For SP
The five assembly segments under Rae Bareli are Bachhrawan, Harchandpur, Rae Bareli, Sareni and Unchahar. Here, the SP’s claim is even stronger. It won four of the five seats in 2022, with the BJP taking Rae Bareli.
Bachhrawan, once a Congress stronghold, was won by the party repeatedly between 1967 and 1991. It returned to Congress in 2007, but the SP won it in 2012, the BJP in 2017 and the SP again in 2022.
Harchandpur and Rae Bareli offer a particularly telling picture of the Congress’s declining assembly presence. The party won both seats in 2017. However, its Harchandpur MLA Rakesh Singh and Rae Bareli MLA Aditi Singh subsequently moved to the BJP. Aditi Singh retained Rae Bareli in 2022 as a BJP candidate, while the SP won Harchandpur. Sareni has also shifted between parties. The Congress last won it in 2007, followed by victories for the SP in 2012, the BJP in 2017 and the SP again in 2022.
Unchahar, meanwhile, was represented by Manoj Kumar Pandey, who won three consecutive elections on an SP ticket before moving towards the BJP.
The result is that the SP has built a substantial assembly-level presence even in a region that remains closely identified with the Gandhi family.
Why The 2024 Lok Sabha Results Do Not Settle The Argument
The Congress has reason to point to its improved performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. It won six seats in Uttar Pradesh, including Amethi and Rae Bareli, while the SP emerged as the state’s biggest party with 37 seats.
But the results also came in an alliance. The Congress’s victories cannot be viewed entirely as a measure of its independent organisational strength, especially when the SP’s support and vote transfer were important to the INDIA bloc’s performance.
This is an argument that SP leaders have repeatedly made during the current negotiations. In October, SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel claimed that the Congress would not have won any seats in Uttar Pradesh without the alliance. He also said Rahul Gandhi had been reluctant to contest from Amethi in 2024 and was persuaded by Akhilesh Yadav to contest from Rae Bareli.
The Congress pushed back against the remarks, with its state spokesperson Anshu Awasthi saying that Patel himself had become an MP because of the INDIA bloc.
The exchange exposed a larger disagreement between the allies: how much of the 2024 electoral success should be credited to the Congress’s revival, and how much to the SP’s support?
For the Congress, the Lok Sabha results show that it has recovered some political ground and deserves a larger role in the state. For the SP, the assembly record remains the more relevant measure when deciding who can win individual constituencies.
Why The One-Seat Offer Has Become A Bigger Issue
The reported offer of just one seat in Amethi and Rae Bareli is part of a much wider disagreement over the overall seat-sharing formula.
The Congress initially sought 131 seats and later revised its demand to 120. The SP, meanwhile, offered 26 constituencies in its initial proposal. According to the SP’s stated reasoning, the 26 included the two seats the Congress won in 2022—Rampur Khas and Farenda—four where it finished second, and 20 additional constituencies.
Jagdishpur was among the four seats where the Congress finished runner-up. The offer, therefore, appears to be based on the party’s recent assembly performance rather than its historical association with the region.
The Congress, however, has a different calculation. Its demand for seats is not limited to constituencies where it won or finished second in the last assembly election. It wants to use the 2024 Lok Sabha results, its traditional pockets of influence and its plans to rebuild its organisation as part of the negotiations.
The dispute is also about local political stakes. In constituencies where the SP has sitting MLAs or leaders who have built their own bases over several elections, giving the Congress a ticket could mean overlooking established party workers and aspirants. For Akhilesh Yadav, that is not a small concession to make.
At the same time, giving the Congress only one seat in the Gandhi family’s political backyard risks sending a message that the party is being treated as a junior partner even in areas central to its identity.
What This Means For The Congress-SP Alliance
Amethi and Rae Bareli are unlikely to decide the entire seat-sharing arrangement on their own. But they capture the central contradiction in the negotiations.
The Congress wants to convert its national leadership, Gandhi family legacy and improved Lok Sabha performance into a larger Assembly presence. The SP wants seat allocation to reflect its stronger organisation and electoral performance in the state.
Akhilesh Yadav has publicly said that winnability should guide the negotiations and that the two parties should work towards consensus candidates capable of defeating the BJP. But the question is who gets to define winnability: the party’s past performance, its current organisational strength, the 2024 Lok Sabha vote, or its potential to expand.
That is where the two sides are struggling to find common ground.
Quick Answers
Amethi and Rae Bareli are deeply tied to the Gandhi family's history, having been represented by leaders like Feroze Gandhi, Indira Gandhi, Sanjay Gandhi, Rajiv Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi, and Rahul Gandhi over the decades. For Congress, these constituencies represent the emotional and political heart of its identity in Uttar Pradesh, making them central to the party's revival plans.

title: Centre To Seize Properties Of Criminals Abroad, Set Up Extradition Cell, Hunt Down Bhatti Gang | Exclusive
description: Under the plan, law enforcement agencies will identify and attach Delhi properties of criminals residing abroad, targeting the financial base that sustains their operations here
author: Pragati Ratti, Ankur Sharma
content:
Centre To Seize Properties Of Criminals Abroad, Set Up Extradition Cell, Hunt Down Bhatti Gang | Exclusive
Under the plan, law enforcement agencies will identify and attach Delhi properties of criminals residing abroad, targeting the financial base that sustains their operations here
Got Question about the News?
The Centre is set to tighten the noose around criminals operating from abroad, with plans to attach their properties, primarily in Delhi, and set up a dedicated extradition cell, government sources said.
The move marks a shift from person-centric to network-centric law enforcement. The government is stepping up its efforts against criminal and terror networks, aiming to dismantle the transnational crime-and-terror ecosystem, the sources said. The directive has come from the highest levels of India’s security grid, they added.
- Delhi AQI Today: Anand Vihar At 336, Akshardham At 327 – Which Areas Have The Worst Air?
- India-Pakistan Ties: Musadik Malik Gets Permission To Visit Taj Mahal And Delhi Landmarks | News18
- FBI Database Hacked Again: Second Cyber Breach This Year Targets Sensitive US Criminal Records
- MEA Clears Pakistani Delegation's Taj Mahal Visit, But Malik Not Keen To Go To Agra | Exclusive
Under the plan, law enforcement agencies will identify and attach Delhi-based properties of criminals residing abroad, targeting the financial base that sustains their operations back home. The extradition cell will build cases and coordinate with foreign agencies to pursue fugitives overseas.
Agencies will also trace users of foreign SIM cards to break the chain of command between handlers abroad and operatives on the ground, the sources said.
Officials said the new approach treats the entire network as the target, rather than chasing individual offenders who can be quickly replaced. “The aim is to target the entire network, nexus and gang instead of hunting down individuals. Multiple agencies will work closely under a coordinated plan, with a focus on delivering results," sources said.
Hunt for Bhatti gang members
The government is also tracking members of the Shahzad Bhatti gang across the country, with more arrests likely in the coming days, the sources said.
Agencies are already conducting multiple large-scale operations to trace and apprehend Bhatti gang members across India.
Who is Shahzad Bhatti?
Bhatti is a Pakistani gangster who began his criminal career in the Lahore underworld and is believed to have operated from Dubai and other Gulf locations for years, moving between Pakistan, the UAE and other parts of the Middle East.
Over the past year, he has moved from being viewed as a gangster to being treated as a terror handler. Indian agencies allege that he operates with the backing of Pakistan’s ISI and is involved in orchestrating weapons and explosives consignments into Punjab and Delhi-NCR.
The Centre has flagged his cross-border network as the “Shahzad Bhatti Network."
Quick Answers
The Centre is shifting from a person-centric to a network-centric law enforcement approach by attaching properties primarily located in Delhi, establishing a dedicated extradition cell, and tracing foreign SIM card users to disrupt communication chains between overseas handlers and local operatives.

title: Tree plantation cannot be paperwork formality while clearing green cover for infra projects: HC
description: The Bombay High Court has raised concerns over the damage caused to the ecosystem while executing development projects, emphasising the need to ensure a balance between the environment and rapid urbanisation.
author: PTI
content:
Tree plantation cannot be paperwork formality while clearing green cover for infra projects: HC
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 10:34 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 10:34 IST
State agencies must execute proactive afforestation rather than treating compensatory plantation as a bureaucratic checkbox while diverting mangrove forests for urban transit projects. The court demanded concrete data on
The Bombay High Court has raised concerns over the damage caused to the ecosystem while executing development projects, emphasising the need to ensure a balance between the environment and rapid urbanisation.
State agencies in Maharashtra cannot treat tree plantation as a mere paperwork formality while rapidly clearing green cover for urban infrastructure, said a bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna on Wednesday.
The court was hearing a petition filed by the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) through advocate Saket Mone seeking permission to divert 0.2869 hectares of mangrove forest land for a transport project.
The approval is required to build an 8.85-km elevated Automated Rapid Transit System (ARTS), a driverless ‘electric pod car’ network, in Mumbai’s premier commercial district, Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC), which has been plagued by traffic snarls for a long time.
The court insisted authorities must take efforts for afforestation in advance rather than first taking permission to fell mangroves and leaving ecological restoration for later.
The bench noted that replantation of saplings, which may or may not grow up to full trees, was not serving any purpose.
“Why damage the eco system? The efforts of replantation have to be sincere and genuine. Once we give permission then efforts are taken for plantation. That would take years,” the HC observed.
The court further said full-grown trees or mangroves (salt-tolerant shrubby trees that thrive on tropical shores) are affected by development projects, but saplings are planted in their place, which take years to grow.
“There has to be a balance in the ecosystem. We are disturbing the ecosystem on account of development. Development is also important. But the rehabilitation of the environment has to move simultaneously. Permission is accorded today, but it would take five to ten years for the tree to grow. Right now we are disturbing the ecosystem,” the HC said.
In its plea, MMRDA, a state-run development agency, claimed no mangroves would be cut down for its project, but six trees would be affected and assured the court it would undertake plantation of 100 trees as compensation.
Their lawyer Mone told the court that the elevated corridor is vital for last-mile connectivity in the busy business district.
The bench questioned why compensatory measures had not been initiated the moment the project had been conceptualised.
Maharashtra Advocate General Milind Sathe explained that a shortage of suitable saline land delays mangrove plantation. He maintained that saplings are planted in pre-monsoon period to ensure their long-term survival.
The court asked the state government to submit concrete data from the past five years showing total green cover, losses, and sapling survival rates before passing orders, and posted the matter for further hearing on November 30.

title: SUV vs Hatchback vs Sedan: Which car offers the best value for Indian buyers
description: SUVs account for 67% of India's passenger vehicle sales, but hatchbacks and sedans offer advantages in mileage, comfort and affordability. Here's how the three body styles compare.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
SUV vs Hatchback vs Sedan: Which car offers the best value for Indian buyers
- Edited byVivek Dubey
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 09:57 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 09:57 IST
Utility vehicles dominate passenger vehicle sales amid rising incomes, yet traditional hatchbacks and sedans maintain distinct advantages in fuel efficiency, boot capacity, and urban manoeuvrability. Find out which body
India's passenger vehicle market is witnessing a shift in consumer preferences, with SUVs and utility vehicles (UVs) gaining ground over traditional hatchbacks and sedans.
Higher ground clearance, spacious cabins and an elevated driving position have made SUVs increasingly popular among buyers. However, hatchbacks and sedans continue to offer advantages in terms of affordability, fuel efficiency and everyday practicality.
According to the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), passenger vehicle sales in India reached a record 46.43 lakh units in FY2025-26, registering 7.9% growth year-on-year. Utility vehicle sales grew 11% to around 31 lakh units, accounting for approximately 67% of total passenger vehicle sales.
The growing share of utility vehicles reflects a change in buying preferences, with more customers considering compact and mid-size SUVs. However, the shift raises an important question for prospective buyers: does an SUV offer better value for money than a hatchback or sedan?
SUVs lead
SUVs have emerged as the preferred choice for a growing number of Indian car buyers. Their higher ground clearance makes them better suited to potholes, uneven roads and waterlogged stretches, while the elevated seating position offers better visibility in traffic.
The introduction of compact SUVs has also made the body style accessible to buyers who would traditionally have considered hatchbacks or sedans. Models such as the Maruti Suzuki Brezza, Tata Nexon, Tata Punch, Hyundai Creta, Kia Seltos and Mahindra Scorpio have contributed to the segment's popularity.
Rising incomes, easier access to vehicle financing and demand for larger vehicles have further supported this trend. However, SUVs generally have larger dimensions and can involve higher fuel expenses, depending on their engine and weight. This can make them less economical for buyers who primarily drive in congested urban areas.
Hatchbacks persist
Hatchbacks continue to appeal to buyers looking for affordable personal mobility and lower running costs. Their compact dimensions make them easier to drive through narrow streets, navigate heavy traffic and park in restricted spaces.
Models such as the Maruti Suzuki WagonR, Swift and Baleno remain popular choices. Their relatively lower fuel consumption also makes them suitable for daily office commutes and small families.
However, the entry-level hatchback segment has lost market share as buyers increasingly move towards larger vehicles, including compact SUVs. Despite this, hatchbacks remain a practical option for customers who prioritise affordability and ease of driving over ground clearance and cabin size.
Sedans struggle
Sedans have lost ground to SUVs in India's passenger vehicle market, although they continue to cater to a specific set of buyers. Their separate boot compartments provide dedicated luggage space, while their lower centre of gravity and aerodynamic design can offer a stable highway driving experience.
The Maruti Suzuki Dzire remains a prominent name in the compact sedan segment. In the mid-size category, models such as the Volkswagen Virtus, Skoda Slavia, Hyundai Verna and Honda City attract buyers looking for spacious cabins and comfortable long-distance journeys.
However, lower ground clearance can make sedans less suitable for roads with deep potholes and uneven surfaces. This has become an important consideration for buyers in several Indian cities.
Three-way comparison
A comparison of three models from different body styles — the Maruti Suzuki Baleno, Tata Punch and Maruti Suzuki Dzire — highlights how their strengths differ.
The Tata Punch offers 193 mm of ground clearance, higher than the Baleno's 170 mm and the Dzire's 163 mm. This gives the SUV an advantage on uneven roads. However, the Dzire offers the largest boot at 382 litres, compared with 366 litres in the Punch and 318 litres in the Baleno.
The Baleno has the longest wheelbase at 2,520 mm, against 2,445 mm for the Punch and 2,450 mm for the Dzire. This can benefit rear-seat passenger space despite its hatchback design.
The three models also differ in their powertrain options. The Baleno and Dzire use a 1.2-litre naturally aspirated petrol engine, producing 81 bhp and 112.4 Nm of torque. The Punch offers a 1.2-litre naturally aspirated petrol engine and a 1.0-litre turbo-petrol option, with the latter producing 118 bhp and 170 Nm of torque.
In terms of claimed fuel efficiency, the Dzire leads with 25–26 kmpl, followed by the Baleno at 23–25 kmpl. The Punch returns a claimed 19–20 kmpl. All three models also offer CNG options, providing an alternative for buyers looking to reduce fuel expenses.
The feature packages vary as well. The Baleno offers equipment such as ventilated seats, a heads-up display and Level 2 ADAS. The Punch gets a larger infotainment screen and an air purifier, while the Dzire offers a more conventional equipment package.
Which offers value
The comparison suggests that no single body style offers the best value for every buyer. Hatchbacks are generally better suited to city commuters looking for affordability, fuel efficiency and easy manoeuvrability.
Sedans appeal to buyers who prioritise luggage capacity, passenger comfort and highway driving. SUVs are more suitable for those who regularly encounter poor road conditions and need higher ground clearance.
Apart from the ex-showroom price, buyers should consider insurance, fuel expenses, maintenance, loan interest and depreciation before making a purchase.
While SUVs currently account for the largest share of India's passenger vehicle market, their popularity does not necessarily make them the most economical choice. The Baleno, Punch and Dzire comparison highlights how a hatchback or sedan can offer advantages that an SUV may not, depending on the buyer's requirements.
Ultimately, the value-for-money choice depends on usage. Buyers who primarily drive in cities may find a hatchback more economical, frequent highway travellers may prefer a sedan, while families dealing with uneven roads may benefit from an SUV.

title: Delhi AQI remains ‘poor’ at 226; Anand Vihar, DTU among most polluted as misty morning adds to pollution woes
description: Delhi air quality remained poor on Thursday with an AQI of 226. Anand Vihar, DTU, and North Campus fell into the very poor category, while GRAP Stage II restrictions remained in force.
author: CNBCTV18.com
content:
Delhi AQI remains ‘poor’ at 226; Anand Vihar, DTU among most polluted as misty morning adds to pollution woes
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 08:19 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 08:19 IST
Morning mist and light winds are trapping pollutants across the capital, keeping several key monitoring zones in the very poor category despite minor improvements. Authorities have enforced strict dust control measures a
Delhi's air quality remained in the ‘poor’ category on Thursday (November 26) morning, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) at 226 as of 7 am.
The reading was two points lower than at the same hour on Wednesday, indicating a marginal improvement, but pollution levels remained elevated across the capital. Of the city's 59 monitoring stations, 56 were reporting, with PM2.5 the leading pollutant at 47 stations.
Anand Vihar recorded the highest AQI at 327, followed by DTU at 308 and North Campus at 302. Pusa recorded an AQI of 298, while ITO stood at 296. The first three stations were in the ‘very poor’ category, while Pusa and ITO were in the ‘poor’ category.
Across Delhi, 34 stations were in the ‘poor’ category, 19 in the ‘moderate’ category and three in the ‘very poor’ category, while three stations were not reporting.
The air quality comes against a backdrop of mist and shallow fog in the morning, with the India Meteorological Department forecasting a minimum temperature of around 9°C and a maximum of 27°C in Delhi on Thursday. Winds are expected to remain relatively light in the morning before picking up during the afternoon.
The combination of cool morning conditions, mist and relatively weak winds can limit the dispersion of pollutants, keeping air quality under pressure. The Air Quality Early Warning System also showed several monitoring locations in the ‘very poor’ range early Thursday, including Anand Vihar and DTU.
GRAP Stage II remains in force in Delhi-NCR, with measures including restrictions on dust-generating construction activity, enhanced road cleaning and dust suppression, and advisories to use public transport.

title: 'अमेरिका पर लगे 25% जवाबी टैरिफ', ट्रंप के प्रस्ताव पर भड़के व्यापारियों ने पीएम को लिखा खत; 5 लाख लोगों के रोजगार पर असर का दावा
description: अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप मे भारत समेत 14 देशों पर नया टैरिफ लगाने का प्रस्ताव रखा है. इस बीच सीटीआई ने केंद्र सरकार को एक चिट्ठी लिखरक जवाबी टैरिफ लगाने की अपील की है. सीटीआई का कहना है कि अमेरिका के इस फैसले से 48 अरब डॉलर का भारतीय निर्यात प्रभावित हो सकता है.
author: अभिनव त्रिपाठी
content:
अमेरिका ने भारत पर 25 प्रतिशत टैरिफ लगाने का प्रस्ताव रखा है. हालिया खबरों में कहा गया कि अगर भारत ने अमेरिका के साथ ट्रेड डील कर ली, तो यह टैरिफ 17 प्रतिशत होगा. अमेरिका की ओर से थोपे जा रहे एकतरफा टैरिफ पर भारत के व्यापारियों में नाराजगी है. व्यापारियों और उद्यमियों के शीर्ष संगठन चैंबर ऑफ ट्रेंड एंड इंडस्ट्री (CTI) ने इस संबंध में केंद्र सरकार को चिट्ठी लिखी है और अमेरिका पर भी जवाबी टैरिफ लगाने की अपील की है.
दरअसल, सीटीआई के अध्यक्ष बृजेश गोयल ने गुरुवार (26 नवंबर) को एक वीडियो जारी किया और कहा कि भारत सरकार को एक्सपोर्ट के लिए दूसरे देशों के विकल्प तलाशने चाहिए, जिससे अमेरिका के व्यापारियों को भी नुकसान पहुंचे. उन्होंने कहा कि अगर अमेरिका भारत पर 25% टैरिफ लगाता है, तो अमेरिका से आयात होने वाले सामान पर भी भारत सरकार 25 प्रतिशत जवाबी शुल्क लगाए.
अमेरिका के राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप ने बुधवार (25 नवंबर) को एक अहम ऐलान किया और दुनिया में हलचल मचा दी. ट्रंप प्रशासन ने भारत और चीन समेत दुनिया के 14 बड़ी अर्थव्यवस्थाओं पर एक नए इंपोर्ट टैक्स लगाने का ऐलान किया. इन लिस्ट में अधिकांश एशियाई देश शामिल हैं. ऐसे में निर्यातकों की टेंशन बढ़ गई है. भारत पर इससे 25 प्रतिशत टैरिफ लगने का खतरा बढ़ गया है. हालांकि, अमेरिका का कहना है कि अगर भारत ट्रेड डील कर लेता है, तो 17 प्रतिशत टैरिफ लगेगा.
अमेरिका के इस प्रस्ताव पर सीटीआई के अध्यक्ष बृजेश गोयल ने प्रतिक्रिया दी है और कहा कि व्यापिरियों ने पीएम नरेंद्र मोदी को एक पत्र लिखकर मांग कि है कि जर्मनी, ब्रिटेन, सिंगापुर, मलेशिया जैसे देशों में इंजीनियरिंग गुड्स की डिमांड बढ़ती जा रही है, ऐसे में भारत को इन देशों में माल बेचने के लिए विकल्प तलाशने चाहिए. उन्होंने कहा कि अमेरिका या किसी भी देश की ऐसी धमकी से डरने की जरूरत नहीं है.
गोयल का कहना है कि मिनरल्स, महंगे रत्न, आभूषण, सिक्के, मेटल्स, न्यूक्लियर रिएक्टर्स और हवाई जहाज के उपकरण, इलेक्ट्रिकल उपकरण, ऑप्टिकल उपकरण, प्लास्टिक समेत कई सामान अमेरिका से भारत आता है, भारत को इन सब चीजों में अमेरिका की निर्भरता कम करनी चाहिए और दूसरे देशों के विकल्प तलाशने चाहिए. सीटीआई चीफ का कहना है कि अगर अमेरिका, भारत पर 25% टैरिफ लगाता है, तो भारत को भी अमेरिका पर 25% जवाबी टैरिफ लगाना चाहिए.

इसके साथ ही सीटीआई चीफ बृजेश गोयल ने कहा कि अमेरिका के 25% टैरिफ का भारत के टेक्सटाइल, लेदर, जेम्स एंड ज्वेलरी, ऑटो कंपोनेंट, केमिकल, फार्मा, सीफूड जैसे सेक्टरों पर बहुत बुरा असर पड़ेगा. इतना ही नहीं, कम से कम इससे देश में 5 लाख लोगों के रोजगार पर संकट पैदा हो सकता है. गोयल के मुताबिक, बढ़े हुए टैरिफ के चलते दूसरे देशों के मुकाबले में भारतीय माल अमेरिका में 25% तक महंगा हो जाएगा, जिसके कारण वहां के खरीददार भारत के मुकाबले में दूसरे देशों को तवज्जो देंगे.
वहीं, सीटीआई महासचिव रमेश आहूजा एवं गुरमीत अरोड़ा और उपाध्यक्ष राहुल अदलखा के मुताबिक, भारत अमेरिका को 53% फार्मास्युटिकल, 53% वस्त्र एवं परिधान, 37% रत्न और आभूषण, 28% ऑटो कंपोनेंट, 13% केमिकल, 22% सीफूड आदि का निर्यात करता है.
ऐसे में व्यापारी वर्ग में एक बड़ा कन्फ्यूजन है कि पहले से जो कंपनियां ऑर्डर ले चुकी हैं या जो माल रास्ते में है और आने या जाने में कुछ समय लगेगा, उनका क्या होगा. सीटीआई ने आंकड़ों के आधार पर बताया कि भारत ने 2024 में अमेरिका को 1.7 लाख करोड़ के इंजीनियरिंग गुड्स निर्यात किए थे. फिलहाल भारत से अमेरिका निर्यात किए जाने वाले सामानों पर 10 प्रतिशत का टैरिफ लगता है.
व्यापारियों का कहना है कि 25 फीसदी टैरिफ लगने के बाद कारोबार करना मुश्किल हो जाएगा. भारत ने अमेरिका को पिछले साल इलेक्ट्रोॉनिक्स गुड्स में 1.25 लाख करोड़ निर्यात किया था, अभी इस पर 0.41 प्रतिशत का टैरिफ लगता था. अब नए टैरिफ के हिसाब से इसकी कीमत भी बढ़ेगी, इस कारण इलेक्ट्रॉनिक कंपनियों का व्यापार भी प्रभावित होगा.

title: दिल्ली में आज भी धुंध और धुआं-धुआं: 250 रहा AQI; 26 नवंबर को कैसा रहेगा मौसम? IMD ने बताया
description: दिल्ली में 26 नवंबर की सुबह मौसम में धुंध और ठंड का असर दिखा. एयर क्वालिटी भी खराब श्रेणी में रही और सुबह के वक्त AQI करीब 240 के आसपास दर्ज हुआ. IMD के मुताबिक आज आसमान साफ रहेगा, लेकिन सुबह कुछ इलाकों में धुंध या हल्का कोहरा छा सकता है. अधिकतम तापमान 24-26 डिग्री तक रह सकता है.
author: श्वेतांक रत्नाम्बर
content:
Weather Update: उत्तर भारत में अब ठंड ने असली रंग दिखाना शुरू कर दिया है. सुबह और रात में ठंड का अहसास होने लगा है. भारतीय मौसम विभाग (IMD) द्वारा जारी पैन इंडिया अपडेट के मुताबिक आज देश में मौसम का मिलाजुला रूप देखने को मिलेगा. कहीं सर्द तो कहीं गर्म और कहीं पर झमाझम बारिश का अलर्ट है. दक्षिण भारत के केरल, तमिलनाडु और पुडुचेरी में भारी बारिश का अलर्ट है. वहीं, दिल्ली, पंजाब, हरियाणा और हिमाचल प्रदेश समेत कई राज्यों में सुबह हल्का कोहरा नजर आया. मध्य भारत में भी आज से तापमान में गिरावट आने के आसार हैं.
वहीं देश भर की सुर्खियों में रहने वाली दिल्ली की हवा की हालत गुरुवार की सुबह भी खराब रही. आज सुबह 5 बजे दिल्ली का औसत AQI 238 दिखा रहा था और इसे खराब श्रेणी में रखा गया. सुबह 6 बजे के आसपास दिल्ली-एनसीआर का एक्यूआई करीब 250 के पार रहा. कमिशन फॉर एयर क्वालिटी मैनेजमेंट (CAQM) के लाइव डैशबोर्ड पर भी 26 नवंबर को दिल्ली की हवा Poor यानी खराब श्रेणी में थी.
26 नवंबर की सुबह दिल्ली के अलग-अलग इलाकों में वायु गुणवत्ता सूचकांक (AQI) में काफी अंतर दर्ज किया गया. अलीपुर में AQI 247, आनंद विहार में 332, आया नगर में 249 और बदरपुर में 214 रहा. बवाना में 247, बुराड़ी क्रॉसिंग में 290 और बुराड़ी में 272 AQI दर्ज किया गया.
पहाड़ी राज्यों के मौसम का हाल: चोटी के इलाकों में बर्फबारी का अनुमान है. इससे मैदानों में ठंड बढ़ सकती है. हिमाचल में राज्य के कुछ हिस्सों में कोहरा नजर आया. मौसम विभाग ने आज भारी बारिश या बर्फबारी का प्रमुख अलर्ट जारी नहीं किया है.
उत्तराखंड में मौसम ड्राई रहेगा. बारिश की संभावना नहीं है.
हरियाणा-पंजाब के मौसम का हाल: पंजाब के कुछ इलाकों में आज से घना कोहरा छाने की आशंका है. सुबह विजिबिलिटी कम रही. हरियाणा में सुबह ठंड महसूस हुई. आज रात से कोहरा का प्रकोप बढ़ने के आसार हैं.
यूपी के मौसम का हाल: मौसम विभाग के मुताबिक 26 नवंबर को पूर्वी और पश्चिमी यूपी में मौसम मुख्य रूप से शुष्क रहेगा. दिन और रात के पारे में शुक्रवार से गिरावट के आसार हैं. इस दौरान दिन और रात का पारा 1 से 2 डिग्री और नीचे खिसक सकता है. सुबह-शाम की ठंड और बढ़ेगी, दोपहर में खिली-खिली गुनगुनी धूप राहत देगी.
बिहार के मौसम का हाल: सुबह-सुबह बिहार के सभी जिलों में कोहरा छाया रहा. सुबह और रात के समय तापमान में गिरावट के चलते ठंड महसूस हो सकती है.
असम, मेघालय, मणिपुर, त्रिपुरा और ओडिशा में आज से कोहरे की स्थिति बनने की आशंका जताई गई है.

title: सीमा पर सख्ती, घुसपैठियों की शामत पक्की! CM शुभेंदु ने दिया 'खोजो और वापस भेजो' का फरमान
description: कूच बिहार जिला में मुख्यमंत्री शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने बांग्लादेश से आए अवैध मुस्लिम घुसपैठियों की पहचान करनी होगी और उन्हें एक-एक करके खोजना होगा. सीएम ने साफ कहा कि बांग्लादेश से आने वाले हिंदुओं को घुसपैठिया नहीं माना जाएगा.
author: राज मिश्रा
content:
पश्चिम बंगाल में अवैध रूप से रह रहे बांग्लादेशियों को वापस भेजा जाएगा. सीएम शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने पुलिस अधिकारियों को एक-एक बांग्लादेशी घुसपैठिये को खोजकर वापस भेजने के सख्त निर्देश दिए हैं. कूच बिहार में 'रास मेला' में एक कार्यक्रम को संबोधित करते हुए सीएम शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने पुलिस अधिकारियों को निर्देश दिया कि वे कूच बिहार जिले में बांग्लादेश से अवैध रूप से आए मुस्लिम प्रवासियों को खोजें और उन्हें वापस भेजने की कार्रवाई करें. कार्यक्रम को संबोधित करते हुए सीएम शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने एसपी मनीष जोशी से कहा कि बांग्लादेश से आए अवैध मुस्लिम प्रवासियों के लिए राज्य में कोई जगह नहीं है और उन्हें उसी रास्ते से वापस भेजा जाना चाहिए, जिसका इस्तेमाल करके वे भारत में दाखिल हुए थे.
घुसपैठिये नहीं हैं हिंदू बांग्लादेशी- CM शुभेंदु
मुख्यमंत्री ने आगे कहा कि इस जिले में बांग्लादेश से आए अवैध मुस्लिम घुसपैठियों की पहचान करनी होगी और उन्हें एक-एक करके खोजना होगा. उन्हें उसी रास्ते से वापस भेजा जाना चाहिए, जिससे वे आए थे. उन्हें बाहर निकालना होगा.
इस दौरान सीएम ने कहा कि बांग्लादेश से आने वाले हिंदुओं को घुसपैठिया नहीं माना जाना चाहिए, क्योंकि वे धार्मिक उत्पीड़न से बचने और अपनी जान बचाने के लिए सीमा पार करके आए हैं. उन्होंने कहा कि जो हिंदू सीमा पार से आए हैं, वे घुसपैठिए नहीं हैं. वे शरणार्थी हैं. वे यहां अपने धर्म की रक्षा करने और अपनी जान बचाने आए हैं. उन्हें आश्रय दिया जाना चाहिए.
बार्डर पर बाड़बंदी के काम में तेजी लाने के निर्देश
इस दौरान मुख्यमंत्री ने राज्य पुलिस और बीएसएफ को इंटरनेशनल बॉर्डर पर सुरक्षा मजबूत करने के लिए साथ मिलकर काम करने के लिए कहा. उन्होंने कहा कि राज्य सरकार ने बॉर्डर पर बुनियादी ढांचे के विकास के लिए और बाड़ बनाने के लिए जमीन उपलब्ध करवा दी है. बॉर्डर पर बाड़ लगने के बाद तस्करी पर भी पूरी तरह रोक लगनी चाहिए.
कूच बिहार में एक जिला अस्पताल बनाने की घोषणा
इसके अलावा मुख्यमंत्री ने जिले में महिलाओं की सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करने के लिए उचित कदम उठाने का निर्देश भी दिए. मुख्यमंत्री ने स्वास्थ्य सेवाओं में सुधार पर भी जोर दिया. उन्होंने जिले में अत्याधुनिक अस्पताल बनाने की घोषणा करते हुए कहा कि जिले के लोगों को सभी प्रकार की बेहतर चिकित्सा सुविधाएं उपलब्ध कराने के उद्देश्य से अस्पताल बनाया जाएगा. मुख्यमंत्री ने मंच से ही जिलाधिकारी और जनप्रतिनिधियों को अस्पताल निर्माण के लिए जमीन चिह्नित करने का निर्देश दिए.

title: 'Priceless Heritage Of Indian Democracy': PM Modi Pays Tribute To Ambedkar On Constitution Day
description: On Constitution Day, PM Modi called the Constitution a "priceless heritage of Indian democracy" and paid tribute to BR Ambedkar, while Congress announced nationwide Samvidhan Raksha Marches.
author: Asian News International
content:
'Priceless Heritage Of Indian Democracy': PM Modi Pays Tribute To Ambedkar On Constitution Day
On Constitution Day, PM Modi called the Constitution a "priceless heritage of Indian democracy" and paid tribute to BR Ambedkar, while Congress announced nationwide Samvidhan Raksha Marches.
- India News
- 4 min read
New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday extended greetings to the people on Constitution Day, describing the Constitution as a "priceless heritage of Indian democracy" and paying tributes to Dr BR Ambedkar and other members of the Constituent Assembly.
In a post on X, the Prime Minister said the Constitution would continue to guide the country in realising the resolve of a developed India. "Best wishes to all the countrymen on Constitution Day. On this auspicious occasion, I pay my respects and obeisances to respected Babasaheb and all the great personalities of the Constituent Assembly," PM Modi said.
Highlighting the significance of the Constitution, he added, "The gift given by him in the form of the Constitution is a priceless heritage of Indian democracy, which will continue to guide us in realising the resolve of a developed India."
The Prime Minister further described Constitution Day as an occasion to honour the makers of the Constitution and reaffirm the country's commitment to its foundational values.
Advertisement
"Greetings on Constitution Day, a day to pay homage to the makers of our Constitution and an occasion to reaffirm our commitment to strengthening the values enshrined in it," he wrote.
PM Modi also shared Sanskrit verses in his video post: "बहुधु बहुभिः सार्धं चिंतिताह सुनिरूपिताः Kathanchinna villiyante vidvadbhischintita nayah॥"
Advertisement
India observes Constitution Day, also known as Samvidhan Diwas, every year on November 26 to mark the adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly in 1949. The Constitution, which formally begins with the words “We, the People of India”, came into effect on January 26, 1950, marking the birth of India as a republic.
November 26 is observed as Constitution Day to commemorate the historic adoption of the country's Constitution and acknowledge the significance of the document in shaping India's democratic framework.
Meanwhile, the Congress will organise massive Samvidhan Raksha Marches across all states on Thursday to mark Constitution Day, as part of its campaign to safeguard the Constitution, according to an official release.
Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi will participate in the march in Lucknow, ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
In a statement, All India Congress Committee (AICC) General Secretary KC Venugopal said that every Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) would organise the march in its respective state, with Kharge participating in the Lucknow programme.
Each march will begin at a statue of Babasaheb Dr BR Ambedkar or Mahatma Gandhi, symbolising the Congress party's commitment to protecting the Constitution.
Following tributes to the founding figures, Congress workers and citizens will collectively read the Preamble, recalling the values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. They will also take an oath to protect the Constitution.
Alongside the marches, Congress workers will reach every polling booth under the Vote Rakshak campaign to verify the voters whose names have been deleted from electoral rolls and help them reclaim their right to vote.
Furthermore, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday announced a 'Save Democracy, Save Constitution' rally in Nagpur starting today. Dipke stated that the organisation would be hosting an event in Nagpur on November 26 (today), on Constitution Day, against the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

title: Delhi AQI Remains 'Poor' At 228, Anand Vihar Records 332; SC Weighs BS-VI Vehicle Curbs
description: Delhi's AQI stood at 228 on Thursday, with Anand Vihar recording 332. As pollution persists, the Supreme Court considers BS-VI vehicle restrictions while CAQM sets fresh reduction targets for 2027.
author: Asian News International
content:
Delhi AQI Remains 'Poor' At 228, Anand Vihar Records 332; SC Weighs BS-VI Vehicle Curbs
Delhi's AQI stood at 228 on Thursday, with Anand Vihar recording 332. As pollution persists, the Supreme Court considers BS-VI vehicle restrictions while CAQM sets fresh reduction targets for 2027.
- India News
- 4 min read
New Delhi: Delhi’s air quality remained in the ‘Poor’ category on Thursday, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at 228 at 8 am, while Anand Vihar registered the highest reading of 332 among the listed monitoring stations, according to data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
North Campus recorded an AQI of 302, IIT Delhi at 241 and Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) at 230. Lodhi Road recorded an AQI of 148, while India Gate and Kartavya Path registered an AQI of 149, both categorised as ‘moderate’.
However, the AQI around AIIMS stood at 188, also in the ‘moderate’ category. Maidan Garhi and Okhla Phase 2 recorded readings of 199 and 193, respectively, while Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium (JLN) registered an AQI of 190.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast mist in the national capital on November 26. The maximum temperature is expected to reach 27 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is likely to settle at 9 degrees Celsius.
Advertisement
According to the CPCB classification, an AQI between 0 and 50 is considered 'good', 51-100 'satisfactory', 101-200 'moderate', 201-300 'poor', 301-400 'very poor ', and 401-500 'severe'.
Meanwhile, in Mumbai, Maharashtra, a layer of smog covered the Wadala area.
Advertisement
Meanwhile, the Supreme Court on Monday indicated that it may consider restricting vehicles operating in Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) to those complying with Bharat Stage-VI (BS-VI) emission norms as part of measures to combat worsening air pollution in the region.
A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the observation while hearing a matter concerning air pollution in the national capital.
"We are clear we will allow only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi, if not NCR," the Bench remarked.
The Bench also suggested an alternative arrangement for the supply of essential commodities, proposing the establishment of warehouses at Delhi's borders where goods could be unloaded and subsequently transported into the city using smaller battery-operated or other non-polluting vehicles.
Separately, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has introduced district-level action plans for the first time, setting a mandatory minimum target of 15 per cent reduction, with the potential to reach 20 per cent, in annual average air pollution levels across Delhi-NCR for 2027.
The Commission has written to the governments of Delhi and other NCR states, calling for comprehensive Annual Action Plans for 2027 at the State, District and Municipal Corporation levels.
The plans aim to shift the focus from listing pollution-control activities to achieving measurable outcomes through defined targets, timelines, monitoring parameters and ground-level accountability.
Earlier, CAQM began assessing and ranking Delhi and neighbouring states on their performance in implementing pollution-control measures. Its 2026 report card, covering progress up to October, highlighted gaps in several areas, including industrial inspections, waste management, public transport and pollution-monitoring infrastructure.
According to the report card, none of the four states and Delhi had established the targeted number of green crematoriums. Against a combined target of 421 across Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, the achievement stood at zero as of October 31.
Industrial inspections also recorded significant shortfalls. Against a combined annual target of 11,607 inspections across the four states, only 2,584 had been completed by October 31.
While Delhi exceeded its target by conducting 1,609 inspections against 979, Haryana completed 177 of its 3,865 targeted inspections. Rajasthan recorded 68 inspections against 2,974, while Uttar Pradesh completed 730 against 3,789.
The CAQM has classified performance of 100 per cent as satisfactory, achievement between 75 per cent and less than 100 per cent as needing improvement, and progress below 75 per cent as unsatisfactory.
The final report card for 2026 is scheduled to be released in January 2027, allowing states and the Delhi government to accelerate the implementation of pollution-control measures during the remaining period of the year.

title: PM Modi Sets December 15 Deadline For Parliament Preparations: Why Winter Session Is Crucial For NDA
description: PM Modi has asked ministers to stay prepared for the Winter Session before December 15. With the delimitation bill facing a numbers challenge and opposition protests looming, here's what's at stake.
author: Shruti Sneha
content:
PM Modi Sets December 15 Deadline For Parliament Preparations: Why Winter Session Is Crucial For NDA
PM Modi has asked ministers to stay prepared for the Winter Session before December 15. With the delimitation bill facing a numbers challenge and opposition protests looming, here's what's at stake.
- India News
- 4 min read
New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has asked his ministers to complete the necessary preparations for the upcoming Parliament session before December 15 and avoid foreign visits in the run-up to it, indicating that the government is preparing for a crucial round of legislative business amid mounting political challenges.
According to reports, PM Modi gave the order during Wednesday's Cabinet meeting. The Prime Minister wants ministries to be completely prepared before Parliament reconvenes, according to those involved with the talks. The ultimate decision about the dates and length of the session will be made by the Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs.
Why Is The Winter Session Facing Questions Over Delay?
The government's preparations come as opposition parties continue to question why the Winter Session has not yet been convened. Although both Houses were adjourned indefinitely on August 13, the Monsoon Session is still officially unprorogued. It had been 103 days since the adjournment by Wednesday night.
The official process used to end a legislative session is called prorogation. Opposition parties have questioned the government's plans as a result of the delay, which has also fueled rumors of a potential special session of Parliament.
Advertisement
The timing is especially important because the government is debating laws related to women's reservations and delimitation. The proposed constitutional change would be one of the most significant political challenges of the next session if it is introduced.
Delimitation Bill: Why Does The Government Need Opposition Support?
The proposed Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, faces a significant numbers challenge. The bill needs a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha, which is equivalent to 361 votes given the House's total membership of 543. The House presently has 540 members, including three vacancies.
Advertisement
With only 320 MPs, the NDA will require the backing of opposition parties in order to pass the law.
However, since the bill was rejected in the Lok Sabha on April 17, the political landscape has shifted. Since then, twenty-six MPs have left the opposition. This includes 20 rebellious members of the Trinamool Congress who joined the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) after breaking away and promising to back the NDA. Another six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs shifted to the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.
Despite these changes, the ruling alliance still needs additional votes to reach the required majority. The DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), which has eight MPs, could therefore play an important role in determining the bill's fate.
SIR Protests, Delimitation: What Could Make The Session Stormy?
The government will also have to deal with opposition demonstrations over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation is being demanded by opposition parties, who have intensified their campaign against the procedure. It is anticipated that these protests would overflow into Parliament, possibly impacting the proceedings.
A member of the ruling alliance has stated that it would be challenging to consider and vote on a bill amending the Constitution unless the House runs smoothly.
The government's goals may also be impacted by procedural requirements. While calling a completely new session necessitates a minimum notice period of 14 days, extending the current session requires at least two days' notice.
Meanwhile, the government is understood to be examining a proposal to increase Lok Sabha seats by 50 per cent across all states. The formula is aimed at addressing concerns, particularly among southern states, that delimitation could reduce their relative political representation.
Under the proposal being considered, the existing proportion of seats allocated to states based on the 1971 Census would be retained. However, the government has not taken a final decision on the formula.
The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, failed to secure the required support during the special sitting of Parliament on April 17. With the Winter Session expected before December 15, its possible reintroduction will be closely watched, particularly as the government navigates both the numbers in the Lok Sabha and an increasingly assertive opposition.
