title: India opens doors to prized missile test range for Japan for first time, hypersonics collaboration on cards
description: Japan was once a military force constitutionally constrained to an exclusively defensive role. However, it is now gradually becoming a force with long-range strike capabilities, an expanding defence industry and a much greater role in Indo-Pacific security
author: Snehesh Alex Philip
content:
India opens doors to prized missile test range for Japan for first time, hypersonics collaboration on cards
Japan was once a military force constitutionally constrained to an exclusively defensive role. However, it is now gradually becoming a force with long-range strike capabilities, an expanding defence industry and a much greater role in Indo-Pacific security
In a major shift in India's defence cooperation policy, New Delhi is preparing to open up its most prized missile-testing facility to a foreign country for the first time, allowing Japan to use the Defence Research and Development Organisation's (DRDO) Integrated Test Range (ITR) at Chandipur in Odisha for its missile programme.
Not just Chandipur, India is also open to allowing Japan access to two upcoming state-of-the-art testing facilities in West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh, government sources told Firstpost.
The move goes beyond providing testing infrastructure. The two countries are also exploring the possibility of sharing technical know-how and collaborating on advanced missile programmes, including hypersonic weapons, sources said.
They added that India and Japan are also looking at cooperating on the shipbuilding front, especially warships. Sources clarified that, contrary to reports of plans to build Mogani-class multi-mission stealth frigates in India, both sides are working on sharing technical know-how and design features.
India has offered its shipyards and defence PSUs to Japan for collaboration, as well as manufacturing for Tokyo itself and exports from India.
Sources explained that manufacturing in India will be cheaper for Japan, and that this is something under discussion. For example, plans are not just to manufacture the Unicorn (Unified Complex Radio Antenna) for the Indian Navy's requirements but also for exports by Japan itself.
These were among the key issues discussed during the India-Japan 2+2 dialogue last week, led by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar.
Following the meeting, the two countries signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) on the utilisation of firing ranges in India.
Why Japan is keen for Indian firing ranges
Under the arrangement, Japan's Self-Defence Forces will, for the first time, be able to conduct live-fire training in India, including trials involving surface-to-ship missiles such as the Type-25, a next-generation anti-ship missile with a reported range of around 1,000 km.
Both sides will now work towards accelerating coordination between their respective defence authorities to operationalise the arrangement at the earliest. Japan is also in talks with Australia for the test ranges.
Japan is undergoing one of the most significant transformations in its military posture since the Second World War.
What was once a military force constitutionally constrained to an exclusively defensive role is gradually becoming a force with long-range strike capabilities, an expanding defence industry and a much greater role in Indo-Pacific security.
Sources said a Japanese military team had visited India in October to assess various missile-testing facilities. The team spent about a week examining potential ranges where Japan could conduct missile trials as well as test its small attack drones.
Japan faces geographical constraints at home, particularly in identifying sufficiently large and safe maritime corridors for long-range missile firing. India's eastern coastline, with its established missile-testing infrastructure and access to the Bay of Bengal, offers an attractive alternative.
Sources said the discussions are not limited to access to testing facilities. India and Japan are also looking at sharing technical expertise and exploring opportunities for collaboration in advanced weapons programmes, particularly hypersonic technologies.
Japan is seeking to develop a multi-layered coastal defence system incorporating large numbers of relatively inexpensive unmanned aerial, surface and underwater vehicles for reconnaissance and attack missions.
These capabilities would complement its growing arsenal of stand-off missiles, which are designed to strike targets from outside an adversary's engagement range.
Tokyo is developing a new generation of missiles to strengthen deterrence against China's growing military activity around its periphery and respond to North Korea's increasingly sophisticated missile arsenal.
Why the Integrated Test Range matters
The Integrated Test Range at Chandipur is among India's most strategically important defence-testing facilities. It is a critical part of the country's missile-development ecosystem, providing the infrastructure required to launch, track and validate advanced missile systems.
Its capabilities include sophisticated radars, telemetry systems, electro-optical tracking equipment and mission-control infrastructure, which allow DRDO scientists to monitor missile trajectories and assess their performance during flight trials.
The facility has played an important role in testing several Indian missile systems, including air-defence and ballistic missile defence interceptors.
Opening up such infrastructure to Japan would mark a significant expansion of bilateral defence cooperation, taking the relationship beyond joint military exercises and conventional defence technology partnerships, sources said.

title: Dalai Lama gets Lutyens' Delhi bungalow as India gives his office a permanent base in capital
description: The Dalai Lama will continue to be based in Dharamshala, but his office now has a dedicated facility in Lutyens' Delhi for official engagements
author: FP News Desk
content:
Dalai Lama gets Lutyens' Delhi bungalow as India gives his office a permanent base in capital
The Dalai Lama will continue to be based in Dharamshala, but his office now has a dedicated facility in Lutyens' Delhi for official engagements
The Indian government has allotted a bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi to the office of the 14th Dalai Lama, giving the Tibetan spiritual leader a dedicated base in the national capital for his visits and official engagements.
The property, located at 20 Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane, has been allotted to the Gaden Phodrang Trust, which serves as the Dalai Lama's official office and manages his spiritual and humanitarian work.
The allotment followed a request from the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), as per news agency PTI. While the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry has not issued an official statement, government accommodation of this kind is generally allotted for three years, with the possibility of an extension.
Security upgrades worth nearly Rs 35 lakh are being carried out at the property. These include reinforced gates, a security cabin and additional protective structures along the boundary wall. The work is intended to strengthen security and regulate access to the premises.
Why does the Dalai Lama need a base in Delhi?
The Dalai Lama's primary residence is in McLeod Ganj, near Dharamshala in Himachal Pradesh, where he has lived since fleeing Tibet in 1959.
He escaped Tibet amid a Chinese crackdown and unrest in Lhasa, eventually reaching India on March 31, 1959. New Delhi granted him asylum, beginning a relationship that has continued for more than six decades. India has since been home to the Dalai Lama and a large Tibetan refugee community.
Although he is based in Dharamshala, the Dalai Lama travels to the national capital for meetings, engagements and other official work. Having a dedicated facility in Delhi is expected to reduce the logistical challenges involved in arranging accommodation and security for him and his staff.
The new bungalow will also provide his office with a permanent base from which to coordinate engagements and its work on Tibetan culture, humanitarian causes and interfaith dialogue.
What is the Gaden Phodrang Trust?
The bungalow has been allotted to the Gaden Phodrang Trust rather than to the Dalai Lama as a private residence.
Gaden Phodrang is the official office of the Dalai Lama. It was registered as a private trust in India in 2011, after he voluntarily gave up his political authority in favour of an elected Tibetan leadership.
The trust is dedicated to preserving the institution of the Dalai Lama and supporting his spiritual and humanitarian work. Its stated commitments include promoting human values, encouraging interfaith harmony, preserving Tibetan culture and identity, protecting the environment and promoting a deeper understanding of ancient Indian wisdom.
The distinction is important: the new facility is intended to support the institution and office of the Dalai Lama, not to shift his residence from Dharamshala to Delhi.
Tibetan leadership welcomes India's move
The allotment has been welcomed by the Tibetan leadership in exile.
Dolma Tsering, Speaker of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, expressed gratitude to the Indian government, saying the accommodation would make the Dalai Lama's visits to the capital more convenient and provide greater comfort and security during his stays.
'This is very welcome news. The accommodation will make His Holiness the Dalai Lama's visits to the national capital far more convenient and provide greater comfort and security during his stays in New Delhi,' she said as cited by news agency ANI.
Choedak Gyatso, a member of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile's standing committee, also welcomed the decision, describing it as a reaffirmation of India's longstanding support for the Tibetan people.
The next Dalai Lama and the battle over who gets to choose
The allotment also comes amid growing international attention on the Dalai Lama's succession, with a US congressional panel recently urging Washington to coordinate with New Delhi on the process.
The bipartisan US-China Economic and Security Review Commission has recommended that the US recognise the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole authority to identify his successor and reject any candidate selected or appointed by Beijing.
It has also called for intelligence-sharing and contingency planning with India, warning that China could use political pressure, cyber operations and disinformation to influence the succession.

title: Delhi reports 83 new lung cancer patients a month, 1 death every 3 days: Air pollution to blame?
description: Around 83 cases of lung cancer were recorded every month across prominent government hospitals in the national capital in the last six and a half year period, with one patient succumbing to the disease every three days
author: Tanishq.Priya
content:
Delhi reports 83 new lung cancer patients a month, 1 death every 3 days: Air pollution to blame?
Around 83 cases of lung cancer were recorded every month across prominent government hospitals in the national capital in the last six and a half year period, with one patient succumbing to the disease every three days
Around 83 cases of lung cancer were recorded every month across prominent government hospitals in the national capital in the last six and a half year period, with one patient succumbing to the disease every three days.
This information was provided in response to an RTI query to AIIMS, RML Hospital, Safdarjung Hospital and the Delhi State Cancer Institute.
Under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, data regarding lung cancer cases and associated deaths between January 1, 2020, and July 31, 2026, were requested from the hospitals. Safdarjung Hospital only provided the number of lung cancer deaths but did not disclose the total number of cases.
A request was also made for data on patients who had never smoked. However, none of the institutes provided any data on it.
According to information provided in response to separate RTI applications filed by PTI Bhasha, 6,581 lung cancer cases were recorded across three of the four hospitals (excluding Safdarjung), averaging 83 cases per month. Across all four hospitals, 913 deaths were reported, which translates to one patient dying every three days.
The national capital is currently grappling with a severe air pollution crisis, an annual affair now in November, which is observed as the Lung Cancer Awareness Month.
Although health experts state that long-term exposure to air pollution increases the risk of lung cancer, it is not the sole cause. Smoking and genetic mutations are two of the other contributing factors.
The highest number of cases was recorded at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). This central government hospital provided data for the period from January 2020 to March 2026, during which 4,860 cases of lung cancer were registered and 158 deaths occurred. This averages to approximately 65 cases per month, with two patient deaths occurring monthly.
According to data from the Delhi State Cancer Institute (DSCI), 1,613 cases of lung cancer were reported between January 1, 2020, and July 2026, resulting in 354 deaths. This translates to an average of 20 cases per month, with four patient deaths occurring monthly during this period.
The institute noted that in 2021, the disease was also diagnosed in two children, and over a span of about six and a half years, 351 women were found to be suffering from lung cancer. However, it did not provide a gender-segregated breakdown of the deaths.
Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital reported 108 cases of lung cancer during this period, including 47 women, with eight deaths recorded. Safdarjung Hospital reported 393 deaths among patients suffering from lung cancer during the same timeframe.
A senior doctor at the DSCI, speaking to PTI on the condition of anonymity, mentioned that the institute receives patients not only from Delhi but also from Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar, and even Nepal.
Regarding the role of air pollution in Delhi on lung cancer cases, the doctor said the primary cause is smoking or exposure to tobacco smoke, though genetic mutations also play a role.
According to doctors, lung cancer has also been detected in non-smoking women; this is suspected to be linked to genetic mutations and pollution.
Doctors also said that the disease is often diagnosed only in its final stages, making treatment extremely challenging.
Dr Geeta Kadayaprath, a senior specialist at the Apollo Athenaa Women’s Cancer Centre, said that long-term exposure to polluted air—common in cities like Delhi—can increase the risk of lung cancer.
She noted that the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), under the World Health Organization, has classified outdoor air pollution and the particulate matter it contains as carcinogenic to humans.
She explained that PM 2.5 particles are so minute that they can penetrate deep into the lungs and, over time, cause damage to cells.
When asked about symptoms, Dr Vikas Maurya, a senior specialist at Fortis Hospital in Shalimar Bagh, explained that there are often no clear symptoms in the early stages.
However, potential warning signs include a persistent cough, coughing up blood, shortness of breath, chest pain, changes in one’s voice, unexplained weight loss, and recurring chest infections.
He further noted that the condition cannot be detected through a standard X-ray; instead, a CT scan is required for diagnosis.
(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by Firstpost staff.)

title: 18 years since 26/11: Remembering the horrors of Mumbai terror attack
description: Eighteen years after 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists unleashed a wave of attacks across Mumbai, the events of November 26, 2008, remain etched in India's memory
author: Vrinda Goel
content:
18 years since 26/11: Remembering the horrors of Mumbai terror attack
Eighteen years after 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists unleashed a wave of attacks across Mumbai, the events of November 26, 2008, remain etched in India's memory
Listen to This Article
Eighteen years ago, on this day, terrorists from the Pakistan-backed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) unleashed mayhem on the streets of India's financial capital, Mumbai. Commonly referred to as 26/11, the coordinated attacks by a group of 10 terrorists targeted crowded public spaces, including the Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST), the Taj and Oberoi hotels, the Jewish centre at Nariman House, Cama Hospital, Metro Cinema and Leopold Cafe.
For three days, the city's fast-paced rhythm came to a halt as the attacks unfolded and a massive security response followed. According to news agency PTI, the incident left 166 people dead and injured more than 300, including civilians, foreign nationals, security personnel and hospital staff.
Nearly 18 years later, the events of those nights remain etched in India's memory for the scale of violence, the prolonged siege and the heroic rescue operations that followed.
How the attack unfolded
The attackers, divided into four teams, set off from Karachi on November 21. On November 23, they hijacked the Indian fishing boat Kuber and killed its crew. They forced the captain to navigate towards Mumbai before murdering him too. The terrorists then approached the city in inflatable boats.
November 26: The night the siege began
Also Read
Evening: Around 7 km off the coast, the terrorists abandoned Kuber and moved towards the city.
8:00 pm: They split into groups and landed at Badhwar Park and Sassoon Docks in south Mumbai.
9:20 pm: The first wave of attacks began. The crowded Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, Nariman House, Leopold Cafe and the Oberoi Trident were hit. Two gunmen stormed the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel and opened fire on guests and staff.
10:30 pm: Violence intensified near Cama and Albless Hospital, where Ajmal Kasab and Abu Ismail Khan attacked police officers responding to the situation. 
November 27: Fire, gunfights and rescues
12:30 am: Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Omble confronted Kasab and grabbed the barrel of his AK-47 rifle. He was shot at close range while holding on, allowing other officers to overpower Kasab. While Kasab was arrested, Ismail Khan was killed. Fires erupted at the Taj, damaging its dome.
1:00 am: Army personnel reached the hotel as firefighters worked to control the flames. Police cordoned off the Oberoi Trident.
6:00 am: National Security Guard (NSG) commandos arrived and launched operations at both hotels, rescuing several hostages.
4:00 pm: Fighting continued across the Taj and Oberoi. At Nariman House, rescue efforts began amid explosions and gunfire.
November 28: Key breakthroughs
7:00 am: NSG commandos landed on the roof of Nariman House from a helicopter, and the operation intensified.
11:00 am: The siege at the Oberoi Trident ended, with the remaining hostages freed and both gunmen killed.
4:00 pm: The standoff at Nariman House concluded, and the surviving hostages were rescued.
November 29: The Taj retaken
6:00 am: After a fierce overnight battle, NSG commandos secured the Taj Mahal Palace hotel. The last attackers were neutralised, ending the 60-hour siege and freeing the remaining hostages.
8:00 am: An all-clear was declared after NSG commandos conducted room-by-room sweeps of the Taj Mahal Palace hotel to defuse unexploded grenades and clear the premises before handing control back to the Mumbai Police.
What followed after the attack?
Following the attacks, then Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil, Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and Deputy Chief Minister RR Patil resigned amid widespread public outrage over intelligence and security lapses.
Several steps were taken to overhaul the security system. Parliament passed laws to create the National Investigation Agency (NIA) and amended the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The government also strengthened coastal surveillance and set up regional NSG hubs in Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad and Kolkata.
Based on the interrogation of the sole surviving attacker Ajmal Kasab and forensic evidence, India compiled dossiers establishing that the attackers belonged to the Pakistan-based group LeT. Kasab was convicted in 2010 and executed in November 2012.
David Coleman Headley, one of the key conspirators who conducted reconnaissance of Mumbai ahead of the attacks, remains incarcerated in the United States, serving a 35-year federal prison sentence. Meanwhile, Tahawwur Hussain Rana, another accused in the conspiracy, was extradited from the US to India in April 2025 and is lodged in New Delhi's Tihar Jail, awaiting the framing of charges in his trial.
The trial against Zabiuddin Ansari, alias Abu Jundal, the handler who taught Hindi to the 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists, is underway in the 26/11 terror attacks case. However, steps to execute proclamation orders against six other accused, including Lashkar operatives Hafiz Saeed and Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi, are yet to be taken.
The scars continue to haunt
The scars left by the tragic events continue to haunt those who witnessed them and the families who lost their loved ones. Every year, floral tributes are paid at the Mumbai Police headquarters to those who made the ultimate sacrifice while fighting the terrorists during the attacks. Homage is also paid at Mumbai CSMT, Cama and Albless Hospital and other locations targeted by the Pakistani terrorists.
Mumbaikars also gather at "Prerana Sthal", the statue of Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Omble, who fought the terrorists with a lathi and was killed while capturing Kasab at Girgaon Chowpatty in south Mumbai.

title: CII-backed Banaras Biennale to bring art and culture to Varanasi's ghats
description: The 35-day industry-backed event, with an investment of upwards of ₹20 crore, will showcase Varanasi's art, culture, textiles and living practices through exhibitions and workshops
author: Anushka Bhardwaj
content:
CII-backed Banaras Biennale to bring art and culture to Varanasi's ghats
The 35-day industry-backed event, with an investment of upwards of ₹20 crore, will showcase Varanasi's art, culture, textiles and living practices through exhibitions and workshops
Listen to This Article
Varanasi, India’s cultural and spiritual hub, is set to position itself as a global destination for art and culture with the debut edition of the ‘Banaras Biennale’. The 35-day event aims to celebrate the city’s art, culture, textiles and living practices. Backed by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), it will kick off on November 27 and will spread across the ghats, museums, universities and streets of Varanasi through exhibitions, cultural programmes, curated walkthroughs, training workshops and textile factory tours.
The Biennale will coincide with the second edition of the India Biennale, organised by the Ministry of Culture, taking place in Delhi from December 4. The Banaras Biennale is, however, an industry-backed initiative with an investment of upwards of ₹20 crore. “The event is entirely funded by the industry, with several industry partners joining in to make it a financial success,” says Madhav Singhania, steering committee chairman of CII Banaras Biennale 2026. Addressing a press conference in Delhi, he added that the first objective would be to create an institution out of the Biennale in the city of Kashi and then to expand it with every edition.
The event, themed ‘Kashi/light: The City as a Sensorium’, will kick off on Friday with a pre-dawn visit to the Kashi Vishwanath temple, followed by a walkthrough — Paani Mein Lakeere — with the lead visual art curator, Gayatri Sinha. The exhibitions, including the textile curation, Ek Dhaga, Ek Duniya: Silk, Zari and the Light of Kashi, and the photography walkthrough, My River, My Witness, will be open on all days during the Biennale. The event will open to the general public from November 28.
The aim, according to the organisers, is to reimagine the existing rich heritage of Banaras to establish it as a global destination. The peaceful riverfront experience will be enhanced by live music concerts bringing the city’s musical heritage to its ghats. The factory tours and artisan workshops will shift the focus to the making of famous Banarasi textiles, including saris and carpets. The walkthroughs across the ghats will also feature culinary demonstrations. Banaras Hindu University (BHU) will be a venue for multiple workshops, panel discussions and exhibitions.
The ghats of Banaras will be illuminated by another industry-backed event, the Mahindra Kabira Festival, from December 4 to 6. Organised by the Mahindra Group, the event will have its milestone 10th edition, spanning folk music, discussions, art demonstrations, boat rides, a food trail and heritage walks.

title: Passport rules: When can authorities stop Indians from travelling abroad?
description: The Passports Act, 1967 specifies when overseas travel can be restricted. Here is what authorities can do when discrepancies surface and what remedies citizens have
author: Mini Raghav
content:
Passport rules: When can authorities stop Indians from travelling abroad?
The Passports Act, 1967 specifies when overseas travel can be restricted. Here is what authorities can do when discrepancies surface and what remedies citizens have
Listen to This Article
Saurav Das, a leader of the upstart Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), said he was stopped at Delhi airport on November 23 when he was on his way to the United Kingdom. According to Das, immigration officials flagged alleged discrepancies in the place-of-birth details in his passport.
The Chennai Regional Passport Office (RPO), which issued his passport in 2019, subsequently sent him a show-cause notice seeking his response to the discrepancies within seven days. He also refrained from using the passport until he submitted his response.
Das said he came to know about the notice only when he reached the immigration counter. The authorities had flagged differences in his birth-related details across documents, including Aadhaar and his passport. The notice initiated proceedings that could lead to the passport being impounded.
The incident raises questions about the government’s power to regulate international travel and the legal safeguards available to passport holders.
Can immigration authorities stop you from travelling despite a valid passport and visa?
A valid passport and visa do not, by themselves, guarantee the right to leave India in every circumstance.
Also Read
Immigration officials can restrict departure if there is a legally valid basis, such as a court order or a Look Out Circular (LOC), as the case may be.
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) governs issues relating to LOCs, which are alerts circulated to immigration authorities at airports and other exit points. Depending on the terms of the LOC, it can restrict a person from travelling abroad.
On what grounds can the government impound or revoke your passport?
Section 10(3) of the Passports Act, 1967, says passport authorities can impound or revoke a passport on specified grounds.
These include wrongful possession of a passport, suppression of material information or submission of incorrect information to obtain it, and situations involving national security or public interest.
“The passport authority must examine the nature of the discrepancy, intention behind it and a distinction has to be made between an innocent mistake and deliberate misrepresentation,” said B Shravanth Shanker, managing partner, B Shanker Advocates LLP.
A discrepancy in the place of birth can legally justify impounding a passport if it was obtained by suppressing material facts or providing incorrect information. However, authorities cannot automatically impound a passport over a minor error; they must follow due process, Shanker added.
Section 10(3)(b) empowers authorities to take action if a passport was obtained by suppressing material information or on the basis of incorrect information.
Separately, Section 12(1)(b) provides for criminal punishment when a person knowingly furnishes false information or suppresses material information to obtain a passport.
Can authorities restrict foreign travel without formally impounding a passport?
There is a difference between a show-cause notice and an order restricting the use of a passport.
A show-cause notice gives the passport holder an opportunity to explain why action should not be taken. It is not, by itself, a final order impounding the passport.
“A show-cause notice is an invitation to answer an allegation, not an executive licence to impose a travel ban,” said Tushar Agarwal, founder & managing partner, CLAP JURIS, Advocates & Solicitors.
“A show-cause notice does not by itself invalidate a passport. Interim suspension is possible under Section 10A, but only where impounding is likely on Section 10(3)(c) grounds: sovereignty, security, foreign relations or public interest,” said Raheel Patel, Partner, Gandhi Law Associates.
This provision does not create a general interim suspension power for every case involving alleged incorrect information under Section 10(3)(b).
Therefore, the legal basis for preventing travel in a particular case must be examined separately, including whether an independent restriction or valid immigration alert was issued.
What legal safeguards protect the right to travel abroad?
The Supreme Court, in Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978), recognised that the right to travel abroad constitutes personal liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution.
It held that any procedure restricting this liberty must be fair, just and reasonable.
“The passport authority must generally give notice, disclose the grounds, allow a reasonable opportunity to reply, and give reasons for any adverse order,” said Alay Razvi, managing partner, Accord Juris.
A notice issued only five hours before a flight may raise concerns about fairness and whether there was a practical opportunity to respond. A court may examine whether the timing was necessary, proportionate and supported by proper material, Razvi added.
Section 10(5) of the Passports Act also requires authorities to record reasons when they pass an order impounding or revoking a passport.
The passport holder can also seek a copy of the reasons, except in specified cases involving national security, friendly relations with foreign countries or public interest.
What can you do if authorities prevent you from leaving India?
An aggrieved person can appeal under Section 11 of the Passports Act before the prescribed appellate authority.
The individual may also approach the High Court with jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution if the action is alleged to be arbitrary or contrary to legal procedure.
“Article 226 is not a remedy available only after the passport authority has pronounced its final decision,” said Tushar Agarwal.
The appropriate legal remedy depends on the nature of the restriction, including whether it arises from a passport order, an LOC or another legal direction.

title: PLI Auto disbursements surge to  ₹4,385 crore in FY27
description: The Centre has disbursed 26% of the scheme's  ₹25,938 crore outlay since FY25, as electric vehicle adoption gathers pace.
author: Manas Pimpalkhare
content:
New Delhi: The Centre has disbursed ₹4,385 crore under its production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for automobiles and auto parts as of 25 November, against a budget estimate of ₹5,939 crore for the full fiscal year, signalling a sharp acceleration in payouts under a scheme that has faced concerns over slow fund utilization. The disbursement takes the cumulative incentives paid under the ₹25,938 crore PLI Auto scheme to ₹6,771 crore since payouts began in fiscal year 2025 (FY25), or about 26% of its total outlay as of November 2026, the ministry said in a statement on Wednesday. The scheme, which has the largest outlay among those run by the ministry, will continue to provide incentives until FY29. As of November, nine automakers and 10 auto component manufacturers were eligible to receive incentives under it. The latest addition to the list is Hyundai Motor India Ltd, which received government approval in September this year to claim incentives under the scheme for two models of its electric Creta car. The PLI Auto scheme provides incentives to manufacturers on sales of zero-emission vehicles, including electric vehicles and some hydrogen-based vehicles. The objective is to lower manufacturing costs and improve manufacturers' margins. The ministry has previously faced questions over low budget utilization from the Rajya Sabha's department-related standing committee on industry. In March this year, the parliamentary panel, headed by MP Tiruchi Siva, flagged the under-utilization of budget estimates. It noted that the PLI Auto scheme, the ₹18,100 crore PLI scheme for batteries and the ₹11,900 crore PM E-Drive electric vehicle subsidy scheme had all seen reductions of more than 30% between budget estimates (BE) and revised estimates (RE) in multiple years. In its response to the committee, the ministry said the initial under-utilization of funds under PLI Auto was because investments by automakers in cleaner vehicle manufacturing took time to fructify, delaying the sales-based incentives that could be disbursed. Under the scheme's original disbursement plan, payouts were targeted at ₹604 crore in the first year, ₹3,150 crore in the second, ₹5,925 crore in the third, ₹7,199 crore in the fourth and ₹9,060 crore in the fifth year. Against these targets, the government's budget estimates stood at ₹3,500 crore in FY25, ₹2,818 crore in FY26 and ₹5,939 crore in FY27. The acceleration in incentive disbursements comes as electric vehicle adoption in India gains momentum. EV registrations rose to 2.55 million in FY26, from 2.04 million in the previous fiscal year, according to the government's VAHAN registry of new vehicles. Based on its analysis of 2025 data, the International Energy Agency (IEA) ranks India as the world's second-largest electric two-wheeler market, the largest electric three-wheeler market and the third-largest electric bus market. India aims to become a net-zero carbon emitter by 2070. Transport accounts for 12% of the country's carbon emissions, according to the IEA. A shift towards electric vehicles could also help reduce India's dependence on imported oil, with the country currently meeting about 90% of its oil requirements through imports. Manas is a New Delhi-based journalist with Mint, where he covers the intersection of economic policy, industry, and emerging sectors shaping India’s growth. He writes on government regulation, manufacturing, and the clean energy transition, with particular depth in areas such as electric mobility, battery ecosystems, and rare-earth supply chains. He has written on India’s efforts to build domestic capacity in electric vehicles and energy storage, as well as the broader push to reduce import dependence and strengthen supply chain resilience. His reports are not limited to capturing the headline; they also aim to explain complex policy simply.

Manas has studied law in Pune, the city where he grew up, followed by a business journalism diploma from the Asian College of Journalism in Chennai. title: Voltas ordered to pay  ₹33,770 for damaging customer's AC during reinstallation
description: Bengaluru consumer commission found deficiency in service on the part of the company's technicians, observing that the deployment of inadequately trained staff had resulted in damage to the appliance and rendered it completely non-functional
author: Livemint
content:
A Bengaluru consumer commission has directed Voltas Ltd to pay ₹33,770 to a customer after holding the company responsible for damage to his air conditioner during reinstallation following his relocation from Chennai to Bengaluru.
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (Bengaluru Urban) found deficiency in service on the part of the company's technicians, observing that the deployment of inadequately trained staff had resulted in damage to the appliance and rendered it completely non-functional.
The commission directed Voltas to pay ₹25,000 as consolidated compensation for the damage and operational loss of the air conditioner, along with 3% annual interest from the date of filing the complaint. It also ordered the company to refund ₹1,770 towards installation charges, pay ₹5,000 for mental agony and harassment, and reimburse ₹2,000 towards litigation expenses, according to a report by The Times of India.
Voltas has been directed to comply with the order within 45 days.
The complaint was filed by S Balaji, 37, who said his Voltas 1.5-tonne split air conditioner (Model 183SY) was in working condition when it was dismantled in Chennai in March 2025.
A technical fitness report issued by Dynamic Cool Center had certified that the appliance was functional before it was transported to Bengaluru.
After relocating, Balaji approached Voltas for reinstallation on April 19, 2025, and paid ₹1,770 for the service. However, he alleged that the company's technicians lacked the necessary expertise and allowed the entire refrigerant gas charge to leak during installation, leaving the appliance non-functional.
According to the complaint, Voltas technicians revisited the premises on May 1 and refilled the refrigerant gas without charging him. However, Balaji alleged that they left the cooling system unpressurised and exposed, allowing atmospheric moisture to enter over the following 12 days.
He claimed that this subsequently damaged the printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) and fan motor.
Despite raising several service requests and escalating the matter through emails, Balaji said the air conditioner continued to develop recurring reset problems before eventually stopping completely.
He also approached the National Consumer Helpline, but his grievances were marked as disposed of without any technical resolution.
The consumer commission noted that Balaji had submitted documents establishing that the air conditioner was functional before its relocation and developed major defects after the reinstallation carried out by Voltas.
It further observed that the company had failed to produce contrary technical evidence or provide a written explanation to refute the allegations.
"The deployment of untrained staff and the subsequent terminal damage to the machine amounts to a deficiency of service," the commission observed.
Commission rejects claim for full purchase value
However, the commission declined to award the entire original purchase price of ₹33,000 sought by the complainant.
It observed that the air conditioner was not a new appliance when it was reinstalled in Bengaluru, as it had already been used in Chennai. Awarding the full purchase value without considering depreciation would therefore be inequitable, it said.
The order was passed on September 30, 2026, by a commission comprising president Ramachandra M S and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani.
Voltas Ltd and its Bengaluru branch manager did not appear before the commission despite receiving notice. Consequently, the proceedings against them continued ex parte.

title: IIT Delhi alumnus reveals how he repaid over  ₹1 cr family debt before 25, quit Google to built own startup
description: A Delhi-graduate man, Yash Garg shared that he earned  ₹2 crore from a side business while also working at Google. He later quit his job and launched his dream startup after overcoming multiple failed attempts.
author: Sneha Biswas
content:
An IIT Delhi graduate shared his extraordinary turnaround story on the internet as he went from a debt of more than ₹1 lakh to securing a job at Google and eventually building his app business. This is the story of Yash Garg, who shared his streak of struggles in life while trying to clear off his family debt. Garg took to X and penned a long note on overcoming his family's financial troubles. He discovered his family was in more than ₹1 crore in debt while he was in the second year. "My father ran a real estate business, and he had invested in under-construction flats from builders like Jaypee and Wave, paying most of the price up front through home loans. Years went by without the flats being delivered, but the banks still wanted their EMIs on time. So my parents borrowed from friends and relatives, and when that was not enough, from credit cards," he shared. As collection agents began visiting his home, Garg made his parents sit down and listed every outstanding payment. He shared that the principal amount alone crossed the ₹1 crore mark. Garg realised that his only way out was to secure a high-paying job and clear the debt before pursuing his dream of building a startup. Despite being ranked second in his department with a CGPA of 9.7, Garg's campus placement plans did not go as expected. While he failed to clear the final round at Tower Research, he said he eventually accepted a job at Cohesity for ₹18 lakh a year. He moved to Bengaluru in July 2019 and lived in a paying guest setup under tight monthly expenses below ₹20,000. "My friends would talk about investing and going on trips, but I did none of that," he added. Garg said that although he sent most of his earnings home, it didn't improve the financial worries. He decided to look for vacancies at Google and upgraded himself accordingly. However, hirings were stopped due to COVID-19. Yash Garg, around the same time, joined Spotnana, hoping to earn more from the role and its equity. However, nothing much changed for him. He added, "About a year after I had started sending money home, I sat down to see where it had gone. Almost my entire salary had been spent on interest for our credit card loans. We had not reduced the principal and had not saved anything either. After a full year of hard work and sacrifice, the list was exactly as long as the day I had written it." Garg called it the lowest point of his life. A referral from a college senior eventually helped him land a job at Google. When he joined the company, he still had ₹80 lakh of debt left. To accelerate repayments, Garg began a side hustle. He launched a mobile apps business with his father. He worked nights and weekends alongside his full-time job. After initially struggling to generate money from Android apps, he said that he shifted his focus to iOS games. "I bought a MacBook Pro for a hefty ₹2.1 lakh, picked our most downloaded game on Android, built its Swift version in six days, and launched it on iOS. Installs were high from day one, and within a couple of days we turned on monetization," he shared. Finally, the business generated ₹6 lakh in its first month, which climbed to ₹24 lakh by the fourth month. Over the next 18 months, Garg's games crossed 2,00,000 downloads, mainly from users in the US, and generated more than ₹2 crore in revenue. Along with his Google salary and the earnings from the app business, Yash Garg was able to repay the outstanding loans. In June 2023, he cleared the debt. While Garg was no longer in debt, it was just the beginning of his dream startup. Soon after, he resigned from Google just before turning 25. He turned to entrepreneurship full-time. After several failed attempts, Garg built Super Workday, a business creating apps for users of the project management platform monday. Now, it has more than 300 paying customers, mostly US-based, and is close to $100,000 in annual recurring revenue (ARR). In January 2025, Yash Garg secured a $400,000 investment from Silicon Valley venture capital firm South Park Commons at a valuation of $5.7 million to build an AI executive assistant, as per his post. "I am ready for whatever comes next," he concluded his post. title: Bengal's legacy needs a Gen Z makeover to power its economic future
description: Faced with the pressing task of economic rejuvenation, West Bengal is striving to retain its youth and attract much-needed investment. During the Economic Times Bengal Ascends event, experts pointed out that the state's traditional economic identity requires transformation. They advocated for improved career opportunities and infrastructure, emphasizing collaboration with micro, small, and medium enterprises to cultivate a supportive investment climate and ensure the regions prosperous future.
author: ET Bureau
content:
These were among the key points raised at a panel discussion on "Imagining the Bengal of Tomorrow" at The Economic Times Bengal Ascends event. The panel featured Suvankar Sen, managing director of Senco Gold and Diamonds; Vibhash Agarwal, general manager at edible oil and foods company Emami Agrotech, Prithish Chowdhary, deputy managing director of Titagarh Rail Systems; and Diva Jain, director at real estate firm Arrjavv.
"Think of Maharashtra and you associate it with finance, Gujarat with enterprise, Tamil Nadu with manufacturing and Karnataka with technology. What comes to mind when we think of Bengal? Glorious past," Jain said. "Of course, our past deserves pride, but we cannot make the case for Bengal's future with this nostalgic and romantic attachment to the past."
GTA 6, the recent global gaming phenomenon, was cited during the discussion as an example of how Bengal recognised its contemporary talent. When the game was launched, much of the attention in Bengal was on Rupa Biswas, whose 1982 disco song featured in it. Less attention went to Devanjana Talukdar, Abhijit Bose, Abhijit Ghosal and Devojit Nandi, who were part of the game's animation team.
Also Read: Bengal needs tech push, talent return to become global business hub, industry leaders say
Sen said Bengal's legacy should be seen as a set of values that could shape its future, rather than as a burden. "For Bengal, legacy would mean the value system. It would be based on creativity, freedom, and thinking out of the box," the Senco Gold and Diamonds MD said, pointing to the state's contributions to India's freedom movement, philosophy, thought and science.
"Let's look at that value system and then connect it to the future, to the new generation. Tell them that this is what we stand for, and let us now change with the times," Sen said. He added that acceptance of modern thinking and a willingness to change were missing in recent years.
Creating opportunities for young people would require Bengal to keep pace with the changing nature of work, Agarwal said. Opportunities in consulting, finance, marketing and agency businesses emerged faster in Mumbai and Delhi, he said. Greater exposure to these sectors opened up new possibilities for young people, and building similar opportunities in Bengal could help reverse the outflow of talent, he said. Jain said Bengal must address the difference in earnings compared with other states, limited opportunities for career progression and the investment gap if it wanted professionals to return. "Ecosystems develop where there is investment," she said.
Chowdhary said Bengal's large micro, small and medium enterprises base could be used to train workers and connect them to larger supply chains. He urged companies to work with industrial training institutes and invest in upskilling young people. Not everyone trained by a company would necessarily join or remain with it, he said, but the effort would help create a larger pool of employable workers. Sen, who is part of the state's National Education Policy Task Force, said colleges were working to make industry participation part of students' courses.

title: Bengal needs tech push, talent return to become global business hub, industry leaders say
description: Industry leaders at The Economic Times Bengal Ascends summit emphasized the need for West Bengal to enhance its technology ecosystem. They noted that improving infrastructure and talent acquisition could position the state as a hub for global services. Key investments, such as Amul's dairy plant expansion, could foster economic growth and benefit local farmers. The role of artificial intelligence in various sectors was also a focal point of discussion.
author: ET Bureau
content:
Jayen Mehta, MD of dairy cooperative Amul, noted that Bengal had 1.5 lakh farmer families, 10 crore population and yet its milk production has stayed below its potential for years.
Amul will invest ₹700 crore in its dairy plant in Howrah to process 30 lakh litres of milk daily and emerge world's largest curd manufacturing facility with a capacity of 10 lakh kg per day. The expansion will potentially transfer nearly ₹5,000 crore annually to dairy farmers in the state. Mehta noted that Bengal needs to expand veterinary and dairy education.
West Bengal should capitalise on its industrial strengths in heavy engineering, chemicals, utilities and banking and develop the technological and domain-specific expertise required by multinational companies.
Pillay said Bengal's biggest untapped opportunity could be its diaspora of experienced technology and business leaders working across India's established GCC hubs.
"If you were to just reach out to the Bengali diaspora all across the country and run a simple ghar wapsi programme, you would get the best talent back here," she said. Sangita Singh, president-India and International at Everforth, said Bengal's economics including land, talent, infrastructure can offer up to 60% cost advantage against other cities for global enterprises to establish engineering hubs. "In the world of AI, I think three things are needed that can help give Bengal a head start," she said, identifying water availability, uninterrupted power and a strong pool of technically skilled professionals.
Also Read: The Great Indian Food Adventure: Indian flavours find a place on global shelves
She said the Ganga basin could support the water requirements of data centres, while the state's power infrastructure and engineering talent could help attract global technology investments. The executives also discussed whether AI could erode India's cost advantage in technology services. KPMG's Pillay said that GCCs are outsourcing routine corporate services and support functions. "Jobs are being redefined. Jobs need to be rethought... What we need to train our young graduates for is very different because the apprenticeship model as we all know it, is collapsing in that avatar," Pillay said. "It started with SAP and we said jobs would go away," Everforth's Singh said.
"It only increased. It started with call centres, and we've seen triple the number of people that you employ in call centres."
Meanwhile, Amul's Mehta discussed an interesting case of how AI is helping India's grassroots levels. Amul's AI voice assistant 'Sarlaben' helps millions of dairy farmers with technical advice in regional languages.
"Sarlaben gives answers on feeding, breeding, animal husbandry, veterinary services, central government schemes and even weather, as well as market prices," Mehta said. "Every day more than 1000 women from Bengal call up Sarlaben."
Manoshi Roychowdhury, co-chancellor of Techno India University, said AI is expanding into education, healthcare, hospitality, design and filmmaking, creating new opportunities for students across disciplines.
However, she cautioned that institutions needed to address the psychological impact of AI on students, particularly concerns about whether automation would eliminate future jobs.

title: ET Bengal Ascends: Can Kolkata become the economic engine of eastern India? Industry leaders spell out wha
description: Political alignment between West Bengal and the Centre is fostering infrastructure development and industrialisation in the state. Key discussions highlight land availability, execution speed, and nurturing first-generation entrepreneurs as crucial factors for growth. Industrialists emphasize the need for Kolkata to be positioned as the economic hub of the East to attract investments. Additionally, establishing trust and overcoming negative perceptions of the state are both essential elements.
author: ET TEAM
content:
Kolkata: Political alignment between West Bengal and the Centre is accelerating infrastructure development and industrialisation in the state, but faster execution, easier land availability, fostering first-generation entrepreneurs and positioning Kolkata as the economic hub of the East are key to sustaining growth, said industrialists, bankers and economists.
Ambuja Neotia Group chairman Harshavardhan Neotia, Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM) member Sanjeev Sanyal, Bandhan Bank MD and CEO Partha Pratim Sengupta, and Matix Fertilisers and Chemicals chairman and promoter Nishant Kanodia deliberated these issues in a panel discussion on West Bengal's 'Road to reindustrialisation: The promises and bumps' at The Economic Times Bengal Ascends event Tuesday.
Also Read | ET Bengal Ascends: From luchi to boardroom deals, Kolkata serves up a feast of ambition
Sanyal said land needs to be made available in Kolkata to drive economic concentration, crucial for achieving high growth rates in West Bengal, and the broader eastern region.
"Even in India, concentration is driving growth," he said. "In the South, it's Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai. In the West, it's Mumbai, Pune and Ahmedabad. Delhi-NCR is a well-defined area. If we want East to grow, some concentration needs to be fired. And here Kolkata is the best bet-be it infrastructure, human capital, business community. Once Kolkata fires, it can then be linked with Bhubaneswar, Ranchi or Patna."
Sanyal termed land as the biggest hurdle to growth. "Concentration means to do a lot of things in an extremely small area," he explained. "Unfortunately, we have a legacy of derelict industrial and other types of land which disallows this concentration. Lot of it in the middle of the city is stuck, owned by the government or private. The rules around urban land ceilings also need to be changed."
Also Read | ET Bengal Ascends: 'We invite businesses to partner govt in industrialisation drive,' says Industries Minister Tapas Roy
Sengupta agreed that land must be allocated and available, with proper conversion, without which industries cannot secure bank loans. "Right governance and infrastructure will attract investors, while the synergy between education institutions and industry will stop the brain drain," he said.
Neotia said the biggest change in the last five decades is the West Bengal government's alignment with the Centre, which will accelerate infrastructure investments and end the constant bickering between the two, facilitating implementation of stalled central schemes.
"The BJP election campaign had put economic development and resurgence as a priority which was a footnote in other campaigns," said Neotia. "In Bengal, which has quite a Left-leaning history, this is kind of a new proclamation which has fired up the entrepreneurs of the state. And Kolkata can be the national hub of the orange economy with the high creative capabilities and the pluralistic atmosphere, where food, fashion, creativity, cinema and art can find commerce and be an important MICE destination which can bring tourism."
Kanodia, whose Matix invested ₹6,500 crore in the state to build India's largest fertiliser plant, said the company is a "classic example of an investor committed to growth for the state", reflecting investor confidence. The benefits of state-Centre alignment are already visible, he said.
"Any large investments need approvals and joint co-operation between the state and Centre," he said. "We are seeing the benefits of a common agenda and the massive infrastructure push. Overall, the level of confidence of investors has increased," he said, stressing that "for the state to prosper, still a lot of effort needs to be made to establish trust."
According to Kanodia, execution speed-from inking MoUs to commissioning plants-is equally critical as West Bengal has considerable catching up to do with other states. "Every time, new plants come up and production starts will enhance the level of confidence and ensure second and third investments come faster," he said. "If the state focuses on developing industrial clusters instead of individual factories, it will be beneficial."
Sengupta said Bengal must overcome its negative perception, which has weighed heavily on the state despite industrialists' enthusiasm. "Let us focus on success stories," he said.
He noted that investors will closely watch policy execution as changing perceptions takes time. "A FII or foreign investor today will not think of Kolkata," he said. "But if there is a consistency in delivery, performance and execution, a year hence can think of Kolkata and even set up a GCC."
Sanyal said Bengal must foster young, first-generation entrepreneurs. "Creative destruction is what drives a great economy," he said. "It will not work by merely having people from outside or existing groups. We need to create a culture which accepts risk taking. And move out of revival of sick units with the resources redeployed to do completely new things."
Neotia and Sanyal also called for "bringing the river back" into Kolkata's urban landscape. Neotia said redeveloping the riverfront could be "magical", while Sanyal said distinctive architecture would "have a dramatic impact in the way people perceive the city."
Neotia said the biggest hurdle is a "change in mindset, including all of us who live in the city that Kolkata can be a vibrant economic hub."
Kanodia said 10-15 large industrial projects and swift resolution of bottlenecks could help change perceptions. "It will send a strong signal that the state means business," he said.
Sanyal agreed some quick-wins are needed to overcome the image problem. "But Bengal should aim for a big, transformational, out of the box project," he said. "Tomorrow's Bengal has to crawl out of the box and embrace the future and think unfettered how the past was," he said.
He further stressed Bengal must move beyond nostalgia for the Ambassador yellow taxi, jhal muri, and Victoria Memorial. "It's perfectly fine to have jhal muri, but it is not an economic model," said Sanyal.

title: CJP प्रोटेस्ट के दौरान हिरासत में लिए गए नेताओं पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने मांगा केंद्र से जवाब, 10 दिन में देना होगा हलफनामा
description: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने 10 अक्टूबर को दिल्ली में हुए विरोध प्रदर्शन के दौरान पूर्व मुख्यमंत्रियों और अन्य नेताओं की कथित हिरासत मामले में केंद्र और दिल्ली सरकार से 10 दिन के अंदर जवाब मांगा है.
content:
सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने 10 अक्टूबर को दिल्ली में हुए विरोध प्रदर्शन के दौरान पूर्व मुख्यमंत्रियों और अन्य नेताओं को कथित तौर पर हिरासत में लिए जाने के मालमे में केंद्र और दिल्ली सरकार से जवाब मांगा है. कोर्ट ने केंद्र सरकार, दिल्ली सरकार और दिल्ली पुलिस को इस बारे में 10 दिन के अंदर हलफनामा दाखिल करने का निर्देश दिया है.
चीफ जस्टिस सूर्यकांत, जस्टिस जॉयमाल्य बागची और जस्टिस वी. मोहना की पीठ ने यह आदेश दिया. कोर्ट ने कहा कि सरकारों के जवाब दाखिल होने के बाद याचिकाकर्ताओं को अपना जवाब यानी रिजॉइंडर दाखिल करने के लिए एक हफ्ते का समय मिलेगा.
दरअसल, मामला 10 अक्टूबर 2026 का है. 10 अक्टूबर को मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी और दूसरे छात्र संगठनों ने विरोध किया था. इस मामले में तृणमूल कांग्रेस की राज्यसभा सांसद मेनका गुरुस्वामी ने इस मामले में बंदी प्रत्यक्षीकरण याचिका दाखिल की है.
यह भी पढ़ें: उमर खालिद और शरजील इमाम को सुप्रीम कोर्ट से झटका, अंतरिम जमानत देने से इनकार
याचिका में आरोप लगाया गया है कि पश्चिम बंगाल की पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री ममता बनर्जी समेत कई नेताओं और प्रदर्शनकारियों को गैरकानूनी तरीके से हिरासत में लिया गया था. हालांकि, दिल्ली पुलिस ने इसे सिरे खारिज किया है. पुलिस का कहना है कि किसी को भी हिरासत में नहीं लिया गया था, बल्कि सुरक्षा प्रोटोकॉल के तहत नेताओं को प्रदर्शन स्थल से हटाया गया था. पुलिस ने यह भी दलील दी कि इस वजह से याचिका का कोई औचित्य नहीं रह जाता.
सुनवाई के दौरान अतिरिक्त सॉलिसिटर जनरल ऐश्वर्या भाटी ने कोर्ट को बताया कि कुछ मामलों में ही हलफनामे दाखिल किए गए हैं. इस पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने सभी मामलों को लेकर एक साथ विस्तृत जवाब दाखिल करने का निर्देश दिया.

title: अमेरिका से इस साल डिपोर्ट हुए 1700 भारतीय नागरिक, MEA ने दी जानकारी
description: MEA ने बताया कि इस साल की शुरुआत से अब तक अमेरिका से 1,700 भारतीय नागरिक डिपोर्ट किए गए हैं. माइग्रेशन और मोबिलिटी पर अमेरिका के साथ हमारा लगातार सहयोग चल रहा है.
author: aajtak.in
content:
विदेश मंत्रालय (MEA) ने बताया कि इस साल की शुरुआत से अब तक अमेरिका ने कुल 1,700 भारतीय नागरिकों को डिपोर्ट किया है. मंत्रालय ने साफ किया कि भारत अवैध इमिग्रेशन के सख्त खिलाफ है और लोगों की मोबिलिटी से जुड़े मुद्दों पर नई दिल्ली और वॉशिंगटन के बीच सहयोग जारी है.
MEA ने बताया, 'इस साल की शुरुआत से अब तक अमेरिका से 1,700 भारतीय नागरिक डिपोर्ट किए गए हैं. माइग्रेशन और मोबिलिटी पर अमेरिका के साथ हमारा लगातार सहयोग चल रहा है और भारत अवैध इमिग्रेशन के सख्त खिलाफ है. डिपोर्टेशन के मामलों पर हमारा अमेरिका के साथ सहयोग है.'
यह भी पढ़ें: 'Nvidia के CEO जेनसन हुआंग को राष्ट्रपति से माफी की जरूरत नहीं...', बोले अमेरिकी उपराष्ट्रपति जेडी वेंस
विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता रणधीर जायसवाल ने बताया कि संभावित डिपोर्टेशन से जुड़े मामलों पर अमेरिकी पक्ष से कम्युनिकेशन मिलने के बाद भारत सरकार संबंधित लोगों की नेशनलिटी का वेरिफिकेशन करती है.
इससे पहले जुलाई में एमईए ने बताया था कि साल 2025 से अब तक अमेरिका ने 4,840 से ज्यादा भारतीय नागरिकों को डिपोर्ट किया है. ट्रंप एडमिनिस्ट्रेशन एक बड़े क्रैकडाउन के तहत अमेरिका में रह रहे अवैध प्रवासियों को टारगेट कर रहा है.

title: तिरुपति बालाजी मंदिर को आज 121 किलो सोना दान करेगा गुमनाम भक्त, 160 करोड़ का मुकुट और गहने, चंद्रबाबू नायडू भी रहेंगे मौजूद
description: आंध्र प्रदेश के तिरुपति स्थित तिरुमला मंदिर में आज सोने की एक बड़ी भेंट दी जाएगी. एक गुमनाम भक्त भगवान श्री वेंकटेश्वर स्वामी के लिए 121 किलो सोने के आभूषण दान करेगा. इनकी अनुमानित कीमत करीब 160 करोड़ रुपये है. इस खास मौके पर आंध्र प्रदेश के मुख्यमंत्री एन. चंद्रबाबू नायडू भी मौजूद रहेंगे.
author: aajtak.in
content:
सोने का मुकुट, भगवान के चरणों के लिए खास आभूषण और कुल वजन 121 किलो. कीमत करीब 160 करोड़ रुपये. आंध्र प्रदेश के तिरुमला स्थित भगवान वेंकटेश्वर स्वामी के मंदिर में एक ऐसी भेंट आने वाली है, जिसकी चर्चा हो रही है. खास बात ये है कि इतना बड़ा दान देने वाले भक्त का नाम किसी को नहीं पता. पहचान गुप्त रखी गई है. आज 26 नवंबर को तिरुमला मंदिर में यह दान औपचारिक रूप से सौंपा जाएगा. इस मौके पर आंध्र प्रदेश के मुख्यमंत्री एन. चंद्रबाबू नायडू भी मौजूद रहेंगे. तिरुमला तिरुपति देवस्थानम (TTD) के अधिकारी इन आभूषणों को प्राप्त करेंगे.
आखिर इस 121 किलो सोने में क्या-क्या शामिल है? और मुख्यमंत्री चंद्रबाबू नायडू का इस कार्यक्रम में क्या शेड्यूल है? आइए समझते हैं. TTD की ओर से जो जानकारी साझा की गई है, उसके मुताबिक, एक श्रद्धालु भगवान श्री वेंकटेश्वर स्वामी को 121 किलो सोने के आभूषण भेंट करेगा. इनकी कीमत करीब 160 करोड़ रुपये बताई गई है. इस भेंट में भगवान के लिए सोने का मुकुट शामिल है.
यह भी पढ़ें: 23 करोड़ कैश, 92 KG चांदी-सोना... सांवलिया सेठ मंदिर को मिला 31 करोड़ का दान, भंडार से निकला सोना
इसके अलावा भगवान के चरणों के लिए विशेष आभूषण भी तैयार कराए गए हैं. इन्हें 'पद्म पादालु' कहा जाता है. यानी यह सिर्फ सोने का एक बड़ा दान नहीं है, बल्कि भगवान की प्रतिमा के लिए तैयार कराए गए विशेष आभूषणों की भेंट है. दान देने वाले व्यक्ति की पहचान गुप्त रखी गई है. इतनी बड़ी कीमत के सोने के आभूषण भगवान को समर्पित किए जा रहे हैं, दान देने वाला व्यक्ति गुमनाम रहना चाहता है.
चंद्रबाबू नायडू का पूरा कार्यक्रम क्या है?
आंध्र प्रदेश के मुख्यमंत्री एन. चंद्रबाबू नायडू 26 नवंबर की सुबह अमरावती से तिरुपति के लिए रवाना होंगे. वे सुबह 10 बजे तिरुपति के एसवी एग्रीकल्चरल कॉलेज स्थित हेलीपैड पर पहुंचेंगे. इसके बाद 10:45 बजे तिरुमला के गायत्री निलयम पहुंचेंगे. वहीं 11:10 बजे वैकुंठम क्यू कॉम्प्लेक्स के रास्ते भगवान वेंकटेश्वर के दर्शन करेंगे. इसके बाद 121 किलो सोने के आभूषणों को सौंपने के समारोह में शामिल होंगे. तिरुमला में कार्यक्रम पूरा होने के बाद मुख्यमंत्री तेलंगाना के भद्राद्री कोठागुडेम जाएंगे. वहां से लौटकर शाम करीब 4:30 बजे अमरावती पहुंचने का कार्यक्रम है.
तिरुपति मंदिर को क्यों खास माना जाता है?
तिरुमला का श्री वेंकटेश्वर मंदिर देश के सबसे प्रसिद्ध और समृद्ध धार्मिक स्थलों में गिना जाता है. यहां हर दिन बड़ी संख्या में श्रद्धालु दर्शन के लिए पहुंचते हैं. भक्त अपनी श्रद्धा के मुताबिक नकदी, सोना और दूसरे कीमती सामान दान करते हैं. ऐसे में 121 किलो सोने के आभूषणों की यह भेंट मंदिर के लिए एक बड़ी पेशकश है. इस बार चर्चा सिर्फ सोने की मात्रा या उसकी कीमत की नहीं, बल्कि उस भक्त की भी है, जिसने इतनी बड़ी भेंट दी और अपनी पहचान सार्वजनिक नहीं की. एक तरफ 121 किलो सोने का मुकुट और आभूषण हैं, दूसरी तरफ एक ऐसा दानदाता है, जिसका नाम तक सामने नहीं आया.

title: प्रणब मुखर्जी की सलाह ने शुभेंदु को बनाया 'कर्मचारी' से 'अधिकारी', बंगाल CM का बड़ा खुलासा
description: शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने बताया कि उन्हें पूर्व राष्ट्रपति मुखर्जी ने कहा था कि अगर वह अपना स्वतंत्र राजनीतिक करियर बनाना चाहते हैं, तो उन्हें TMC छोड़ कर बीजेपी का दामन थामना चाहिए,
author: धर्मेंद्र बैरागी
content:
प्रणब मुखर्जी की सलाह ने शुभेंदु को बनाया 'कर्मचारी' से 'अधिकारी', बंगाल CM का बड़ा खुलासा
शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने बताया कि उन्हें पूर्व राष्ट्रपति मुखर्जी ने कहा था कि अगर वह अपना स्वतंत्र राजनीतिक करियर बनाना चाहते हैं, तो उन्हें TMC छोड़ कर बीजेपी का दामन थामना चाहिए,
पश्चिम बंगाल के मुख्यमंत्री शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने पूर्व राष्ट्रपति प्रणब मुखर्जी को लेकर बड़ा खुलासा किया है. शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने कहा है कि उन्हें पूर्व राष्ट्रपति प्रणब मुखर्जी ने तृणमूल कांग्रेस छोड़ने और प्रधानमंत्री नरेन्द्र मोदी के साथ जुड़ने की सलाह दी थी.
पीटीआई भाषा की खबर के अनुसार, शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने बताया कि उन्हें पूर्व राष्ट्रपति मुखर्जी ने कहा था कि अगर वह अपना स्वतंत्र राजनीतिक करियर बनाना चाहते हैं, तो उन्हें ऐसा करना चाहिए, वरना वे ममता बनर्जी के नेतृत्व वाली पार्टी में सिर्फ एक ‘कर्मचारी’ बनकर रह जाएंगे. मुख्यमंत्री अधिकारी कूच बिहार में रास मेला के दौरान पत्रकारों से बात करते हुए यह बात की है. उन्होंने इस बारे में और कुछ बताने से इनकार कर दिया और कहा कि वह कांग्रेस के दिवंगत नेता के बारे में और चर्चा नहीं करना चाहते. उन्होंने मुखर्जी को ‘महान व्यक्तित्व’ बताया.
प्रणब मुखर्जी महान व्यक्तित्व
कभी तृणमूल के एक प्रमुख नेता और ममता बनर्जी सरकार में मंत्री रहे अधिकारी दिसंबर 2020 में पश्चिम बंगाल विधानसभा चुनाव से पहले भाजपा में शामिल हो गए थे. मुख्यमंत्री ने कहा, ‘‘प्रणब बाबू अब ईश्वर के पास चले गए हैं. वह अब हमारे बीच नहीं हैं. वह एक महान व्यक्तित्व थे. वह एक सम्मानित हस्ती हैं और मैं इस पर कोई अनावश्यक चर्चा नहीं करना चाहता.’’ अधिकारी का यह बयान उस घटना के एक दिन बाद आया है, जिसमें उन्होंने याद किया कि कैसे मुखर्जी ने उन्हें तृणमूल छोड़ने की सलाह दी थी.
TMC में थे कर्मचारी
कोलकाता में 'इकोनॉमिक टाइम्स' के एक कार्यक्रम में अधिकारी ने तृणमूल को ऐसी पार्टी बताया था जिसे पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री ममता बनर्जी और उनके भतीजे अभिषेक बनर्जी नियंत्रित करते हैं. उन्होंने इसकी कार्यप्रणाली की तुलना एक निजी कंपनी से की, जिसमें अध्यक्ष और प्रबंध निदेशक होते हैं. उन्होंने 2020 में तृणमूल छोड़ने के अपने फैसले का जिक्र करते हुए कहा, 'मैं भी वहां (तृणमूल में) था, लेकिन मैं एक कर्मचारी बनकर नहीं रहना चाहता था. इसलिए मैं बाहर आ गया.' मुख्यमंत्री ने मुखर्जी को अपना 'असली सलाहकार' बताया और याद किया कि मुखर्जी के राष्ट्रपति बनने के बाद वह उनसे मिलने राष्ट्रपति भवन गए थे.
अधिकारी के अनुसार, उस समय मुखर्जी ने उन्हें यह सोचने की सलाह दी थी कि क्या वह तृणमूल नेतृत्व के तहत काम करना चाहते हैं, या फिर मोदी के साथ जुड़कर स्वतंत्र रूप से अपनी राजनीतिक आकांक्षाओं को आगे बढ़ाना चाहते हैं. हालांकि, मुख्यमंत्री ने यह नहीं बताया कि यह बातचीत कब हुई थी. उन्होंने कहा कि वह एक ऐसे नेता के शब्दों को लेकर विवाद खड़ा नहीं करना चाहते, जो अब इस दुनिया में नहीं हैं.

title: 'एक-एक को घुसपैठिए को खोजकर वापस भेजो', बंगाल पुलिस से बोले CM शुभेंदु अधिकारी
description: बंगाल के मुख्यमंत्री शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने पुलिस को अवैध रूप से भारत में आए बांग्लादेशी घुसपैठियों को खोजकर वापस भेजने का आदेश दिया है.
author: रत्नाकर पाण्डेय
content:
'एक-एक को घुसपैठिए को खोजकर वापस भेजो', बंगाल पुलिस से बोले CM शुभेंदु अधिकारी
बंगाल के मुख्यमंत्री शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने पुलिस को अवैध रूप से भारत में आए बांग्लादेशी घुसपैठियों को खोजकर वापस भेजने का आदेश दिया है.
पश्चिम बंगाल के मुख्यमंत्री शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने पुलिस को बड़ा निर्देश दिया है. उन्होंने बुधवार (25 नवंबर) को कहा कि कूचबिहार जिले में बांग्लादेश से अवैध रूप से आए मुस्लिम घुसपैठियों को वापस भेजा जाए. उन्होंने कहा कि एक-एक की पहले पहचान करो और फिर देश से बाहर निकालो. उन्होंने यह भी कहा कि बांग्लादेश से आने वाले हिंदुओं को घुसपैठिया नहीं माना जाना चाहिए.
सीएम शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने कूच बिहार में 'रास मेला' के दौरान एक कार्यक्रम को संबोधित करते हुए एसपी मनीष जोशी से कहा, बांग्लादेश से आए अवैध मुस्लिम घुसपैठियों के लिए राज्य में कोई जगह नहीं है और उन्हें उसी रास्ते से वापस भेजा जाना चाहिए, जिससे वे भारत में दाखिल हुए थे.
बांग्लादेशी हिंदुओं के लिए क्या बोले शुभेंदु अधिकारी
उन्होंने कहा, 'बांग्लादेश से आए अवैध मुस्लिम घुसपैठियों की पहचान करनी होगी और उन्हें एक-एक करके खोजना होगा. इसके बाद बाहर निकालना होगा. लेकिन बांग्लादेश से आने वाले हिंदुओं को घुसपैठिया नहीं माना जाएगा, क्योंकि वे धार्मिक उत्पीड़न से बचने के लिए आ रहे हैं. वे जान बचाने के लिए बॉर्डर पार करके आए हैं. वे शरणार्थी हैं. उन्हें आश्रय दिया जाना चाहिए.'

बांग्लादेश बॉर्डर को लेकर क्या बोले सीएम
शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने राज्य पुलिस और सीमा सुरक्षा बल यानी कि बीएसएफ को इंटरनेशनल बॉर्डर पर सुरक्षा मजबूत करने के लिए साथ मिलकर काम करने के लिए कहा है. उन्होंने कहा कि राज्य सरकार ने बॉर्डर पर बुनियादी ढांचे के विकास के लिए और बाड़ बनाने के लिए जमीन उपलब्ध करवा दी है. शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने कहा कि बॉर्डर पर बाड़ लगने के बाद तस्करी पर भी पूरी तरह रोक लगनी चाहिए.

title: घर-घर जाएंगे BLO, SIR के दौरान हुई गलतियों को सुधारने के लिए चुनाव आयोग का बड़ा कदम
description: आयोग ने मतदाता सूची में नाम, जन्मतिथि, संबंधियों के नाम, मोबाइल नंबर और फोटो सहित अन्य विवरणों की जांच के निर्देश दिए हैं. गलतियां मिलने पर बीएलओ घर-घर जाकर मतदाताओं का सत्यापन करेंगे.
author: अंकित गुप्ता
content:
घर-घर जाएंगे BLO, SIR के दौरान हुई गलतियों को सुधारने के लिए चुनाव आयोग का बड़ा कदम
आयोग ने मतदाता सूची में नाम, जन्मतिथि, संबंधियों के नाम, मोबाइल नंबर और फोटो सहित अन्य विवरणों की जांच के निर्देश दिए हैं. गलतियां मिलने पर बीएलओ घर-घर जाकर मतदाताओं का सत्यापन करेंगे.
चुनाव आयोग ने विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SSR) के दौरान मतदाता सूची में संभावित गलतियों को सुधारने के लिए नए निर्देश जारी किए हैं. बुधवार ( 25 नवंबर) को जारी पत्र में आयोग ने 1 जनवरी 2027 की अर्हता तिथि के आधार पर मतदाता सूची में नाम, जन्मतिथि, संबंधियों के नाम, मोबाइल नंबर और फोटो सहित अन्य विवरणों की जांच के निर्देश दिए हैं. गलतियां मिलने पर बीएलओ घर-घर जाकर मतदाताओं का सत्यापन करेंगे. जरूरत पड़ने पर उनसे हस्ताक्षरित फॉर्म-8 लिया जाएगा.
आयोग ने साफ किया है कि बिना फॉर्म-8 और निर्धारित प्रक्रिया के कोई संशोधन नहीं होगा. ऑटोमैटिक पहचान के आधार पर बदलाव नहीं किए जाएंगे. पूरी प्रक्रिया ECINet के माध्यम से होगी. इस प्रक्रिया के लिए 1 जनवरी, 2027 को पात्रता की तारीख निर्धारित की गई है. इस पहल का मकसद आगामी चुनावों से पहले मतदाता डेटाबेस की सटीकता और विश्वसनीयता तय करना है.
EC ने दिए ये निर्देश
25 नवंबर को जारी निर्देश में आयोग ने मध्य प्रदेश, छत्तीसगढ़, उत्तर प्रदेश, राजस्थान, ओडिशा, पश्चिम बंगाल, तमिलनाडु, कर्नाटक, गुजरात सहित कई राज्यों और केंद्रशासित प्रदेशों के मुख्य निर्वाचन अधिकारियों को मौजूदा मतदाता विवरणों की विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण प्रक्रिया के दौरान जुटाए गए आंकड़ों से तुलना करने को कहा है.
आयोग के मुताबिक, मतदाताओं के नाम, संबंध संबंधी जानकारी, जन्मतिथि, मोबाइल नंबर और तस्वीरों सहित अन्य जानकारियों का पुनरीक्षण प्रक्रिया के दौरान जुटाए गए डेटा से मिलान किया जाएगा. इस दौरान सामने आने वाली विसंगतियों और अंतर को चिह्नित कर उनका फील्ड वेरिफिकेशन कराया जाएगा और जरूरी सुधार किए जाएंगे.
EC ने साफ किया है कि चिह्नित सभी एंट्री का फिजिकल वेरिफिकेशन अनिवार्य होगा. BLO को पुनरीक्षण प्रक्रिया के दौरान संबंधित मतदाताओं के घर जाकर उनके विवरणों का सत्यापन करने और जहां सुधार की जरूरत हो, वहां विधिवत भरे और हस्ताक्षरित फॉर्म-8 आवेदन प्राप्त करने के निर्देश दिए गए हैं. इसके बाद इन आवेदनों की जांच और निपटारा सहायक निर्वाचक रजिस्ट्रीकरण अधिकारी और निर्वाचक रजिस्ट्रीकरण अधिकारी निर्धारित प्रक्रिया के अनुसार करेंगे.
चुनाव आयोग का पारदर्शिता पर जोर
पारदर्शिता और सटीकता पर जोर देते हुए आयोग ने कहा है कि केवल स्वचालित पहचान प्रणाली के आधार पर मतदाता विवरण में कोई सुधार नहीं किया जाएगा. मतदाताओं के जनसांख्यिकीय विवरण में बदलाव से जुड़ी इस प्रक्रिया में प्रत्येक सुधार के लिए हस्ताक्षरित फॉर्म-8 आवेदन जरूरी होगा और निर्धारित सत्यापन के बाद सक्षम अधिकारी की मंजूरी से ही बदलाव किया जाएगा.

title: मोदी बोले- विपक्षी पार्टी मुसलमानों को आरक्षण देना चाहती है: वह OBC आरक्षण में कटौती को तैयार; नारी शक्ति व...
description: PM Modi Constitution Day blog analysis on opposition politics and governance. Latest Updates. प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने संविधान दिवस पर लिखे ब्लॉग में कांग्रेस और विपक्ष पर निशाना साधा। उन्होंने कहा कि विपक्ष की सबसे बड़ी पार्टी विरोध पक्ष से ज्यादा अवरोध पक्ष बनती जा रही है।
author: दैनिक भास्कर
content:
- Hindi News
- National
- Samvidhan Diwas: PM Modi Slams Opposition For Blocking Progress | Statement
मोदी बोले- विपक्षी पार्टी मुसलमानों को आरक्षण देना चाहती है:वह OBC आरक्षण में कटौती को तैयार; नारी शक्ति वंदन बिल रोकना महिलाओं का अपमान
- कॉपी लिंक
प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने गुरुवार को संविधान दिवस पर ब्लॉग लिखकर कांग्रेस पर निशाना साधा। उन्होंने कांग्रेस का नाम लिए बिना कहा- विपक्ष के एक प्रमुख दल ने महिला आरक्षण विधेयक पारित नहीं होने देिया।
मोदी ने कहा- विपक्ष की सबसे बड़ी पार्टी ने एक बार फिर बता दिया कि संवैधानिक मूल्यों के प्रति उसके मन में कितना कम सम्मान है। वह OBC आरक्षण कम करके मुसलमानों को आरक्षण देना चाहती है।
पीएम बोले- नारीशक्ति को न्याय दिलाने का संकल्प नहीं रुकेगा
मोदी ने ब्लॉग में लिखा- इस साल के शुरू में जो हुआ, उसने हम सभी को शर्मसार कर दिया। संविधान की यात्रा उन महिलाओं को याद किए बिना पूरी नहीं हो सकती, जिन्होंने इसे बनाने में अहम भूमिका निभाई।
पीएम ने लिखा- मैं देश की नारीशक्ति को भरोसा दिलाता हूं कि उन्हें न्याय दिलाने के हमारे संकल्प को दुनिया की कोई ताकत रोक नहीं सकती।
मोदी बोले- नक्सलवाद ने गरीबों को संवैधानिक अधिकारों से दूर रखा
मोदी ने नक्सलवाद का भी जिक्र किया। उन्होंने कहा- दशकों तक देश के अनेक हिस्सों में, खासकर आदिवासी क्षेत्रों में, नक्सलियों ने बंदूक के दम पर सबसे गरीब व्यक्ति को उन अधिकारों से वंचित रखा, जो हमारे संविधान ने उसे दिए हैं। इस साल नक्सलवाद के खात्मे से मुझे विशेष संतोष मिला है।
मोदी बोले- 1951 और 42वें संविधान संशोधन से संविधान कमजोर हुआ
मोदी ने 1951 में हुए पहले संविधान संशोधन और आपातकाल के दौरान किए गए 42वें संशोधन का जिक्र किया। उन्होंने कहा- पहले संशोधन से नागरिकों की मौलिक स्वतंत्रता प्रभावित हुई। उस समय अंतरिम संसद ने अपने बहुमत का इस्तेमाल कर यह संशोधन किया था।
मोदी ने कहा कि यह देश के पहले आम चुनाव से कुछ महीने पहले हुआ था। उनके मुताबिक, इसका मकसद विरोध की आवाज दबाना और चुनाव प्रक्रिया को प्रभावित करना था।
प्रधानमंत्री ने कहा कि आपातकाल के दौरान हुए 42वें संशोधन ने न्यायिक समीक्षा की शक्ति सीमित की और देश की संस्थाओं के बीच शक्तियों का संतुलन बदला। उन्होंने युवाओं से 38वें और 39वें संविधान संशोधनों का भी अध्ययन करने को कहा।
मोदी ने आरोप लगाया कि तब की सरकारों ने चुनी हुई राज्य सरकारों को बर्खास्त करने के लिए अनुच्छेद 356 का बार-बार इस्तेमाल किया। उन्होंने कहा कि एक राजनीतिक दल के नाम करीब 100 बार इस अनुच्छेद के इस्तेमाल का रिकॉर्ड है। एक पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री ने तो इस मामले में अर्धशतक भी लगाया था।
अनुच्छेद 370 और 35-A से जम्मू-कश्मीर में पूरा संविधान लागू नहीं हुआ
मोदी ने कहा कि संविधान निर्माताओं की इच्छा थी कि पूरे देश में संविधान अपने मूल स्वरूप और भावना के साथ लागू हो। लेकिन अनुच्छेद 370 और 35-A के कारण 70 साल से ज्यादा समय तक जम्मू-कश्मीर में पूरा संविधान लागू नहीं हो पाया।
उनके मुताबिक, इस दौरान वहां SC, ST, OBC वर्ग और महिलाओं के अधिकारों का हनन होता रहा। उन्होंने कहा कि 2019 में इस ऐतिहासिक अन्याय का अंत हुआ।
101वें, 102वें और 103वें संविधान संशोधन का जिक्र
मोदी ने अपनी सरकार के दौरान हुए तीन संविधान संशोधनों का उल्लेख किया। उन्होंने कहा कि 101वें संशोधन से GST लागू करने का रास्ता खुला। इसे उन्होंने लंबे समय से इंतजार किए जा रहे बड़े सुधारों में गिनाया। 102वें संशोधन से राष्ट्रीय पिछड़ा वर्ग आयोग को संवैधानिक दर्जा मिला।
वहीं, 103वें संशोधन से आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्ग (EWS) को 10% आरक्षण दिया गया। मोदी ने कहा कि इससे उन समुदायों को लाभ मिला, जो पहले आरक्षण व्यवस्था के दायरे से बाहर थे।
संविधान का नया संस्करण 22 भाषाओं में जारी
प्रधानमंत्री ने कहा कि 1950 के बाद पहली बार संविधान का अपडेटेड संस्करण आठवीं अनुसूची की सभी 22 भाषाओं में उपलब्ध कराया गया है। इससे संविधान आम लोगों के और करीब आया है। उन्होंने भारतीय न्याय संहिता का भी जिक्र किया।
मोदी ने कहा कि आजादी के बाद भी देश में अंग्रेजों के समय की दंड संहिता लागू थी। भारतीय न्याय संहिता के जरिए आपराधिक न्याय व्यवस्था में बदलाव किया गया है। पहले की व्यवस्था में दंड पर जोर था, जबकि नई व्यवस्था में नागरिक और न्याय को महत्व दिया गया है।

title: रोहतक में गैंगवार, 4 युवकों की हत्या: होटल में खाना खाते समय गोलियां बरसाईं, हिमांशु गैंग पर आरोप, मरने वाल...
description: Rohtak Milan Dhaba gangwar firing incident involving Baba and Himanshu Bhau gang latest news updates. रोहतक के गांव खरावड़ के पास मिलन ढाबे पर रात करीब 1 बजे बाबा गैंग व हिमांशु भाऊ गैंग के बीच गैंगवार देखने को मिली। दोनों तरफ से ताबड़तोड़ फायरिंग की गई, जिसमें 4 लोगों की मौत हो गई।
author: दीपक कुमार
