title: Migrant Workers in Surat Fight for Rest and Fair Wages
description: Surat’s embroidery workers face dismissals and police action for demanding weekly offs and overtime pay. Explore the class struggle behind their fight for labour rights.
author: Gautam  Nirmal Doshi
content:
In one of the many power looms of Surat’s sprawling textile industry, Vishal Baghi, a 25-year-old from Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh, has spent over four years working 12-hour-shifts in the embroidery line. In late August, at around 11 pm, Baghi was fired by his employer. This was the second time he was fired in less than two weeks. The reason: demanding a weekly day off from work.
“I was removed [from my job] only because I was raising awareness for a weekly off and for reasonable shifts,” Baghi said. He showed his social media profile with videos of him speaking at gatherings of migrant workers who are made to work 12-hour shifts each day, throughout the year, with three days off in a year at most.
The migrant embroidery workers started agitating on August 16, with weekly off as the primary demand. As per a report by The Indian Express, the protest began at the embroidery units of the Vedanta industrial area in Amroli, Surat. Soon, it spread to Anjani Industries, Katargam, Sachin GIDC, Pipodara, and Kadodara. Workers halted operations and staged demonstrations in other factories as well. An FIR was registered against 500 workers at the Amroli police station on August 17. Violence was also reported in some areas, and eight persons were arrested, as per the report.
Talks between the factory owners and the authorities followed. The workers’ demands were met with a lacklustre response from the owners. Now, the situation has worsened for the workers with the police detaining some of them and a few even losing their jobs because of their participation in gatherings and demonstrations.
“I was fired on that day [August 16] itself for participating in the dharna. Not one owner spoke to us. Instead, they recorded the protests with on phones. Over the next few days, at least 200 workers were fired because they were seen in these protests and demonstrations,” Baghi told Frontline.
Also Read | A new blow to workers
As per news reports, a memorandum submitted to the police by Janmabhumi Bharat Majdoor Union president Ajay Dubey states that the approximately 18 lakh migrant workers in Surat’s textile industry do not get benefits such as provident fund, insurance, and gratuity.
Surat is one of India’s most concentrated textile hubs and employs over 20 lakh workers. According to the Surat International Textile Expo (SITEX), an initiative of the Southern Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SGCCI), approximately 65 per cent of the country’s synthetic textiles are produced in Surat with an annual sales value of Rs.85,000 crore. Production, in value terms, has been growing at the rate of 12 per cent per annum.
The advent and installation of automatic machines have been pivotal to the transformation of the sector in Surat. Labour-intensive tasks such as weaving and embroidery are now mechanised, requiring fewer but better skilled workers. There are 1.5 lakh embroidery machines, as per SITEX, spread across the city, with factories working round-the-clock, with workers across two 12-hour shifts.
Demands of workers
On October 23, the workers gathered at Citi Industrial Estate in Udhna, Surat, to negotiate with one of the factory owners about the continuation of their employment and weekly offs. The demands of the workers Frontline met were fairly simple. First, one weekly day off from the rigorous routine. Second, 8-hour shifts with compensation for overtime work, with an additional half-a-day wage for a 12-hour shift. Third, timely payment in the first week of the month, as opposed to irregular payment in the third or fourth week as is the case sometimes, according to a few workers.
Kamalnath Kushwaha, an embroidery worker from Satna in Madhya Pradesh who has been in Surat for at least 12 years, said, “We are not asking for a common day off [like Sunday] for everyone. You can give people different off-days so that work doesn’t stop. This is a simple demand.”
Rohit, a factory worker in Udhna, said, “We were not given a holiday on August 15 [Independence Day] either. When everyone else celebrates by hoisting and waving our country’s flag, don’t we have the right to get the day off and celebrate as well? But, instead, we worked 12-hour shifts as usual. Are we not humans?”
Kushwaha added, “We were not even given two hours off to go out. It’s ironic because it was Independence Day.”
Rohit has been working in Surat for over 15 years, and now has a wife and a young daughter. “I don’t get time to spend with my little daughter at all. We finish work at 8:30 pm, head home, do our daily chores, and then we’re just exhausted. It’s difficult to wake up again and head straight to work when you’re so tired. We’re just asking for a day off so that we can rest and recuperate,” he said, asking for the weekly off even if no other is demand is met.
Baghi, who is unmarried, said it is hard to do anything besides work: “I go home, make dinner, and it’s late by the time I eat and clean. I wake up at 7 am, prepare and pack my lunch and rush to work. I don’t get time to speak to my family back home [in Mirzapur] who go to sleep before I finish my chores.”
For the workers, leisure is a dream. Baghi and the others said they rarely even go to a park or meet friends, which would require sacrificing their much-needed sleep. “I know very few places in Surat because I haven’t explored it at all, despite being here for over 4 years,” said Baghi. Embroidery workers in Surat earn between Rs.20,000 to Rs.30,000, depending on their experience and the type of work and machine they handle.
A choice that wasn’t
Following weeks of unsuccessful attempts since August to get their demands met, the workers along with labour union leaders like Malkhan Singh Verma, president of the Sarvajanik Mazdoor Ekta Union, had notified the authorities that they would stage a peaceful protest on October 1. On September 29, the office of the Deputy Labour Commissioner in Surat sent a letter to the Textile Embroidery Jobwork Association of Surat (TEJAS), a non-profit trade association for embroidery factory owners and entrepreneurs, and to the SGCCI. It directed the organisations to implement the provisions of the four labour codes: The Code of Wages, 2019; The Occupational Safety, Health, and Working Conditions Code, 2020; The Code on Social Security, 2020; and The Industrial Relations Code, 2020.
The letter stated that “provisions have been made for wages, working hours and holidays as per the Wages Code, 2019 and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. Therefore, all the members associated with your association are requested to take action as per the provisions of the labour codes and to inform you accordingly so that the labour codes can be implemented smoothly. If any legal guidance is required in this regard, you are advised to contact this office”.
Verma said, “The workers were happy with this letter, and the protest stopped too. But the owners were still not meeting the demands. They are running these factories as per their own rules and regulations, and don’t want to change that. The migrant workers from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and other States work according to what other workers, who are not aware of the [labour] laws, tell them.”
On October 10 and 11, TEJAS offered a resolution for the concerns around wages, shift structure, and other operational guidelines. As per local news reports, its unanimous decision was that if embroidery karigars (skilled workers) wished to work as per rules, they will be paid Rs.550 for an 8-hour shift, instead of the minimum wage of Rs.522. Alternatively, they can opt for the existing system of a monthly salary between Rs.25,000 and Rs.30,000, based on performance.
Additionally, TEJAS placed a ban on mobile phones on factory floors. It said that if the factory owner suffers any loss due to the use of mobile phones, 50 per cent of the loss amount must be paid by the worker concerned. Now, effectively, if a worker opts for the 8-hour shift system (48 hours per week), the monthly wage will be Rs.14,300, factoring in the four weekly offs without compensation.
As per the Union Ministry of Labour and Employment’s Code on Wages, 2019, and The Occupational Safety, Health, and Working Conditions Code, 2020, workers are eligible for
• a “day of rest in every period of seven days which shall be allowed to all employees or to any specified class of employees and for the payment of remuneration in respect of such days of rest”; and
• wages at the rate of twice the rate of wages for overtime work.
Additionally, as per The Gujarat Shops and Establishments (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) (Amendment) Act, 2026, which amended the 2019 Act, no worker shall be required or allowed to work for more than 10 hours a day and 48 hours a week. But embroidery workers in Surat work 12 hours a day and 84 hours a week.
The resolution offered by TEJAS allows workers to opt for 48-hour work weeks, with a day off, but at a salary of just Rs.14,300, with no remuneration for rest days as per Union Ministry of Labour and Employment’s stipulated guidelines. However, some workers do think that if they are paid overtime, this could still work.
Rohit said, “We are okay with the decision [of Rs.550 per day] if we get paid overtime for 12 hour shifts. They will need three sets of workers for 8-hour shifts so that the factories can run round-the-clock. Getting so many additional workers is difficult. So they will have to continue with two sets of workers, and if we get paid for overtime, then we are okay with this.”
Four hours of overtime at twice the wage rate would add up to Rs.1,100 every day, or Rs.28,600 for a 30-day period with four days off and 24 hours of overtime per week. But this rests on the hope of getting the stipulated overtime wage rate, which TEJAS has said nothing about. Verma said: “The workers are asking at the least, a weekly off, as per the labour laws. They are not asking for a stake in the ownership of the factory. Why does TEJAS need to intervene?”
He added, “The workers don’t get an ID card, payslip, gratuity, bonuses, or anything. So, if you want to give them Rs.550 for an 8-hour shift as per the stipulated rules, what about the rest [of the rules]?”
Surveillance, loss of work, and lack of dignity
The workers alleged that those who participated in protests and gatherings have been surveilled through recordings on smartphones, and their photos, videos, and details like names are being shared with groups of factory owners.
Kushwaha said, “I was removed from my job on October 4 on the pretext that I was asking for weekly offs. In a few days, I got a job elsewhere and just as it was being finalised, I got a call that they could not hire me. The only logical explanation is that the owners communicate among themselves, and we are blacklisted because of our simple demands.”
Baghi also uploads videos of his speeches and interviews with other workers on social media. A few days after being fired on August 16, he got a job at another factory. But he was fired again, on the first day of work.
He said, “The owners have recordings of the protests, and our details, and share our videos and profiles on their [chat] groups. We are not selected [for work] anywhere. There are some who went back to their villages after being fired, but many have stayed, hoping they will get work somewhere and send money back home.”
Speaking about the humiliation of workers, Verma said, “No one can be expected to work 365 days a year. Please think of these skilled workers as humans.”
Senior national spokesperson of the Indian Youth Congress and labour activist Shaan Khan stated that the work requires a lot of effort, despite the technological developments.
Frontline visited a factory floor in an embroidery unit in Surat at around 10 pm, when a worker was operating a large machine with over 20 units, each comprising different heads for different beads and decorative accessories.
The temperature on factory floors in the area is regulated through windowless openings in walls, but the heat and noise near the machines are still significantly high. The worker has to know his way around the machine’s software to start the process. It must also be halted for several reasons, such as inserting more thread, beads, and so on.
Baghi said, “The machines always stay on. Even during lunch, we are not allowed to go together. If I leave, the worker on the adjacent machine looks after mine as well. And I do the same for him.”
In one embroidery unit, a small place to cook is located right outside the bathroom. A worker who did not wish to be named said, “The working conditions are really bad.” He was neither wearing gloves nor any safety gear.
Verma said, “There is no provision for workers’ safety in these units. Gloves, helmet, eye-protection wear, nothing is given.” Across the power loom with this embroidery unit, workers were easing into their night shifts that day.
Lathicharge and preventive detentions
With their demands not met and the half-hearted response of TEJAS, on October 15, the workers, union leaders, and activists staged a peaceful protest march towards the Collector’s office. They had requested permission from the police but were not given one. The protest was not called off, and this led to preventive detentions of Khan, Baghi, and Verma.
Khan said, “I was picked up on the night of October 14 itself.” Baghi was detained at around 11 pm the same night. “I was let go the next evening and was not able to participate in the protest. From the night of October 14 until 10 am the next day, people were detained successively.”
Verma said, “I was called to the police station at 7 am for a chat but wasn’t allowed to leave until 8 pm.” He added, “Those not detained who participated in the protest were met with hundreds of police personnel outside the Collector’s office, as if they were some sort of criminals.” Verma, Baghi, and Khan said that there was a lathicharge, and some workers were hurt. The workers believe that the authorities are complicit with the factory owners because of how the events unfolded.
Govind, who hails from Deoria in Uttar Pradesh and has been in Surat for several years, was also detained during the protest. He said, “Almost 90 of us were detained and not released until that evening. With their [TEJAS’] response, it is clear that even the authorities might be okay with this because they are not making efforts to implement the provisions in the [labour] laws.”
Govind said he was fired on October 15 due to his participation in the protest. “I spoke to them and I’m starting again tomorrow [October 24]. But several workers were fired, and many are planning to go back home. We are labelled as outsiders but we’ve spent our entire childhood in Surat, working. Now, even our kids study in schools here,” he said. TEJAS facilitated a gathering of around 25,000 embroidery workers on October 10. The workers were disappointed that they could not do the same without a confrontation with the police.
Deflated hope and the way forward
Union Minister of Textiles Giriraj Singh visited Surat on October 9 and 10, and as per news reports, his only comment was that the workers and owners should resolve the issues through dialogue. On October 14, as per news reports, union leader Dubey was arrested on charges of extorting a trader. He was released last week, but this has dented his credibility among workers. Nevertheless, most workers remain undeterred in their struggle for better working conditions.
TEJAS’s Karunesh Ranpariya has posted videos about the workers’ and factory owners’ disagreements on his social media profile. In one post, he wrote that “workers go to the machine owner’s place to operate the machine on their own will. The worker sees the machine, the design running—suit, sari, chaniya [lehenga], or garment—and the worker and owner mutually agree on a salary for 30 days. This has been the system for more than 30 years.” He blamed the union leaders “who neither operate the machine nor are machine owners, [but] create conflicts between workers and owners by raising the issue of an 8-hour shift and holidays on Sunday just to run their own shop.”
Also Read | Dictatorship of the employer?
He also posted videos of CCTV footage from a factory floor of a worker manhandling an embroidery machine. He further said that owners have identified other non-workers “causing outrage” about the issue, and even noted that TEJAS would support embroidery machine owners and make them its members if they sign up with a cancelled cheque.
According to Gujarati news reports, Ranpariya was one of five people accused of embezzling crores in donations under the name of “various social organisations in Surat”, including TEJAS. He was arrested in Madhya Pradesh in June 2023 after the investigation was handed over to the Amroli police station. As per his social media posts, he joined the BJP in November 2023.
Baghi said, “If I go home, I’ll have to work in construction with a pay of Rs.400 at most, that too in a place 25 km away. I have to find work here because I’m not experienced in anything else.”
While the workers have other demands, the primary one is just a weekly day off. At Citi Industrial Estate on October 23, one of the workers said, “The owner agreed to give us two paid days off in a month. We should have taken that.” Seemingly, a weekly day off would be far-fetched.

title: TVK’s Muslim appeasement on full display: Tamil Nadu govt apologises, blames Devasthanam’s non-approval for breach of SC order; petitioners point to “deliberate attempt at non-compliance”
description: The TVK govt of Tamil Nadu furnished a status report on the issue and blamed the tustees for disregarding the SC order. | OpIndia News
category: Editor's picks, Featured, News Reports, Opinions, Politics
author: Rukma Rathore
content:
On 25th November (Wednesday), the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government of Tamil Nadu apologised in the Supreme Court after it lit the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the traditional Uchipillayar Deepa Mandapam rather than the Deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram hill, in violation of its order.
Notably, the government was instructed to use the stone pillar for the ceremonial lamp ceremony by both the Supreme Court and the Madras High Court. Now, the apex court has stated that it will review the state government’s status report on the issue alongside considering the contempt plea presented by the petitioners.
Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan initially brought up the matter on behalf of the authorities, before a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi, conveying, “As the Collector, I was supposed to file a status report on what took place. We have just had that filed. We have a number. I think Your Lordships may take it up because unfortunately the lamp didn’t get lit. So I, as a Collector, have traced out all the steps that I was supposed to comply with.”
The state claimed that the order was not executed because of the Board of Trustees. It alleged, “I sincerely apologise for the lamp not being lit at the Deepathoon. The district administration made every effort to secure the authorisation of the Devasthanam and the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon. However, the Board of Trustees, by its resolution dated 24th November, resolved to light the lamp at the customary place. I will submit an additional status report with all supporting documents along with the same.”
The state argued that “every arrangement was complete and every possible difficulty had been offered an immediate solution” by the district administration, adding, “The only step remaining was the authorisation of the team by the Devasthanam. The time for the ceremony was fixed at 6.00 pm to 6:30 pm as proposed by the Executive Officer herself. No team authorised by the Devasthanam came forward within that time, and no request for any extension of time was received. At 7:32 pm, the temple’s press release was received.”
Afterwards, the Executive Officer asserted that she could not intervene because of a resolution passed by the trustees.
#BREAKING Madurai District Collector tells #SupremeCourt that all arrangements were made by the District Administration to light the Kartigai Deepam at the Thiruparankundram Deepathoon. However, it could not be lit there as the Board of Trustees of the Temple Devasthanam did not authorise the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon, as they took the stance that it can be lit only where it was being customarily done at the Uchaipillaiyar Mandapam.
— Live Law (@LiveLawIndia) November 25, 2026
Petitioners expose the government’s dubious conduct
Senior lawyer Guru Krishna Kumar, who represented the Hindu petitioners, called out the deceptive tactics of the government and charged, “This is like anticipatory breach, anticipatory mentioning. Most unfortunate, My Lords. State tells the High Court some prohibitory orders were. They use the Board of Trustees, and I say this, to say the custom does not permit it, and the sthanikars have said it cannot be done.”
He further stated that the government and the devasthanam joined hands to defend the contravention of the verdict and mentioned, “In the evening, later, sthanikars say that ‘no, we didn’t make any such statement; no opinion was sought from us.’ Deliberate attempt at not complying with the order, and they’ve succeeded by stratagem and devices. Most unfortunate. There is a complete infraction of the rule of law. This is the majesty of the law that we are looking at.”
The petitioners demanded to start suo motu contempt proceedings, and direct that the flame currently burning at the conventional location be moved to the Deepathoon. They also highlighted how the state government consistently promised the High Court that it would implement the ruling, right up until the last moment, only to willfully fail to carry it out under the guise of trustees. “You file the necessary plea. You take the steps. We will consider,” responded Justice Aravind Kumar.
No lengths too far for Muslim appeasement
The TVK government had already expressed its objection to the court’s resolution through its review petition. The measure to brazenly disregard it predictably did not originate from any independent decision by the Devasthanam or its trustees, who function under the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department, which has long faced allegations of exploiting temple funds, undermining Hindu traditions and interfering in religious affairs.
The institution being made a scapegoat in this case is not an independent body but one that operates under the state government’s control. As the petitioners had already pointed out, this was nothing more than a collusive effort by the two sides to create a smoke-and-mirrors show.
The glaring truth that the government is attempting to obscure through its absurd explanations is that the TVK, much like its predecessor, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), which wanted to eradicate Sanatan Dharma, is following the well-worn formula of “secularism” centred on pandering to Muslims.
The latter invoked the purported need to “preserve law and order” and “prevent communal tensions” to justify flouting the High Court judgement and preventing Hindu devotees from lighting the lamp at the stone pillar last year. The more things have changed, the more they visibly stayed the same.
The TVK government is pursuing the route set by its predecessor, willing to compromise not only Hindu religious rights and faith but also showing little regard for even the courts of the country. Moreover, alliance partners including the Indian National Congress, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), Communist Party of India (Marxist), Communist Party of India (CPI) and Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) put tremendous pressure to disobey the judicial mandate.
The action has already faced fierce opposition from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Hindu groups for its vote bank motive. A similar instance of this was observed earlier this month, when the Joseph Vijay-led government in Tamil Nadu decided to regularise encroachments by issuing pattas to thousands of mosques, churches and dargahs.
According to A M Shah Jahan, Minister for Minorities Welfare, the government was working to regularise religious institutions that lack ownership documentation. He informed that minority groups petitioned the government for pattas for unlawful houses of worship that had been on government property for 25-50 years.
Hence, a decision was made to comply with the demands of Christians and Muslims, and the required paperwork would be completed shortly. To cater to its vote bank, the government has even given the green light to illegal occupation, setting a deeply troubling and equally dangerous precedent.
Furthermore, the government has been accused of diverting public funds towards freebies and schemes targeting its Muslim vote bank even as the state’s coffers come under strain. It has set aside Rs 20 crore for female students from the community and announced the expansion of the Tamil Nadu Waqf Board scholarship for Muslim girls from Classes 1-8 to Classes 9-10 at Rs 2,000 per year, totalling Rs 8.28 crore.
Tamil Nadu also introduced a Rs 100 crore interest-free revolving amount to provide loans for developing income-generating assets on Muslim and Christian properties, and allocated an estimated Rs 40 crore for a new headquarters for the state Waqf Board while raising its administrative grant to Rs 5 crore.
On the other hand, the Joseph Vijay-led coalition did not even allow the lighting of a lamp on the stone pillar on a single occasion, as pronounced by the Supreme Court.
In this political calculus, Hindus, along with their rights and religious beliefs, are turned into soft targets by these self-proclaimed secularists, while the authority of the courts is rendered virtually meaningless. It would not be wrong to call this yet another low point, shameful but hardly surprising, in India’s brand of “secular politics,” where even the judiciary is sacrificed at the altar of Muslim appeasement.
The comrades in the media have commenced the whitewashing, carefully steering clear of any mention of a possible link between the government’s breach of court orders and its vote-bank interests. The News Minute has already been consistently accusing Hindus of disturbing the supposed communal harmony by refusing to look the other way when their religious beliefs and practices go for a toss.
The latest episode is merely a continuation in this direction, prioritising the consolidation of minority, particularly Muslim, vote bank above all else. However, the question is how far these political parties are prepared to go in pursuit of their demented agenda, trampling upon everything from Hindus to the judiciary. It also remains to be seen whether the courts will hold them accountable for such conduct or tolerate their free run.
Meanwhile, nothing has changed for the majority community, which continues to be forced to struggle for even its most basic religious rights, from Ayodhya to Thiruparankundram hill.

title: Thiruparankundram Deepam Row: 1923 court decree declared Hill temple property, dargah had rights over three specific areas, Deepathoon outside its land
description: A century of judicial rulings, from the 1923 civil court decree to the 2025 Madras High Court order, clarified the temple's ownership of Thiruparankundram hill, the Dargah's limited property rights and the Deepathoon's location outside Dargah land. | OpIndia News
author: Jinit Jain
content:
A controversy erupted earlier today after the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government defied the Supreme Court-mandated order to light the Karthigai Deepam at Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai and instead lighted the traditional lamp at its usual spot, triggering outrage among the Hindu population. The Hindu outfits slammed the Vijay government, criticizing it for what they called a brazen display of Muslim appeasement.
The issue has, nevertheless, brought renewed attention to a century-old legal dispute between the Subramaniya Swamy Temple and the Sikkandar Badusha Dargah. Historical court records reveal that a civil court declared the temple the owner of Thiruparankundram hill in 1923, while recognising the Dargah’s ownership and possession of certain specific areas and structures. The original decree was subsequently restored by the Privy Council in 1931.
The legal history has assumed significance amid the latest dispute over the traditional lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar situated on the upper reaches of the hill.
A detailed account of the century-old litigation was reproduced in the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court’s June 24, 2025 judgment in a batch of petitions concerning Thiruparankundram hill.
How the dispute between the temple and Dargah began
The dispute dates back to 1917, when the Sikkandar Badusha Dargah proposed constructing a mandapam on Thiruparankundram hill. The Subramaniya Swamy Temple objected to the construction, asserting that the entire hill belonged to the temple.
The temple subsequently instituted a civil suit, initially numbered O.S. No. 101 of 1917, which was later renumbered as O.S. No. 4 of 1920 before the First Additional Subordinate Judge, Madurai.
The temple sought a declaration of ownership over the entire hill, an injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with its possession and recovery of possession of certain portions of the property. The Dargah and the government were among the defendants in the proceedings.
After examining the rival claims, the civil court delivered its decree on August 25, 1923, recognising the temple’s ownership and possession of the hill, subject to specific exceptions.
What the 1923 civil court decree said about ownership
The decree made an important distinction between the temple’s ownership of the hill and the rights of the Muslim defendants over particular portions.
The court declared the Subramaniya Swamy Temple the owner and possessor of the whole of Thiruparankundram hill and the Giri Veedhi, except certain assessed and occupied lands, Nellithope, the new mandapam, the flight of steps leading from Nellithope to the mosque and the top rock on which the mosque and the Muslim flagstaff stood.
The court separately recognised the Muslim defendants as owners and in possession of Nellithope, everything situated within it, the flight of steps, the new mandapam and the entire top of the hillock on which the mosque and flagstaff stood.
The decree also recognised the Kasi Viswanathaswamy Temple and its sacred water body as belonging to the Hindu temple.
Thus, the civil court recognised the temple’s ownership over the hill while protecting the Dargah’s rights over specifically identified properties and structures. It did not declare the Dargah the owner of the entire hill.
How the Privy Council restored the temple’s ownership decree in 1931
The Dargah challenged the civil court’s decision by filing First Appeal No. 34 of 1924 before the Madras High Court. On May 4, 1926, the High Court dismissed the Dargah’s appeal while allowing a cross-appeal filed by the government.
The Subramaniya Swamy Temple subsequently approached the Privy Council in Appeal No. 5 of 1930.
On May 12, 1931, the Privy Council allowed the temple’s appeal and restored the original decree passed by the Subordinate Judge on August 25, 1923.
The Privy Council observed that the temple had established its possession over the unoccupied portions of the hill from time immemorial and that its authorities had consistently treated the property as belonging to the temple.
It concluded that the original Subordinate Judge had arrived at the correct decision and that there was no sufficient ground to disturb the decree.
The Privy Council consequently set aside the Madras High Court’s decree and restored the original civil court judgment.
Subsequent disputes over the hill
The litigation did not end with the Privy Council’s decision.
In 1958, the temple instituted another civil suit, O.S. No. 111 of 1958, seeking an injunction against the removal of stones from portions of the hill outside Nellithope and the assessed and occupied areas.
The trial court passed a permanent injunction restraining the defendants from cutting stones from the specified portions. It also directed that the exact location and extent of Nellithope and the assessed and occupied areas be determined through further proceedings.
The decree was modified by the District Court in 1961, which directed that the boundaries be identified through a survey commission.
Further proceedings followed in subsequent years, reflecting continuing disagreements over the precise extent of the properties and the respective rights of the parties.
What is the present dispute over Thiruparankundram Deepathoon?
The historical ownership dispute has acquired renewed significance because of the controversy over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon.
The Subramaniya Swamy Temple, situated at the foothills of Thiruparankundram, is one of the six sacred abodes of Lord Murugan. The Sikkandar Badusha Dargah is situated on the hilltop, while a Shiva temple and Jain religious remains are also found on the hill.
The present controversy centres on the demand by Hindu organisations and devotees to light the traditional Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar situated near the Dargah.
Hindu organisations maintain that the pillar is situated on temple-owned land and that lighting the ceremonial lamp there is part of the religious tradition associated with the hill. They cite historical civil court decrees and the Privy Council’s decision to support their position.
The Dargah and Muslim organisations have opposed the proposed lighting at the location, citing its proximity to their place of worship. The dispute has consequently involved questions concerning property boundaries, access, religious practices and the respective rights of the temple and the Dargah.
The controversy reached the courts again in 2025. In its June 24 judgment, the Madras High Court’s Madurai Bench examined several petitions concerning religious practices at the Dargah, including animal sacrifice, prayers and gatherings.
The two-judge bench delivered separate opinions on the issues, resulting in a split verdict and a reference to the Chief Justice for further proceedings. The judgment also discussed the historical civil court decrees recognising the rights of both parties over specified portions of the hill.
December 2025 Madras High Court order: Deepathoon does not fall within Dargah property
Then in December 2025, Justice G.R. Swaminathan of the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court allowed a batch of petitions seeking permission to light the ceremonial lamp at the ancient Deepathoon on Thiruparankundram hill.
The judge extensively examined the 1923 civil court decree and the Privy Council’s subsequent decision. He held that the Muslim community’s ownership rights extended to only three specific portions of the hill: Nellithope, the flight of steps leading to the mosque and the actual site on which the mosque stands.
The rest of the hill, including its unoccupied portions, belonged to the temple’s Devasthanam.
Rejecting the argument that the petitioners should approach a civil court again for fresh demarcation of the property, Justice Swaminathan observed that the boundaries of Nellithope had already been determined through earlier proceedings. Since the Deepathoon was not situated within Nellithope, there was no requirement to reopen the ownership dispute.
The judge also made an important observation about the geographical location of the Deepathoon.
Thiruparankundram hill has two peaks. The Sikkandar Badusha Dargah and mosque are situated on the higher peak, while the Deepathoon is located on the lower peak, at a distance of at least 50 metres from the mosque.
Justice Swaminathan noted that the Dargah had a compound wall and that the Deepathoon was situated outside it, on an unoccupied portion of the hill. He concluded that the pillar belonged exclusively to the temple.
The judge observed that the entire upper portion of the hill did not belong to the Dargah and that the earlier judgments had already settled the ownership question.
He further noted that the Devasthanam could reach the Deepathoon by climbing steps from the Nellithope area, with the temple having the benefit of an earlier injunction protecting its access.
Court says lighting the Deepam is necessary to protect temple property
Justice Swaminathan went beyond examining the historical ownership dispute and addressed the temple administration’s responsibility to protect its property.
He observed that refusing to light the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon could undermine the temple’s ability to assert its ownership over the unoccupied portions of the hill.
The judge noted that despite the 1923 decree and the subsequent Privy Council ruling clarifying the ownership rights, there had been attempts by the mosque trustees to disturb the existing status quo. He said the temple administration had a responsibility to remain vigilant against any attempts to encroach upon its property.
The court also rejected the argument that lighting the lamp at the Deepathoon would interfere with the religious rights of the Dargah or the Muslim community. It observed that the ceremonial lighting would not affect the Dargah’s structure, which was situated at a safe distance.
Justice Swaminathan held that the temple had a legal duty to light the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon in addition to the customary location near the Uchipillaiyar Temple.
The court quashed the decision taken by the temple’s Executive Officer to conduct the ritual only at the usual Deepa Mandapam, observing that a decision of such importance should have been taken by the temple’s Trust Board rather than the Executive Officer.
It directed the temple administration to conduct the ritual at the Deepathoon from 2025 onwards and ordered police protection to ensure that it could be performed peacefully.

title: 250-400 Muslims stormed Hindu family’s house, tore women’s clothes, pelted stones: Victims reveal pre-planned attack in Gujarat’s Vadgam, share daily torment – Exclusive Ground Report
description: A Muslim mob attacked a Hindu Rajput family in Vadgam, Gujarat. They assaulted women, and pelted stones at their house. | OpIndia News
author: લિંકન સોખડિયા
content:
A series of attacks on members of the Hindu community in villages falling under the Vadgam Assembly constituency of Gujarat’s Banaskantha district shows no signs of stopping. Notably, Congress leader Jignesh Mevani is an MLA from the constituency.
The recent incident of an attack on young Hindu Dalits for bursting Diwali crackers in Bhagal village of Palanpur taluka is still fresh. Now, another shocking incident has come to light from Teywada village in Vadgam taluka, where a Muslim mob entered the house of a Hindu Rajput family and attempted to assault its members. The attackers also pelted stones and tore the clothes of the women in the house.
The OpIndia Gujarati team reached Tewari village and spoke to the affected women, residents and an injured man undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Palanpur.
The mob entered the house when there were only women and a child sleeping in a crib
When the OpIndia team visited the victim’s house, they found broken windowpanes and signs of damage caused by stone-pelting. Stones were also seen lying around the cradle in which a small child had been sleeping when the incident took place. Fortunately, one of the girls in the family quickly picked up the child, fortunately preventing any injury.
Speaking exclusively to OpIndia, the victim women narrated their ordeal; the family had gone to the fields or were away for work when the attackers arrived. Only women and children were at home at the time.
The victim said: “Initially, five Muslim men came and directly attacked, making provocative remarks like ‘entering the houses of Hindus-Rajputs and robbing them of their girls and women.’ Women who were alone in the house were pushed down, their sarees and blouses were torn off, and attempts were made to strangle them. The T-shirts and clothes of the daughters who were trying to save them were also torn off.”
Another victim said that the incident left her so traumatised that she could not speak for two days.
Victims reveal attack was planned, name two local Muslim men
During the ground report, the affected women and villagers called the attack a planned attack and informed about the role of two local Muslim men: ‘Imran Doctor’ and former village sarpanch ‘Ilyasbhai’.
The victim women further said: “First five people came and attacked, then Imran Doctor and former Sarpanch Ilyasbhai came there. They first turned the people away on the pretext of making peace and removed their four-wheelers parked in the square and put them in a safe place so that their vehicles would not be damaged in the stone pelting. Then a crowd of 250 to 400 people gathered and climbed on the roof and pelted our houses with stones, and Imran Doctor himself incited the crowd to rob the honour of women.”
‘Hindus are being forced to leave their villages due to the lack of houses’
Another victim woman from Teywada village told OpIndia that Hindu families are often harassed because they are fewer in number compared to Muslims living in the village. The villagers said that they are being harassed by throwing garbage on the road, making fun of the Hindu daughters coming and going, and psychologically pressuring them to flee by saying, “You should leave this village and run away.”
Injured man says attackers broke his hand; underwent surgery
The men of the Hindu family have sustained serious injuries in this attack. The elders of the family are admitted to the hospital in serious condition. The OpIndia team also spoke to the injured Hindu man Sureshbhai, who is undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Palanpur.
Sureshbhai said: “While I was outside, my brother called me and said that we had been attacked. As soon as I reached there on my bike, I was attacked with weapons like a hatchet and a spade. I have a fracture in my hand and had to undergo an operation to have a plate inserted, which cost around Rs 1.5 lakh to Rs 1.75 lakh. This attack was not sudden, but was carried out with complete planning.”
Police register complaints from both sides, detain 19 people
OpIndia Gujarati team also contacted the PI of the Chaphi police station to get official details about the entire attack. As per the information given by him over the phone, as he was busy with court proceedings, the police have registered a complaint against both parties in this incident, and so far a total of 19 people from both sides have been detained. Currently, police are deployed in the village, and the situation is peaceful.
Meanwhile, villagers also said that some Hindu youths who were victims of the attack had also been falsely implicated through counter-complaints. They demanded strict action against those seen pelting stones in videos of the incident.
Why are Hindus unsafe in MLA Jignesh Mevani’s constituency?
The incident has also brought attention to the recent cases of violence against Hindus reported from villages in the Vadgam Assembly constituency of Gujarat, represented by Congress MLA Jignesh Mevani.
On the one hand, in Bhagal village, where the Gujarat ATS arrested Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) terrorists in July 2026, Hindu Dalit youths were attacked for bursting firecrackers during Diwali. On the other hand, in Teywada village, a Muslim mob attempted to force its way into the house of a Hindu Rajput family and assaulted the women.
The question arises as to why Jignesh Mevani, the Congress-backed MLA from Vadgam, who delivers speeches across the country invoking the Constitution and advocating Dalit and women’s rights, has remained silent over these attacks on Hindu families and Dalit youths in his own constituency. Are extremist elements in the area receiving political protection to appease a particular vote bank?
While people have confidence in Gujarat’s law and order machinery, there is an urgent need for exemplary and strict action against those accused of assaulting women and carrying out premeditated stone-pelting in Teywada village. The viral video of the incident should also be examined as part of the investigation.
(Note: This article is a translation of the original article published on OpIndia Gujarati. The complete ground report of Teywada village can be viewed on OpIndia Gujarati’s YouTube channel.)

title: India's Mega Infrastructure Push: PM Modi Reviews Rs 78,000 Crore Projects Across Road, Railways, Power And Coal Sectors In PRAGATI Meet
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the 55th meeting of Pragati, the ICT-enabled governance platform for Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementat
author: Swarajya Staff
content:
Infrastructure
Swarajya Staff
Nov 26, 2026 | Updated 10:25 AM GMT+5:30

Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the 55th meeting of Pragati, the ICT-enabled governance platform for Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth on Wednesday (25 November).
During the session, he reviewed five critical infrastructure projects spanning the road, power, coal and railway sectors, with a combined investment exceeding Rs 78,000 crore.
The Prime Minister emphasised that infrastructure delays carry consequences beyond cost escalation, as they postpone benefits intended for citizens, businesses and the economy.
He called upon officials to resolve pending issues with clear responsibility and realistic timelines, stressing that timely execution must be accompanied by high construction standards.
Reviewing road projects, PM Modi reiterated the need to focus on outcomes over outlays and called for expeditious implementation.
For the power sector, he suggested exploring innovative models for decentralised solar and wind projects closer to consumption centres, aiming to improve affordable power availability and ease pressure on transmission infrastructure.
On coal projects, the Prime Minister stressed that rehabilitation and resettlement should be undertaken in a timely and dignified manner alongside project implementation.
The meeting also reviewed the Industrial Training Institute ecosystem, including the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs initiative.
PM Modi called upon chief ministers and chief secretaries to strengthen ITIs and deepen industry participation. He advocated a 'Classroom–Company–Career' approach to connect training with employment, emphasising that skilling should be organised around industrial clusters and sectoral requirements.
The Prime Minister urged public sector undertakings to establish stronger linkages with ITIs for training and recruitment aligned with future manpower needs.

title: India Eyes Regional Aviation Repair Hub Status As Cabinet Clears Aircraft Maintenance Partnership With Singapore
description: The Union Cabinet approved a Memorandum of Understanding with the Republic of Singapore yesterday (25 November) to strengthen India's aircraft mainten
author: Swarajya Staff
content:
Infrastructure
Swarajya Staff
Nov 26, 2026 | Updated 09:45 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!

The Union Cabinet approved a Memorandum of Understanding with the Republic of Singapore yesterday (25 November) to strengthen India's aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul sector.
The agreement focuses on skills development and industry expansion, aiming to reduce the country's reliance on overseas servicing facilities.
Under the pact, both nations will jointly develop an industry-focused curriculum for Aircraft Maintenance Engineer training.
The MoU also covers internship and exchange programmes with Singaporean MRO entities, enabling Indian students to gain practical industry experience with established operators.
Union Minister of Civil Aviation Ram Mohan Naidu stated the agreement aligns with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of self-reliance, with the objective of positioning India as the regional aviation workshop.
He emphasised that every aircraft component, from landing gear to cockpit displays, should be repaired domestically.
The civil aviation ministry indicated the MoU aims to spur partnerships that expand domestic MRO facilities and capacity, with stated goals of lowering repair costs and cutting aircraft downtime caused by sending work overseas.
The agreement leverages Singapore's established MRO ecosystem alongside India's growing fleet demand.
Officials presented the pact as a framework for medium- to long-term capacity building.
The partnership is considered particularly relevant given commercial links such as Singapore Airlines' 25.1 per cent stake in Air India, and comes as India witnesses unprecedented growth in air traffic with airlines steadily expanding their aircraft fleets.

title: Union Cabinet Greenlights Second Container Terminal At Kamarajar Port To Handle Ultra-Large Vessels
description: The Union Cabinet approved today the development of a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited in Tamil Nadu under
author: Arjun Brij
content:
News Brief
Arjun Brij
Nov 25, 2026 | Updated 07:26 PM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
The Union Cabinet has approved a Rs 4,288.26 crore investment to develop a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port in Tamil Nadu, adding 2 million TEUs of annual handling capacity and enabling the port to accommodate some of the world's largest container ships.
The project will be developed under the public-private partnership (PPP) model through a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) arrangement, with a concession period of 40 years.
The selected private operator will fund the construction, while Kamarajar Port will separately spend Rs 450 crore on dredging.
The proposed terminal will have a 900-metre berth, a design draft of 18 metres and the capacity to handle container vessels measuring up to 400 metres in length with a carrying capacity of 24,346 TEUs.
The facility is expected to improve the port's access to international shipping routes and accommodate growing export-import cargo volumes from the Chennai–Ennore industrial belt and the southern hinterland.
Construction will be divided into two phases. The first phase, costing Rs 2,429.32 crore, will provide capacity for 1.1 million TEUs, while the second phase will add another 0.9 million TEUs at an estimated cost of Rs 1,858.94 crore.
The entire project is scheduled to be completed within 48 months, with the first phase expected to become operational in the 25th month.
The expansion comes as the existing container terminal is operating close to capacity. Kamarajar Port handled around 0.7 million TEUs against its installed capacity of 0.8 million TEUs in 2025-26, translating into utilisation of approximately 88 per cent.
The port handled 49.08 million tonnes of cargo and 1,008 vessels during the financial year. Container traffic has grown at an annual rate of around 9.9 per cent over the past five years, creating the need for additional capacity.
The project will be awarded through global competitive bidding, with the concessionaire recovering its investment through user charges.

title: The Newslaundry website and app are now accessible
description: Screen reader compatibility, voice search, transcripts, colour contrast settings, dyslexia mode and a lot more.
author: Chitranshu Tewari
content:
Screen reader compatibility, voice search, transcripts, colour contrast settings, dyslexia mode and a lot more.
Product experts have long cited empathy as the secret sauce behind successful products. Until you truly understand the needs, usage, and perspective of the user you serve, you won’t be able to build meaningful products.
Empathy is also at the heart of all storytelling in journalism. Journalists take risks to speak truth to power because they empathise with the subjects in their stories.
Yet this empathy is largely absent when it comes to product decisions regarding news websites and apps. Most of us in the news know how excruciatingly painful it is for a disabled person to access a news website or simply think they are not our ‘target audience’. This translates to products that are inaccessible and discriminate against millions of users with disabilities.
At Newslaundry, we are changing that.
Last year at The Media Rumble, our annual media conference, we previewed a set of features and system overhauls that would make our website and app accessible to people with disabilities. A string of structural changes that would make our website and app compatible with screen readers used by blind users and features that disabled users rely on to access the internet and computers.
We’re stoked to announce that these changes are now live! It’s been a long road to get here, given that we started working on overhauling our front-end code and putting in the systems for accessibility last year. But before I get to the details, here are quick highlights of the changes:
Screen reader compatibility
Users with visual impairments rely on screen reader software to navigate apps. These set of features make our website app compatible with screen readers present in iOS, Windows, MacOS, and Android, as well as leading screen reader software such as JAWS and NVDA. We also have semantic HTML and ARIA labels, hints and roles that help visually disabled users with additional context.
A user using iOS voiceover with the Newslaundry app.
Colour filters and contrast themes
Our app now offers colour themes for those with visual impairments alongside dark and light modes. Users can choose between high-contrast and low-contrast designs to tweak the contrast between text and background for better readability.
If you already use accessible settings in your operating system, we also have a Sync With System option where we will sync your contrast settings for the app to the settings on your device.
Dyslexia font and motion control
Dyslexia font to make text more readable for dyslexic users, and motion control to help users with ADHD.
Interactive: Drag the bar in the middle to see the difference default screen and one with dyslexia-friendly font.
Are accessible designs only for disabled users?
One of the biggest myths about accessibility is that it is only for users with disabilities. The truth is that an accessible product and design improves the overall user experience, helping users across the board. The benefits of an accessible product extend to everyone. It’s about ensuring everyone can access the product, without any barriers.
Here are the features that best demonstrate this.
Transcripts and subtitles
An in-built, one-click transcript for all Newslaundry podcasts, and read-aloud functionality for all text stories. Plus, closed captions for all videos.
Voice search
Search by speaking with just a tap, with filters for authors, sections and tags.
A user using voice search to search for stories.
Reader mode
At Newslaundry, we have always tried to create a clean, no-distraction design. It helps that we don’t have any ads. After all, we all hate pop-ups, banners and ads in the middle of a story page.
We are now taking this further with a reader mode on the app. Enhance the reader experience by eliminating all distractions in the form of sidebars and banners, presenting stories in a clean format optimised for reading.
Interactive: Drag the bar in the middle to see the reader mode on a story page.
Our journey to accessibility
We first stumbled upon accessibility as a problem when one of our young subscribers wrote to us about the website being inaccessible. That led to speaking with more users and accessibility experts and researching web accessibility. We learned early on that deploying quick fixes just to claim an accessible tag wouldn’t help us serve disabled users. There are countless examples of how fixes in the form of widgets and accessibility overlays often end up making it worse for disabled users.
This meant revisiting systems and processes that had been in place for over a decade. Accessibility is among the most basic product requirements and is relatively easy to deliver if considered from the start. On the other hand, implementing it on a decade-old tech stack and a mix of third-party products was a nightmare.
Our small team of developers worked tirelessly to go back to the code, make systemic changes, and then build on the features. It didn’t help that as a news publisher, you tend to work with a host of third-party products that you have zero influence on. As a result, we had to circumvent the products we rely on for our day-to-day publishing operations.
It took us over six months to put this together. But given that there are hardly any Indian news websites and apps that are accessible, we wanted to ship responsibility instead of resorting to a bandaid, overlay approach.
Like any product cycle, we will continue making improvements to get better. Accessibility should be a default approach baked into the user experience. We have also changed how we write and present our stories to make them more accessible, ranging from alternate text for images to better colour choices for new products.
A round of thanks
It has really taken a village to make this possible. First up, we are indebted to Shakul Sonker, Vineet Saraiwala, Prashant Ranjan Verma, Shashank Pandey and Shubhanku Kochar. All of them helped us understand the right approach to accessible products and challenges faced by disabled users in accessing the internet.
I am immensely proud of our small engineering team, which made this a reality. Rishabh, Aditya, Danish, and Dhananjai didn’t let the many, many challenges deter them and executed the work that we set out for ourselves. Also, my colleagues who contributed immensely to the project before they moved on from Newslaundry: Yatharth, Prachi, Rishabh, and Akshat. This is a reality because each of them punched way above their weight and understood we were onto something big.
A big thank you to Google. We knew revamping our website and app to make them accessible would take time, resources, and skilled engineers—often a rarity in the newsroom. We pitched accessibility as an idea and its need to Google News Initiative Innovation Challenge, a global programme to empower news organisations that pioneer new-age thinking in online journalism. Folks at Google backed the idea, helping us fund much of our engineering effort.
Massive shoutout to our subscriber Himanshu, who helped us with UI-UX. Design often becomes an afterthought for a resource-crunched newsroom. He helped us with many user screens through the app. Plus, Gobindh, our in-house designer, made the artwork.
We also partnered with the students at the University of Michigan School of Information. Tiara, Kexuan, Qiyue, and Harrison tested the product with multiple users and carried out a heuristic evaluation of our app and website. Shoutout to Joyojeet Pal, who made the partnership happen.
Last but not least, our subscribers who power everything we do at Newslaundry. We are blessed to have them.
What’s next
This is not a we-are-ready-to-move-on product update. There are still a lot of things that we can improve upon. We have prioritised engineering over design, so there’s a lot of room for improvement in design and UI-UX. Write to chitranshutewari@newslaundry.com for feedback, suggestions and bugs. If you’re a disabled user or use accessibility settings, we would love to hear from you.
More importantly, we hope this nudges other publishers to take up accessibility. We are also working on an accessibility resource guide for newsrooms. More on that later.
Click here to download the app. You can access all accessibility settings by clicking on the accessibility icon in the bottom navigation bar. On the website, simply hit the settings icon at the top right of the homepage.

title: Modi hints at Parliament session ahead of December 15
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has reportedly urged his ministers to prepare for the next Parliament session before December 15, advising against foreign travel. This comes amidst opposition questions over delays in convening the Winter Session. Speculation is rife about the potential introduction of the delimitation-linked women's reservation bill, which faces challenges in securing the required two-thirds majority. The political landscape has shifted, but the government still needs opposition support for the crucial constitutional amendment.
author: Hemant Waje
content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has reportedly urged his ministerial colleagues to prepare for an early Parliament session before December 15, sparking speculation about the potential introduction of the crucial women's reservation bill and its challenging path to securing a two-thirds majority.
Key Points
- Prime Minister Narendra Modi has reportedly asked ministers to prepare for the next Parliament session before December 15 and avoid foreign travel.
- The move comes amid opposition concerns about the delay in convening the Winter Session, with the Monsoon session still unprorogued.
- There is speculation that the government might introduce the delimitation-linked women's reservation bill in the upcoming session.
- Securing the two-thirds majority (361 votes) for the Constitution amendment bill will be challenging for the ruling NDA, despite recent shifts in political alliances.
- The government is exploring a formula to increase Lok Sabha seats by 50 per cent across states while retaining the 1971 Census basis for inter-state seat share.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is learnt to have suggested to his ministerial colleagues that they complete preparations for the next Parliament session before December 15 and advised them against undertaking foreign travel in the run-up to it, indicating that the government wants its ministers to remain available.
Preparations For Upcoming Session
Sources aware of the matter said the issue of the next Parliament session figured at Wednesday's Cabinet meeting chaired by Modi.
The prime minister suggested that the session be convened before December 15, the sources said, adding that the Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs will finalise when it will commence and its duration.
Modi stressed the need for preparations, asking the ministers to ensure that their respective ministries are ready for the upcoming session.
As of Wednesday night, the Monsoon session remains unprorogued even after 103 days since the two Houses were adjourned indefinitely on August 13.
The developments assume significance amid mounting questions from the opposition over the delay in convening the Winter Session of Parliament.
The opposition parties have pointed out that more than 100 days have passed since the Monsoon Session was adjourned, but the House has not yet been prorogued – the formal ending.
The delay has fuelled speculation about a possible special session, particularly in the context of the proposed delimitation of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies.
Women's Reservation Bill On The Cards?
With the next parliamentary sitting likely before December 15, all eyes are on whether the government will bring the delimitation-linked women's reservation bill.
However, securing the numbers for the crucial Constitution amendment legislation could prove tricky.
The bill requires a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha, or 361 votes in the present 543-member House.
With three vacancies, the House has 540 members at present.
The ruling NDA has 320 members and would need the support of opposition parties to cross the threshold.
Since the bill's defeat in the Lok Sabha in April, the political arithmetic has changed, with 26 MPs moving out of the opposition camp.
While 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA, six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.
While these developments have strengthened the government's position, it would still need additional support.
The DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP-Sharadchandra Pawar with eight, could assume significance in the evolving numbers game.
Political Hurdles And Opposition Protests
The political challenge extends beyond numbers.
The opposition parties, which have stepped up their campaign against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, are expected to carry their protests into Parliament, potentially setting the stage for another stormy session.
A ruling alliance MP said that debate and voting on a Constitution amendment bill would not be possible unless the House functioned in an orderly manner.
An extended sitting of the existing session requires a minimum notice of two days, while convening a fresh session requires at least 14 days' notice.
Delimitation Formula Under Consideration
The government is learnt to be exploring a formula under which Lok Sabha seats would be increased by 50 per cent across states to address concerns, particularly among the southern states, over the implications of delimitation.
The proposed framework is also understood to retain the existing inter-state share of seats based on the 1971 Census, though no final decision has been taken yet.
The proposed legislation – The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 – failed to secure the requisite numbers during a special sitting of Parliament on April 17, making its fate in the winter session a key political and legislative test for the government.

title: Pune FDA Seizes Banned Gutka Worth Over Rs 60 Lakh In Major Raids
description: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in Pune conducted two raids, seizing banned gutka and flavoured tobacco products valued at over Rs 60 lakh. These operations were part of the 'Safe Food, Safe Maharashtra' campaign, leading to registered cases and a call for public vigilance against illegal product sales.
author: Text Feed
content:
Pune's Food and Drug Administration has conducted significant raids, seizing banned gutka and flavoured tobacco products valued at over Rs 60 lakh as part of its ongoing 'Safe Food, Safe Maharashtra' campaign.
Key Points
- Pune FDA seized banned gutka and flavoured tobacco products worth over Rs 60 lakh in two separate raids.
- The operations were conducted on Tuesday as part of the regulator's 'Safe Food, Safe Maharashtra' campaign.
- Significant seizures occurred in Handewadi (Rs 25.9 lakh) and Fursungi (Rs 35.9 lakh), where a vehicle was also seized.
- Authorities have registered cases and vowed strict action against those involved in the storage and sale of prohibited food products.
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has seized banned gutka and flavoured tobacco products worth over Rs 60 lakh in two separate raids in Pune city, officials said.
FDA's 'Safe Food, Safe Maharashtra' Campaign
The raids were conducted on Tuesday as part of the regulator's 'Safe Food, Safe Maharashtra' campaign.
An FDA team raided a premises near JSPM College in the Handewadi area of Hadapsar and seized banned gutka and flavoured tobacco products worth Rs 25.9 lakh, officials said on Wednesday.
In the Fursungi area, FDA recovered the banned substances worth Rs 35.9 lakh and also seized a vehicle, they said.
A senior FDA official said cases have been registered in connection with the seizures. He said strict action would be taken against those involved in the storage and sale of prohibited food products.
He also urged people to inform the administration if they come across the storage, transportation or sale of such products.

title: Delhi Police Encounter Leaves Alleged Gangster Associate Injured
description: Aman Gurjar, a man allegedly linked to gangster Naseem Durrani, was injured in his leg during an exchange of fire with Delhi Police in the Yamuna Khadar area early Thursday. Gurjar reportedly opened fire on police during an operation, leading to police retaliation. His alleged connections to D-Company and Durrani's network are being probed but remain unconfirmed.
author: Text Feed
content:
Delhi Police engaged in an exchange of fire in Yamuna Khadar early Thursday, resulting in injuries to Aman Gurjar, an individual allegedly connected to gangster Naseem Durrani, as authorities probe his potential underworld ties.
Key Points
- Aman Gurjar, allegedly linked to gangster Naseem Durrani, was injured in an exchange of fire with Delhi Police early Thursday.
- Gurjar sustained a bullet injury in his leg during the encounter in the Yamuna Khadar area near New Usmanpur.
- He allegedly opened fire at a Special Staff team, prompting police retaliation.
- Police are investigating his unconfirmed alleged links with the D-Company and Durrani's criminal network.
A man allegedly linked to gangster Naseem Durrani was injured in an exchange of fire with the Delhi Police in the Yamuna Khadar area near New Usmanpur early Thursday, police sources said.
Details Of The Encounter
The accused, identified as Aman Gurjar, sustained a bullet injury in his leg during the encounter and was taken to a hospital, they said.
According to preliminary information, a team of the northeast district Special Staff was conducting an operation in the Yamuna Khadar area when it signalled Gurjar to stop.
However, he allegedly opened fire at the police team, following which the personnel retaliated, injuring him in the leg, the sources said.
Police are also probing his alleged links with the D-Company and the criminal network associated with Durrani. However, his alleged underworld connections have not been officially confirmed.
Further details are awaited.

title: Aligarh Police Arrest 12 Bangladeshi Nationals For Illegal Entry Into India; Aadhaar, PAN, Voter ID And EPFO
description: Aligarh Police arrested 12 Bangladeshi nationals for allegedly entering India illegally. Aadhaar, PAN and voter ID cards, bank records and EPFO cards were recovered. Police also seized mobile phones containing evidence of communication with relatives in Bangladesh.
author: ANI
content:
Aligarh: Aligarh Police have arrested 12 Bangladeshi nationals for allegedly entering India illegally, with documents including Aadhaar cards, PAN cards, voter ID cards, bank savings account records and Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) cards recovered from their possession, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Aditya Bansal said.
According to the SSP, the arrests were made following information received by the police. During the operation, the police apprehended 12 Bangladeshi nationals, who allegedly disclosed during questioning that they had entered India illegally.
Sharing details of the arrests, Bansal said the police acted on confidential information and recovered several documents from the arrested individuals, including identity cards and financial records.
"Acting on confidential information, 12 Bangladeshi nationals have been arrested. They have disclosed that they had entered India illegally," Bansal said.
The SSP further said the documents recovered from their possession included Aadhaar cards, PAN cards, voter identity cards, bank savings account records and EPFO cards.
"Documents including Aadhaar cards, PAN cards, voter ID cards, bank savings account records, and EPFO cards were recovered from them," he said.
Apart from the documents, the police also seized mobile phones belonging to the arrested individuals. According to Bansal, the examination of the seized mobile phones revealed evidence of communication with their relatives in Bangladesh through calls and messages.
"Their mobile phones were also seized, containing evidence of calls and messages exchanged with their relatives in Bangladesh," the SSP said.
The police have registered a case against the 12 arrested individuals under relevant legal sections. Further legal proceedings in the matter are being undertaken by the police.
"A case has been registered against them under relevant legal sections," Bansal added.
