title: Gang War Or 'Act Of Revenge'? 4 Shot Dead During Dinner At Haryana Eatery
description: The incident took place barely 50 steps from the Kharawar police post, raising serious questions about the law-and-order situation in the region.
author: Gurpreet Singh Chhina, Mukesh Singh Sengar
content:
Four young men were shot dead in a suspected gang-related attack at Milan Dhaba in Haryana's Rohtak district late Wednesday night by five armed assailants who allegedly arrived in a car and opened indiscriminate fire.
The incident took place barely 50 steps from the Kharawar police post, raising serious questions about the law-and-order situation in the region.
According to preliminary information, five armed men arrived at the dhaba in a Swift car at around 12.30 am and opened fire on a group of youths who were having dinner. The sudden burst of gunfire triggered panic among customers and staff, with people scrambling for cover and hiding behind tables and chairs to save their lives.
Three of them were killed on the spot while they were sitting at the dining table. The fourth victim reportedly managed to escape the initial attack and ran outside. However, the assailants chased him and shot him dead too.
Another man, identified as Sunny Ritoli, managed to escape the shooters.
The attackers allegedly continued to roam around the spot for several minutes, openly brandishing their weapons before fleeing in their vehicle.
The victims are reportedly from Jhajjar district, with three belonging to Deeghal village and the fourth from the Beri area.
Rohtak Range IG Hamid Akhtar reached the crime scene around midnight, while SP Gaurav Rajpurohit and other senior district police officials also rushed to the spot. Teams from the CIA, Special Cell and Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) were deployed to collect evidence and examine the crime scene.
A post shared from an Instagram account 'rohitbajrang07' claimed responsibility for the murder in the name of the Bhau Ritolia gang. Describing the murder as an "act of revenge", the post warned of further incidents, writing, "Let's see who's next."
The post also tagged several other individuals, asking them to respond.
However, the authenticity of the post could not be verified.
According to sources, the Himanshu Bhau gang members wanted to kill Sunny - who escaped the scene.
Investigators are probing a possible connection with the rivalry between the Bhau and Sunny Ritolia gangs. However, the motive behind the attack has not yet been officially established.
"We have registered an FIR (first information report), and the identification process is underway. Whether this is a gang war or not is a matter of investigation. We have deployed several teams to investigate the case and hope to find some important clues soon," Deputy Superintendent of Police Rishikant told the media.
Police are also reviewing footage from nearby CCTV cameras and have deployed multiple teams to trace and arrest the assailants.

title: 'Are we your servants?' Congress MP Imran Masood continues tirade against ally SP over seat-sharing
description: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood on Thursday questioned ally Samajwadi Party's approach to seat-sharing for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly
author: Abhishek Mishra
content:
Congress MP Masood continues to take aim at SP over seat-sharing
NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood on Thursday questioned ally Samajwadi Party's approach to seat-sharing for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, saying there was little meaning in holding alliance talks if SP went ahead and announced candidates before finalising the arrangement.His remarks came a day after the Akhilesh Yadav-led party announced five candidates while discussions over seat-sharing with the Congress were still under way."It is no alliance if one partner 'leaves' seats for the other after announcing its candidates," Masood said, questioning whether the two parties were being treated as equal partners. He also asserted that he would remain with the Congress and said his party was not there to do the SP's bidding."What else should I say? You (SP) release the list. Then you leave the seats. Are we alliance partners or your servants? Did we ask you to leave these seats for us? We had discussed the matter, and now an order has been issued that we should not speak about those discussions," he said.Masood, who was part of the seat-sharing discussions, said the exercise made little sense if the SP was going to announce its candidates unilaterally.
He declined to comment on the SP's manifesto, scheduled to be released later in the day, saying the functioning of an alliance should involve joint announcements and press conferences."It is their decision. How can I comment on it? The meaning of an alliance is that there should be joint press conferences and everything should be joint. If something else is happening here, I do not know about it," he said.The Congress MP from Saharanpur also recalled that his party had contested 107 seats when Akhilesh Yadav was the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, adding, "Now, he is yet to become the chief minister."Separately, Masood criticised the denial of permission for the Congress's Samvidhaan Raksha March, questioning the authorities' decision."What can I say? The Constitution that gives you power is the same Constitution that you want to trample upon," he said.
Asked why permission was granted to a conference organised by AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi and Bhim Army chief Chandra Shekhar Azad, he said, "That is precisely the irony. This is the game, and people should understand it… People can draw their own conclusions."Saharanpur MP Imran Masood has continued to express his displeasure with INDIA bloc ally Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing arrangements for poll-bound UP.Masood stepped up his criticism after the Akhilesh's party announced its first list of candidates.Questioning the SP's decision to offer the Congress only 26 "winnable" seats, Masood asked earlier, "Are we beggars?" and objected to the ally's "unilateral" approach to the negotiations.
Abhishek Mishra is a Digital Content Producer at The Times of India, working with the news desk. He writes with a keen eye on foreign policy, defence developments, and the shifting currents of geopolitics-and yes, Indian politics always finds a way onto his radar too.

title: Supreme Court rules PMLA Adjudicating Authority cannot confirm ED property attachment without judicial member
description: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has ruled that the Adjudicating Authority under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) cannot confirm provisional
author: Ayush Pandey
content:
NEW DELHI: The 
Supreme Court
 has ruled that the Adjudicating Authority under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) cannot confirm provisional property attachment orders issued by the 
Enforcement Directorate
 (ED) without the presence of a judicial member.
The ruling concerns the composition and functioning of the adjudicating authority, which examines whether properties provisionally attached by the ED are linked to money laundering under Section 8 of the PMLA.
The matter involved a legal challenge to the practice of single-member benches, particularly those without judicial expertise, confirming attachment orders.

title: Church on ‘government land’ vandalised in Odisha village, peace committee formed
description: Villagers vandalise a church on alleged government land in Odisha; peace committee formed as police investigate.
author: PTI
content:
Residents of a village in Odisha's Koraput district protested against the construction of a church-cum-prayer hall allegedly on government land and vandalised the structure, prompting the local administration to form a peace committee to maintain communal harmony in the area, police said on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
The incident occurred at Patraguda village under the Kotpad block, where tribal people objected to the construction of the church, following which a district administration team visited the site and issued a show-cause notice to the man who had built the structure, a senior officer said.
ALSO READ | Christians increasingly under attack in Odisha, claim activists
The incident came to light after Durjyadhan Harijan, belonging to the only Christian family in the tribal village, lodged a police complaint on November 21, alleging that a group of locals had vandalised the Beersheba Pentecostal Church.
The villagers were also accused of damaging the cross and parts of the prayer hall, the officer said.
"The villagers alleged that the church was established on government land which was meant for community use and not for one family. The person had failed to produce any land documents to establish his ownership of the site. He demolished the structure as he failed to reply to the show-cause notice," Kotpad Tehsildar Parsuram Bhatra said.
A peace committee had been formed, and a meeting was held in the presence of senior police officers and villagers to maintain communal harmony, he said.
ALSO READ | Church vandalised in Odisha over allegations of sexual assault
"I have also asked the revenue inspector concerned to submit a status report on the plot and the demolished structure. Further action will be taken based on the report," Mr. Bhatra said.
The police registered a case against seven people named in Mr. Harijan's complaint, the officer said.
Kotpad Inspector-In-Charge Runu Majhi said the case was under investigation and no arrest had been made so far.
Mr. Bhatra said the only Christian family in the 250-household village has six members.
Mr. Harijan, however, claimed that the plot belongs to his father and that the structure had been built for his family to hold church services every Sunday.
The man also alleged that some villagers had opposed the construction of the church, and accused his family of being involved in religious conversions, a charge he denied.

title: CM Vijay inaugurates 148 houses for Sri Lankan Tamils in Krishnagiri rehabilitation camp

author: The Hindu Bureau
content:

title: Amid rising costs, Keralam’s aided primary school headteachers seek higher fund allocation for noon meal scheme
description: Headteachers in Kerala’s aided primary schools demand higher noon meal funds amid rising costs of eggs, milk, vegetables, and LPG.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Headteachers of aided primary schools in Keralam are concerned that the noon meal scheme is becoming a financial burden on them amid rising prices of essential commodities, particularly eggs and milk.
N.C. Abdullakutty, State president, and M.I. Ajikumar, general secretary, Kerala Private Primary Headmasters’ Association, say the government allocates ₹6.78 per student in the lower primary (LP) sections (Classes 1 to 4) and ₹10.17 per student in the upper primary (UP) sections (Classes 5 to 8). Additionally, as per a supplementary nutrition programme, the schools are required to distribute one egg a day, and 150 ml of milk on two other days, every week.
The sanctioned rates are ₹6 per egg and ₹52 per litre of milk. In the open market, however, the price ranges from ₹8 to ₹10 per egg, while milk costs between ₹65 and ₹70 a litre if it is procured from milk cooperative societies, and ₹60 a litre through Milma. Though the price of eggs has come down a bit in recent days, this situation may not continue for long, the teachers say.
Mr. Abdullakutty points out that if the price of Milma milk is raised by ₹10 a litre, the noon meal scheme would have to be implemented while incurring a loss of ₹18 to ₹25 a litre.
High gas prices
The headteachers also claim that the price rise of other commodities such as vegetables and groceries and the frequent hikes in LPG cylinder refills are also burning a hole in their pockets. The price of non-domestic cooking gas has doubled compared with last year. A 19-kg non-domestic LPG cylinder now costs around ₹2,870, which can last up to two weeks.
For LP schools with fewer than 100 students, the allocated funds are insufficient to cover even the cost of the monthly gas cylinder refill, let alone vegetables and groceries, they say. Most often, the headteachers are forced to carry on the financial burden on their own. Some of them are now depending on sponsorships and financial help from the PTA.
“The above-mentioned rates were fixed around five-six years ago. We are demanding that the government increase the funds for the noon meal scheme. The allowance for eggs should be adjusted to reflect the current market rates and the allocation for milk be raised to ₹60 a litre. Also, the availability of LPG cylinders should be guaranteed,” Mr. Abdullakutty says.
The association has also urged the government to implement a community kitchen system, similar to those in some neighbouring States, and to relieve headteachers of the responsibilities associated with the scheme.

title: Jealous of 27-year-old being invited to Oxford: Dipke on Saurav Das travel row
description: Dipke hit out at the government over the Saurav Das travel row saying the Centre stopped the 27-year-old from visiting Oxford and LSE out of quotjealousyquot over his international recognition and accused the government of trying to silence dissent
author: India Today News Desk
content:
Jealous of 27-year-old being invited to Oxford: Dipke on Saurav Das travel row
Dipke hit out at the government over the Saurav Das travel row, saying the Centre stopped the 27-year-old from visiting Oxford and LSE out of "jealousy" over his international recognition and accused the government of trying to silence dissent.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday said that co-convenor Saurav Das was prevented from travelling to the London School of Economics and Oxford University because the government was “jealous” that the 27-year-old had been invited to the institutions, the Press Trust of India reported.
Das approached the Delhi High Court on Wednesday after he was stopped from flying to the United Kingdom for an event at Oxford University, where he was scheduled to speak on the “cockroach movement”.
The Ministry of External Affairs later said he had been issued a notice asking him to explain discrepancies in the place of birth recorded on his passport, following inputs from the relevant authorities.
Speaking to the media after visiting Deekshabhoomi ahead of the party's “Save Democracy, Save Constitution” rally in Nagpur, Dipke said he, Das and co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka had received invitations and decided that Das would travel to the UK.
“We had decided that Ashutosh and I would travel across Maharashtra because there is a drought in the state, and we wanted to visit the affected areas. We had decided that Saurav Das would go to the London School of Economics and Oxford. But when he went to the airport, he was stopped,” Dipke said, according to PTI.
“I think there is some insecurity somewhere I think there is someone in our country who feels that only he should go on a world tour. Perhaps they felt a little jealous that a 27-year-old was being invited to Oxford University,” he said.
Dipke said that some people were jealous because they were not being invited anywhere and were perhaps wondering how Das was receiving so much international recognition.
He said the Jantar Mantar movement, which brought the CJP into the mainstream, had succeeded by following the path shown by Babasaheb Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi.
“But there are some big narcissists in our country who think that not just the country, but the entire world should revolve around them, and that only they should go on world tours,” Dipke said.
Asked about his allegations that CJP leaders were being pressured, Dipke said the government's approach was to find ways to “crush the voices against it”. He said the government could take such action but should remember that although it held power, the Constitution given to the country by Babasaheb Ambedkar was on their side.
“The Constitution is on our side. Power may be yours, but the Constitution is ours. The Constitution belongs to 140 crore people. Whenever a tyrant in power tries to snatch away people's rights, it is this very Constitution of Dr Babasaheb that will protect them, just as it has protected us,” he said.
Dipke said that Ranka had been kept in Tihar Jail for eight days for waving the Tricolour, while he himself had been detained for a day.
“But today, Babasaheb's Constitution has saved us. It is therefore very important for us to protect the Constitution to safeguard every citizen's rights and freedom. If the Constitution does not remain, India will not remain,” he said.

title: Best response was Op Sindoor: IAF chief on India's post-26/11 shift
description: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit described Operation Sindoor as India039s strongest response to terrorism since the Mumbai attacks He underscored the country039s tougher position on cross-border terrorism and its increased deterrence
author: India Today News Desk
content:
Best response was Op Sindoor: IAF chief on India's post-26/11 shift
Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit described Operation Sindoor as India's strongest response to terrorism since the Mumbai attacks. He underscored the country's tougher position on cross-border terrorism and its increased deterrence.
India could not deliver a befitting response when terrorists struck Mumbai on November 26, 2008, but that has changed since, with Operation Sindoor being the strongest example, Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit said on Thursday.
Speaking on the 18th anniversary of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, the Indian Air Force chief said India had since developed the capability and resolve to respond decisively to terror attacks.
"It happened in 2008, and we could not give a response. But after that, whatever events like this have happened, we have been able to give a befitting response. The best response you have seen was in Operation Sindoor, which is still ongoing," Dixit said.
Operation Sindoor was launched on May 7 last year following the killing of 26 civilians by terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam in April. India struck terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, triggering a three-day war between the two countries.
Shortly after the hostilities ceased, Prime Minister Narendra Modi defined a "new normal" where India will "strike precisely and decisively" without tolerating any nuclear blackmail.
ON INCREASED DETERRENCE
Addressing a guest lecture hosted by the University of Mumbai, Dixit also paid tribute to the victims of the 26/11 attacks and those who fought the terrorists.
"Today is 26th November. It is a day no Indian can forget. 18 years ago today, terrorists attacked the city. 166 innocent people lost their lives. Our police, our NSG commandos, our security personnel, and many ordinary citizens confronted the attackers with great courage. Several of them made the supreme sacrifice," he said.
"I pay homage to every life we lost. And to every brave heart who laid down his life protecting Mumbai and the nation. I also remember their families who have carried that loss with quiet dignity for 18 years," he added.
Dixit, who took charge as the IAF chief on October 31, also referred to the government's tougher position on cross-border terrorism, citing PM Modi's assertion that "terror and talks will not go together, water and blood will not flow together, and the differentiation between a terrorist and his supporter will no longer be there".
"It's a very great thing, and we are all prepared to do this. So, hopefully, the amount of deterrence which we have now created, such events should not happen at all," he said.

title: A railway announcer's voice cut through gunfire to save lives during 26/11 attack
description: Station announcer Bablu Kumar Deepak had been in the job for barely a year when terrorists stormed the busy railway station 18 years ago Fearing for his life he continued making announcements urging passengers to evacuate even as the attack unfolded
author: India Today News Desk
content:
A railway announcer's voice cut through gunfire to save lives during 26/11 attack
Station announcer Bablu Kumar Deepak had been in the job for barely a year when terrorists stormed the busy railway station 18 years ago. Fearing for his life, he continued making announcements, urging passengers to evacuate even as the attack unfolded.
A last-minute shift change placed railway announcer Bablu Kumar Deepak behind a microphone at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus during the 26/11 terror attacks, turning his voice into a lifeline for hundreds of trapped commuters, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
Deepak, now 51, was barely a year into his role as an announcer when terrorists attacked the busy railway station 18 years ago. He continued warning passengers to leave the station even as he feared he might not survive.
A native of Bihar's Munger district, Deepak had joined the Railways as a bungalow peon 11 years before the attack. On November 26, he reported for his routine morning shift at Byculla station at 7 am but was asked by the control room to cover the evening shift at CST. He eventually remained on duty for 27 hours.
"At that moment, I felt that today could be my last day," Deepak told PTI ahead of the 18th anniversary of the attacks. He said the memories had not faded despite the passage of nearly two decades.
"Even now, whenever someone starts talking about it, those same scenes start playing in my mind. My body begins to tremble. It was such a terrifying sight that it cannot be erased," he said.
At around 8.45 pm, Deepak noticed thick smoke near platforms 12 and 13 and heard continuous gunfire and loud, blast-like sounds. The Hyderabad-bound Hussain Sagar Express had just departed, while the Indrayani Express from Pune had arrived around that time.
Through the public address system, he warned passengers that firing was taking place in the platform hall and urged them to use the exit at the rear of the station.
"I thought I had the public address system and could alert people through announcements. Many passengers were buying tickets near the booking counters, while others were having tea and snacks. At least they could hear the announcements, become alert and move outside, which could save their lives," he told PTI.
Terrorists Ismail Khan, also known as Abu Ismail, and Ajmal Amir Kasab fired indiscriminately at people trying to escape. Deepak said the firing in the main-line section continued for about five to six minutes.
From his cabin above the station master's office on the first floor, Deepak could see smoke, the attack unfolding and people lying in pools of blood. He contacted Vishnu Zende, the announcer in the suburban section, and Vishwas Bhatt, an announcer in the railway control room, to tell them that terrorists appeared to have entered the station.
"I called Zende first and then informed Vishwas Bhatt in the control room. Bhatt even recorded in his diary the exact time when I called him and informed him about the incident," Deepak said.
As the firing continued, Zende also made announcements asking passengers to leave through the rear end of Platform No. 1, which he believed was relatively safe at the time.
The announcements helped save hundreds of commuters at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, PTI reported. Of the 166 people killed in the 26/11 attacks, 52 died at the railway station and 108 were injured in the firing there.
"I felt that everyone should always remain alert," said Zende, who has been working as a train manager, or guard, with Central Railway since 2014.
Deepak recalled seeing children and adults lying injured in the station's central hall, with blood splattered around. He also saw one of the terrorists stop near an ATM close to Platform No. 8 to reload his weapon before moving towards the suburban section while firing.
His work continued even after the firing stopped. As passengers struggled to locate their relatives, the main-line announcement system was used throughout the night to help reunite families.
"We were making announcements one by one, asking passengers whose names were being called to come near the station master's cabin," he said.
Deepak continued working until 10 am the next day, after having begun his duty at Byculla at 7 am on November 26.
He later approached a senior divisional commercial manager and received a Chief Commercial Manager's award, comprising a certificate and Rs 500.
Asked whether he felt overlooked when another announcer received greater recognition for the announcements made during the attack, Deepak said he had been new to the job and had eventually accepted what happened.
"Whatever was in my destiny, I got. It does hurt for some time, but eventually one lets it go. Whatever was written in my fate happened," he said.
Nearly two decades later, Deepak remains conscious that he survived the ordeal. Recalling the warnings that helped passengers escape and the long hours spent reuniting families, he said: "Whatever happened, the big thing is that I survived, thanks to everyone's blessings."

title: Sundarbans sees simultaneous erosion and land accretion, Ghoramara loses 55% of land in 50 yrs: Panel
description: A joint committee told the NGT that Ghoramara island lost 55.4% of its land between 1969 and 2019, while new sedimentary landforms emerged elsewhere in the Sundarbans. | India News
author: Jasjeev Gandhiok
content:
Jasjeev Gandhiok is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times, where he covers environment, climate change, the clean energy transition and wildlife at the National Bureau. Gandhiok has over a decade of experience in journalism and is based in Delhi. He has reported extensively on Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR). This includes the region's air pollution woes, a polluted Yamuna and on urban wildlife still thriving in the region. He joined HT in October 2021. Prior to that, he had five-year stint at The Times of India in Delhi, where he also covered Delhi, with a focus on environment and wildlife. Gandhiok has covered some recent events around the Capital too, ranging from the farmers' protests, the northeast Delhi riots and the CAA-NRC protests, reporting from the ground on all of these. He also travels across the country to report on how environment and climate change impact everyday life, while also writing on endangered species. His reports in 2019 on toxic leachate from Delhi's landfills led to the National Green Tribunal (NGT) taking suo motu cognisance and ultimately asking the state government to start bio-mining to flatten and remove all three landfills in the capital. He also closely tracks the implementation of government policies on climate, renewable energy and environmental protection. His focus remains on impactful, public-interest journalism which explains how environmental decisions affect people's everyday lives.
Sundarbans sees simultaneous erosion and land accretion, Ghoramara loses 55% of land in 50 yrs: Panel
A joint committee told the NGT that Ghoramara island lost 55.4% of its land between 1969 and 2019, while new sedimentary landforms emerged elsewhere in the Sundarbans.
The Sundarbans is not simply losing land to the sea: while some islands are shrinking, new sedimentary landforms are emerging elsewhere in the estuarine landscape. A joint committee examining coastal erosion has found that Ghoramara island in West Bengal lost 55.4% of its mapped area between 1969 and 2019, but has cautioned against trying to hold back the sea with hard-engineering structures along its entire shoreline. Instead, it has recommended targeted protection for vulnerable settlements and infrastructure, alongside mangrove conservation.
The report, dated November 25, was submitted by the Union environment ministry to the National Green Tribunal (NGT), which had taken suo motu cognisance of a news report in August last year highlighting the shrinking landmass of Ghoramara island.
In an order dated February 17, 2026, the tribunal constituted a joint committee comprising the deputy director general of forests (Central), representing the environment ministry’s regional office in Bhubaneswar, and the principal chief conservator of forests, West Bengal, to examine coastal erosion in the Sundarbans and prepare a comprehensive plan for mangrove protection and coastal erosion management. The environment ministry’s regional office in Bhubaneswar was designated as the coordinating agency. HT has seen the report.
“The available evidence establishes substantial historical and spatial changes in Ghoramara Island and the surrounding estuarine landscape, involving erosion, sediment deposition, channel migration and landform development,” the report said.
It said erosion at Ghoramara was occurring alongside accretion and the formation or expansion of landforms elsewhere in the estuarine system. “Shoreline change is therefore spatially variable and influenced by the evolving configuration of channels, sedimentary landforms and hydrodynamic conditions.”
The committee cited Geological Survey of India (GSI) data showing that Ghoramara’s area declined from 8.59 sq km in 1969 to 3.83 sq km in 2019.
A separate assessment by the National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (NCSCM), also cited in the report, found that the island’s mapped area contracted from 458.23 hectares in 2011 to 326.25 hectares in 2026, a reduction of nearly 29%.
The NCSCM assessment also classified 93% of the island’s shoreline as experiencing high erosion during the pre-monsoon period, with the figure rising to 95% post-monsoon. The shoreline perimeter shrank by nearly 25% over 36 years, from 10.09 km in 1990 to 7.53 km in 2026.
The committee said the available studies did not establish the relative contribution of individual processes, including tidal currents, sediment transport, cyclones, storm surges, sea-level rise and possible land subsidence, to erosion along specific stretches. It also found no evidence to attribute the island’s erosion to any single human intervention.
The report noted that the West Bengal forest department had said earlier paved and bank-protection structures had not yielded the desired results in controlling erosion. The state’s irrigation and waterways department had reported protection, restoration and strengthening works covering 12.24 km, at an expenditure of ₹6.25 crore.
“The management approach should focus on reducing risks to settlements, essential infrastructure, agricultural areas and other vulnerable assets, rather than attempting to arrest the natural evolution of the entire island,” the committee said.
It recommended maintaining and strengthening existing embankments wherever necessary, undertaking localised protection measures at critical erosion-prone locations and conserving existing mangroves. It also cautioned against indiscriminate mangrove plantation along actively eroding banks, saying plantations should be undertaken only at suitable locations.
The report further recommended setting up a state-level coordination committee, with the West Bengal Coastal Zone Management Authority as the nodal agency, to oversee the implementation of the proposed measures.

title: 2008 murder case: CBI facilitates deportation of wanted accused from UAE
description: Based on the pending Red Corner Notice (RCN) against the accused, the UAE authorities recently placed him under arrest after geo-locating him there and alerted the Indian authorities | India News
author: HT Correspondent
content:
2008 murder case: CBI facilitates deportation of wanted accused from UAE
Based on the pending Red Corner Notice (RCN) against the accused, the UAE authorities recently placed him under arrest after geo-locating him there and alerted the Indian authorities
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has completed the deportation formalities of a man wanted in a 2008 murder case from the United Arab Emirates (UAE), based on a pending Interpol Red Corner Notice (RCN ) against him.
The accused, Sujith Kumar, was wanted by the Kerala police in a murder case registered in October 2008.
Based on the pending RCN against the accused, the UAE authorities recently placed him under arrest after geo-locating him there and alerted the Indian authorities.
Following due process, the UAE authorities approved Kumar’s deportation to India, to face trial in the case, CBI officials said on Thursday.
With assistance from the CBI, a Kerala police team went to the UAE a few days ago, where the accused was handed over to them. The Kerala police team brought the accused to Cochin, Kerala, on Wednesday.
The CBI, as Interpol’s nodal agency in India, coordinated the deportation with the ministry of external affairs, the ministry of home affairs and the Kerala police.
Also Read: Police arrest man deported from Dubai over alleged China-linked fraud racket at Mumbai airport
The accused was allegedly actively involved in the October 2008 murder, which took place due to previous enmity, according to the Kerala police. In the incident, Kumar, along with other co-accused persons, allegedly formed an unlawful assembly, armed with deadly weapons, to ambush the victim.
It was alleged that the accused persons attacked the victim while he was engaged in a conversation with the case’s complainant on the side of a street. The assailants inflicted grievous injuries on the victim who subsequently died while undergoing treatment at a hospital the same day. Kumar, who is among the accused chargesheeted in the case, absconded, however.
At the request of the Kerala Police, the CBI facilitated the issuance of an RCN against Kumar by Interpol, which eventually led to his return to India. The CBI coordinates with law enforcement agencies across the country to facilitate international police cooperation.

title: Who qualifies as a journalist? SC to ponder question of protection for scribes
description: Who qualifies as a journalist? SC to ponder question of protection for scribes | India News
author: PTI
content:
Who qualifies as a journalist? SC to ponder question of protection for scribes
New Delhi, The Supreme Court on Thursday said it will consider who qualifies to be a journalist and whether accredited media persons should enjoy greater protection than self-proclaimed reporters while covering protests.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that journalistic freedom has to be balanced with the administration of public order and law.
The top court relegated to the high-powered committee headed by former top court judge R Subhash Reddy to examine pleas over the alleged detention of seven journalists, assault, and obstruction of journalists covering protests in Delhi on 10 and 11 October 2026.
It asked the petitioners to submit material before the five-member committee.
"You will go back to the committee which we have constituted to factually demonstrate whether your petitioners were, in fact, present there. If present, whether they were subjected to excessive force.
"Whether they were subjected to force and, if subjected, whether such force was excessive in relation to the proportion necessary for maintenance of public order," Justice Bagchi observed.
Self-proclaimed journalists may not have the same protection as accredited journalists, he then added.
The Kerala Union of Working Journalists and the Delhi Union of Journalists, in their plea, submitted that journalists were forcibly removed from reporting sites, prevented from recording events, and subjected to physical force.
According to the plea, accredited journalists documenting the protests were restrained, dragged away, manhandled and detained despite displaying their press credentials.
Senior advocate PV Dinesh said seven journalists working with established organisations, not reel-makers, were taken into custody.
"The question is, when established journalists, who are recognised journalists, are covering events, can they be taken into custody?" the lawyer submitted.
The Delhi Police earlier told the top court that social media "reel-makers" and influencers cannot claim the same protections as journalists covering protests.
In an affidavit, the city police submitted that journalists "constitute a distinct category" from social media content creators who use cameras and microphones to make reels for commercial gain, arguing that the latter cannot automatically claim the protections afforded to the press while covering protests.

title: Hyderabad Gets Its First Apple Store: Check Location, Opening Date And What Customers Can Expect
description: Apple is bringing its own retail experience to Hyderabad, expanding to six Indian cities. The new store also has a design inspired by the city's pearl heritage
category: Bengaluru, Cities, Hyderabad, India, Mumbai, New Delhi, Noida, Pune
author: Parishmita Saikia
content:
Hyderabad Gets Its First Apple Store: Check Location, Opening Date And What Customers Can Expect
Apple is bringing its own retail experience to Hyderabad, expanding to six Indian cities. The new store also has a design inspired by the city's pearl heritage
Got Question about the News?
HYDERABAD: Apple is expanding its retail presence in India with the launch of its first company-owned store in Hyderabad. Named Apple Kukatpally, the outlet will open at Lake Shore-Y Junction Mall in the city’s Kukatpally area on December 10 at 5 pm.
The opening will take Apple’s physical retail network in India to seven stores across six cities. Hyderabad will become the sixth city to get an Apple-owned store, joining Mumbai, New Delhi, Noida, Bengaluru and Pune.
- Apple Kukatpally: The First Apple Store In Hyderabad Is Opening On December 10- Location, Opening Time And More
- Thanksgiving Menus Across Restaurants In Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi And Hyderabad
- BGMI Air Beta Goes Live In India: Download Details, Supported Devices And Launch Date
- Youth Congress Workers Vandalise Meta's Hyderabad Office Over Suspended Accounts | Video
Ahead of the launch, Apple has unveiled the store’s barricade design, featuring a pearl-inspired Apple logo set against iridescent colours. The design draws on Hyderabad’s identity as the ‘City of Pearls’ and its long association with the processing and refining of pearls sourced from around the world.
@Apple to open its 7th official retail store (Apple Kukatpally) in Hyderabad, Telangana, India on December 10th.Location of the Store: LG-08, Lake Shore Mall – Y JunctionKukatpally, Hyderabad, TG.
@johnternus @tim_cook https://t.co/KPNVWRWZzC
— Kunal Kulkarni (@Kunalk_1380) November 26, 2026
Where Are Apple’s Seven Stores In India?
Apple began its physical retail operations in India in April 2023, opening its first two stores – Apple BKC in Mumbai and Apple Saket in New Delhi.
It has since expanded its network with five more outlets, including the upcoming Hyderabad store. Its existing stores are:
- Mumbai: Apple BKC at Jio World Drive, Bandra-Kurla Complex, and Apple Borivali at Sky City Mall.
- New Delhi: Apple Saket at Select CITYWALK.
- Noida: Apple Noida at DLF Mall of India.
- Bengaluru: Apple Hebbal at Phoenix Mall of Asia.
- Pune: Apple Koregaon Park at The KOPA.
- Hyderabad: Apple Kukatpally at Lake Shore-Y Junction Mall, opening on December 10.
The expansion marks a steady increase in Apple’s direct retail footprint in India. The company opened its first two stores in 2023, added outlets in Bengaluru and Pune in September 2025, followed by Noida in December 2025 and Borivali in Mumbai in 2026.
What Will Customers Get At Apple Kukatpally?
The new store will allow customers to explore Apple’s product range, including its latest iPhones, MacBook Pro and other devices. They will also be able to seek assistance from Apple Specialists and technical experts, as well as dedicated teams for business customers.
Apple plans to offer its Today At Apple programme at the store. These sessions will include guidance on using Apple devices and workshops covering photography, video creation and drawing.
The company has also released exclusive Apple Kukatpally wallpapers and digital stickers for customers. An Apple Music playlist inspired by the sounds of Hyderabad has been created to mark the opening.
Why Is Hyderabad’s First Apple Store Significant?
The opening gives Apple a direct retail presence in one of India’s major technology and business hubs. Until now, customers in Hyderabad could buy Apple products through online channels and authorised resellers, but the city did not have an Apple-owned retail outlet.
The development is also significant because Hyderabad already plays an important role in Apple’s operations in India. The city is home to the company’s Research and Development and Retail Customer Care teams. The new store will add a direct customer-facing retail operation to that existing presence.
For customers, an official Apple store means access to the company’s product range, in-person guidance, technical assistance and learning sessions under one roof. For Apple, it provides another channel to build relationships with customers in a market where it has been steadily expanding its retail network.
Quick Answers
Apple Kukatpally is scheduled to open on December 10 at 5 pm at the Lake Shore-Y Junction Mall in the Kukatpally area of Hyderabad.

title: Bomb Threat Targets Amitabh Bachchan's 'Jalsa' Residence, Mumbai Mayor's Office
description: Bollywood veteran actor Amitabh Bachchan and Mumbai mayor's office on Thursday received bomb threats.
author: Shankhyaneel Sarkar
content:
Bomb Threat Targets Amitabh Bachchan's 'Jalsa' Residence, Mumbai Mayor's Office
Bollywood veteran actor Amitabh Bachchan and Mumbai mayor's office on Thursday received bomb threats.
Got Question about the News?
Bollywood veteran Amitabh Bachchan and the Mumbai mayor’s office received bomb threats on Thursday. A threat was also issued against singer Diljit Dosanjh’s concert in the city. According to CNN-News18, Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde and Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) Commissioner Ashwini Bhide had received bomb threats.
The Acharya Metro station also received a bomb threat.
- Mumbai Mayor’s Office Receives Bomb Threat Email, Security Alert Issued Across City | News18
- Diljit Dosanjh Faces Fresh Song Curbs! Ahmedabad Child Panel Seeks Police Action Ahead Of Concert

- Diljit Dosanjh Reacts To 'Tu Bahar Se Aaya Hai' Remark At Ahmedabad Concert: 'Honolulu Mein Thodi Paida Hua'
The threats come as Mumbai marks the 18th anniversary of the 26/11 terror attacks, one of the deadliest terrorist attacks on the city and the country, on Wednesday.
Fadnavis on Thursday described the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks as an assault on the Constitution, asserting that India would not tolerate attacks on its soldiers or citizens and would strike back against those responsible.
Speaking at a programme at the Gateway of India commemorating the martyrs of the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, Fadnavis said the terrorists had deliberately selected locations frequented by foreign nationals and members of the diplomatic community to cause maximum casualties and send a message to the world that India could be attacked.
The attack was not merely on Mumbai but also on the Constitution of India, he said.
Recalling the bravery of police personnel who fought the terrorists, Fadnavis paid tribute to officers who lost their lives, particularly Tukaram Omble, who captured Pakistani terrorist Ajmal Kasab despite being shot multiple times.
“Kasab had a gun, while Omble had only a lathi. Despite being shot, he managed to capture Kasab," the chief minister said.
He also paid tribute to senior police officers Hemant Karkare, Ashok Kamte and Vijay Salaskar, as well as NSG Major Sandeep Unnikrishnan, who were killed while fighting the terrorists.

title: Months After Flash Floods, Nepal Begins Process To Declare 213 Missing Indians Dead
description: Nepal has begun the process to declare 213 missing Indian nationals dead following devastating floods, with the Indian Embassy inviting objections until December 2
author: Meemansa Shekhawat, News Desk
content:
Months After Flash Floods, Nepal Begins Process To Declare 213 Missing Indians Dead
Nepal has begun the process to declare 213 missing Indian nationals dead following devastating floods, with the Indian Embassy inviting objections until December 2
Months after floods in Nepal that caused massive destruction, the Nepalese government has begun the process of presumption and declaration of death for 213 Indian nationals who have been missing since August this year, according to the Indian Embassy in Nepal.
The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) has released a list of the 213 missing Indian nationals for presumption and declaration of death on its website, the Embassy said in a press release on Wednesday, November 25, alongside inviting objections for additions, deletions or amendments in the details.
If the family members of persons who are missing or have any concerns, they can get in touch with the Indian Embassy before December 2, said the release. They could contact via the given email address eoikathmandufloodsupport@gmail.com or mobile phone number +9779851316807.
Once the process of seeking comments or amendments is complete, the Nepalese government will finalised the list and formally issue the declaration of death. The Embassy will then start obtaining death certificates for these individuals from authorities in Nepal.
Nepal Flash Floods
The flash floods that struck Nepal on August 23 were the country’s worst natural disaster in recent years. The flooding that took place in the Trishuli-Bhote Koshi river system killed at least 1,453 people, leaving more than 5,000 missing, according to the NDRRMA.
An ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border triggered flash floods that wreaked havoc on towns and villages in northern and central Nepal.
With inputs from PTI
Quick Answers
Family members with concerns can contact the Indian Embassy in Nepal by emailing eoikathmandufloodsupport@gmail.com or calling the mobile phone number +9779851316807 before December 2.

title: 14,928 two-wheelers, just 23 cars: Flex fuel registrations rise, but passenger vehicles lag
description: Toyota’s ₹19.99 lakh Innova HyCross Flex Hybrid brings a new proposition to India’s ethanol-fuel market. However, with nearly 99.9% of flex fuel vehicle registrations coming from two-wheelers, the passenger vehicle segment continues to lag.
author: Shivani Bazaz
content:
14,928 two-wheelers, just 23 cars: Flex fuel registrations rise, but passenger vehicles lag
- Edited byVivek Dubey
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 14:12 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 14:12 IST
Commuter motorcycles are driving the vast majority of early flex fuel adoption due to minimal price gaps, while passenger cars lag behind amid higher upfront costs and scarce high-blend fuel infrastructure. Find out whet
India’s flex fuel vehicle market may be expanding, but early adoption remains far from balanced. Vahan data shared with CNBC-TV18 shows 14,951 flex fuel vehicle registrations so far, of which 14,928 are two-wheelers and just 23 are light motor vehicles.
In percentage terms, two-wheelers account for 99.85% of registrations, while light motor vehicles contribute only 0.15%. The figures underline how flex fuel technology has so far found greater acceptance among affordable commuter motorcycles than passenger cars.
The category began taking shape in June, when Hero MotoCorp unveiled flex fuel versions of the Splendor+ and HF Deluxe on June 3, followed by Maruti Suzuki’s Wagon R Bioflex. Hero’s motorcycles are compatible with ethanol-petrol blends ranging from E20 to E85, bringing the technology to some of India’s most popular commuter models.
The price equation
One of the key reasons behind the difference in adoption could be the upfront cost of switching to flex fuel.
Hero’s HF Deluxe Flex Fuel is priced at ₹72,792, just ₹172 more than the standard model. The Splendor+ Flex Fuel, priced at ₹82,710, carries a premium of around ₹5,153 over its regular petrol counterpart. For buyers in the commuter segment, the additional cost is relatively small.
The price equation is different for passenger vehicles. Maruti Suzuki’s Wagon R Bioflex, based on the top-spec ZXi+ variant, was launched at ₹7.24 lakh, carrying a premium of around ₹85,000 over the comparable petrol version. This represents a substantially higher upfront cost for a technology whose long-term savings may not yet be clear to consumers.
Toyota’s bet on flex fuel
Toyota Kirloskar Motor has now entered the passenger vehicle market with the Innova HyCross Flex Hybrid Electric Vehicle, launched on November 25 at a starting price of ₹19.99 lakh.
The vehicle combines a locally manufactured 2.0-litre flex fuel engine with Toyota’s fifth-generation strong hybrid system. It can run on ethanol-petrol blends ranging from E20 to E85, while retaining the convenience of a self-charging hybrid powertrain. Toyota says the new model combines fuel flexibility with electrification, while supporting localisation and India’s energy security goals.
The entry-level flex hybrid is priced just ₹40,000 above the regular petrol HyCross's entry price of ₹19.59 lakh. However, this is not a direct like-for-like comparison. The ₹19.99 lakh model is a new G Hybrid grade, while the ₹19.59 lakh vehicle is the GX petrol variant. The flex fuel model also comes with strong hybrid technology.
Toyota’s move is significant because it is not introducing flex fuel as a standalone niche offering. The company has said the HyCross strong hybrid will now be available only in flex hybrid form, making ethanol compatibility an integral part of its hybrid proposition going forward.
The infrastructure challenge
Wider adoption of the technology will depend on more than vehicle prices. While E20 petrol is already part of India's fuel landscape, higher ethanol blends such as E85 are not yet widely available across the country. This could limit the practical benefits of flex fuel capability for consumers looking to use higher ethanol blends.
There are also questions around fuel economy and running costs. Ethanol has a lower energy content than petrol, meaning consumers need to assess whether any potential fuel-price advantage offsets the difference in mileage. For flex fuel technology to move beyond early adopters, buyers will need confidence that it is convenient, affordable and supported by adequate fuel infrastructure.
Toyota’s Innova HyCross Flex Hybrid could therefore become an important test case for the passenger vehicle market. Its strong hybrid system, familiar MPV format and relatively small entry-price gap may help make the technology more attractive to buyers.
However, the real test will be registrations. With just 23 light motor vehicles recorded in the Vahan data so far, India’s flex fuel market has a long way to go before it becomes a meaningful passenger vehicle category.
Toyota has now made its move. Whether flex fuel technology can move beyond commuter motorcycles and find a place in Indian car buyers’ garages will depend on pricing, fuel availability and the economics of running these vehicles.

title: Sunjay Kapur estate dispute: SC mediation fails, family feud heads back to court
description: The Supreme Court-directed mediation in the Sunjay Kapur family estate dispute has failed, with Rani Kapur, Priya Kapur and the interests of Karisma Kapoor's children unable to reach a settlement. The dispute over the RK Family Trust, its valuation and competing claims is now set to return to litigation.
author: Ashmit Kumar
content:
Sunjay Kapur estate dispute: SC mediation fails, family feud heads back to court
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 14:10 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 14:10 IST
The Supreme Court-directed mediation in the Sunjay Kapur family estate dispute has failed, with Rani Kapur, Priya Kapur and the interests of Karisma Kapoor's children unable to reach a settlement. The dispute over the RK Family Trust, its valuation and competing claims is now set to return to litigation.
The Supreme Court-directed mediation in the dispute over late industrialist Sunjay Kapur's family assets has failed, with the parties unable to reach an agreement on the distribution of the estate. The matter is now set to return to litigation, with the apex court noting that the parties have not arrived at a settlement.
The mediation was being conducted under the supervision of former Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud and involved Sunjay Kapur's mother Rani Kapur, his widow Priya Kapur, and the interests of his children from his previous marriage to actor Karisma Kapoor.
The dispute centres on the control and distribution of the RK Family Trust, which holds interests in the Kapur family's business assets, including shares in auto-component maker Sona Comstar.
According to submissions made by Priya Kapur's counsel, the trust corpus is valued at around ₹30,000 crore. Rani Kapur is seeking ₹6,000 crore, representing 20% of the trust corpus, while Priya Kapur is staking a claim to 60% of the assets. The remaining 40%, according to Priya Kapur's position, is meant for Sunjay Kapur's children, although the precise scope of this claim, including whether it covers all his children, remains unclear.
Karisma Kapoor's children have separately staked a claim to 26% of the trust corpus, which they have valued at around ₹60,000 crore. The valuation figures and competing claims underline the significant differences between the parties over the size of the estate and their respective entitlements.
The Supreme Court had referred the dispute to mediation on May 7, appointing former CJI DY Chandrachud to facilitate discussions. The move came after the court encouraged the family members to explore an amicable resolution rather than get drawn into prolonged litigation.
Also read: SC wants an important change in food product labels
In August, the apex court had expressed optimism about the mediation process, noting that six sessions had taken place and that the mediator had interacted with all members of the family. The court had also noted that a senior chartered accountant and a tax expert had assisted in the discussions. It subsequently allowed the mediation to continue until November 2, 2026, while expressing hope that the parties would reach a comprehensive settlement.
The dispute has its roots in the constitution and management of the RK Family Trust. Rani Kapur has challenged the trust, alleging that it was created using forged, fabricated and fraudulent documents, and has sought restoration of the estate to its position before the trust was set up. Priya Kapur, on the other hand, has defended the trust and its structure.
The legal battle also involves questions around Sunjay Kapur's estate and the rights of his children from his marriage to Karisma Kapoor. The dispute has been playing out before the Delhi High Court as well as the Supreme Court.
With mediation failing to produce a settlement, the parties are now set to pursue their claims through the legal process.

title: LOC issued against CJP's Saurav Das, discrepancies in passport: Centre tells Delhi HC
description: The Centre on Thursday informed the Delhi High Court that a Look Out Circular has been issued against CJP coconvener Saurav Das, who was stopped at the airport from travelling to the United Kingdom.
author: PTI
content:
LOC issued against CJP's Saurav Das, discrepancies in passport: Centre tells Delhi HC
- Published OnNov 26, 2026 | 14:04 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 26, 2026 | 14:04 IST
The travel restriction stems from an ongoing inquiry into alleged discrepancies involving passport details and citizenship verification requested by state authorities. While the travel ban prevents his trip to an academi
The Centre on Thursday informed the Delhi High Court that a Look Out Circular has been issued against CJP co-convener Saurav Das, who was stopped at the airport from travelling to the United Kingdom.
The submission was made before Justice Amit Mahajan, who issued notice and sought a response from the Centre on Das’s plea challenging the government’s move to stop him from travelling.
The court listed the matter for further hearing on December 9.
Senior advocate Akhil Sibal, representing Das, submitted that he was not made aware of any Look Out Circular (LOC), the reason for its issuance or its purpose.
Also Read: CJP leader Saurav Das moves Delhi HC after being stopped from flying to UK for Oxford event
He sought a copy of the LOC. However, the Centre’s counsel said it cannot be furnished to him.
The court was hearing a plea by Das, who was stopped from flying to the United Kingdom for an event at Oxford University, where he was slated to speak on the "cockroach movement”.
Das has alleged that he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport before boarding his flight to London on the night of November 23.
During the hearing, the Centre’s counsel said a request was made by the Maharashtra Police to open an LOC against Das, and it was issued on the intervening night of November 22-23.
Now, Das has to challenge the LOC before an appropriate forum, he said.
Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Chetan Sharma and standing counsel Ashish Dixit, representing the Centre, said a show-cause notice was also issued to Das on November 23, and he is yet to respond to it.
The law officer said there are multiple objections to the maintainability of the petition, its premise, and the factual and legal aspects of the petition.
He said Das has only been advised not to travel and the advisory was “in his favour”. The ASG was referring to the show-cause notice, which asks Das not to travel due to an ongoing inquiry linked to alleged discrepancies in his passport.
Sharma said there were certain discrepancies in the details given in his passport and on August 20, an inquiry was initiated in Puducherry to ascertain the veracity of his place of birth, address and parentage because he has left the column of father blank.
He further submitted that the Bureau of Immigration is only the executing agency, and it cannot form a judgment on its own.
"There is no order today which either invalidates the passport, suspends the passport. It is only a show-cause notice he has to reply,” the ASG said.
He said Das had to respond to the notice on November 24, but he chose to first file a petition in the high court, and now he has to respond on November 30.
The Centre’s counsel contended that the alleged discrepancies highlighted in the passport may have a bearing on Das’s citizenship.
He also said, assuming that the passport officer concludes that Das’s explanation is inadequate, he will be stuck in a no-man’s land, and thus the advisory issued to him is in his favour.
Also Read: PwC explains what Delhi HC's GST ruling on corporate guarantees means for companies
The ASG also informed the court that the Madras High Court on October 30 issued notice on a plea seeking inquiry into the antecedents of Das.
Sibal said that the pendency of a show-cause notice does not mean that Das will be stopped from travelling, which is a fundamental right.
He submitted that the show-cause notice states that inputs were received that Das’s place of birth was incorrect and the passport was obtained by suppressing material facts, thus requiring clarification along with supporting documents, failing which his passport may be suspended or impounded.

title: 'पाकिस्तान पर क्यों नहीं लिया एक्शन?', 26/11 आतंकी हमले पर BJP ने राहुल गांधी को घेरा; पूछे तीन तीखे सवाल
description: बीजेपी ने साल 2008 के मुंबई आतंकी हमले को लेकर राहुल गांधी पर निशाना साधा है. बीजेपी का आरोप है कि कांग्रेस के नेतृ्त्व वाली यूपीए सरकार ने आतंकी हमले के बाद पाकिस्तान पर हमला करने के बजाए क्लिन चिट दे दी. बीजेपी ने कांग्रेस से तीन सवाल पूछे.
author: अभिनव त्रिपाठी
content:
गुरुवार (26 नवंबर) को बीजेपी ने साल 2008 में मुंबई में हुए आतंकी हमले को लेकर कांग्रेस और राहुल गांधी पर निशाना साधा और उनसे तीन सवाल किए. बीजेपी का आरोप है कि कांग्रेस ने उस हमले के दौरान राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा के बजाय वोट बैंक की राजनीति को चुना. सोशल मीडिया प्लेटफॉर्म एक्स पर बीजेपी के राष्ट्रीय प्रवक्ता प्रदीप भंडारी ने सवाल किया कि 26/11 के मुंबई आतंकी हमलों के बाद कांग्रेस के नेतृत्व वाली यूपीए सरकार ने पाकिस्ता पर हमला क्यों नहीं किया.
दरअसल, आज मुंबई में हुए आतंकी हमले की आज बरसी है. इसी दिन बीजेपी ने कांग्रेस पर निशाना साधते हुए इस हमले को लेकर तीन सवाल पूछे हैं. मुंबई में हुए इस आतंकी हमले में 166 लोगों की जान गई थी और 300 से अधिक लोग घायल हुए थे. भारत के किसी भी शहर में हुए सबसे घातक आतंकी हमले में से एक था.
सोशल मीडिया प्लेटफॉर्म एक्स पर बीजेपी के प्रवक्ता प्रदीप भंडारी ने कांग्रेस पर आरोप लगाते हुए बड़ा सवाल खड़ा किया. उन्होंने कहा कि 26/11 के मुंबई आतंकी हमलों के बाद कांग्रेस के नेतृत्व वाली यूपीए सरकार ने पाकिस्तान पर हमले क्यों नहीं किए. इसके अलावा इस हमले के बाद पाकिस्तान को क्यों क्लिन चिट दे दी गई. बीजेपी ने कहा कि राहुल गांधी और कांग्रेस पार्टी को 26/11 मुंबई आतंकी हमलों को लेकर तीन सवालों के जवाब देने चाहिए:
भंडारी ने अपनी पोस्ट में एक रिपोर्ट का हवाला देते हुए लिखा कि गांधी-वाड्रा परिवार की वोट बैंक की राजनीति के कारण, कांग्रेस ने 26/11 मुंबई आतंकी हमले के बाद पाकिस्तान को क्लीन चिट दे दी! उन्होंने देश की सुरक्षा से ऊपर वोट बैंक को चुना!
Rahul Gandhi and the Congress Party must answer three questions on the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks: 1. Why did the Congress-led UPA government not attack Pakistan after 26/11 Mumbai Terror Attack? 2. Why did Congress give clean chit to Pakistan by calling Mumbai Terror Attack “RSS Ki Sajish” ? 3. Why was Rahul Gandhi partying just days after 26/11 Mumbai terror attack? गौरतलब है कि 26 नवंबर 2008 को पाकिस्तान के समुद्र के रास्ते मुंबई आए लश्कर-ए-तैयबा के 10 भारी हथियारों से लैस आतंकवादियों ने शहर में आम नागरिकों पर एक भयानक आतंकी हमला किया. इस घटना में 166 लोगों की जान गई थी और 300 से अधिक लोग घायल हुए थे.
साल 2008 में हुए आतंकी हमलों के पीड़ितों को बीजेपी के तमाम नेताओं ने श्रद्धांजलि अर्पित की. इसके साथ ही उन सुरक्षाकर्मियों को याद किया, जिन्होंने देश की रक्षा करते हुए अपने जान की आहूति दे दी. रक्षा मंत्री राजनाथ सिंह ने कहा कि आज, मैं 26/11 मुंबई आतंकी हमलों के पीड़ितों को अपनी विनम्र श्रद्धांजलि अर्पित करता हूं और उन बहादुरों को याद करता हूं जिन्होंने हमारे देश की रक्षा में अपना सर्वोच्च बलिदान दिया.

title: एक ईमेल और मुंबई में मचा हड़कंप! खालिस्तानी निशाने पर मायानगरी, BMC दफ्तर और बिग-बी के बंगले को ड्रोन से उड़ाने की धमकी
description: अमिताभ बच्चन के बंगले जलसा को ड्रोन से उड़ाने की धमकी दी गई है. धमकी भरे ईमेल में ऋतु तावड़े के कार्यालय और बीएमसी दफ्तर को ड्रोन के जरिए उड़ाने की बात कही गई है. फिलहाल, पुलिस पूरे मामले की जांच कर रही है.
author: राज मिश्रा
content:
बॉलीवुड के महानायक अमिताभ बच्चन को एक बार फिर से धमकी मिलने का मामला सामने आया है. जानकारी के मुताबिक, अमिताभ बच्चन के बंगले जलसा को ड्रोन से उड़ाने की धमकी दी गई है. इसी के साथ मुंबई की मेयर और बीएमसी दफ्तर को भी एक धमकी मिली है. पुलिस सूत्रों के मुताबिक, मुंबई की मेयर ऋतु तावड़े के कार्यालय को आज (गुरुवार, 26 नवंबर) एक धमकी भरा ईमेल मिला है. इस ईमेल में ऋतु तावड़े के कार्यालय और बीएमसी दफ्तर को ड्रोन के जरिए उड़ाने की बात कही गई है. ईमेल में अमिताभ बच्चन के बंगले और पंजाबी सिंगर दिलजीत दोसांझ के मुंबई में होने जा रहे कॉन्सर्ट को भी निशाना बनाने की बात कही गई है. सूत्रों के अनुसार, इस धमकी भरे ईमेल में एक खालिस्तानी संगठन का नाम लिखा है. फिलहाल, पुलिस पूरे मामले की जांच कर रही है.
बीएमसी कार्यालय पहुंची BDDS की टीम
वहीं, धमकी भरा ईमेल मिलने के बाद बम डिटेक्शन एंड डिस्पोजल स्क्वॉड (BDDS) की टीम बीएमसी कार्यालय पहुंची और दफ्तर के चप्पे-चप्पे की जांच की. सूत्रों के अनुसार, अमिताभ के बंगले जलसा की सुरक्षा भी बढ़ा दी गई है. मुंबई पुलिस ने बच्चन परिवार के घर के बाहर पहरे को सख्त कर दिया है.
3 दिन पहले भी मिली थी धमकी
बता दें कि इससे पहले भी दोनों कलाकारों को धमकी मिल चुकी है. तीन दिन पहले ही 23 नवंबर को पुणे डिस्ट्रिक्ट कोर्ट को एक धमकी भरा ईमेल मिला था, जिसमें दिलजीत दोसांझ के मुंबई कॉन्सर्ट में बम ब्लास्ट करने और बिग-बी के बंगले जलसा को ड्रोन से उड़ाने की बात कही गई थी.
ईमेल में लिखे थे खालिस्तान नारे
धमकी भरे इस ईमेल में महालक्ष्मी स्टेडियम में आईफोन के जरिए बम धमाका करने की बात कही गई थी. इस ईमेल में भी खालिस्तान के नारों का जिक्र था. ईमेल में लिखा था- 'बम धमाके बचन-दिलजीत, मुंबई बोलेगा खालिस्तान जिंदाबाद, बच्चन जलसा विच ड्रोन दे हमले विच मरना, खून दा बदला खून, बच्चन दा हाय नारा, जिस नल सिखन दे नसलकुशी.'
अमिताभ बच्चन की सुरक्षा बढ़ाई गई
धमकियों के बीच अमिताभ बच्चन बुलेटप्रूफ ग्लास के पीछे से अपने फैन्स से मिलते दिखाई दिए थे. बता दें कि अमिताभ हर रविवार को अपने बंगले जलसा के बाहर फैंस से मुलाकात करने निकलते हैं. लगातार मिल रही धमकियों से उनकी सुरक्षा को लेकर पुलिस प्रशासन के साथ-साथ उनके सुरक्षागार्ड भी चिंतित हैं. यही वजह है कि अब बिग-बी को सार्वजनिक कार्यक्रमों में शामिल होने से रोक दिया गया है.

title: Explainer: प्रत्यर्पण या अपनी मर्जी से वापसी? शेख हसीना के मामले में भारत के सामने कैसी कानूनी चुनौती?
description: बांग्लादेश की पूर्व पीएम शेख हसीना ने ऐलान किया है कि वह 16 दिसंबर को ढाका वापस जाएंगी. हालांकि, बांग्लादेश के अधिकारियों का कहना है कि हसीना केवल प्रत्यर्पण के रास्ते ही वापसी कर सकती हैं. ऐसे में सवाल है कि खुद बांग्लादेश लौटने की इच्छा के बाद भी क्या भारत को शेख हसीना का प्रत्यर्पण करना होगा.
author: अभिनव त्रिपाठी
content:
बांग्लादेश की पूर्व पीएम शेख हसीना आगामी 16 दिसंबर को वापस ढाका लौटना चाहती है. बांग्लादेश वापस जाने के लिए उन्होंने 'विक्ट्री डे' को चुना है. हालांकि, बांग्लादेश ने स्पष्ट किया है कि शेख हसीना को कानूनी प्रक्रिया का पालन करते हुए प्रत्यर्पण के जरिए वापस ढाका में प्रवेश मिल पाएगा. बांग्लादेश ने हसीना की ओर से मांगी गई मदद को भी खारिज कर दिया है.
दरअसल, शेख हसीना की इस प्रस्तावित घर वापसी ने भारत के सामने बड़ा कानूनी सवाल खड़ा कर दिया है. सवाल उठ रहा है कि जब किसी शख्स को दूसरे देश की अदालतें ढूंढ रही हों और वह खुद लौटने को तैयार हो, तो इस स्थिति में कानून क्या कहता है. सवाल यह भी है कि क्या जिस देश में वह व्यक्ति अभी रह रहा है, उसे फिर भी उसका प्रत्यर्पण करना होगा?
शेख हसीना बांग्लादेश लौटने का विरोध नहीं कर रही हैं, बल्कि उन्होंने ढाका की सरकार से खुद मदद मांगी और कहा कि उनके लिए 'बिमान बांग्लादेश एयरलाइंस' की फ्लाइट का इंतजाम किया जाए, जिससे वह वापसी कर सकें. हसीना के प्रवक्ता सैयद मोजम्मेल अली का दावा है कि हसीना बांग्लादेश जाकर अदालतों का सामना करना चाहती हैं.
शेख हसीना के इस प्रस्ताव को बांग्लादेश की तारिक सरकार ने खारिज कर दिया. ढाका सरकार का कहना है कि हसीना अपने अनुसार, वापसी नहीं कर सकती हैं. उनको लौटने के लिए औपचारिक प्रत्यर्पण प्रक्रिया का पालन करना होगा. हाल में ही बंग्लादेश के विदेश राज्य मंत्री हुमायूं कबीर ने इस संबंध में एक कड़ा बयान दिया था.
इन सभी घटनाक्रमों ने भारत-बांग्लादेश प्रत्यर्पण संधि के साथ भारत के कानूनों पर सभी का ध्यान खींचा है. ऐसे में सवाल खड़ा है कि क्या कि शेख हसीना के लौटने की इच्छा से कानूनी प्रक्रिया बदल जाएगी, जिसका भारत को पालन करना है. बता दें कि अपनी मर्जी से देश लौटने के लिए तैयार हो जाने से प्रत्यर्पण की प्रक्रिया अपने आप खत्म नहीं होती है.
इसके लिए हमें साल 2013 की भारत-बांग्लादेश प्रत्यर्पण संधि के नियमों को समझना होगा. इस संधि के तहत दोनों देश अपने इलाके में मौजूद ऐसे लोगों को सौंपने के लिए सहमत हैं, जिनपर कोई भी कानूनी आरोप हैं. ऐसे में यह नियम उन लोगों पर भी लागू होता है, जो किसी अपराध में दोषी ठहराए जा चुके हैं. दोनों देशों के बीच हुई इस संधि के तहत कुछ तय प्रक्रियाएं हैं.
संधि के अनुच्छेद 10 के अनुसार, प्रत्यर्पण की मांग करने वाले देश को कूटनीतिक रास्ता अपनाना होता है और औपचारिक अनुरोध भेजना होता है. इसके अलावा उस व्यक्ति, अपराध के साथ उससे जुड़े कानूनों की जानकारी भी देनी होती है. वहीं, जिस व्यक्ति के प्रत्यर्पण की मांग की जा रही है, अगर वह पहले से दोषी ठहराया जा सका है, तो दोषसिद्धि के जरूरी दस्तावेज भी देने होते हैं.
इसके बाद आता है कि आर्टिकल 16, जो शख्स को सौंपने से जुड़ा है. अगर इन सभी के बाद संबंधित देश प्रत्यर्पण की मंजूरी दे देता है, तो शख्स को एक बिंदू तक पहुंचाने की व्यवस्था करनी होगी. यही कारण है कि यह केवल किसी शख्स के खुद लौटने का फैसला नहीं है. इसमें दोनों सरकारों की सहमति और एक्शन शामिल है. संधि की पूरी प्रक्रिया को छोड़ा नहीं जा सकता है.
विदेश मामलों के जानकार और दयाल सिंह कॉलेज में एसोसिएट प्रोफेसर डॉ. मनोज कुमार का कहना है कि भारत इस मामले को शुद्ध रूप से कानूनी और प्रक्रियात्मक मान रहा है. स्वैच्छिक वापसी को प्रत्यर्पण से अलग रखकर वह दोनों पक्षों के बीच दबाव कम रखने की कोशिश कर रहा है. अंतिम फैसला अदालती, एवं प्रशासनिक प्रक्रिया और राष्ट्रीय हितों पर निर्भर करेगा.
उन्होंने कहा कि भारत जल्दबाजी में कोई कदम नहीं उठाएगा और बांग्लादेश को भी रचनात्मक संवाद के लिए तैयार रखने का प्रयास करते रहना चाहिए . स्वैच्छिक वापसी और बांग्लादेश का प्रत्यर्पण अनुरोध अलग-अलग हैं, दोनों को जोड़ा नहीं जा सकता है.
प्रत्यर्पण अनुरोध प्रक्रिया के तहत जांच में है. स्वैच्छिक वापसी शेख हसीना और बांग्लादेश सरकार के बीच का मुद्दा है. भारत को विस्तृत टिप्पणी से बचना चाहिए. अप्रैल 2025 से जांच जारी है कोई समयसीमा या अंतिम फैसला सार्वजनिक नहीं हुआ है. भारत रचनात्मक संबंध बनाए रखना चाहता है.
इन सबके बाद आता है भारत का प्रत्यर्पण अधिनियम, 1962, जो ऐसे अनुरोधों से निपटने का कानूनी ढांचा देता है. इस भारतीय कानून की धारा 4 से 8 में आगे की कार्यवाही के नियम हैं. इसके तहत मजिस्ट्रेट की जांच, सबूतों की परख और व्यक्ति को सौंपने का फैसला लेना शामिल है. भारत-बांग्लादेश की संधि और प्रत्यर्पण अधिनियम में कहीं भी खुद से लौटने के लिए कोई अपने आप चलने वाली प्रक्रिया शामिल नहीं है.
दोनों नियमों में कही इस बात उल्लेख नहीं है कि खुद लौटने के इच्छुक व्यक्ति को विवादित प्रत्यर्पण जांच के हर चरण से गुजरना होगा. ऐसे में दोनों नियमों को ध्यान में रखते हुए भारत के अधिकारियों को कानूनी स्थिति की जांच करनी होगी. अधिकारियों को ही यह तय करना होगा कि व्यक्ति की सहमति का पूरी प्रक्रिया पर क्या असर होगा?
बांग्लादेश छोड़ने के बाद शेख हसीना का डिप्लोमैटिक पासपोर्ट को ढाका की सरकार ने रद्द कर दिया. उसके बाद से उन्होंने कई बार बांग्लादेशी यात्रा दस्तावेज पाने की कोशिश की. बावजूद इसके उन्होंने कई बार अड़चनों का सामना करना पड़ा. ढाका ने हालिया एक बयान में कहा था कि दोषी ठहराए जाने के बाद शेख हसीना नए पासपोर्ट के लिए योग्य नहीं है और उनके लौटने का सही रास्ता प्रत्यर्पण ही है.
इस पूरे मामले को ध्यान में रखते हुए भारत के विदेश मंत्रालय ने अंतरराष्ट्रीय यात्रा के लिए यात्रा दस्तावेजों की अहमियत पर जोर दिया. MEA प्रवक्ता रणधीर जायसवाल ने कहा कि यह एक कानूनी मामला है और इसको सही तरीके से निपटा जाएगा.
उन्होंने कहा कि तय प्रक्रिया के तहत अनुरोध की जांच की जा रही है. किसी नागरिक का अपनी मर्जी से लौटना प्रत्यर्पण के अनुरोध से अलग मामला है. ऐसे में अगर शेख हसीना खुद से वापस लौटने का फैसला करती भी हैं, तो यह एयरपोर्ट जाकर आम फ्लाइट पकड़ने जितना आसान नहीं होगा.
दोनों देशों के बीच की यह संधि कुछ खास मामलों में भारत को प्रत्यर्पण के अनुरोध को ठुकराने का आधार भी देती है. हालांकि, केवल राजनीतिक मकसद का आरोप लगाने से प्रत्यर्पण अपने आप नहीं रुक जाता. इस संधि का अनुच्छेद 6 राजनीतिक अपराध से जुड़ी छूट देता है.
ऐसे में अगर अपराध राजनीतिक प्रकृति का माना जाए, तो देश प्रत्यर्पण से इनकार कर सकता है. वैसे यह छूट कई गंभीर अपराधों में लागू नहीं होती. जिसमें हत्या, सदोष मानव वध, अपहरण जैसे अपराध शामिल हैं. वहीं, संधि का अनुच्छेद 8 इनकार करने का एक और आधार देता है, जिसमें अगर किसी को सौंपना अन्यायपूर्ण हो, तो प्रत्यर्पण से मना किया जा सकता है.
गौरतलब है कि शेख हसीना को ढाका वापस जाने के लिए वैध यात्रा दस्तावेजों की जरूरत होगी और बांग्लादेश को उन्हें स्वीकार करने के लिए सहमत होना होगा. वहीं, अगर बांग्लादेश के अनुरोध पर हसीना को भारत ढाका के अधिकारियों को सौंपता है, तो प्रत्यर्पण के नियम लगेंगे.
वहीं, अगर भारतीय अधिकारी हसीना को वैध दस्तावेजों के साथ जाने की अनुमति दें और ढाका उन्हें स्वीकार करे, तो यहां पर स्थिति अलग होगी. ऐसे में भारत सरकार को उनकी रवानगी पर लगी कानूनी पाबंदियों के साथ-साथ लंबित प्रत्यर्पण अनुरोध के असर को समझना होगा और उसका आकलन करना होगा.

title: 'Strong Alliance Will Be Formed, We Will Form Government': Supriya Shrinate Confident Of Congress-SP Tie-Up Ahead Of 2027 UP Polls
description: Congress leader Supriya Shrinate expresses confidence in a strong SP-Congress alliance for the 2027 UP Assembly elections as seat-sharing talks continue amid differences over the number of constituencies. Sources say SP has offered 26 seats, while Congress is seeking 120.
author: Asian News International
content:
'Strong Alliance Will Be Formed, We Will Form Government': Supriya Shrinate Confident Of Congress-SP Tie-Up Ahead Of 2027 UP Polls
Congress leader Supriya Shrinate expresses confidence in a strong SP-Congress alliance for the 2027 UP Assembly elections as seat-sharing talks continue amid differences over the number of constituencies. Sources say SP has offered 26 seats, while Congress is seeking 120.
- India News
- 4 min read
Lucknow: Congress leader Supriya Shrinate on Thursday expressed confidence that the Congress and Samajwadi Party would form a strong alliance ahead of the forthcoming 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, saying discussions on seat-sharing were underway and that both parties understood the need to contest the polls together.
Speaking to reporters, Shrinate said she was not directly involved in the seat-sharing negotiations but maintained that responsible leaders from both sides were working towards finalising the arrangement.
"I am not involved in the seat-sharing process. The respected and responsible individuals who are involved are working on it. Both sides understand that seat-sharing is necessary. There are responsible people on both sides. Just wait and see—seat-sharing will happen, a strong alliance will be formed, and we will form the government. That is precisely why the other side is in a state of panic," she said.
Separately, JMM leader Manoj Pandey, speaking in Ranchi, also expressed confidence in the Congress-SP alliance, saying discussions were ongoing and that the alliance had not broken down.
Advertisement
"I am making it clear that talks about an alliance are currently underway ahead of the elections. It is being finalised how many seats each party will contest in the alliance. The alliance has not broken down on either side. Talks are ongoing, and that is a very positive thing. There will be an alliance," Pandey said.
The remarks come amid differences over seat-sharing, with Congress MP Imran Masood criticising the Samajwadi Party for announcing candidates while alliance discussions were still underway.
Advertisement
On the meeting between Meta representatives and Congress leaders over suspended accounts and alleged content restrictions, Shrinate accused the social media platform of interfering in India's electoral democracy by selectively restricting opposition content.
She said that social media platforms, including Meta, were American platforms and alleged that selectively removing opposition content or withholding opposition accounts in India amounted to interference in the country's democratic and electoral processes.
"The reality is that any social media platform—whether it is Meta or any other—is an American platform. If you systematically remove only the content belonging to the opposition, or withhold only the accounts of the opposition—withholding their content within India—then you are interfering in the democracy of this country. You are interfering in the very process of India's electoral democracy, and that will not be tolerated," she said.
Alleging that Meta was treating AI-generated content posted by the Congress differently from that posted by the BJP, Shrinate said, "The way in which Meta removes our AI-generated content while leaving the BJP's AI-generated content entirely untouched—that is a biased approach. How is it that the accounts of the head of the IYC (Indian Youth Congress) and the person in charge of the IYC get withheld? We want to know: what has become of freedom of expression? There is outrage among our people; there is anger against Meta among the public—I can tell you that."
Shrinate also criticised the alleged denial of permission to opposition leaders for holding rallies, claiming that leaders who opposed the BJP were being treated differently.
"When we said that the 'B-team' of the BJP had been activated, you all laughed. A red carpet is being rolled out for the BJP's 'B-team'—they are granted permission, provided with police protection, and their rallies are facilitated. Anyone who opposes the BJP, however, has their permission revoked," she said.
She added that the Constitution empowered citizens to question and protest, asserting that the Congress remained committed to its protection.
"But the Constitution of this country empowers us all to ask questions and to protest. Today is Constitution Day, and we will celebrate it with great enthusiasm. Our president, Kharge-ji, is arriving here today, and we are all committed to protecting the Constitution at any cost," Shrinate said.
Speaking on Congress-SP seat sharing, Congress MP KL Sharma from Amethi said, "No one should be making such tall claims. This will be decided by the leadership of the Samajwadi Party and the Congress. Others who are making such statements have no authority to do so. You should only consider statements from those who are officially authorised to speak on this matter..."
The remarks come amid ongoing seat-sharing discussions between the two INDIA bloc allies. The SP has offered 26 seats to the Congress in the initial round of discussions, while the Congress has sought 120 seats and is unwilling to accept a lower number, according to sources.
