title: 'Should Not Have Made Those Comments': Delhi Police Registers FIR Over Yash Maheshwari's Remarks On Bihari Women, Chhath Puja
description: Delhi Police registers an FIR over comedian Yash Maheshwari's alleged remarks on Bihari women and Chhath Puja. The comedian apologised on November 24 as outrage spread, while Patna Police also registered a case.
author: Shruti Sneha
content:
'Should Not Have Made Those Comments': Delhi Police Registers FIR Over Yash Maheshwari's Remarks On Bihari Women, Chhath Puja
Delhi Police registers an FIR over comedian Yash Maheshwari's alleged remarks on Bihari women and Chhath Puja. The comedian apologised on November 24 as outrage spread, while Patna Police also registered a case.
- India News
- 4 min read
Patna, Bihar: The controversy surrounding stand-up comedian Yash Maheshwari's remarks about women from Bihar and Chhath Puja has taken a legal turn, with the Delhi Police registering an FIR following a complaint over his performance at a comedy club in South Delhi.
A case was filed at Saket Police Station related to an event that took place on October 24, 2026. The complaint says the comedian made comments about Bihari women that are considered inappropriate, including things about their homes and the religious and cultural traditions connected to Chhath Puja.
The FIR has been registered under Sections 79, 196, 296, and 352 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. These rules cover actions that are meant to disrespect a woman's dignity, creating hatred between different groups, engaging in sexual or inappropriate behavior, and deliberately insulting someone to cause public disorder. However, the FIR does not name Maheshwari.
The complainant has also asked the police to look at the performance recordings, social media posts, and other digital stuff related to the incident. The police will look at these materials as part of their investigation.
Advertisement
What Did Yash Maheshwari Say That Triggered The Backlash?
The controversy started when videos from Maheshwari's stand-up comedy show, called 'Morally Questionable', began spreading on social media. The performance reportedly included comments about women from Bihar, their family lives, and traditions connected to Chhath Puja.
One of the comments that faced a lot of backlash was about the long streak of sindoor, which is traditionally worn by married women during the festival. The comments caused a lot of heated reactions online, with many people criticizing the comedian for joking about women's respect and being disrespectful to religious beliefs and the culture of Bihar.
Advertisement
The performance was uploaded to his YouTube channel on November 21, following which excerpts spread across platforms, including Instagram and X. The growing backlash also led to demands for police action against him.
Comedian Apologises, Removes Performance Amid Growing Outrage
As criticism mounted, Maheshwari posted an apology video on November 24 via his YouTube channel. The video, titled 'Public Apology to All the People of Bihar', admitted that his remarks about the state's cultural traditions were inappropriate.
"Recently, I uploaded a video in which I was talking about certain cultural aspects of Bihar. I think I should not have done that. I completely stand by that, and I apologise. I should not have made those comments in that manner," he said.
He further clarified that he did not intend to hurt anyone's religious sentiments or offend people who celebrate Chhath Puja. Admitting his mistake, he expressed regret and said he would exercise greater caution over the content he shares in the future.
Despite the apology, the controversy continued. The comedian subsequently removed the controversial performance from his YouTube channel, while his Instagram account was also deactivated.
Delhi FIR Comes Days After Police Action In Patna
The Delhi case is not the only police complaint against Maheshwari over the performance. On November 24, Patna Cyber Police registered a separate FIR against him over the alleged derogatory remarks about Bihari women on his YouTube channel.
The Patna case was filed under Sections 75(1), 79, 351 and 352 of the BNS, along with Sections 66C and 66D of the Information Technology Act. Police said the remarks could potentially disturb social harmony and create hostility between communities.
Meanwhile, the Delhi BJP's Purvanchal Morcha also approached Central Delhi DCP Rohit Rajbir Singh with a separate complaint, seeking action against the comedian.

title: 'India Will Go Inside Pakistan And Hit There': CM Fadnavis Pays Tribute To 26/11 Martyrs, Says Terrorists Cannot Break Mumbai's Spirit
description: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis paid tribute to 26/11 martyrs at Mumbai's Gateway of India, recalling Pakistan's role in the attacks and warning that India will retaliate against attacks on its soldiers and citizens.
author: Asian News International
content:
'India Will Go Inside Pakistan And Hit There': CM Fadnavis Pays Tribute To 26/11 Martyrs, Says Terrorists Cannot Break Mumbai's Spirit
Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis paid tribute to 26/11 martyrs at Mumbai's Gateway of India, recalling Pakistan's role in the attacks and warning that India will retaliate against attacks on its soldiers and citizens.
- India News
- 6 min read
Mumbai: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Thursday paid tribute to the martyrs of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks at a memorial event held at the Gateway of India, saying that the attack was not merely an assault on the Taj Hotel and other targeted locations but an attempt to strike at India's diplomatic community and convey that the entire country was under attack.
Fadnavis, along with several other leaders, attended the memorial event marking the anniversary of the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, in which several people, including security personnel, lost their lives.
Addressing the gathering, the Chief Minister said the terrorists had targeted locations where they could kill as many people as possible and sought to send a message that the whole of India was under attack. However, he said the security forces not only stopped the terrorists but also exposed Pakistan's conspiracy by capturing terrorist Ajmal Kasab alive.
"The 26/11 attack was not just an attack on the Taj Hotel or the other locations targeted; it was an attack targeting the diplomatic community and big gatherings where they could kill as many people as possible and give a message that the whole of India is under attack, but people in our security forces not only stopped those terrorists, but also tore apart the veil on the conspiracy of Pakistan by capturing Qasab alive," Fadnavis said.
Advertisement
Paying his respects to those who sacrificed their lives in the attack, he said the anniversary should serve as a reminder of the need to ensure that such an incident never takes place in the country again.
"Today, on the anniversary of that attack, we all have to make a resolution that we will never let such an attack happen in our country while we pay our deepest gratitude to all the people who sacrificed their lives for this country," he said.
Advertisement
Emphasising Mumbai's resilience in the aftermath of the attacks, Fadnavis said terrorism could not undermine the spirit of the city.
"Mumbai didn’t stop then. Mumbai is not stopping now and will never stop in future either. Terrorists cannot demean the spirit of Mumbai," he said.
Referring to subsequent security challenges, including the Uri and Pahalgam attacks, the Chief Minister said India would not tolerate attacks on its soldiers and citizens, irrespective of where they occurred. He said the country had demonstrated its resolve to retaliate against attacks.
"Whether it's Uri or Pahalgam. India will not tolerate any attacks on its soldiers and citizens, no matter where they happen. India will go inside Pakistan and hit there... We also showed there that we'll strike back and take revenge if attacked," he said.
Stressing the importance of remembering historical events and drawing lessons from them, Fadnavis said societies that forget their history cannot secure their future.
"That's why we always need to learn from history and look to the future, because societies that forget their history... They have a present, but they don't have a future," he said.
He added that the memorial programme was important not only to remember the events of November 26, 2008, and pay tribute to the martyrs but also to learn lessons while looking ahead.
The Chief Minister further said terrorist incidents in Mumbai and the country had ended over the last 12 years under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership. He acknowledged that attempts had been made but said they had been thwarted with the help of the police and security forces.
"In the last 12 years in Mumbai or the country. Terrorist incidents have completely ended. Some attempts were made, but they've been completely rooted out. With the help of our police and our soldiers, we've built a secure India," he said.
During his address, Fadnavis also spoke about issues concerning police personnel and their families, acknowledging the work being undertaken by Rahul Dubale through the Police Boys Association to raise matters concerning the police force.
He said he had been observing Dubale's efforts for the past 10 years and appreciated his work in raising police-related issues without any personal interest. Fadnavis added that the state government was making efforts to address these concerns and had already resolved several issues.
Referring to housing for police personnel residing in the BDD chawls, the Chief Minister said that when he first became Chief Minister, the state government had submitted an affidavit before the Bombay High Court stating that police personnel should also receive housing benefits if other residents of the chawls were being provided houses.
"When I first became Chief Minister, we submitted an affidavit to the Hon'ble High Court stating that if we were providing houses to the other residents of the BDD chawls, then the police there should also be given houses, and we went ahead and did that," he said.
He assured that the remaining issues raised during the programme would also be addressed.
Fadnavis, who has also held the Home portfolio, said that the state had undertaken significant police recruitment during his tenure, claiming that more recruitment had taken place under his watch than under any other Home Minister in the state's history. He added that the ongoing recruitment process could potentially set a national record.
The Chief Minister said the state government continued to take decisions concerning police recruitment, training, the welfare of police personnel and support for their families. He added that while such decisions had to comply with rules and laws and take into account their implications for other government employees, the police force needed to be treated with special consideration.
Concluding his address, Fadnavis congratulated Dubale on the launch of a cardiac ambulance for police families and assured the Police Boys Association of his personal support in its efforts to work for police personnel across Maharashtra.
"I assure them that I will personally make sure they get whatever help they need while they continue to serve the police selflessly," he said.
Fadnavis concluded by paying his respects to the martyrs and saying, "Jai Hind, Jai Maharashtra."
This year marks 18 years since terrorists from the Pakistan-backed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) unleashed mayhem on the streets of India's financial capital, Mumbai. Commonly referred to as 26/11, these coordinated assaults by a group of 10 terrorists sent shockwaves through the nation and the world.

title: Why Make in India is making Trump's America nervous
description: USTR report names Make in India, PLI and Atmanirbhar Bharat, alleging that government-backed industrial expansion is distorting global competition across four key sectors
author: Dheeraj Kumar
content:
Why Make in India is making Trump's America nervous
USTR report names Make in India, PLI and Atmanirbhar Bharat, alleging that government-backed industrial expansion is distorting global competition across four key sectors
India wants to manufacture more, import less and become a global production hub. From mobile phones and pharmaceuticals to steel, solar panels and medical devices, New Delhi has spent years trying to build domestic industrial capacity and attract global companies looking to diversify their supply chains beyond China.
But this manufacturing ambition has now become a subject of scrutiny in the US. The administration of US President Donald Trump has named India's flagship industrial programmes, including Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, in a major trade investigation into alleged excess manufacturing capacity.
In a 189-page report released on Wednesday, the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) argued that India's industrial policies, financial incentives, labour practices and market access restrictions contribute to manufacturing capacity beyond what market conditions would otherwise support.
The US has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The proposed rate could be capped at 17 per cent if New Delhi reaches a trade agreement with Washington that addresses the findings of the investigation.
India has rejected the central allegation, maintaining that it does not have structural excess capacity in any sector. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said the government was examining the USTR determination and that trade-related concerns should be resolved through the ongoing bilateral trade negotiations.
The dispute, however, goes beyond tariffs. At its heart is a disagreement over how countries should build manufacturing capacity, support domestic industries and compete for a larger share of global production.
Here is why India's manufacturing ambitions have come under the Trump administration's scanner.
Why has Trump targeted Make in India and PLI schemes?
The USTR report specifically identifies Make in India, launched in 2014, and the Production Linked Incentive programme, introduced in 2020, alongside Atmanirbhar Bharat and the India Brand Equity Foundation's export promotion initiatives.
These programmes are central to India's efforts to transform itself from a largely consumption-driven economy into a major manufacturing and export destination.
Make in India seeks to encourage companies to manufacture and assemble products domestically, attract investment and increase manufacturing's contribution to the economy. The programme has an ambition of raising manufacturing's share of GDP to 25 per cent.
The PLI scheme takes this approach further by offering financial incentives to eligible companies based on incremental sales of products manufactured in India. Initially introduced in three sectors, it has expanded to 14 sectors, including electronics, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, textiles and food processing.
Atmanirbhar Bharat, meanwhile, seeks to strengthen domestic production capabilities, reduce dependence on imports and make Indian businesses more competitive.
From New Delhi's perspective, these initiatives are necessary to overcome India's manufacturing constraints, create employment, develop domestic supply chains and attract companies looking to diversify production beyond China.
The USTR, however, sees a different problem.
It argues that government-backed incentives encourage companies to expand production capacity irrespective of whether domestic and global demand can absorb the additional output. According to Washington, this can create persistent overcapacity, push down prices and put manufacturers in other countries at a disadvantage.
The report specifically flags financial incentives linked to incremental production and sales, arguing that such support can encourage manufacturing expansion beyond what would happen under market-oriented conditions.
It also questions India's ambition to increase manufacturing's share of GDP, arguing that the combination of industrial targets, financial support and export promotion can distort competition.
In other words, Washington is not merely questioning whether India is producing more. It is questioning the government-backed model through which New Delhi wants to achieve that growth.
What does the US mean by excess manufacturing capacity?
Structural excess capacity refers to a situation in which an economy persistently produces more than domestic and global markets can absorb, with government policies or interventions contributing to the expansion.
The USTR argues that such capacity can lead to overproduction, falling prices, underutilised factories and greater export competition.
For example, if a country provides incentives to manufacturers to build factories and expand production, but domestic consumption does not grow at the same pace, companies may look towards overseas markets to sell the additional output.
Washington argues that this can hurt manufacturers in countries that do not provide similar levels of government support.
The USTR report examines several indicators to establish its case against India. These include manufacturing's share of GDP, investment levels, labour's share of manufacturing income, the presence of persistently unprofitable companies, trade balances and imports from countries classified by the US as non-market economies.
It also looks at the extent to which foreign investment and imported intermediate goods contribute to manufacturing expansion.
Why is the US worried about India's manufacturing growth?
One of the central arguments in the USTR report is that India is expanding manufacturing capacity and investment faster than domestic consumption and demand.
The report estimates that manufacturing accounted for an average of 13.5 per cent of India's GDP between 2021 and 2025. It compares this with 9.9% for the US and 15.4 per cent for the global average.
It also points to India's investment-to-GDP ratio, which averaged 34% during the same period, compared with 21.6 per cent in the US.
Washington argues that high investment and manufacturing expansion, when not accompanied by sufficient domestic demand, can encourage companies to direct additional production towards export markets.
The US has another concern. India's goods trade surplus with America has continued to grow even though the country runs an overall global goods trade deficit.
According to the USTR report, India's global goods trade deficit stood at approximately $309 billion in 2025. At the same time, its goods trade surplus with the US increased from $42.5 billion in 2023 to $45.2 billion in 2024 and $57.3 billion in 2025.
For Washington, this combination indicates that Indian manufacturers are gaining ground in the American market while US producers face greater competition.
The report argues that India's industrial policies reduce commercial opportunities for American manufacturers both in India and in third-country markets.
It also raises concerns about labour protections, wage formation and financial policies, claiming that these can lower production costs and give Indian manufacturers an artificial competitive advantage.
These are the US administration's findings and interpretations, which India has disputed.
Solar, steel, pharma: Why these four sectors matter
The USTR report identifies four major areas of concern in India: steel, solar products, pharmaceuticals and information and communications technology (ICT).
These are not random sectors. They are closely linked to India's ambitions to build strategic manufacturing capabilities, reduce import dependence and expand exports.
1. Solar manufacturing: Capacity nearly three times domestic demand
India's solar manufacturing expansion is among the most prominent examples cited by Washington.
According to the USTR report, India's solar module manufacturing capacity has reached 154 gigawatts (GW), nearly three times domestic demand of 53 GW.
The report also points to a sharp increase in investment in the sector. Annual investment in India's solar industry rose from $84 million in 2018 to $10 billion in 2025, according to figures cited from Rhodium Group.
Government incentives, domestic sourcing requirements and the PLI scheme have encouraged companies to establish manufacturing facilities and expand production.
For India, the objective is to reduce dependence on imported solar equipment, particularly from China, and develop a domestic manufacturing ecosystem.
But Washington argues that production capacity has grown faster than actual demand, creating the risk of excess inventory, falling prices and financial pressure on manufacturers.
The report also highlights India's dependence on Chinese inputs such as polysilicon, ingots and wafers, despite the country's push to manufacture solar modules domestically.
This creates a contradiction in India's self-reliance strategy. The country is expanding its domestic manufacturing capacity but remains dependent on China for important components and raw materials.
2. Steel: India is adding capacity as global overproduction becomes a concern
Steel is another important sector in the USTR investigation.
India has been expanding steelmaking capacity to support infrastructure development, construction, automobiles and industrial growth.
The report cites figures from the Global Forum on Steel Excess Capacity, which indicate that India's steelmaking capacity increased by 11.4, per cent or 18.3 million metric tonnes, compared with late 2023.
India is also expected to add another 30.4 million metric tonnes of steelmaking capacity between 2025 and 2027, according to the figures cited by the USTR.
The concern is that rising production capacity across major steel-producing economies could put pressure on global prices and manufacturers.
However, there is an important distinction. The same Global Forum data cited in the USTR report showed that India recorded a steel trade deficit of 0.13 million metric tonnes in the second quarter of 2025.
This means India imported more steel than it exported during that period, even as its production capacity expanded.
The USTR nevertheless argues that the planned capacity additions could contribute to global excess supply in the coming years.
3. Pharmaceuticals: India is a major US supplier but still depends on China
India's pharmaceutical industry presents a different kind of challenge.
The country is one of the world's leading suppliers of generic medicines and has become an important part of the US healthcare supply chain.
The USTR report estimates that Indian manufacturers account for around 47 per cent of generic prescriptions dispensed in the US. It also cites estimates that India produces approximately 61 per cent of generic solid oral drug doses sold in the American market.
Around one-third of India's pharmaceutical exports are destined for the US, making America a critical destination for Indian drugmakers.
However, Washington has highlighted India's continued dependence on China for active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and bulk drug materials.
The report cites estimates that around 87 per cent of India's imported antibiotic ingredients by value come from China.
This is particularly significant because India has introduced PLI incentives to strengthen domestic manufacturing of bulk drugs, APIs and critical pharmaceutical ingredients.
The US argues that India's manufacturing expansion continues to rely on imported inputs from non-market economies, particularly China, which can create economic security risks.
4. Information technology and electronics: The supply-chain question
Information and communications technology is the fourth sector identified by the USTR.
India has been trying to expand electronics manufacturing, particularly mobile phones, telecom equipment and IT hardware, through incentives and investment promotion.
The PLI scheme has played an important role in this effort.
According to figures cited in the USTR report from Invest India, domestic mobile phone production increased from 5.8 crore units in 2014-15 to 33 crore units in 2023-24. Imports fell from 21 crore units to 0.3 crore units during the same period, while exports reached nearly five crore units.
This shift from importing mobile phones to manufacturing and exporting them is one of the major developments in India's manufacturing story.
However, Washington questions whether India's domestic demand can absorb the additional production capacity being developed across the ICT sector.
It also raises concerns about India's reliance on imported components and intermediate goods, particularly from China.
The USTR argues that these imports can help Indian manufacturers expand production at lower costs while creating dependence on external suppliers for critical manufacturing inputs.
Why is China's role in India's manufacturing push also under scrutiny?
One of the more interesting aspects of the USTR report is its focus on India's growing dependence on Chinese manufacturing inputs.
India has been trying to position itself as an alternative to China in global supply chains. Yet, several of its expanding manufacturing industries continue to rely on Chinese raw materials, components and intermediate goods.
The USTR report estimates that India's intermediate goods imports from China increased by $44 billion, or 97 per cent, between 2017 and 2025.
Imports of intermediate goods from all economies classified by the US as non-market economies increased by $91 billion, or 152 per cent, during the same period.
Washington argues that these imports make Indian downstream manufacturing more competitive by providing access to relatively inexpensive components and materials.
It also says that Chinese investment in Indian manufacturing, particularly in sectors such as steel and solar, contributes to the expansion of production capacity.
This is a significant concern for the Trump administration because it sees the movement of Chinese capital, components and manufacturing capacity into other countries as a potential way of extending China's industrial influence beyond its borders.
For India, however, the issue is more complicated.
Building an alternative manufacturing ecosystem takes time. Domestic companies need access to raw materials, advanced components, technology and machinery. Until local supply chains develop sufficiently, imports remain necessary.
The challenge for New Delhi is to expand domestic production without simply shifting dependence from finished Chinese products to Chinese components and industrial inputs.
Is Trump targeting India alone?
No. The USTR investigation covers 16 economies, with determinations issued against 14 of them on November 25.
These include China, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Cambodia, Singapore, Switzerland and the European Union.
Mexico and Norway were not included in the latest determinations because their investigations remain under way.
The US has accused several of these economies of using industrial policies, financial support, export incentives and other measures that contribute to excess manufacturing capacity.
China faces particularly extensive scrutiny, with the USTR identifying industrial subsidies, state-owned enterprises, financial support and export-oriented manufacturing policies among its concerns.
India's inclusion is significant because New Delhi has been seeking to strengthen economic and strategic cooperation with Washington while attracting companies looking to diversify away from China.
The latest investigation shows that the US is applying its concerns about government-backed industrial expansion to several trading partners, not just Beijing.
What happens next for India?
The immediate challenge is to prevent the proposed tariffs from becoming another obstacle to the India-US trade agreement.
The USTR has proposed a tariff ceiling of 25 per cent on Indian goods, with the possibility of reducing it to 17 per cent if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement that addresses the findings of the investigation.
These are proposed duties and have not yet taken effect.
Interested parties have until January 5, 2027, to submit written comments and requests to appear at public hearings, which are scheduled to begin on January 25.
India has said it is examining the USTR determination and remains committed to concluding the bilateral trade agreement. New Delhi has also maintained that trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of the ongoing negotiations.
The larger issue, however, is unlikely to disappear with a trade agreement.
India's ambition to increase manufacturing's share of GDP, build domestic supply chains and become a global production hub will require continued government support, investment and access to international markets.
Washington's latest investigation raises questions about how far such support can go before it is viewed by trading partners as distorting competition.

title: Delhi Police tightens security at stations after Jama Masjid attack
description: New SOPs mandate 24/7 armed sentries, restricted gate access, visitor frisking and round-the-clock CCTV monitoring
author: FP News Desk
content:
Delhi Police tightens security at stations after Jama Masjid attack
New SOPs mandate 24/7 armed sentries, restricted gate access, visitor frisking and round-the-clock CCTV monitoring
The Delhi Police has announced a comprehensive overhaul of security protocols at police stations across the national capital following an attack on police personnel near Jama Masjid. The decision was taken after a high-level meeting of senior Delhi Police officials, with the Police Headquarters issuing fresh Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to strengthen security at police establishments.
The move follows concerns that the modus operandi adopted by Nabeel in the attack could be replicated by terrorist organisations to target police establishments and personnel.
Armed guards round the clock
Under the revised SOPs, an armed sentry will be deployed at the entrance of every police station 24 hours a day. The main entrance gate will remain closed for general access, with visitors required to use a smaller designated entry gate. The main gate will be opened exclusively for police vehicles.
Visitors will be subjected to security checks and frisking wherever necessary. Duty officers will also be provided with alarm systems to alert personnel during emergencies, while officers assigned to emergency duties will remain armed.
CCTV surveillance intensified
The new guidelines also place greater emphasis on surveillance and controlled public access. CCTV cameras monitoring both the entrances and the interiors of police stations will be kept under continuous observation.
Investigating officers will meet members of the public only in designated common areas or other controlled spaces within police station premises. The move is aimed at reducing security vulnerabilities and ensuring better monitoring of visitor movement.
Terror threats prompt review
The security overhaul follows concerns over potential threats to police establishments and personnel. Pakistani terrorist Shahzad Bhatti and Khalistani terrorist Happy Pasia have previously been linked to targeting police establishments and personnel, both within and outside Punjab.
Officials are understood to be concerned about the possibility of similar attacks being carried out against police infrastructure in the national capital, prompting a review of existing security arrangements.
Delhi has 194 district police stations, including 15 dedicated cybercrime police stations. In addition, the capital has seven railway police stations, 16 metro police stations and two airport police stations.

title: Add ‘high sugar, salt, fat’ warning labels on packaged foods, Supreme Court directs FSSAI
description: The Supreme Court has directed the food safety regulator FSSAI to introduce separate, prominent warning labels for high sugar, high salt, and high fat content in packaged food products.
author: Toufiq Rashid
content:
Add ‘high sugar, salt, fat’ warning labels on packaged foods, Supreme Court directs FSSAI
The Supreme Court has directed the food safety regulator FSSAI to introduce separate, prominent warning labels for high sugar, high salt, and high fat content in packaged food products.
The Supreme Court has directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to introduce separate, prominent warning symbols for high sugar, high salt, and high fat in packaged food products.
It also said that each nutrient of concern must carry its own hexagonal symbol rather than being clubbed together in a single warning.
The warnings must feature a standardised pictorial representation of the nutrient, accompanied by the words HIGH SUGAR, HIGH SALT, or HIGH FAT, as applicable. This means that consumers should be able to identify which specific nutrient makes a product unhealthy, rather than interpreting a combined warning.
"The authority shall ensure that the FOPNL provides for a separate hexagon for each nutrient of concern. Each containing the words high fat, high sugar, high salt, respectively, alongside their corresponding pictograms, rather than a single combined hexagon," the SC directed.
The Supreme Court has also directed that each warning symbol occupies at least 4-5 per cent of the principal display panel of the package, in line with international practices, unless there are explicit reasons to depart from this requirement. FSSAI must also prescribe the font size within the hexagons to ensure the text is prominent, conspicuous, and readily legible under normal purchase and use conditions.
Advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi described the directive as a "landmark development".
"This is certainly a landmark development in the nutritional history of the country, which has brought the right to know the nutritional value of the food product in the center of the fundamental rights of the citizen and the health of the future generation of the country," said Dvivedi, who represented the petitioner, Kerala-based 3S and Our Health Society, before the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court also directed that each warning symbol should occupy at least 4-5 per cent of the package's principal display panel, in line with international practice, unless there are explicit reasons to depart from that requirement. FSSAI has also been instructed to prescribe a minimum font size within the hexagons to ensure that the warnings are prominent, conspicuous, and readily legible under normal purchasing and usage conditions.
These directions form part of the Supreme Court's broader examination of front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FOPNL), which is intended to help consumers identify products high in nutrients associated with diet-related diseases and make more informed food choices.
The apex court has also made an important change to the proposed criteria for determining which products should carry these warnings. It has directed FSSAI to consider total sugar rather than added sugar, and saturated fat rather than added fat, alongside salt. This is significant because the earlier proposal relied on added sugar and added fat, which the court said would not adequately capture the nutrients of concern.
"The FSSAI shall ensure that the FOPNL treats total sugars and saturated fat rather than added sugar and added fat as the nutrients of concern alongside salt in alignment with its own long-standing consensus existing prior to the DGI 2024," the Supreme Court said.
FSSAI has been asked to recalculate the threshold levels for each nutrient rather than simply adopting the values set out in the 2024 Dietary Guidelines for Indians. The court cautioned against setting thresholds so low that almost every packaged product carries a warning, "leading to consumers becoming desensitised to the labels".
At the same time, it said the thresholds should not be so high that products containing excessive amounts of sugar, salt, or saturated fat escape warning labels.
The objective, the court observed, is to provide consumers with meaningful information that helps them distinguish products containing high levels of potentially harmful nutrients.
Four-month timeline for regulations
The Supreme Court accepted FSSAI's submission that approximately four months would be required to complete the regulatory process, including publishing the draft amendment regulations for a 60-day public consultation period, reviewing stakeholder feedback, and issuing the final notification. The court described the proposed timeline as "reasonable".
However, the Supreme Court made it clear that the regulator must adhere strictly to this schedule. It cautioned against delays arising from attempts to secure consensus among all stakeholders, particularly the food industry, public health experts, and consumer groups, whose interests and positions may diverge.
The court further stated that where consensus proves difficult, FSSAI must prioritise the approach that best serves public health and consumer interests.
"Every day of delay means that packaged foods continue to be sold without such labels to the detriment of the right to health, food and informed choice respectively. Any delay in bringing out the draft regulations must therefore be avoided. The FSSAI should anticipate potential impediments and take active measures to ensure that they are resolved or adequately addressed," the SC said.
Nutrition education in schools
The judgment also places emphasis on nutritional literacy, recognising that warning labels alone are unlikely to lead to healthier food choices unless consumers understand the information they convey.
The Supreme Court directed the Union government to ensure the strict implementation of existing regulations, including the 2020 rules, and to strengthen nutrition education in schools. The court said this effort should extend beyond revisions to textbooks and curricula to include interactive workshops along with extracurricular and co-curricular activities that enable children to develop and practise nutritional literacy.
The court has directed its registry to list the matter again after 10 weeks. The FSSAI must submit an affidavit detailing the progress made on the draft regulations within these 10 weeks.
The judgment frames front-of-pack warning labels as more than a packaging requirement, placing them within the state's constitutional responsibility to protect public health and enable consumers to make informed choices.
Speaking to Firstpost, Dr Arun Gupta, paediatrician and convenor of Nutrition Advocacy in Public Interest (NAPi), who has been a leading advocate for mandatory front-of-pack warning labels (FOPWL) in India, described the order as a "win".
"Very good things have been said, and it is a win, but I would like to read the full judgment to understand certain aspects, such as the threshold for each ingredient," said Gupta.
The issue reached the Supreme Court through a public interest petition filed by the Kerala-based 3S and Our Health Society, which sought mandatory warning labels on packaged foods high in fat, sugar, and salt. The Supreme Court has repeatedly expressed concern over delays in introducing the system, particularly in light of the growing burden of obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease. In August, the SC urged FSSAI to make progress on the issue, stressing the need to protect public health, particularly that of children.
Toufiq Rashid is a journalist with over 25 years of experience in print and digital media. She covers health and lifestyle.

title: India leads the world in YouTube video takedowns, ahead of the US: Report
description: YouTube removed 11.15 million videos globally for violating its Community Guidelines in the April-June 2026 quarter, with child safety violations accounting for the largest share
author: Anjaly Raj
content:
India leads the world in YouTube video takedowns, ahead of the US: Report
YouTube removed 11.15 million videos globally for violating its Community Guidelines in the April-June 2026 quarter, with child safety violations accounting for the largest share
Listen to This Article
India accounted for the highest number of videos removed by YouTube for violating its Community Guidelines in the April-June 2026 quarter, according to the latest YouTube Community Guidelines Transparency Report.
The report, which tracks YouTube’s enforcement of its content policies, showed that the video platform removed a total of 11.15 million videos globally during the three months for violating its Community Guidelines.
India was followed by the US, Indonesia, Brazil and Bangladesh, while Pakistan ranked sixth.
The data is based on the country or region of upload, determined by the uploader’s Internet Protocol (IP) address at the time the video was uploaded. YouTube said its Community Guidelines are enforced consistently across the world and that videos removed for violating these policies are taken down globally.
Why did YouTube remove videos?
The report showed that child safety violations accounted for the largest share of video removals, at 68.2 per cent of the total, while harassment and cyberbullying accounted for the second-largest share, at 11.3 per cent.
Also Read
These were followed by violent or graphic content at 5.2 per cent, harmful or dangerous content at 5.1 per cent, and nudity or sexual content at 4.9 per cent.
How does YouTube detect content violations?
YouTube said it relies on a combination of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered systems and human reviewers to enforce its content policies.
Automated systems were the source of first detection for 11 million videos removed during the quarter, while users flagged 123,855 videos and organisations flagged 30,400. A government agency was identified as the source of first detection for one video that was subsequently removed.
YouTube removes 2.73 million channels over policy violations
The quarterly report also highlighted the scale of enforcement against spam and abusive activity on the platform. YouTube removed 2.73 million channels globally during the quarter, with spam, deceptive practices and scams accounting for 84.5 per cent of channel removals.
When a channel is terminated, all videos uploaded to it are removed. As a result, 86.68 million videos were taken down during the quarter as part of channel-level terminations.
Separately, YouTube removed nearly 1.55 billion comments for violating its Community Guidelines during the April-June period. Automated systems accounted for 99.9 per cent of the first detections of comments subsequently removed.
YouTube said its moderation process combines automated detection with human review, particularly for content that requires a deeper understanding of context and nuance. Trained human reviewers assess such material, while their inputs are also used to refine YouTube’s enforcement models.

title: Centre asks Netflix to block streaming of Pakistani content in India
description: The directive came after the I&B Ministry received several complaints and representations regarding the possible release in India of Pakistan-based web series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo'
author: Press Trust of India
content:
Centre asks Netflix to block streaming of Pakistani content in India
The directive came after the I&B Ministry received several complaints and representations regarding the possible release in India of Pakistan-based web series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo'
Listen to This Article
The Information and Broadcasting ministry has received several complaints on the possible India release of Netflix's first Pakistani show "Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo" and has asked it to ensure that content originating in Pakistan is not streamed here, official sources said on Thursday.
The trailer dropped on Tuesday but Netflix is yet to comment on whether the show's December 4 release includes India or is only aimed at Pakistan and other countries. Two cine worker bodies in India have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi asking for a ban.
Sources said the ministry has asked Netflix to adhere to its advisory dated May 8, 2025, and ensure that streaming content originating in Pakistan is not available in India.
The ministry has also asked Netflix to stand by the commitment it gave in June -- when it informed the government that it had made no film or series originating in Pakistan available to subscribers in India -- and maintain the position it conveyed at the time.
The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) have said the show's release in the country would be a violation of the ministry's advisory, following last year's Pahalgam terror attack, when it asked OTT platforms and streaming services to discontinue Pakistani-origin content.
Also Read
In its letter, also marked to Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Netflix India, the AICWA termed Pakistan a "terrorist country" that will never wish well for India.
"After the Pulwama attack, AICWA banned Pakistani artists from working in the Indian film industry. After the Pahalgam attack, the Government of India also imposed restrictions on Pakistani artists and content," stated the letter signed by AICWA president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta.
The AICWA, which states on its website that it is affiliated with the Maharashtra government and works for the rights of the people related to the film industry, went on to say that the release of the series would go directly against the spirit of that advisory and against the sentiments of the nation.
The FWICE, an umbrella body of 32 associations with five lakh members, asked the prime minister to intervene and direct the ministry and other concerned authorities to urgently examine the proposed release of the Pakistani series and take appropriate measures.
The FWICE has also warned that it would "ensure the shoot of all the Netflix projects comes to a halt" if the series is released in India.
"We want to express that we have an objection to the Pakistani show. For us, the country comes first, and Pakistani artists are not welcome," its president B N Tiwari told PTI.
In Pakistan, Planning and Development Minister Ahsan Iqbal used the hashtag #GrowUpIndia to push back and say this amounted to weaponising art and culture.
"First weaponising sports, then water, and now art and culture. The All Indian Cine Workers Association is urging New Delhi to permanently ban Pakistani content. How insecure do you have to be to see a cricket match as a political threat and a television drama as a national security concern? India, grow up," Iqbal said on X.
Created, directed and produced by Momina Duraid, "Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo" adapts Pakistani novelist Farhat Ishtiaq's 2013 bestselling Urdu novel of the same name. It is titled "All the Love Our Hearts Carry" in international markets.
It reunites Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan and Sanam Saeed, all familiar to Indian audiences. It also features other big names in Pakistan's entertainment industry, including Ahad Raza Mir, Iqra Aziz, Hania Aamir and Hamza Ali Abbasi.

title: Constitution Day 2026: History, significance and what leaders said today
description: India marks Constitution Day to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution in 1949. Here's a look at its history, significance and what PM Modi, Amit Shah, Rahul Gandhi said on the occasion
author: Unis Ahmad Dar
content:
Constitution Day 2026: History, significance and what leaders said today
India marks Constitution Day to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution in 1949. Here's a look at its history, significance and what PM Modi, Amit Shah, Rahul Gandhi said on the occasion
Listen to This Article
India observes Constitution Day, or Samvidhan Divas, on November 26 to commemorate the Constituent Assembly's adoption of the Constitution in 1949.
The day honours the framers' vision, particularly that of Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar, and highlights the constitutional values of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity that continue to shape the country's democratic framework.
The Dr Ambedkar Foundation is marking the occasion this year with the theme, "The Constitution @76: Dr BR Ambedkar's Constitutional Vision and the Future of Indian Democracy", at an event in New Delhi.
Why is Constitution Day celebrated on November 26?
The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on November 26, 1949, after nearly three years of deliberations.
The Constitution, however, came into force on January 26, 1950, marking India's transition to a sovereign democratic republic. The date was chosen to honour the Indian National Congress's declaration of Purna Swaraj (complete independence) in 1930.
Also Read
While January 26 is celebrated as Republic Day, November 26 marks the adoption of the Constitution.
In 2015, the government officially designated November 26 as Constitution Day to promote awareness of constitutional values and recognise BR Ambedkar's contribution to drafting the Constitution. Until then, the day was observed as National Law Day.
What is the significance of Constitution Day?
Constitution Day, observed every year on November 26, is more than a commemoration of the adoption of a historic document. It serves as a reminder of the values that hold India's democracy together: constitutional accountability, equality before the law and individual freedoms.
At the heart of the Constitution is the Preamble, which lays down the foundational ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. These principles continue to guide India's democratic institutions and the framework of governance.
The day also encourages citizens to understand their constitutional rights and duties, and to reflect on the responsibilities that come with being part of a democratic society.
PM Modi, other leaders on Constitution Day
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday extended greetings to citizens on Constitution Day, paying homage to Babasaheb BR Ambedkar and the members of the Constituent Assembly.
“The gift they bestowed upon us in the form of the Constitution is a priceless heritage of Indian democracy, one that will continue to guide us in realising the resolve of a ‘Viksit Bharat’,” PM Modi wrote in a post on X.
Home Minister Amit Shah also greeted citizens on the occasion of Constitution Day. In a social media post, Shah paid tribute to Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar, Rajendra Prasad, and all the other distinguished members of the Constituent Assembly who made invaluable contributions to framing the Indian Constitution.
Nitin Nabin is scheduled to address a Constitution Day programme in Patna, highlighting the significance of the Constitution and the legacy of its principal architect, BR Ambedkar.
Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi described the Constitution as the soul of the nation. In his X post, he pledged to “protect it under all circumstances, and keep fighting for every Indian’s rights.”
Congress is set to mark Constitution Day with its nationwide 'Samvidhan Raksha March' campaign, aimed at highlighting what it describes as threats to constitutional values and democratic rights.
Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said the campaign was not about any single political party but about whether India would remain a democracy. He also argued that if a citizen's vote is taken away, other rights guaranteed by the Constitution lose their meaning.
Kharge and Gandhi are scheduled to participate in the party's Lucknow programme.

title: Same units, different electricity bill? When you use power could matter soon as Centre plans to introduce new rules
description: India’s proposed power rules would introduce time-based electricity tariffs for most consumers by April 2029, with agricultural users exempt.
author: Sounak Mukhopadhyay
content:
Electricity charges could vary by time of day for most consumers by April 2029. The Ministry of Power has proposed changes to encourage electricity use when supply is plentiful. Consumers could also be encouraged to shift usage to periods of lower demand. The draft rules are proposed to take effect on April 1, 2027, according to Saur Energy International Magazine. Consumers with maximum demand above 10 kW would move to Time-of-Day tariffs first. Their deadline is April 1, 2028. Other consumers would switch by April 1, 2029, with agricultural consumers exempt. The rates would vary across time slots and apply to the energy charge on bills. State electricity commissions would consider demand patterns and renewable power generation when setting those slots. They would look at both the state and the electricity supplier. The cost of buying power varies throughout the day and across seasons. Commissions would consider those costs, power exchange prices and what existing meters can measure. Consumers who also generate renewable power could face a storage requirement from April 1, 2028. State commissions could require storage equal to at least 20% of the system’s daily generation. A commission could set a different share. Without a specified threshold, the requirement would apply to systems above 10 kW. The draft sets deadlines for new connections and changes to existing ones. Suppliers would have three days in metropolitan and municipal corporation areas. The limit is seven days in other municipal areas and 15 days in rural areas. Rural areas in hilly states and Union Territories would have a 30-day limit. These deadlines apply after consumers submit complete applications. Suppliers could take up to 90 days if they must extend mains or commission substations. They would have to connect the premises immediately after completing that work. Suppliers would have to flag unusually high or low electricity use in their billing systems. This applies when usage exceeds five times the average of the previous six billing cycles. Bills showing consumption below one-fifth of that average would also be flagged. State commissions could set other limits for identifying such cases. Suppliers would have 30 days from the date the electric bill is generated to resolve flagged cases. Consumers could avoid disconnection by paying for average usage over the previous six billing cycles. Those payments would continue until the supplier resolves the issue. The billing safeguards would take effect within six months of the amended rules. They could begin earlier if the supplier is ready. title: Paneer made with laundry whitener, caustic soda? UP raid exposes alleged adulteration unit amid wedding rush
description: Authorities in Uttar Pradesh raided an alleged adulterated paneer unit in Raebareli, where chemicals including optical whitener were reportedly used in production. Officials destroyed 1,500 litres of milk and more than three quintals of paneer.
author: Livemint
content:
Amid rising demand for paneer during the wedding season, authorities in Uttar Pradesh have busted an alleged adulterated paneer manufacturing unit in Raebareli, where a laundry-product optical whitener was allegedly used to make the dairy product.
The Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) raided the unit in Aghaura village, under Bachhrawan police station limits, on Monday night. An FIR has been registered against the owner, Dhirendra Paswan, and six workers under Sections 264 and 265 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), according to a Times of India report.
Officials allegedly found Ranipal optical whitener, refined palmolein oil, citric acid and caustic soda being used to manufacture paneer under unhygienic conditions.
“We have collected samples of all the chemicals used in making adulterated paneer, besides samples of milk and paneer. Around 1,500 litres of milk and over three quintals of paneer were destroyed,” Vineet Kumar Pandey, assistant commissioner, FSDA, told TOI.
Pandey said the wedding season, which drives up paneer demand, creates opportunities for such units to make money by supplying adulterated products.
Consumption of non-food-grade optical whiteners may cause gastrointestinal irritation, nausea and vomiting, depending on their chemical composition and concentration. Caustic soda, meanwhile, can cause severe burns to the mouth, throat, oesophagus and stomach if consumed in sufficiently high concentrations, Pandey warned.
He added that even permitted ingredients such as citric acid and palmolein could constitute adulteration when used to pass off a product as genuine dairy paneer.
Samples collected during the raid will undergo laboratory testing to determine the extent of adulteration.
Earlier this month, the Food Safety and Drug Administration Department in Mathura intercepted 2,500 kg of contaminated and suspicious paneer being brought into the border district from Rajasthan.
Ordering the destruction of the entire consignment, the officials sent samples for testing and arrested the driver of the vehicle transporting the product, they said.
Assistant Commissioner (Food) Jatin Kumar Singh said that given the high demand for khoya and paneer for sweets prepared during the Diwali season, large quantities of substandard khoya, paneer and other food items are being brought into Mathura from neighbouring states -- Rajasthan and Haryana as well as from other districts.
Singh said that on Thursday, the department received information that a large quantity of substandard, synthetic paneer was being transported to Mathura from the Kaman tehsil of Rajasthan's Deeg district.
Acting on the information, two teams were deployed along different routes and around 1.30 am (on the intervening night of Thursday and Friday), they intercepted a suspicious pick-up van near Bathen Gate in the Kosi Kalan area on the Delhi-Agra National Highway.

title: Nandini curd price cut from Nov 29: How much cheaper are 500 g and 1 kg packs?
description: Karnataka’s KMF has cut Nandini curd prices by  ₹2 per kg following a state government directive. From November 29, the 500 g pack will cost  ₹33 and the 1 kg pack  ₹66.
author: Livemint
content:
Following a direction from the Karnataka government, the Karnataka Co-operative Milk Producers' Federation Ltd. (KMF) has reduced the selling price of Nandini curd by ₹2 per kg, with the revised rates coming into effect from November 29.
In an official statement, KMF said the decision was taken in the interest of consumers following a direction from the state government.
Under the revised pricing, the 500 g pack of Nandini curd, which was earlier priced at ₹34, will now cost ₹33. Similarly, the price of the 1 kg pack has been reduced from ₹68 to ₹66.
KMF said it functions on cooperative principles, balancing the interests of consumers and milk producers. For five decades, the federation has been supplying dairy products while supporting the economic empowerment of lakhs of dairy farmers in Karnataka.
It added that the Nandini brand is backed by modern processing technology, quality checks and food safety standards.
According to KMF, following a request from milk producers, the prices of Nandini milk and curd were revised from November 1, 2026. However, the state government subsequently directed the federation to reduce the price of curd by ₹2 per kg in the interest of consumers.
Earlier, the Karnataka Cabinet had approved an increase of ₹8 per litre in Nandini milk prices, effective November 1. KMF also revised curd prices, raising the 1 kg pack from ₹54 to ₹68 and the 500 g pack from ₹28 to ₹34.
The price revision had drawn criticism from consumers, opposition leaders and hotel associations.
The latest reduction will bring the price of the 1 kg curd pack to ₹66 and the 500 g pack to ₹33 from November 29.
(With inputs from ANI)

title: Puri Jagannath Temple resumes inventory of Ratna Bhandar after 48 years
description: Inventory efforts for the Ratna Bhandar at Jagannath Temple have resumed. The initial inventory process, which began in March, was conducted after a 48-year gap. Ongoing activities include counting and weighing valuables in the Bhitar Bhandar, with the entire inventory process was videographed. Gemologists and committee members assist with the inventory process, ensuring accuracy and transparency.
author: ET Online
content:

PTI, citing officials, reported that the inventory began in March this year after 48 years, with the exercise being conducted for 93 hours and 51 minutes over 17 days.

title: J&K Waqf Day: Religious scholars offer repentance prayer for standing during Vande Mataram rendition, MMU
description: A group of Muslim religious scholars in Jammu and Kashmir said they offered prayers of repentance after standing during the rendition of ‘Vande Mataram at the Waqf Boards November 23 event, after videos of the ceremony triggered criticism. The Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama has also objected to the song being played at official functions, arguing that compulsory rendition conflicts with Islamic beliefs and religious freedom.
author: Hakeem Irfan Rashid
content:
The Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama (MMU) Jammu and Kashmir, an umbrella body representing religious organisations and institutions across various schools of Islamic thought, also strongly objected to the playing of 'Vande Mataram' at the 'Waqf Day' ceremony, where Union minister Kiren Rijiju was the chief guest. Waqf board chairperson Darakhshan Andrabi, ruling National Conference MP Mian Altaf and prominent Shia politician Imran Ansari were among those present.
Following the event, a video showing religious scholars standing during the rendition of 'Vande Mataram' went viral on social media, triggering widespread condemnation. Subsequently, a group of preachers, mostly from Jammu, released a video statement saying they had “offered repentance prayers” after the event and had even "recited the Kalima afresh”.
“We offered repentance immediately after the event, as some things that happened there were against Sharia,” said Maulana Farooq from Jammu. Prominent Kashmiri preacher Abdul Rashid Dawoodi said that “standing up for 'Vande Mataram' was a legal compulsion and our hearts were not with it”.
In its statement, the MMU said that while Islam encourages love for one’s homeland, it draws a clear distinction between love for the motherland and its worship or deification.
“Any expression or practice that attributes divinity to the motherland is contrary to the fundamental Islamic belief of Tawheed and is, therefore, un-Islamic and impermissible for Muslims,” the MMU statement read.
The MMU pointed out that the All India Muslim Personal Law Board had also categorically clarified the Islamic position on 'Vande Mataram' and strongly opposed its compulsory rendition on both religious and constitutional grounds.
“It is highly regrettable and unacceptable that 'Vande Mataram' was played at a function organised by the Waqf board itself, an institution entrusted with safeguarding Muslim religious endowments and their sanctity. There was no legal obligation to play 'Vande Mataram' simply because it was an official function, and its rendition was optional. Yet the Waqf board went ahead with it, showing utter disregard for the fundamental religious beliefs and sensitivities of Kashmiri Muslims, which has caused deep hurt and anguish among people,” the statement read.
The MMU also expressed grave concern over the increasingly routine inclusion of 'Vande Mataram' at official government functions across Muslim-majority Jammu and Kashmir, despite the well-known religious reservations of Muslims. “Such imposition disregards their religious convictions and constitutional rights and deepens distrust and alienation,” it said.
The MMU said it was seeking legal opinion on the matter and would also submit a formal representation to the concerned authorities, seeking an immediate end to the forcible imposition of 'Vande Mataram' at government functions, educational institutions and other public events in J&K. It also urged the authorities to respect the constitutionally guaranteed freedom of faith and conscience.

title: Public confidence in judicial authority must be continuously earned through independence: CJI
description: Chief Justice Surya Kant highlighted the significance of engaging with criticism as part of a constitutional democracy. He noted that constitutional governance requires institutions to understand both their authority and limitations. Challenges such as delays and unequal access to legal representation affect citizens' experience in the justice system. The CJI appealed for a justice system that is independent, accessible, and humane in its approach.
author: PTI
content:
New Delhi: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Thursday said a confident institution must have the capacity to engage with criticism without treating every disagreement as a challenge to its authority, underlining that disagreement is not a weakness of a constitutional democracy.
Addressing a Constitution Day function organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) at the apex court lawns, the CJI also said that the Constitution is not tested only during extraordinary political or institutional crises, but it is tested every day.
"It is tested every day, in the ordinary exercise of power. The manner in which an authority treats a vulnerable citizen, the willingness of an institution to acknowledge its limitations, and the readiness to correct an error are all expressions of constitutional commitment," the CJI said.
Also read: Govt plans amendments to ensure time-bound resolution of challenges to arbitral awards
The CJI said a confident institution must have the capacity to engage with criticism without treating every disagreement as a challenge to its authority.
"What matters is that such engagement must remain guided by reasons, professional integrity and respect for institutional processes," he said.
As pointed out by Attorney General R Venkataramani, "it must not be motivated by political agendas or personal gains to attack the institution only because it does not suit you in a particular situation," he said.
He said one often understands the Constitution through its provisions, institutions and distribution of powers.
"These are its essential foundations, but the Constitution must ultimately be judged by what it means to the people whom it governs," the CJI said.
He said constitutional governance requires every institution to remain conscious not only of the authority it possesses, but also of the limits within which that authority must operate.
Also read: Sharad Pawar admitted to Breach Candy hospital in south Mumbai
"Institutional restraint, mutual respect and accountability are therefore essential to the proper functioning of our constitutional democracy. Each institution must discharge its responsibilities with due regard for the constitutional space within which other institutions are expected to function," he said.
The CJI said ultimately, the strength of the Constitution will be measured not simply by the institutions it establishes, but by the confidence it inspires in the citizen.
"Judicial authority is an essential feature of our constitutional system, but public confidence in that authority must be continuously earned through independence, fairness, and consistency. We must also recognise that disagreement is not a weakness of constitutional democracy," he said.
While referring to the challenges facing the justice delivery system, the CJI said pendency, delays and unequal access to legal representation continue to affect the experience of the judiciary for many citizens.
"Behind every case number is a person awaiting the resolution of a dispute, the protection of a right, or the vindication of a claim. The responsibility for improving this situation is shared," he said.
The CJI said courts must continue to strengthen their processes and make justice more accessible, and the Bar must contribute through focused and honest advocacy, responsible case management, and professional discipline.
He said the true tribute to the framers lies not merely in remembering their work, it lies in carrying forward the constitutional responsibilities they entrusted to us.
"Citizens may not remember every judgment or be familiar with every constitutional provision, but they will remember whether they were heard, whether they were treated fairly, and whether the justice system stood by them when they needed it most. That ultimately is the measure of our constitutional commitment," he said.
"Let us continue to work towards a justice system that is independent in its functioning, accessible in its reach, and humane in its approach.The Constitution has given us the framework. Giving life to its promises remains our collective responsibility," the CJI said.
Besides the CJI, the Attorney General, SCBA president and senior advocate Pradeep Kumar Rai and others also addressed the gathering.
Referring to certain issues pointed out by the SCBA president, the CJI said he thinks that periodical training of members of the Bar is a very significant issue.
The CJI said he can assure the Bar members that some structured training program will be introduced in a very short time.
In his address, Venkataramani said it is one matter that we talk of improving administration of justice and ease of justice.
"It is an entirely different matter that we denigrate our justice institutions, our judges, and the supreme value of independence by mindlessly or deliberately challenging it," he said.
"The lawns of the Supreme Court where we have assembled are part of the court and meant to be valued to celebrate the Constitution, not to demean the court. This is not Hyde Park," Venkataramani said.
He said any attempt to devalue the court on any assumed count or to malign the judges must be strongly discouraged and stopped.
"Let no partisan considerations assume self-importance of freedom. Seemingly being independent can invisibly impact the court's ability to be without fear or favour," he said.
Constitution Day, also known as 'Samvidhan Divas', is celebrated in the country on November 26 every year to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India.

title: No Pakistani content in India: Centre reminds Netflix amid ‘Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo’ row
description: Reminding the streaming platform of its earlier advisory, the government has asked Netflix to not release the Fawad Khan-Mahira Khan starrer in India.
author: DH Online
content:
Poster of Netflix's 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo'.
Credit: Instagram/Netflix MENA
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has directed Netflix to ensure that content originating in Pakistan is not made available for streaming in India, in compliance with its May 8, 2025 advisory.
The ministry has asked Netflix to stand by that commitment it gave then and maintain the position it conveyed at the time.
The reminder comes just days after the All India Cine Workers Association has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking a ban on the Pakistani Netflix series.
In a letter dated November 24, signed by Suresh Shyamlal Gupta, President of AICWA, the film body has demanded a complete, permanent ban on the Pakistani drama series, which is commissioned by Netflix MENA, and boasts a star-studded cast.
Directed by Momina Duraid, Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo, internationally titled All The Love Our Hearts Carry, is scheduled to stream on December 4 on Netflix.
