title: SAD-BJP reunion signals retreat from BJP’s Punjab ambitions
description: The SAD-BJP reunion ahead of Punjab's 2027 elections signals a retreat from the BJP's bid for dominance amid rural resistance and lingering farm law anger.
author: Manish Anand
content:
While return of the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) in the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) may reassure the Bharatiya Janata Party, for the oldest ally is back in the fold, the occasion arrives on an ominous note: the BJP’s bid to dominate Punjab politics has vanished four months ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly election.
On Tuesday, Union Minister for Home Affairs Amit Shah shared a dais at the BJP headquarters to welcome Sukhbir Singh Badal, former Punjab Chief Minister and the SAD supremo, back into the NDA. Shah showed no hesitation in declaring that the SAD will be in the role of a “bade bhai” (big brother). Ironically, Badal had said they are “judwa bhai” (twin brothers) in response to a reporter’s question on who will be the lead partner for the Punjab polls. But Shah declared the SAD the big brother in the alliance.
To leave no room for ambiguity, Shah also said on the question of who will be the Chief Minister if the alliance were to win the polls: “I’ve already said in Hindi. Bade bhai means the CM will be from the SAD only.”
The BJP, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Shah at the helm of the party’s affairs, keeps symbolism high. The SAD returned on the day when Punjab and elsewhere Sikhs celebrated Guru Nanak Jayanti. Modi had earlier sported the traditional Punjabi headscarf, as he attended Shabad Kirtan at the Lok Bhavan in Delhi, organised by the city’s Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu.
The SAD founder and former Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal had famously described ties with the BJP as “nau maas ka rishta” (nine-month bond). He had summed up BJP-SAD relations in an apparent emotional phrasing: a bond of blood and flesh.
The BJP-SAD relations had ruptured when the Modi-led dispensation rushed with three contentious farm laws. Fresh with a mammoth majority win in the Lok Sabha in the 2019 general elections, the Modi government seemed sanguine to ideas circulating in the NITI Aayog of central legislations to open up the agriculture sector.
Having won 303 Lok Sabha seats, the BJP approached Parliament with a newfound josh. Time to make big changes had arrived, the party seemed to suggest. In August 2019, Shah had shown that Article 370 could simply be abrogated with the passage of a Bill in Parliament.
Next year, in 2020, the Modi-led government took the Presidential Ordinance route to unveil the three contentious farm laws. The urgency was such that the government didn’t even wait for the Monsoon session of Parliament in September.
For at least three years leading to the promulgation of three contentious farm laws, Ramesh Chand, NITI Aayog Member (Agriculture), argued at any occasion that came his way that agriculture in India is deprived of high growth opportunity because States are not reforming mandis and not freeing land for ease of farming with suitable laws.
On his watch, the NITI Aayog had come out with model Bills to reform agricultural mandis and also for contract farming—The State/UT Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2017, and a similar draft for contract farming, Model Contract Farming, in 2018.
Chand travelled across the country to push the case for the States to adopt the model Bills. Within two years, he started sounding frustrated, as the States’ response didn’t match his josh. Even the BJP-ruled States dragged on committing to the ideas floated by Chand and the NITI Aayog. Chand began saying that India’s agriculture faced roadblocks because States were not pushing with reforms.
But Chand carried weight within the Modi-led dispensation. His long tenure as a member of the NITI Aayog, over a decade, shows his proximity to the Prime Minister. Besides, he was a regular in meetings held by Rashtriya Swayamsewak Sangh (RSS) sympathiser groups.
Harsimrat’s warning and farmers’ protest
In the end, the Prime Minister decided for Central laws to adopt the ideas argued by Chand and the NITI Aayog. Three contentious farm laws first came out as Presidential Ordinances, and when legislative proposals were brought before Parliament, then Union Minister and SAD leader Harsimrat Kaur Badal erupted in anger and anguish. She pleaded with the government to withdraw the Bills. Her speech amid the din in the Lok Sabha almost sounded hysterical, as she warned the government of backlashes.
The government ignored her warnings. The SAD quit the NDA government at the Centre and also left the NDA in September 2020.
The BJP-SAD relations showcased as brotherly Hindu and Sikh ties broke down. Soon, the Modi government understood the import of Harsimrat Kaur Badal’s warning, as farmers from Punjab launched an intense agitation. A year later, Modi realised the political cost of sticking to those farm laws, and appeared on DD News to announce their withdrawal.
In 2022, the BJP contested on 73 Assembly seats. It won two seats. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP score chart read zero in Punjab.
After the 2022 poor show, the BJP embarked on a journey to infuse flesh and blood into the party’s skeleton in Punjab by wholesome imports from the Congress. First, the BJP brought Captain Amarinder Singh, former Punjab Chief Minister. Afterwards, Sunil Jakhar also joined the saffron tent. In between the two prominent faces, the BJP showcased a large number of Sikh leaders joining the party at the national headquarters.
Shah held regular strategy meetings at his residence. Punjab was marked as a State where the BJP’s domination must be established. Punjab had defied Brand Modi. In Ferozepur in 2022, Modi had faced his most embarrassing moments when his cavalcade was stuck on a flyover as farmers blocked the pathway. He spent almost 15 minutes on the flyover.
The Prime Minister abruptly returned to New Delhi without visiting Hussainiwala. He also didn’t attend functions organised for laying foundation stones for development projects in Ferozepur. Dominating Punjab politics for the BJP would, thus, have come as a balm to those embarrassing moments for the Prime Minister. Punjab is among those few States where Modi has gone the least as the Prime Minister of the country.
Shah, as the political sherpa of Modi, had seemingly taken the task to win the Punjab turf for the BJP. Tarun Chugh, BJP leader from Amritsar in Punjab, emerged as Shah’s key aide. Chugh apparently embarked on engineering defections from the ranks of the Aam Aadmi Party in Punjab. The Congress imports into the BJP were not enough for the party to dominate Punjab politics.
In April this year, seven Rajya Sabha MPs of the AAP joined the BJP. The saffron sentiment soared, for AAP’s former Punjab in-charge Raghav Chadha was now in the BJP. More importantly, the BJP seemed to have sensed that the party had grabbed the key to Punjab politics as Sandeep Pathak was part of the flock that joined the saffron outfit. For the AAP, the loss of Pathak was more painful than that of Chadha. Pathak had been AAP’s chief organisational strategist in Punjab. He knew AAP workers in Punjab by their names.
The buzz in the BJP grew afterwards that the party alone is in a position to win Punjab Assembly elections. Arguments came in plenty: the AAP is facing major anti-incumbency, the infighting within the Congress is insurmountable, and many more.
Believing that the BJP actually can write the script of Punjab politics, the BJP even sought to send a subtle message to the people in Punjab: the party has a Sikh face for the CM post. In July this year, Union Minister of State Ravneet Singh Bittu resigned from the government. He was sent to Punjab for full-time focus. Bittu, an import from the Congress, also carries legacy of late Beant Singh, former Punjab Chief Minister who was killed by terrorists.
Bittu hit the deck hard. With Chugh, he began touring the length and breadth of the State. Together, they picked up the issue of drug abuse as the poll pivot. The issue is close to the heart of Chugh, who believes that it can pull away women and elder voters to the BJP from the AAP. A number of yatras were undertaken.
The BJP leaders began noting that the strategy and their outcomes are not shifting from the paper to the ground. The yatras were taken, but the people were mostly onlookers. The AAP imports into the BJP failed to show their earlier skills in rallying the people to their new party.
In the summer of this year, the BJP leaders argued that an alliance with the SAD will undo all the hard work done by the party so far. “The SAD is discredited in Punjab politics. The people associate this party with every menace in the State. The rise of the AAP in Punjab is solely because of the abject failure of the SAD in governance. An alliance with the SAD will automatically transfer the legacy of governance failure to the BJP,” a key BJP strategist engaged in Punjab works said.
A few months later, the BJP leaders began sensing that an alliance with SAD is a necessity because the Jat Sikh in rural Punjab is refusing all outreach of the party. The agrarian Jat Sikh hasn’t yet forgotten those contentious farm laws. They have also not forgotten months spent at the Haryana border, where labels and insinuations were thrown at them as they held out for protests against the farm laws.
Sooner, the buzz in the BJP spoke of a tactical alliance with the SAD: “The BJP will focus on 57 Assembly seats and leave rest for the SAD as a part of a tactical adjustment without a formal alliance.” Punjab has a total of 117 seats in the Assembly.
The past two months have brought sombre notes to the BJP. The rural parts of the country, particularly in the western parts, are turning restive. In Gujarat, farmers held months-long agitation. In Maharashtra, farmers are regularly hitting the street. In Rajasthan, the BJP just suffered a major defeat in the Panchayat elections without a parallel for three decades.
Punjab farmers already have an old battle to settle with the BJP: the pain and suffering on account of the contentious farm laws.
The SAD in 2022 had faced its worst defeat in Punjab elections. In 2024, Bathinda saved blushes for the SAD as Harsimrat Kaur Badal retained the family bastion. The writing on the wall for the SAD also became clear that the 2027 Assembly elections’ key players are the AAP and the Congress. Joining hands with the BJP will help the SAD gain urban Hindu votes. But the BJP seems to have read the sign that the saffron season is waning and the party now needs more allies to meet the challenges.
Manish Anand is a senior Delhi-based journalist, who for over two decades has covered the Indian politics for India’s leading English dailies.

title: Fake Books in Tamil Nadu Libraries Point to a Deeper Institutional Rot
description: Tamil Nadu’s public library scam exposes deep-rooted corruption in book procurement, with thousands of AI-generated and fake books entering library shelves.
author: Ilangovan Rajasekaran
content:
Spurious books, fictitious authors, sham translations, and plagiarised content—the shelves of Tamil Nadu’s public libraries are flooded with AI slop, and the exposé of a massive procurement scam has led to widespread outrage in a State that takes pride in its rich literary, linguistic, and cultural heritage.
On November 6, the well-known Tamil writer Perumal Murugan flagged the issue first in an article on the Tamil online portal Sindhai, in which he expressed shock at the presence of hundreds of such fake books in the recently inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam Library in Coimbatore. Incidentally, Murugan served on a committee that was assigned the task of recommending books for the State’s special libraries in Tiruchi, Madurai, Cuddalore, Salem, and Tirunelveli. The writer, who has been writing on corruption in libraries for quite some time, in his latest article said that these crude AI-generated books had committed “an intellectual fraud” on Tamil society.
Murugan alleged that nearly 1,800 books had been procured from at least one single, and previously unknown, publishing house called Agal Vilakku Publishers, which was not part of the committee’s original list of recommended publishers.
It has also come to light that numerous other books from dubious publishers were procured at exorbitant prices, many of them with questionable International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs).
DVAC probe
The government swung into action after Murugan’s exposé. The School Education Department referred the matter to the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) for investigation, while the Minister for School Education, A. Rajmohan, ordered an inquiry into the procurement process. IAS officer S. Jayanthi was relieved of her charge as Director of Public Libraries.
On the basis of a complaint filed by the School Education Department Secretary, the anti-corruption team held an enquiry and filed a first information report (FIR) before the designated court for anti-corruption on November 15. The Directorate of Public Libraries under the School Education Department has also reportedly ordered the removal of over 70,000 books by these publishers from more than 4,700 libraries across the State.
The police report largely agrees with what Murugan alleged in his article. For instance, he had pointed out that one dubious book claimed that “Naladiyar” was a poet-philosopher; “Naladiyar” is actually the name of an ancient Tamil literary work.
What Murugan exposed in his article is just the tip of the iceberg. The procurement process for books for public libraries has been a contentious issue for decades now. Several writers and publishers have expressed their displeasure on social media and complained about the endemic corruption that vitiates the process.
The publisher Kannan Sundaram of Kalachuvadu Publications, a prominent publishing house, said in a media report that libraries across the State were suffering from the problem of substandard and fake books. “An exhaustive investigation alone can eradicate this menace.”
A Tamil writer, who chose to remain anonymous, said: “It is an attack on the very idea of intellectual creativity and the lofty principles of a diverse democratic society it represents.”
2024 petition and court response
In 2024, the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, while responding to a PIL petition by V. Ramasubbu of Tirunelveli on the procurement of books for state-run libraries, voiced concern and asked the government to revisit its policy.
Following this, the then Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) government issued guidelines through a series of government orders (GOs), including GO No. 69 dated March 7, 2024, of the School Education Department, to ensure transparency in procurement.
It also launched a “Transparent Book Procurement Portal” on March 11, 2024, through the Directorate of Public Libraries. Later, the government issued a special GO No. 250 on November 5, 2025, to procure materials for special libraries in Coimbatore, Tiruchi, Madurai, Cuddalore, and Tirunelveli, and for new libraries in six newly formed districts. It also sanctioned Rs.50 crore each for the purchase of books, e-books, and other materials for its new special libraries through GO No. 198, dated September 3, 2024. Of this, a sum of Rs.30 crore was given as an advance.
The police investigation into the latest scandal, however, has found prima facie evidence of irregularities, illegalities, and procedural violations in book procurement for special libraries and other district libraries that violate these GOs issued to ensure transparent procurement. In other words, a syndicate of middlemen along with a few senior officials in the Directorate of Public Libraries were able to bypass the gatekeeping mechanism.
The police investigation has revealed that what was initially thought to be a scandal confined to the Periyar Arivulagam Library was actually a widespread malaise, involving a much bigger scandal in the bulk procurement process for all public libraries.
The police’s nine-page FIR states that from February 7, 2026, the Directorate of Public Libraries started placing purchase orders with publishers, including the two publishers under the scanner, Agal Vilakku and Phoenix. These two received purchase orders on February 13 and February 14, respectively, and are both owned by a Chennai-based individual named R. Mohan, who was subsequently arrested on November 16, on charges of criminal conspiracy, cheating, fabrication of documents, and criminal breach of trust.
The probe found that the books procured from these two publishing houses were AI-generated and spurious. The two publishers received purchase orders for a total of 1,857 books, and their books were received by the Librarian and Information Officer, Periyar Arivulagam, in two consignments, on February 25 and March 19, respectively. Payments were made before the end of the financial year in March 2026. There seems to have been a hurry to complete the whole exercise, with the State heading into the Assembly election.
The police report details how the two publishing houses cheated the public exchequer in connivance with a “few unknown” officials, whom the police have not named yet.
Phoenix Publications, which supplied spurious English language books, also followed the same modus operandi, with one of its titles a fake book in the name of the famous economist Jean Dreze, titled Democracy and People’s Rights in the Contemporary World. Dreze has categorically denied having written any such book.
A book titled Deepfakes: The Coming Infocalypse, was published under the author names of “Manisha Saravanan” for Agal Vilakku Publishers and “Charulatha Vivek” for Phoenix. However, the original author is Nina Schick, who published the book in 2020 with a unique ISBN number. In fact, some of these fake books received ISBNs only on February 7, the day the High Level Committee on book purchases finalised the list.
It is disturbing to note how easily these two publishing houses were able to procure ISBNs for spurious publications. A total of 94 books supplied to the library received ISBNs on February 4 and February 5. A perusal of the ISBN portal revealed that the publisher listed 418 authors, of whom six were credited with more than 100 books each on a total of 745 unrelated subjects, which was a clear indicator that the books were most likely plagiarised or AI-generated, but no flags were raised. A few books did not even carry an ISBN number.
Rigged procurement process
The entire procurement process appears to have been rigged to benefit two dubious publishing houses. The police have registered cases against Mohan and “unknown officials” under Sections 61 (2), 316(4), 316(5), 318 (2), 336 (1), 336 (3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, or BNS, besides the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, and the Copyright Act, 1957.
The investigation report points to “unknown public servants of the Directorate of Public Libraries of the Chennai Anna Centenary Library and the Coimbatore Periyar Arivulagam Library, and other unknown persons” as having colluded to commit the crime. However, Mohan is the only accused named in the FIR.
Although the police report is silent on the identities of these public servants, the government suspended five senior officers of the Directorate of Public Libraries on the day the FIR was filed. They are S. Kamatchi, Chief Librarian and Information Officer (in-charge), Anna Centenary Library, Chennai; Dinesh Kumar, Chief Librarian and Information Officer (in-charge), Kalaignar Centenary Library, Madurai; V. Santhanakrishnan, Librarian and Information Officer, Kalaignar Centenary Library, Madurai, and In-charge of Periyar Library, Coimbatore; S. Santhana Karthikeyan, Librarian and Information Officer, Anna Centenary Library, Chennai; and J. Juliet, Chief Accounts Officer, Directorate of Public Libraries.
Taken aback by the magnitude of the scam, the DVAC has said in its report that the investigation “is to be extended further to unearth whether other publishers supplied similar books to the public libraries”.
In 2024, when the DMK government decided to popularise the library movement, it took a series of initiatives to modernise and upgrade public libraries and construct new ones to provide the infrastructure and required materials for the modern age. To ensure transparency and address grievances that only a few publishers and authors were being favoured, the government set up a series of committees with domain experts, officials, librarians, scholars, journalists, authors, and publishers. The government issued GOs that laid down the rules and specific tasks of each committee.
The Book Recommendation Committee, with 137 members, was tasked with assessing lists of books and e-books, in English and Tamil, supplied by the Directorate of Public Libraries, and pick titles from these lists. A committee member said: “We were given 700 to 800 titles each and asked to pick the best in the shortest time possible. We had no option but to just browse and forward our lists.”
The lists from the Recommendation Committee was received and analysed by a 13-member Book Selection Committee, chaired by Prof. J. Jeyaranjan, Vice-Chairman, State Planning Commission. The committee also had to recommend academic books, Braille and audio books, and children’s books, both in Tamil and other languages.
The final list was sent to a five-member Book Procurement Negotiation Committee, whose main job was to shortlist the recommendations and negotiate with publishers on the number of copies to be purchased at the best prices. The Negotiation Committee was headed by the Joint Director of the Directorate of Public Libraries and included the Deputy Secretary (Education II), Department of Finance, the Deputy Director, Directorate of Public Libraries, the Principal Audit Officer, Directorate of Public Libraries, the Chief Librarian, Directorate of Public Libraries, and the Principal Librarian, Anna Centenary Library, Chennai.
The last link in the procurement process was a five-member High Level Committee, headed by the Principal Secretary of the School Education Department, with members from the Departments of Finance, Public Libraries, and Tamil Development, and the Tamil Nadu Textbook and Educational Services Corporation (TNTESC), and it took the final call.
The Books Recommendation Committee recommended some 26,000 books. Its members are unaware how fake books not recommended by them found a place in the final list. Many members told Frontline that they were not aware of these “unsolicited insertions”.
According to the DVAC report, apart from the above-mentioned committees, a Coordination Committee was officially formed by the then Director of Public Libraries on November 18, 2025, with officials from the Directorate of Public Libraries, and it had “added books that the Books Recommendation Committee had not recommended and placed them before the Books Selection Committee for consideration and approval”.
This was in clear violation of the procurement process. The police suspect the involvement of a few members of this Coordination Committee in accepting and adding lists from the two dubious publishers. The DVAC said that this gives reasonable grounds to believe that “unknown officials” of the Directorate of Public Libraries had colluded with Mohan and other “unknown publishers” to procure the fake books.
What is still a mystery, however, is how bulk orders from dubious publishers escaped the attention of the High Level Committee. While the new procurement system benefited a few new and small publishers, the two dubious publishing houses cornered a lion’s share of the orders, reportedly worth Rs.1.74 crore. Other deserving publishers were left out. Vasuki Baskar, editor of Neelam Publications, known for its Ambedkarite and Dalit perspectives, said: “We received orders for very few books and for a paltry sum.”
The issue has snowballed into a major controversy, with both the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and the opposition DMK trading charges. The intervention of the higher judiciary has further amplified it.
A two-member bench of Justices G.R. Swaminathan and M.D. Sumathi asked the State government to file a status report on the total purchases made for all State libraries. The bench ordered the issuance of statutory notices to three senior IAS officers, namely B. Chandramohan, former School Education Secretary; S. Jayanthi, former Director of Public Libraries, and M. Aarthi, former Managing Director, TNTESC. “The people at the helm of affairs are bound to answer. Let them explain,” it said.
Clamour for transparency
The anti-corruption team’s initial probe was confined to Mohan, the owner of two of the errant publishing houses, and a few officials. The full extent of fake content that has infiltrated the State’s libraries is yet to be ascertained. To reveal the extent to which the procurement process may have been manipulated, the government must audit all taluk, village, district, and central libraries.
The renowned Tamil writer Cho. Dharman asked the government to “publish the list of all publishers from whom books were purchased and the money paid to them”. Sharing his views on social media, he said that there was no transparency in the procurement of books. He also urged the government to make public the details of the annual International Book Fair, such as its funding and its beneficiaries.
The publisher Badri Seshadri, who runs Kizhakku Pathippagam, told the High Court bench that a Recommendation Committee of eminent personalities would not have suggested books with fake content.
The writer and translator Marudhan said: “A publisher’s credentials must be stored in the procurement databases, which can deter the entry of an unknown publisher like Agal Vilakku.”
Tamil Nadu has 16,871 public libraries, including those run by the State government and local bodies. The Directorate of Public Libraries oversees a network of 4,661 public libraries across the State, which includes State public libraries, district central libraries, branch libraries, and village libraries. The Department of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj administers around 12,000 libraries.
Unless urgent measures are initiated to root out institutional corruption, this painstakingly built intellectual infrastructure of the State could become a symbol of collective shame.

title: From correcting historical wrongdoings to exposing the Opposition’s agenda: 10 takeaways from PM Narendra Modi’s op-ed on the Indian Constitution
description: The Prime Minister described the abrogation of Articles 370 and 35A in 2019 as the correction of a historical wrong. For over 70 years, Article 370 denied the full Constitution to the people of Jammu and Kashmir, particularly trampling over the rights of SC, ST, OBC communities, and women. | OpIndia News
category: Editor's picks, Featured, News Reports, OpIndia Explains
author: Balendu Singh Angad
content:
On Thursday, 26th November, Prime Minister Narendra Modi penned a hard-hitting op-ed on the Indian Constitution, titled “The Constitution – Our guiding force,” coinciding with Constitution Day. In the article, PM Modi paid tribute to the Constitution’s framers and reflected on how the sacred document has transformed his life. He also slammed the Opposition for its anti-constitutional mindset.
From recalling his humble beginnings to exposing the Congress party’s repeated misuse of Article 356, the Prime Minister’s article is a comprehensive critique of those who have historically undermined constitutional values. Here are the 10 biggest takeaways from PM Modi’s op-ed.
A tribute to the framers and the civilisational Roots
The Prime Minister opened his piece by honouring the visionaries of the Constituent Assembly, including Dr. Rajendra Prasad and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar. He emphasised that the genius of these leaders lay in their ability to draw from India’s ancient civilisational wisdom while simultaneously crafting a modern, forward-looking document. For a nation as incredibly diverse as Bharat, the Constitution was envisioned not just as a legal framework, but as a document that resonates with the collective consciousness of its people, far beyond the confines of Parliament and the courts.
Birth no longer determines the limits of one’s future
In a deeply personal reflection, PM Modi recalls growing up in a family of modest means, with “no privileges or advantages of birth.” PM Modi stated that the Constitution is an “inseparable part” of his life journey. He states that it is the Constitution that made it possible for a child like him to one day be entrusted with the responsibility of serving the world’s largest democracy. The Prime Minister asserts that the extraordinary nature of the Indian Constitution lies in the fact that the circumstances of one’s birth no longer determine the limits of one’s future.
Social and economic justice is becoming a lived reality
The Prime Minister cited renowned constitutional scholar Granville Austin. He described the Indian Constitution as “first and foremost a social document.” He highlighted that the quest for social and economic justice is woven into the very fabric of the Constitution. This vision, he asserted, is being realised through transformative welfare schemes. He cited the World Bank’s finding that nearly 50 crore Indians have moved out of poverty. He illustrated how the constitutional promise of dignity acquires meaning through initiatives like PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala Yojana, Ayushman Bharat, and MUDRA loans, which provide tangible economic justice and healthcare security.
Landmark amendments that addressed long-standing demands
The op-ed highlighted several landmark amendments that have strengthened the constitutional framework. The 101st Amendment ushered in GST, the 102nd granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes, and the 103rd provided reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). He addressed the long-overlooked aspirations of economically disadvantaged families outside the existing reservation framework.
Furthermore, the Prime Minister noted that for the first time since 1950, the Constitution is available in all 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule. He also underscored a fundamental shift in the criminal justice system with the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, moving from a colonial emphasis on punishment (Dand) to a citizen-centric pursuit of justice (Nyay).
The Constitution is now closer to every Indian
For the first time since 1950, an updated version of the Constitution is now available in all 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule. IT brings this sacred document closer to the people and makes it more accessible across India. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has noted that the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita has brought about a fundamental shift in the criminal justice system. It moves away from the colonial emphasis on punishment (Dand) and towards a citizen-centric pursuit of justice, or Nyay. This change reflects a broader vision of governance in which laws are not merely instruments of retribution but tools for delivering fairness, dignity and timely justice to citizens.
Power-hungry Congress, Muslim appeasement and onslaught against OBC reservation
In a sharp attack on the Congress, PM Modi criticises how the First Amendment of 1951 restricted fundamental freedoms and how the 42nd Amendment curtailed judicial review. He urges youngsters to study the 38th and 39th Amendments to understand “what a power-hungry and anti-constitutional leadership can do.” The Prime Minister also cites the repeated misuse of Article 356, noting that one party has imposed President’s Rule almost 100 times, with one former Prime Minister alone using the provision more than 50 times to dismiss elected state governments. He said that the Congress party wants to reduce OBC reservation and introduce Muslim reservations. The framers of the Constitution. notably Dr Ambedkar, were strongly opposed.
Correcting historical wrongs: Article 370 and the fight against Naxalism
The Prime Minister described the abrogation of Articles 370 and 35A in 2019 as the correction of a historical wrong. For over 70 years, Article 370 denied the full Constitution to the people of Jammu and Kashmir, particularly trampling over the rights of SC, ST, OBC communities, and women. He also celebrated the successful elimination of Naxalism this year. He stated it has ensured that the poorest of the poor can finally exercise their constitutional rights without fear, while warning against the persistent efforts of “Dimagi Naxals” to derail the nation’s growth.
The opposition as an “Avrodh Paksh,” Not a “Virodh Paksh”
The Prime Minister articulated the constitutional role of the Opposition but lamented that the leading Opposition party has become more of an “Avrodh Paksh” (obstructionist) rather than a “Virodh Paksh” (opposition). He asserted that disrupting democratic processes is no substitute for discharging constitutional responsibilities, signalling a strong rebuke of the disruptive tactics employed by the Opposition in Parliament. He also held the opposition responsible for disallowing legislation aimed at giving women adequate representation in legislative bodies, assuring the “Nari Shakti” of India that no force can prevent justice from being delivered to them.
The duty to vote and the celebration of first-Time voters
In a direct appeal to citizens, PM Modi emphasised the responsibility of strengthening democracy by exercising the right to vote. He urged citizens to never miss the opportunity to vote in national, state, and local elections. To instil this sense of duty early on, he suggested that schools and colleges celebrate Constitution Day by honouring first-time voters turning 18, making them feel like active participants in the process of nation-building.
“India First” in thought and “Kartavya” in action
Concluding his article, PM Modi calls upon citizens to embrace two simple yet powerful principles to build a Viksit Bharat by 2047: “India First” in thought and “Kartavya” (duties) in action. He emphasises that the spirit of Kartavya has already found expression in mass movements from Swachh Bharat to environmental protection, and that with the Constitution as the source of strength, these guiding principles can secure a bright future for generations to come.

title: No Pakistani Content In India, Centre Tells Netflix Ahead Of Fawad Khan Series Release
description: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has told Netflix to keep Pakistani content out of India amid a row over 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo',
author: Arun Dhital
content:
News Brief
Arun Dhital
Nov 26, 2026 | Updated 02:15 PM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has told Netflix to keep Pakistani content out of India amid a row over 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo', the platform's first Pakistani original series, due for global release on 4 December.
Acting on several complaints about the show's possible release in India, the ministry, according to sources, asked Netflix to "honour" its 8 May 2025 advisory directing OTT platforms, streaming services and digital intermediaries to stop carrying Pakistani-origin content.
That advisory, issued on national security grounds after the 22 April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, invoked the Code of Ethics under the IT Rules, 2021. The code asks platforms to be careful with material that could affect India's sovereignty, security, foreign ties or public order.
In June 2025, Netflix had informed the ministry that no Pakistani film or series was available to its Indian subscribers. The ministry said the company "must stand by that commitment".
Also marketed abroad as 'All The Love Our Hearts Carry', the romantic drama is adapted from Pakistani writer Farhat Ishtiaq's bestselling Urdu novel. The cast includes Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan, Hania Aamir and Hamza Ali Abbasi. Commissioned by Netflix's MENA unit, it was filmed in Pakistan, Italy and the UK.
Earlier on Thursday, the All Indian Cine Workers Association demanded that Netflix pull the show from its Indian catalogue before launch, warning of a 'gherao' at the company's India office and a nationwide boycott. It also objected to Netflix giving work to Abbasi, pointing to his past remarks backing Hafiz Saeed, the Lashkar-e-Taiba founder and UN-designated terrorist.
"Pakistan was, is, and will remain a terrorist country. Its series, films, songs, podcasts, and all other content have no place on Indian screens," the association wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Netflix and the ministry.

title: Supreme Court Sets Aside Bihar Government's Remission For Former MP Anand Mohan In 1994 Murder Case
description: The Supreme Court on Thursday (26 November) set aside the Bihar government's decision to grant remission to former MP Anand Mohan, who was convicted i
author: Arun Dhital
content:
News Brief
Arun Dhital
Nov 26, 2026 | Updated 01:46 PM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
The Supreme Court on Thursday (26 November) set aside the Bihar government's decision to grant remission to former MP Anand Mohan, who was convicted in the 1994 killing of Gopalganj District Magistrate G Krishnaiah.
The court held that the state's move to amend its prison manual could not be defended, noting that the government had failed to explain the reasoning behind the change. The amendment, made on 10 April 2023, cleared the way for Mohan's release on 24 April that year.
Mohan has been directed to surrender within a month, and a fresh remission process can begin only after he does so. The court clarified that the state was not barred from granting him remission, provided due process was followed.
It also allowed the petition filed by Krishnaiah's widow challenging Mohan's premature release.
Krishnaiah, a 1985-batch IAS officer of the Bihar cadre, was serving as Gopalganj District Magistrate when he was attacked near Muzaffarpur on 5 December 1994. His car was caught in a crowd accompanying the funeral procession of gangster-turned-politician Chhotan Shukla, who had been killed a day earlier. The officer was pulled out of the vehicle, beaten and shot dead.
Mohan was accused of instigating the mob and was later convicted for his role in the killing. A trial court awarded him the death penalty in 2007, which the Patna High Court reduced to life imprisonment in 2008. The Supreme Court upheld his conviction in 2012.
His release, made possible by the Nitish Kumar government's changes to the state's remission rules, had sparked a political row.

title: European Parliament Blocks Two Indian Ship Recycling Yards At Alang From EU Approved List
description: The European Parliament on Wednesday (25 November) voted 377 to 214, with 24 abstentions, to block a European Commission proposal adding two shipbreak
author: Arun Dhital
content:
News Brief
Arun Dhital
Nov 26, 2026 | Updated 01:33 PM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
The European Parliament on Wednesday (25 November) voted 377 to 214, with 24 abstentions, to block a European Commission proposal adding two shipbreaking yards at Gujarat's Alang to the EU's approved ship recycling list, despite New Delhi's backing.
The yards, YSI Recycling Services LLP and Shree Ram Vessel Scrap Pvt Ltd, operate three plots in the Alang-Sosiya cluster. Parliament's environment committee had rejected it on 4 November.
The Commission must now revisit the draft, and EU member states will vote before a final decision. With the India-EU trade pact due for signing in mid-December, the outcome also leaves 32 more Alang plots awaiting inspection in limbo.
The Commission had proposed the listing on 22 July after independent inspections found both yards compliant with EU ship recycling rules. Commerce Department Additional Secretary Darpan Jain had called it a breakthrough after nearly a decade, one that could make India the first non-OECD country with EU-approved yards.
In August, the Directorate General of Maritime Administration called the draft's claim that Indian law had no procedure for approving recycling plans "factually outdated". It also argued a tidal location alone did not prove non-compliance.
The Gujarat Maritime Board backed both yards, and the Ship Recycling Industries Association (India) credited the "proactive support" of the PMO and shipping authorities for improving compliance.
The objection centres on beaching, where ships are run onto intertidal mudflats for dismantling. Belgian non-profit Shipbreaking Platform, which welcomed the vote, says the practice cannot satisfy EU rules requiring impermeable floors and drainage to contain oil and hazardous materials.
Commission officials had said in October that an intact hull could contain waste during initial cutting under strict procedures.
On 24 November, eight global shipping bodies, including BIMCO, urged MEPs to trust the inspection reports, saying the listing would widen recycling options for large vessels.

title: COP31 collapses: The first climate summit without a deal since 2009
description: The climate summit has concluded without any overarching political agreement. Fossil fuels have been left off the table entirely. Adaptation finance is gone and India has not signed up to the electrification pledge.
author: Samarth Grover
content:
The climate summit has concluded without any overarching political agreement. Fossil fuels have been left off the table entirely. Adaptation finance is gone and India has not signed up to the electrification pledge.
The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) in Antalya, Turkey, ended without an overarching political agreement, the first time this has happened since the 2009 Copenhagen summit. The European Union and several other countries rejected the final proposal from the Turkish and Australian COP leadership, which avoided naming fossil fuels or calling for their phase-out.
That is a retreat from COP28 in Dubai, where countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels. Since then, Saudi Arabia, Russia and other petrol states have resisted turning that commitment into action, while carbon capture, an expensive and energy-intensive technology, gained prominence.
The other fault line was over adaptation finance. A proposed target of $120 billion a year for adaptation finance by 2035 was dropped, with no clarity on when or how funds would reach vulnerable countries.
Turkey also pushed to raise electricity’s share of total consumption from 21% to 35% by 2035. Nearly 100 countries signed a separate pledge backing it. India did not, arguing that countries should choose their own energy pathways.
With COP32 in Ethiopia next, the question is whether countries will find their courage before it's too late.

title: How CBI Coordinated UAE Deportation Of Murder Accused
description: The CBI successfully coordinated the deportation of Sujith Kumar, a fugitive wanted in a Kerala murder case, from the UAE. Kumar was brought back to India on November 25 after extensive collaboration between various Indian ministries and the Kerala Police. He is accused of a 2008 murder and was apprehended following an INTERPOL Red Notice.
author: Text Feed
content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation successfully orchestrated the deportation of Sujith Kumar, a fugitive wanted in a 2008 Kerala murder case, from the UAE, highlighting effective international law enforcement cooperation.
Key Points
- Wanted fugitive Sujith Kumar was deported from the UAE to India on November 25 by the CBI in connection with a murder case.
- Kumar is accused in an October 2008 murder case registered by the Kerala Police, where he and others allegedly attacked a victim who later succumbed to injuries.
- The deportation was a result of coordination between the CBI, Ministry of External Affairs, Ministry of Home Affairs, and Kerala Police, following an INTERPOL Red Notice.
- UAE authorities geo-located and arrested Kumar, subsequently agreeing to his deportation to India after due legal process.
- The CBI, acting as India's National Central Bureau for INTERPOL, has facilitated the return of over 300 wanted criminals since 2019.
The CBI has secured the deportation of wanted fugitive Sujith Kumar from the UAE in connection with a murder case registered by the Kerala Police, officials said on Thursday.
Kumar, who had been absconding for a long time, was brought to India on November 25 following coordination between the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Ministry of External Affairs, the Ministry of Home Affairs, and the Kerala Police, an official statement said.
Details Of The 2008 Murder Case
According to the CBI, the case relates to an incident in October 2008, when Kumar and other accused persons allegedly formed an unlawful assembly armed with deadly weapons and attacked a victim due to previous enmity.
The assailants inflicted multiple injuries on the victim, who was conversing with the complainant on the roadside. He succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment at a hospital on the same day.
"A chargesheet has already been filed before the competent Court," the statement said.
International Cooperation For Deportation
At the request of the Kerala Police, the CBI's National Central Bureau (NCB), New Delhi, obtained an INTERPOL Red Notice against Kumar.
Subsequently, UAE authorities geo-located and arrested him.
"Following due legal process, the UAE authorities agreed to deport the subject to India," the statement said.
With coordination by the CBI, an escort team from the Kerala Police travelled to the UAE, where Kumar was handed over to Indian authorities.
The team, along with the fugitive, arrived in Kochi on November 25.
CBI's Role In Bringing Fugitives To Justice
The CBI, as India's National Central Bureau for INTERPOL, coordinates with law enforcement agencies across the country through BHARATPOL to facilitate international police cooperation.
Since 2019, over 300 wanted criminals, including 76 fugitives during 2026, have so far been successfully brought back to India through INTERPOL channels, the statement added.

title: Kerala Court Convicts Man In Brutal Murder, Child Abandonment Case
description: A court in Kerala has found Manjunath P R guilty of murdering his second wife, Shobha, in 2017 and abandoning her two young children on a train. The case, which inspired the Malayalam film 'Uyir', also uncovered the alleged murder of Shobha's first husband. The sentence for Manjunath will be pronounced on Friday.
author: Text Feed
content:
A Kerala court has delivered a guilty verdict against Manjunath P R for the 2017 murder of his second wife and the subsequent abandonment of her children, a chilling case that later inspired the Malayalam film 'Uyir'.
Key Points
- A court on Thursday found Manjunath P R guilty of murdering his second wife in 2017 at Iritty, Kerala.
- Manjunath was also convicted for abandoning Shobha's two young children on a Mumbai-bound train in Bengaluru.
- The murder case later inspired the Malayalam film 'Uyir', which was released in June this year.
- The investigation revealed Manjunath allegedly killed Shobha after she threatened to expose their involvement in the murder of her first husband, Raju, in 2015.
A court on Thursday found a Karnataka man guilty of murdering his second wife in 2017 at Iritty here and abandoning her two young children on a train.
The sentence will be pronounced on Friday.
The murder case later inspired the Malayalam film 'Uyir', starring Roshan Mathew, which was released in June this year.
Conviction And Charges In The Iritty Murder Case
Thalassery Additional District Judge Denny C J found Manjunath P R guilty of offences under Sections 302 (murder) and 201 (causing disappearance of evidence) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 75 (cruelty to children) of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.
The accused was remanded to judicial custody and sent to the Central Prison, Kannur.
The case relates to the murder of Shobha, a nomadic woman from Tumakuru in Karnataka, whose decomposed body was found in a well near the old Iritty bridge on January 21, 2017.
A case was initially registered as an unnatural death before the investigation established that she had been strangled and her body dumped in the well.
Unravelling The Crime And Child Abandonment
According to the prosecution, Manjunath and Shobha had been living together with her two children while moving around parts of Wayanad and Kannur, earning their livelihood through begging.
Manjunath decided to kill her after she opposed his return to his native place in Karnataka and threatened to reveal their involvement in the murder of her first husband, Raju.
Investigators found that Manjunath had allegedly strangled Shobha on January 14, 2017, and dumped her body in a well. After the murder, he took Shobha's two children, then aged five and four, to Bengaluru.
On January 17, he allegedly abandoned them in a Mumbai-bound train at the city's Majestic railway station before fleeing.
The children were later traced in Mumbai following an investigation led by the then probationary Sub-Inspector Anshad S, who is now a Circle Inspector with Thrissur East police.
Discovery Of A Previous Murder
The investigation also brought to light the alleged murder of Shobha's first husband, Raju, in Karnataka on December 21, 2015.
According to the investigation, Shobha and Manjunath had allegedly strangled Raju in a forest area at Unchinaluhalla in Tumakuru district and set his body on fire. That case is being dealt with separately by the Karnataka police.

title: How Police Cracked Rs 25 Lakh Cyber Fraud Case
description: Two men have been arrested from Lucknow in connection with a Rs 25 lakh cyber fraud. A company representative was allegedly cheated after inadvertently transferring Rs 25 lakh instead of Rs 2.5 lakh for travel services. Police have recovered Rs 15 lakh and seized various items related to the fraud.
author: Text Feed
content:
Police have arrested two individuals in Lucknow in connection with a Rs 25 lakh cyber fraud where a company representative was duped after an accidental over-transfer for travel services.
Key Points
- Two men, Buddan Ramjanam Yadav and Gautam Yadav, were arrested from Lucknow on Thursday in connection with a Rs 25 lakh cyber fraud.
- A company representative was allegedly cheated after inadvertently transferring Rs 25 lakh instead of Rs 2.5 lakh for travel services.
- Police investigation involved analysing financial transactions, bank accounts, and call detail records to trace the money trail.
- The defrauded amount was transferred to various accounts and used to purchase gold jewellery.
- Police have recovered Rs 15 lakh of the defrauded amount and seized three mobile phones, eight SIM cards, seven ATM cards, two cheque books, and one gold chain.
Two men have been arrested from Lucknow in connection with a Rs 25 lakh cyber fraud in which a company representative was allegedly cheated on the pretext of providing travel services, police said on Thursday.
The accused have been identified as Buddan Ramjanam Yadav alias Shrikesh (32) and Gautam Yadav (22), both residents of Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh, they said.
Details Of The Cyber Fraud
Police said the complainant, a chartered accountant and authorised representative of a company, was searching for travel services for his firm when he finalised a deal with some people.
He was asked to pay an advance of Rs 2.5 lakh and was provided with the bank account details of Shrikishun Travels. However, he inadvertently transferred Rs 25 lakh instead of Rs 2.5 lakh, following which the recipients allegedly became unresponsive, police in a statement said.
Police Investigation And Recovery
A case was registered at the Cyber Police Station in Shahdara on October 7, following which a team was formed to trace the accused and recover the money.
"During the investigation, police analysed financial transactions, bank accounts, call detail records and mobile numbers linked to the case. It emerged that Rs 20 lakh was transferred to an account of Shiva Traders through two transactions of Rs 15 lakh and Rs 5 lakh, while Rs 2 lakh was transferred to another account," read the statement.
The remaining Rs 3 lakh was used to purchase gold jewellery from a jeweller in Lucknow through a point-of-sale machine, it read.
According to police, Yadav withdrew Rs 20 lakh through a cheque from a second-layer bank account and handed over the cash to his associates. He also purchased two gold chains worth Rs 3 lakh and handed them over to his associates in exchange for a 20 per cent commission.
Gautam allegedly facilitated the fraud by providing a SIM card registered in his name, which was linked to the first-layer bank account. Police have recovered three mobile phones, eight SIM cards, seven ATM cards, two cheque books and one gold chain. An amount of Rs 15 lakh has also been recovered and refunded to the complainant, read the statement. Further investigation is underway.

title: Sharad Pawar Admitted To Mumbais Breach Candy Due To Dehydration; Third Hospitalisation This Month
description: NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar's daughter and MP Supriya Sule confirmed the development on X, stating that he needed to reduce his travel and workload. The 85-year-old former Union minister had undergone hospitalisation twice earlier this month.
author: Sapna Dodmani
content:
Mumbai: Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) chief Sharad Pawar was once again admitted to Mumbai's Breach Candy Hospital on Thursday due to dehydration.
Supriya Sule Confirms Hospitalisation
NCP (SP) leader and MP Supriya Sule confirmed the latest development. Taking to her X account, Sule wrote, “We are admitting Baba to Breach Candy Hospital. It appears to be dehydration. He needs to slow down and travel less, but Baba just doesn't listen. He loves his work far too much. Thank you all for your concern and good wishes.”
Previous Hospitalisations In November
This is the third time this month that Pawar has been admitted to a hospital.
The 85-year-old former Union minister was initially admitted to Pune’s Ruby Hall Clinic on November 2 and discharged on November 4. On the same day, he was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai and discharged on November 7.
However, no further details regarding his health have been released following his hospitalisation on Thursday.

title: Bring My Boy Back: Mother Breaks Down After Son Dies In Punes Bopdev Ghat Crash
description: The family of 20-year-old engineering student Siddhesh Raje, who died after a speeding goods vehicle rammed into students waiting at a bus stop near Trinity College of Engineering and Research in Yewalewadi on Wednesday, has demanded financial assistance for the bereaved families and urgent road safety measures at the accident spot
author: Varad Bhatkhande
content:
Pune: The family of 20-year-old engineering student Siddhesh Raje, who died after a speeding goods vehicle rammed into students waiting at a bus stop near Trinity College of Engineering and Research in Yewalewadi on Wednesday, has demanded financial assistance for the bereaved families and urgent road safety measures at the accident spot.
The family, who reside in Walhekarwadi in Pimpri-Chinchwad, said Siddhesh had been their only son and that they had taken loans to support his engineering education.
CCTV of the incident:
Siddhesh's father, a farmer, had taken loans to fund his engineering education and moved his family to Pune so that his only son could study. Siddhesh was in the third year of computer science engineering and hoped to join a multinational company after completing his course.
The family hoped he would secure a job after graduation and help repay the education loans.
Photo of Siddhesh Raje, who died in Bopdev Ghat accident on 25th November | Sourced
His uncle, Dr Sachin Raje, said financial assistance from the government would help the bereaved families deal with immediate difficulties, although it could never compensate for their loss.
"There is no point arguing now over whose fault it is. That is a separate matter. But a blessing that was within reach has been lost. The boy had studied so hard, and he was just beginning to build his future," he said.
Family Demands Speed-Control Measures
The family has urged the administration to introduce speed-control measures on the stretch where vehicles descend from Bopdev Ghat.
Siddhesh's father, Jayprakash Raje, said his son had appeared for his first examination paper on Wednesday and was waiting at the bus stop to return home when the accident occurred.
"The vehicle came down at high speed and hit the boys. Even after the accident, the driver argued with local residents. Our only request to the administration is to control the speed of vehicles and introduce measures such as speed breakers. This is not an issue limited to one day. Something or the other keeps happening there," he said.
Sachin also urged the authorities to introduce safety measures similar to those implemented at Navale Bridge.
Student Travelled Eight Hours Daily to Save Money
Siddhesh's friend Jaysingh Rajput said the student had stayed in a hostel for two years but began commuting daily this year because of the family's financial difficulties.
He had purchased a six-month travel pass worth ₹3,000 to reduce his expenses. He travelled around four hours each way between home and college, spending nearly eight hours commuting every day.
Rajput said Siddhesh's mother had to divide her time between Pune and the village.
"He always wanted to do something for his parents. He knew about their financial difficulties and wanted to start earning soon. He had dreams of supporting his family," Rajput said.
He demanded strict action against the driver and alleged that the latter was driving rashly and at high speed, disputing claims that a mechanical failure had caused the accident.
Uncle Raises Concerns Over Emergency Response Awareness
Sachin also raised concerns about the lack of public awareness of emergency medical services and the importance of treatment during the golden hour after an accident.
He said neither the students nor the teachers at the spot appeared to know about the 108 ambulance service. He argued that greater awareness of emergency numbers and immediate medical intervention could have helped the injured students.
"The government provides the 108 ambulance service, but people must know that they can call it and get medical assistance at the accident spot. There should be awareness about golden-hour management. Even displays mentioning emergency numbers such as 100, 112, 101 and, most importantly, 108 should be put up at prominent locations," he said.
He urged the administration to conduct awareness programmes in educational institutions and public places.
However, the sequence of emergency calls, ambulance response time and medical assistance provided immediately after the accident remain unclear.
Parents Struggle to Cope With Loss
Siddhesh's mother, Jayashri Raje, was inconsolable.
"Bring my boy back to me. I do not want anything else from anyone. I have been waiting since yesterday, thinking he would return home," she said.
Jayaprakash said Siddhesh was their only child and the family had placed all its hopes in his education and future.
He also said that no one from the administration or the Guardian Minister's office had contacted the family regarding financial assistance at the time of the interview.
The accident occurred around 2.30 pm when the goods vehicle travelling downhill from Bopdev Ghat reportedly hit a car before losing control and crashing into the students. Three students, including Siddhesh, died, while two others sustained injuries.
The police have taken the 22-year-old driver, identified as Pratik Maruti Chavan, into custody. The preliminary police account indicates that the driver lost control of the vehicle while speeding. The exact cause of the accident, including claims of mechanical failure, remains to be established.

title: Setback For Lalu Yadav, Family As Delhi HC Upholds Charges In IRCTC Case
description: The trial court had observed that the land and share transactions in the case could potentially be an example of “crony capitalism”, allegedly facilitated under the pretext of inviting private participation in the Railways' hotel projects in Ranchi and Puri.
author: Vinay Mishra
content:
In a setback to RJD chief Lalu Yadav and his family, the Delhi High Court on Thursday rejected their pleas against the framing of charges against them in the corruption case linked to the IRCTC scam investigated by the CBI.
Justice Surya Kanta Sharma also dismissed the pleas of the other accused in the cases.
Charges framed against 14 accused
In October last year, the trial court had framed charges against Lalu Yadav, Rabri Devi, Tejashwi Yadav and 11 others.
The accused were charged with cheating and criminal conspiracy.
"A common charge is directed to be framed against all (14) accused under section 120B (criminal conspiracy) IPC read with section 420 IPC and section 13(2) read with section 13(1)(d)(ii) and (iii) PC Act," the trial court order read.
Trial court's observations on transactions
The trial court had observed that the land and share transactions in the case could potentially be an example of “crony capitalism”, allegedly facilitated under the pretext of inviting private participation in the Railways' hotel projects in Ranchi and Puri.

title: Mandar Kiwale : जमिनीच्या वादातून एका वर्षापूर्वी शुभमला संपवलं, बदला म्हणून कोर्टाबाहेर हल्ला; मंदारची स्थिती बघून उपस्थितांच्या अंगावर काटा
description: Pune Mandar Kiwale Attack Case : कात्रजमधील संतोषनगर येथे राहणारा शुभम सुभाष चव्हाण (वय २८) याचा २० एप्रिल २०२५ रोजी जमिनीच्या वादातून खून झाला होता. चव्हाण कुटुंबाने २०२१ मध्ये घराशेजारी दोन गुंठे जागा खरेदी केली होती.
author: Prashant Patil
content:
Pune Mandar Kiwale Attack Case : कात्रजमधील संतोषनगर येथे राहणारा शुभम सुभाष चव्हाण (वय २८) याचा २० एप्रिल २०२५ रोजी जमिनीच्या वादातून खून झाला होता. चव्हाण कुटुंबाने २०२१ मध्ये घराशेजारी दोन गुंठे जागा खरेदी केली होती.
प्रशांत श्रीमंदिलकर, पुणे : जमिनीच्या वादातून झालेल्या शुभम चव्हाणच्या खुनाचा बदला घेण्यासाठीच शिवाजीनगर न्यायालयाबाहेर मंदार किवळे याच्यावर जीवघेणा हल्ला करण्यात आल्याचा संशय पोलिसांकडून व्यक्त केला जात आहे. भरदिवसा न्यायालयाच्या प्रवेशद्वाराबाहेर गोळीबार करून कोयत्याने सपासप वार करण्यात आल्याने पुण्यातील कायदा-सुव्यवस्थेचा प्रश्न पुन्हा ऐरणीवर आला आहे. विशेष म्हणजे, हल्ल्यानंतर आरोपींनी ‘शुभम दादा, तुझ्या खुनाचा आम्ही बदला घेतला आहे, आम्हीच कात्रजचे राजे आहोत’, अशी घोषणा दिल्याची माहिती समोर आली आहे.
जमिनीच्या वादातून शुभम चव्हाणची हत्या
कात्रजमधील संतोषनगर येथे राहणारा शुभम सुभाष चव्हाण (वय २८) याचा २० एप्रिल २०२५ रोजी जमिनीच्या वादातून खून झाला होता. चव्हाण कुटुंबाने २०२१ मध्ये घराशेजारी दोन गुंठे जागा खरेदी केली होती. या जागेवर मालकी हक्काचा फलक लावणे आणि पत्र्याचे शेड उभारण्यावरून एप्रिल २०२५ मध्ये वाद निर्माण झाला. १९ एप्रिलला हा वाद विकोपाला गेल्यानंतर दुसऱ्या दिवशी म्हणजेड २० एप्रिल रोजी पहाटे सुमारे २.४५ वाजता चौघांच्या टोळक्याने शुभमवर लाकडी बांबू आणि काठ्यांनी हल्ला केला. या हल्ल्यात त्याचा मृत्यू झाला.
या खून प्रकरणात आंबेगाव पोलिसांनी मंदार किवळे याच्यासह चार जणांना अटक केली होती. त्यानंतर न्यायालयीन कोठडीत असलेला मंदार काही दिवसांपूर्वी जामिनावर बाहेर आला होता. मात्र, त्याच्या सुटकेनंतर काही दिवसांतच शिवाजीनगर जिल्हा न्यायालयाच्या गेट क्रमांक चारबाहेर त्याच्यावर हल्ला करण्यात आला. काल बुधवारी रोजी दुपारी सव्वा एकच्या सुमारास चार ते पाच हल्लेखोरांनी मंदारला लक्ष्य केले. प्रथम गोळीबाराचा प्रयत्न करण्यात आला आणि त्यानंतर कोयत्याने वार करण्यात आले. या हल्ल्यात मंदार गंभीर जखमी झाला असून त्याच्यावर रुग्णालयात उपचार सुरू आहेत.
पिस्तुलातून 'मिस फायर'
दरम्यान, या घटनेप्रकरणी पोलिसांनी सहा संशयितांना ताब्यात घेतलं असून, हल्ल्यामागे शुभमच्या खुनाचा बदला घेण्याची भावना होती का? याचा तपास सुरू आहे. दोन गुन्ह्यांमधील वैरातून न्यायालयाच्या परिसरातच हिंसक संघर्ष उफाळल्यानं शहरातील गुन्हेगारी टोळ्यांच्या वाढत्या मुजोरीवर प्रश्नचिन्ह उपस्थित झालं आहे. काल बुधवारी दुपारी कोर्टाच्या बाहेर दोन दुचाकीवरून आलेल्या सहाजणांनी किवळे याच्यावर पिस्तुलातून गोळीबार केला. पिस्तुलातून 'मिस फायर' झाल्यामुळे त्याला गोळी लागली नाही. मात्र हल्लेखोरांनी त्यांच्याजवळील असलेल्या कोयत्याने मंदार किवळेवर सपासप वार केले. हे वार इतके तीक्ष्ण होते की किवळे याचे दोन्ही हात जवळपास शरीरापासून वेगळे झाले होते. हल्ला केल्यानंतर तात्काळ हल्लेखोरांनी घटनास्थळावरून पळ काढला होता.
लेखकाबद्दलप्रशांत पाटीलप्रशांत पाटील 'महाराष्ट्र टाईम्स ऑनलाईन'(TIL) या आघाडीच्या डिजिटल माध्यम समूहात सीनियर डिजिटल कंन्टेट प्रोड्युसर पदावर कार्यरत आहेत. पुणे जिल्ह्यातील नामांकित 'थोडक्यात' न्यूज वेब पोर्टल, हैदराबादमधील 'आधान शॉर्ट न्यूज अॅप', 'सकाळ मिडिया ग्रुप' आणि आता 'महाराष्ट्र टाइम्स ऑनलाईन', असा जवळपास पाच ते साडेपाच वर्षांपेक्षा अधिक काळ ते कार्यरत आहेत. प्रशांत पाटील यांना महाराष्ट्रातील ग्रामीण भागातील सर्व गुन्हेगारी, अपघात, शेतकरी विषयक बातम्या, ग्रामीण भागात यश संपादन केलेल्या तरुणी किंवा तरुणांच्या सक्सेस स्टोरीज् आणि महाराष्ट्र हायपर लोकल अशा विविध विषयांची आवड आहे. ऑगस्ट (2026) पासून 'महाराष्ट्र टाईम्स ऑनलाईन'साठी (TIL) काम करत आहेत. या दरम्यान, राज्यातील विधानसभा, लोकसभा आणि स्थानिक स्वराज्य संस्थाच्या निवडणुकींच्या बातम्यांवर विशेष लक्ष ठेवतात. याआधीही त्यांनी याच माध्यम समूहासोबत तीन वर्ष काम केलं आहे.
प्रशांत पाटील यांनी पुण्यातील नामांकित आबासाहेब गरवारे महाविद्यालयातून मास कम्युनिकेशन विषयात पदव्युत्तर शिक्षण घेतलं आहे. शिक्षण घेत असतानाच त्यांनी 'थोडक्यात' या न्यूज वेब पोर्टलला काम केलं. तिथे डिजिटल माध्यमासाठी लेखन करत असताना त्यांना डिजिटल क्षेत्रातलं कसं काम करतात? हे यश संपादन केलं. त्यानंतर त्यांना मुंबईत 'महाराष्ट्र टाइम्य ऑनलाईन' (TIL) या नामांकित माध्यम समूहामध्ये काम करण्याची संधी मिळाली. 28 मार्च 2022 रोजी ते 'महाराष्ट्र टाइम्स ऑनलाईन' या मोठ्या ब्रँण्डसोबत पहिल्यांदा जोडले गेले. तिथे त्यांनी प्रदीर्घ काळ म्हणजे तीन वर्ष डिजिटल विभागात काम केलं. त्यांनतर त्यांनी फेब्रुवारी 2025 ला 'सकाळ मिडिया ग्रुप'ला काम करण्याची संधी मिळाली. परंतु तिथे ते काम करत असताना त्यांना पुन्हा 'महाराष्ट्र टाइम्स ऑनलाईन' (TIL) या माध्यम समूहाने संधी दिली. त्यानंतर ऑगस्ट 2026 पासून प्रशांत पाटील हे 'महाराष्ट्र टाइम्स ऑनलाईन'सोबत (TIL) काम करताय.
'महाराष्ट्र टाइम्स ऑनलाईन'मध्ये (TIL) काम करताना त्यांना खूप मोठमोठ्या संध्या मिळाल्या. जसे की, व्हिडिओ करणे, महाराष्ट्रातील संपूर्ण जिल्ह्यातील रिपोर्टर यांच्याशी समन्वय साधणे, जिल्हा प्रतिनिधींकडून वेळोवेळी काम करुन घेणे, विशेष आणि काही महत्वाच्या बातम्या मागवून घेणे, अशा बऱ्याच गोष्टींची त्यांना इथे मिळाली. प्रशांत पाटील हे सकाळच्या शिफ्टला काम करत असताना लाईव्ह ब्लॉग, रिपोर्टरशी बोलणे, ब्रेकिंग बातम्या, हायपर लोकल बातम्या, ग्रामीण भागातील सर्व घडामोडींकडे लक्ष देण्याचं काम ते करतात.... आणखी वाचा

title: Pune Mandar Kiwale Case: पुण्यात भरदिवसा तरुणावर हल्ला; घटनेची न्यायाधीशांनी घेतली गंभीर दखल, थेट पोलीस आयुक्तांना कोर्टात पाचारण
description: Pune Mandar Kiwale Case: न्यायालय परिसरातील कायदा आणि सुव्यवस्थेची परिस्थिती, तसेच न्यायालयाच्या सुरक्षेच्या प्रश्नावर पोलीस आयुक्त अमितेश कुमार यांच्याशी चर्चा केली जाणार आहे. न्यायालयाच्या आवारात व परिसरात वकील, पक्षकार, न्यायालयीन कर्मचारी आणि नागरिकांची मोठ्या प्रमाणात वर्दळ असते. अशा संवेदनशील ठिकाणी भरदिवसा गोळीबार आणि कोयत्याने हल्ला होणे ही अत्यंत गंभीर बाब मानली जात आहे.
author: Akshay Shitole
content:
Pune Crime News: न्यायालयासारख्या महत्त्वाच्या ठिकाणीच कायदा-सुव्यवस्थेचा प्रश्न निर्माण झाल्याने आता पोलीस प्रशासन कोणती ठोस पावले उचलणार, याकडे लक्ष लागले आहे.
पुणे : शिवाजीनगर येथील पुणे जिल्हा सत्र न्यायालयाच्या प्रवेशद्वाराबाहेरच काल दिवसाढवळ्या सहा जणांच्या टोळक्याने खुनाच्या गुन्ह्यात जामिनावर कोठडीबाहेर आलेल्या तरुणावर गोळीबार व कोयत्याने सपासप वार करून त्याचा खून करण्याचा प्रयत्न केला. या क्रूर हल्ल्यात तरुणाचे दोन्ही हात गंभीर जखमी झाले असून, डाव्या हाताचा पंजा मनगटापासून वेगळा होऊन लोंबकळत होता. त्याच्या हाताला आणि पाठीला गोळी घासून गेली. हल्ल्यानंतर टोळके दोन दुचाकींवरून हातात कोयते हवेत नाचवून ‘आम्ही कात्रजचे भाई, आमच्या नादी लागू नका,’ असे म्हणत पसार झाले होते. मंदार मारुती किवळे (३५) असे जखमी तरुणाचे नाव आहे. या धक्कादायक घटनेची न्यायालयाने गंभीर दखल घेतली असून न्यायालयाच्या परिसरातच अशा प्रकारची जीवघेणी घटना घडल्याने सुरक्षेचा प्रश्न ऐरणीवर आला आहे. या पार्श्वभूमीवर पुणे प्रधान जिल्हा व सत्र न्यायाधीश अंजू शेंडे यांनी पुण्याचे पोलीस आयुक्त अमितेश कुमार यांना न्यायालयात पाचारण केले आहे.
न्यायालय परिसरातील कायदा आणि सुव्यवस्थेची परिस्थिती, तसेच न्यायालयाच्या सुरक्षेच्या प्रश्नावर पोलीस आयुक्त अमितेश कुमार यांच्याशी चर्चा केली जाणार आहे. न्यायालयाच्या आवारात व परिसरात वकील, पक्षकार, न्यायालयीन कर्मचारी आणि नागरिकांची मोठ्या प्रमाणात वर्दळ असते. अशा संवेदनशील ठिकाणी भरदिवसा गोळीबार आणि कोयत्याने हल्ला होणे ही अत्यंत गंभीर बाब मानली जात आहे. शिवाजीनगर सत्र न्यायालयाच्या गेट क्रमांक चारबाहेर काल दुपारी काही हल्लेखोरांनी युवकावर गोळीबाराचा प्रयत्न केला. त्यानंतर त्याच्यावर कोयत्याने सपासप वार करण्यात आले. या घटनेमुळे न्यायालय परिसरात एकच खळबळ उडाली होती. या हल्ल्याचे गांभीर्य लक्षात घेता न्यायालयाने सुरक्षाव्यवस्थेबाबत थेट पोलीस प्रशासनाशी चर्चा करण्याचा निर्णय घेतला आहे. या चर्चेत न्यायालय परिसरातील सुरक्षा व्यवस्था अधिक सक्षम करणे, प्रवेशद्वारांवरील तपासणी, पोलिस बंदोबस्त आणि भविष्यात अशा घटना रोखण्यासाठी करावयाच्या उपाययोजनांवर भर दिला जाण्याची शक्यता आहे. हल्ल्याप्रकरणी आतापर्यंत काय कारवाई? मंदार किवळे याच्यावर झालेल्या हल्ल्याप्रकरणी सहा संशयितांना पोलिसांनी दौंड येथून ताब्यात घेतले असून, शिवाजीनगर पोलिस ठाण्यात गुन्हा दाखल करण्यात आला आहे. घटनास्थळावरून दोन पिस्तुले आणि एक पुंगळी जप्त करण्यात आली आहे.
लेखकाबद्दलअक्षय शितोळेअक्षय शितोळे हे २०१८ पासून डिजिटल मीडियात कार्यरत असून सध्या मटा ऑनलाइनमध्ये प्रिन्सिपल डिजिटल कंटेंट प्रोड्युसर म्हणून जबाबदारी सांभाळत आहेत. राज्यभरातील रिपोर्टर्ससोबत समन्वय साधत महाराष्ट्रातील गावगाड्यापासून मोठ्या शहरांमधील दैनंदिन घडामोडी मटा ऑनलाइनसाठी वेगवान आणि अचूक पद्धतीने मिळवण्याचा त्यांचा प्रयत्न असतो. राजकीय बातम्यांमध्ये विशेष रस, बातम्यांमागची बातमी अर्थात घडामोडींचा विश्लेषणात्मक आढावा घेण्याचा सातत्याने प्रयत्न असतो. शेती आणि ग्रामीण जीवन हे जिव्हाळ्याचे विषय आहेत.
पत्रकारितेतील अनुभव
अक्षय शितोळे यांनी २०१८ मध्ये आपल्या पत्रकारितेतील प्रवासाचा प्रारंभ केला. सुरुवातीला न्यूज १८ लोकमत या वेबसाईटसाठी काम करताना ट्रेनी, सब एडिटर असा त्यांचा प्रवास राहिला. या कार्यकाळात प्रामुख्याने राजकीय बातम्यांसह स्थानिक पातळीवरील विविध घडामोडी कव्हर करण्याचे काम त्यांनी केले. २०१९ च्या विधानसभा आणि लोकसभा निवडणुकीदरम्यान त्यांनी विविध राजकीय घडामोडींचा विश्लेषणात्मक आढावा घेतला. पुढे २०२१ मटा ऑनलाइनमध्ये डिजिटल कंटेट प्रोड्युसर म्हणून जॉइन झाले. यावेळी राजकीय बातम्यांसह विविध जिल्ह्यांतील प्रतिनिधींशी समन्वय ठेवत वेबसाईटसाठी वेगवान आणि अचूक बातम्या मिळवण्याचा त्यांचा प्रयत्न राहिला. तसंच मटा ऑनलाइनला २५ वर्षे पूर्ण झाल्याच्या पार्श्वभूमीवर त्यांनी महाराष्ट्राच्या दोन दशकांच्या सामाजिक वाटचालीचा आढावा घेणारा विशेष लेख लिहिला होता. "आरक्षणाचे लढे आणि तिढे, टोकदार जातीय अस्मिता ; २५ वर्षांत कसं ढवळून निघालं महाराष्ट्राचं समाजमन?" शीर्षकाखाली लिहिलेल्या या लेखाच्या माध्यमातून महाराष्ट्रात मागील २५ वर्षांत जी सामाजिक स्थित्यंतरे झाली, ज्या घटनांनी महाराष्ट्राच्या सामाजिक रचनेवर परिणाम केला, अशा घडामोडींचा सविस्तर आढावा घेतला होता. २०२३ मध्ये त्यांनी लोकमत ऑनलाइनसोबतही काम केले असून ते २०२५ पासून पुन्हा मटा ऑनलाइनमध्ये प्रिन्सिपल डिजिलट कंटेंट प्रोड्युसर म्हणून रुजू झाले. विविध जिल्ह्यांतील रिपोर्टर्ससोबत संवाद साधत स्थानिक घडामोडींसह राज्यभरात महत्त्वाच्या बातम्या कव्हर करण्याचा त्यांचा प्रयत्न असतो. तसंच विश्लेषणात्मक व्हिडिओच्या माध्यमातून राजकीय घटनांचे अन्वयार्थ प्रेक्षकांसमोर उलगडण्याचा त्यांचा प्रयत्न असतो. महाराष्ट्रात २०२५-२६ साली झालेल्या स्थानिक स्वराज्य संस्थांच्या निवडणुकीदरम्यान त्यांनी विविध विश्लेषणात्मक व्हिडिओंच्या माध्यमातून राजकीय घडामोडींचं सोप्या शब्दांत विश्लेषण केले. तसंच महानगरपालिका निवडणूक निकालानंतर राजकीय विश्लेषकांची मुलाखत घेत या निवडणूक निकालाचा वेध घेण्याचा प्रयत्न केला.

title: व्हॉट्सॲप चॅट बॅकअपसाठी आता मोजावे लागणार पैसे? स्टोअरेजच्या नियमात होणार मोठा बदल
description: व्हॉट्सॲप युजर्सना आता त्यांच्या चॅट बॅकअप स्टोअरेजसाठी एक नवीन पर्याय मिळणार आहे. कंपनी स्वतःची स्वतंत्र क्लाउड सर्व्हिस लाँच करण्याच्या तयारीत आहे. यामुळे आता गुगल ड्राइव्ह (Google Drive) आणि आयक्लाउड (iCloud) व्यतिरिक्त युजर्सना बॅकअपसाठी तिसरा पर्याय उपलब्ध होईल, ज्यामुळे स्टोअरेजचे गणित पूर्णपणे बदलणार आहे. चला तर मग याविषयीची माहिती पुढे जाणून घेऊया.
author: शुभम कुलकर्णी
content:
व्हॉट्सॲप युजर्सना आता त्यांच्या चॅट बॅकअप स्टोअरेजसाठी एक नवीन पर्याय मिळणार आहे. कंपनी स्वतःची स्वतंत्र क्लाउड सर्व्हिस लाँच करण्याच्या तयारीत आहे. यामुळे आता गुगल ड्राइव्ह (Google Drive) आणि आयक्लाउड (iCloud) व्यतिरिक्त युजर्सना बॅकअपसाठी तिसरा पर्याय उपलब्ध होईल, ज्यामुळे स्टोअरेजचे गणित पूर्णपणे बदलणार आहे. चला तर मग याविषयीची माहिती पुढे जाणून घेऊया.
व्हॉट्सॲपवर चॅट बॅकअप ठेवण्यासाठी आता पैशांचे नियोजन करावे लागण्याची शक्यता आहे. कंपनीच्या नवीन धोरणानुसार, व्हॉट्सॲप स्वतःची क्लाउड स्टोअरेज सिस्टीम आणत आहे. या नवीन सुविधेमुळे युजर्सचा डेटा गुगल किंवा ॲपलवर सेव्ह न होता व्हॉट्सॲपच्या स्वतःच्या सर्व्हरवर सुरक्षित ठेवता येईल, ज्यासाठी नवीन नियम लागू केले जातील. एका रिपोर्टमध्ये म्हटले आहे की, व्हॉट्सॲपचे हे क्लाऊड स्टोरेज अँड्रॉइड तसेच आयफोन युजर्स वापरू शकतील. जर तुम्हाला सोप्या भाषेत समजले तर तुम्हाला व्हॉट्सॲपवर तुमच्या चॅटचा बॅकअप घेण्यासाठी गुगल ड्राइव्ह आणि आयक्लाऊडशिवाय आणखी एक पर्याय मिळेल आणि व्हॉट्सॲपचे स्वतःचे क्लाऊड स्टोरेज असेल.
फायदा व्हॉट्सॲप युजर्सना होणार
आयफोनच्या उदाहरणावरून समजून घेतले तर युजरला फक्त 5 GB फ्री आयक्लॉड स्टोरेज मिळते. यात फोटो, डॉक्युमेंट्स, ॲप डेटा आणि डिव्हाइस बॅकअप आहे. आता जर तुम्ही त्यात व्हॉट्सॲपचा बॅकअप जोडला तर ही जागा खूप कमी आहे. एकदा क्लाऊड स्टोरेज भरल्यानंतर, आपल्याला एकतर फायली हटवाव्या लागतील किंवा अधिक स्टोरेजसाठी Apple ला पैसे द्यावे लागतील. ॲपलच्या सर्वात स्वस्त प्लॅनमध्ये 50 GB स्टोरेजसाठी तुम्हाला दरमहा सुमारे 100 रुपये द्यावे लागतील. व्हॉट्सॲपचा क्लाऊड आता तुम्हाला या समस्येपासून वाचवेल.
2 GB स्टोरेज फ्री मिळणार
व्हॉट्सॲपच्या प्लॅनमध्ये 2 GB स्टोरेज फ्री दिले जाणार आहे. यामध्ये तुम्ही चॅटचा बॅकअप स्टोअर करू शकता. जर तुम्हाला यापेक्षा जास्त स्टोरेजची आवश्यकता असेल तर तुम्हाला यासाठी पेड प्लॅन घ्यावा लागेल. रिपोर्ट्सनुसार, व्हॉट्सॲप दरमहा एक डॉलर (सुमारे 95 रुपये) मध्ये 50 GB स्टोरेज ऑफर करेल. जर तुम्हाला यापेक्षा जास्त स्टोरेजची आवश्यकता असेल तर कंपनी 1TB पर्यंतचा प्लॅन ऑफर करेल. यासाठी तुम्हाला दरमहा जास्त पैसे द्यावे लागतील.
व्हॉट्सॲपचा क्लाऊड एंड-टू-एंड एन्क्रिप्टेड असेल
व्हॉट्सॲपच्या क्लाऊटवर स्टोअर केलेला चॅट बॅकअपही एंड-टू-एंड एन्क्रिप्टेड असेल. म्हणजेच, बॅकअपमधून देखील कोणताही थर्ड पार्टी आपल्या चॅटमध्ये प्रवेश करू शकणार नाही. Apple चा iCloud एंड-टू-एंड एन्क्रिप्शन ऑफर करतो, परंतु ते पर्यायी आहे. म्हणजेच युजरला ते इनेबल करावे लागेल. व्हॉट्सॲपमध्ये असा कोणताही त्रास होणार नाही. हे डीफॉल्टनुसार चालू असेल आणि एंड-टू-एंड एन्क्रिप्शन बंद करण्याचा पर्याय नसेल. हा बॅकअप पासकी आणि पासवर्ड, एन्क्रिप्शन कीसह देखील सुरक्षित केला जाऊ शकतो.
व्हॉट्सॲपचा क्लाऊड कधी लाँच होणार?
रिपोर्टमध्ये असे नोंदवले गेले आहे की कंपनी सध्या यावर काम करत आहे आणि त्याची सार्वजनिक चाचणी सुरू झालेली नाही. तर ते रोल आउट होण्यास काही आठवडे लागू शकतात.
लेखकाबद्दलशुभम कुलकर्णीशुभम कुलकर्णी जवळपास 6 वर्षांपासून मराठी माध्यमांमध्ये काम करतोय. आकाशवाणी (छत्रपती संभाजीनगर) पासून माध्यम क्षेत्रात कामाला सुरुवात केली. एका मुखपत्रासह मुंबईतील नामांकित मराठी वृत्तवाहिन्यांमध्ये ‘बुलेटिन प्रोड्यूसर’ म्हणून जबाबदारी सांभाळली. शुभमला राजधानी दिल्लीतही बातमीवर संस्कार करण्याची संधी मिळाली. राजकारण, व्यापार-उद्योग, क्रीडा, तंत्रज्ञान, ऑटो या विषयावर लिहायला त्याला आवडतं. निसर्गाच्या सानिध्यात बसायला, फावल्या वेळेत चित्रपट, वेब सिरीज पाहाण्याचा शुभमचा छंद आहे.... आणखी वाचा
