title: The Leela luxury resorts to open in Port Blair, Neil Island by 2030
description: NEW DELHI: The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts Thursday announced signing of two luxury resorts in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
author: TNN
content:
NEW DELHI: The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts Thursday announced signing of two luxury resorts in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Located in Sri Vijaya Puram (formerly Port Blair) and Shaheed Dweep (formerly Neil Island), the properties will add a combined 160 keys to the luxury hospitality brand’s portfolio. The Leela will manage both resorts for the Sheeraj Group under hotel management agreements.The 100-key Leela Sri Vijaya Puram is expected to open in 2029 and will be close to the airport. The 60-key Leela Shaheed Dweep is expected to open in 2030. The projects are being undertaken by the Sheeraj Group through long-term public-private partnership concessions with the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Integrated Development Corporation (ANIIDCO). Under the hotel management agreement, The Leela will manage the two properties.The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts CEO Anuraag Bhatnagar said: “The Andaman and Nicobar Islands represent an exciting opportunity in the evolution of India’s luxury leisure landscape. Their extraordinary natural beauty and growing appeal among discerning travellers make them a strategic addition to The Leela’s portfolio. Our expansion into Sri Vijaya Puram and Shaheed Dweep reflects our commitment to taking the brand to destinations where we can create meaningful, differentiated experiences.
We are delighted to partner with the Sheeraj Group on these two distinctive developments, bringing The Leela’s expression of True Indian Luxury to one of India’s most remarkable island destinations.”Sheeraj Group founding chairman Rajender Singh said: “Our vision is to create globally acclaimed luxury resorts rooted in sustainability. Through these projects and our partnership with The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts, Sheeraj is committed to setting international benchmarks in hospitality, responsible development and long-term value creation.
The Leela understands how to make a guest feel genuinely welcomed and connect to a place. Together we want to give global travellers a reason to come to the Islands and to return.”The signings are in sync with The Leela’s capital-light and management agreement led growth strategy. With 15 operating properties and 12 under development, the brand's footprint spans Jaisalmer, Mumbai, Srinagar, Bandhavgarh, Ayodhya, Sikkim, Agra, Ranthambore, Tadoba and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Four of these are scheduled to open by end of 2027. These include The Leela Jaisalmer, The Leela Luxury Residences Mumbai, The Leela Bandhavgarh and The Leela Srinagar.

title: ‘105 days of Operation Lotus’: Opposition targets Centre over special Parliament sitting amid delimitation bill buzz
description: NEW DELHI: Opposition leaders on Thursday criticised the Centre's decision to convene a special sitting of Parliament from November 30, alleging that the
author: Yashasvi Vasistha
content:
NEW DELHI: Opposition leaders on Thursday criticised the Centre's decision to convene a special sitting of Parliament from November 30, alleging that the move was aimed at securing the numbers to pass the delimitation-linked Constitution amendment Bill that was defeated in April.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh accused the Narendra Modi government of attempting to manufacture a two-thirds majority after what he described as "105 days of Operation Lotus", while Congress MP Manish Tewari said the proposed sitting mocked Parliament and should not replace the regular Winter Session.Communist Party of India (Marxist) MP John Brittas also alleged that the government was using political manoeuvring to secure support for delimitation under the cover of the Women's Reservation Bill.The reactions came after Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2 to transact essential government business. The sittings may conclude on December 3, depending on the business, he said.
Congress alleges attempt to secure numbers for Constitution amendment
In a post on X, Ramesh linked the announcement to the government's earlier attempt to pass the delimitation-linked legislation, which failed to secure the required majority in April.
"On the evening of Ambedkar Jayanti on April 14, 2026, the Modi Govt had made the Delimitation Bills public that met their well-deserved fate on the night of April 17, 2026.
"Now on Constitution Day, after 105 days of Operation Lotus, the Modi Govt announces a special session, hoping that it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass a Constitution amendment bill. Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution?"The fight is on," he wrote.Tewari, the Congress MP from Chandigarh, questioned the decision to convene a special sitting instead of a regular Winter Session."This request mocks the institution of Parliament. It is time for the Winter Session to convene. A special session is a mechanism for convening sitting during the inter-session period. It can and should not become a substitute for a regular Winter Session," he said in a post tagging Rijiju.
"Why not just convene a regular Winter Session when the government can, if it chooses, 'regurgitate' defeated legislation," he added.The proposed sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but has not been formally prorogued.
CPI(M) MP alleges political manoeuvring to push delimitation
Brittas alleged that the government was attempting to secure a parliamentary majority through political mergers and defections to push through the delimitation exercise."Modi Govt's so-called amalgamations, takeovers, mergers and buyouts appear to have one sinister objective: manufacture a majority to push through delimitation under the guise of the Women's Reservation Bill. The real 'expenditure' for the session will be humongous!!" he wrote on X.
He also cautioned against using women's empowerment as a cover for changes to the country's electoral framework."A majority manufactured through political manipulation is not a mandate. It is a mockery of democracy. If this is how India's electoral future is being reshaped, the special session of Parliament on November 30 could mark the saddest chapter in the history of Indian democracy. Women's empowerment must never become a smokescreen for electoral engineering," Brittas added.Congress MP Karti P Chidambaram, meanwhile, appeared to suggest that the BJP may have secured the support of the DMK and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) for the proposed legislation."Guess the BJP government has got its ducks in a row!" he wrote on X, tagging the official accounts of the BJP, DMK and NCP-SP.
However, NCP-SP MP Shashikant Shinde said his party would decide its position only after examining the proposed legislation."There is a lot of discussion today about what delimitation might look like, but no bill or proposal has been presented yet. Once the proposal is introduced in the session, our party's MPs will study it and discuss it in Parliament," he said.
Shinde added that party leaders Supriya Sule and Amol Kolhe would decide the party's position and course of action after the details were made available.Sule had also recently said it would be premature to oppose the delimitation Bill before its contents were known. "Let the bill come. Perhaps there could be something good in the Delimitation Bill," she told news agency PTI.
What is behind the special sitting?
The announcement has renewed speculation that the government may reintroduce the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation and facilitate the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in legislatures.The Bill, introduced in April along with the Delimitation Bill, 2026 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17.A constitutional amendment requires the support of at least 361 members in the present 543-member House. With three vacancies, the Lok Sabha currently has 540 members. The ruling NDA has around 320 MPs and would need additional support to cross the threshold.The political arithmetic has changed since the Bill's defeat. According to the PTI background report, 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA, while six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.The DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP-SP, with eight, could also play a role in the numbers required.The Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet on Friday and is likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation, according to sources.A Congress Parliamentary Strategy Group meeting is also scheduled for Friday to discuss the party's approach to the parliamentary sitting.The opposition INDIA bloc has demanded that the 33 per cent women's reservation be implemented in the existing 543-member Lok Sabha, without linking it to delimitation.
The government, meanwhile, has maintained that delimitation is necessary to reflect updated population data and facilitate the implementation of the quota.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday reiterated his commitment to women's representation, saying no force could prevent the government from ensuring justice for women. He also blamed an opposition party for the defeat of the Constitution amendment Bill in April.

title: 'Wish Akhilesh spent 6 months in jail': Azam Khan quips; gets witty reply from SP chief
description: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party veteran Azam Khan on Thursday said he wished party chief Akhilesh Yadav had spent at least six months in prison to understand
author: Rajeev Singh
content:
Azam Khan said he wished party chief Akhilesh Yadav had spent at least six months in prison.
NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party veteran Azam Khan on Thursday said he wished party chief Akhilesh Yadav had spent at least six months in prison to understand the emotional and physical hardships of incarceration.Akhilesh Yadav responded that he had felt Khan's pain over the years, adding a light-hearted remark about the jails built during the SP's tenure.The exchange took place at the launch of the SP's manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Khan also spoke about the distress of being separated from his son Abdullah during a prison transfer and the fear that they might never see each other again.Recalling his time behind bars, Khan said he would sometimes tell Abdullah and other inmates that he wished Yadav could experience prison life, even if only for six months."My heart wished Akhilesh ji, too, could come to jail for six months, so he could know how the days and nights pass and what one goes through," Khan said.
Asked by reporters about Khan's remarks after the manifesto launch, Yadav said, "He is a member of our party and our family. I have felt his pain from time to time."Yadav also responded with a quip about the prisons constructed when the SP was in power."I told Azam Khan that SP built best jails in Etawah during its tenure.
We will also work on how to further improve jails in future," he said.
Azam Khan recalls 'prison trauma'
Khan described his separation from Abdullah during a transfer between prisons as one of the most painful experiences of his incarceration. He said the uncertainty over his son's whereabouts left him fearing that they might never meet again.The veteran leader also spoke about having to see his young son remain in prison with him for years. Earlier at the event, Yadav had assured Khan that the party would do whatever was necessary to fulfil the promises made in its manifesto.
Khan's repeated stints behind bars
The 10-time MLA from Rampur served as a cabinet minister in the Akhilesh Yadav-led government between 2012 and 2017, holding portfolios including parliamentary affairs and urban development.
He was released from Dasna jail in Ghaziabad on November 18 after the Allahabad high court granted him interim bail in a money laundering case registered by the Enforcement Directorate in connection with the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur.The ED had arrested Khan on October 31, shortly after he was released from Rampur jail in another case. He had spent nearly 11 months behind bars during that earlier stint.Yadav has met Khan during some of his periods in custody. He visited him at Sitapur jail shortly after his arrest in February 2020 and again in March 2024, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, to discuss candidate selection in Rampur and neighbouring constituencies.During Khan's latest incarceration, Yadav met him at Rampur jail on October 22, 2026, for around 45 minutes ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.
Rajeev Singh is a Digital Content Producer with The Times of India. He covers politics, policies, defence, and conflicts for readers curious to know their implications. He loves digging into legal maxims and political trivia. On off days, when not turning pages or learning русский, he lives in the reverie of “what ifs” and “how abouts.”

title: Vellappally Natesan says he has ‘no differences’ with Keralam CM Satheesan
description: Vellappally Natesan claims no differences with Kerala CM Satheesan, signaling a softening amid past exchanges before the UDF's rise.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
In an apparent effort at thawing the frosty relationship with V.D. Satheesan, Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam general secretary Vellappally Natesan praised Chief Minister on Thursday (November 26), saying he was highly capable, something that was now universally acknowledged.
Speaking to mediapersons at Kanichukulangara, Mr. Natesan said that he had no personal enmity but just differences of opinion on specific issues with Mr. Satheesan, signalling a further thaw in relations after the acrimonious exchanges that were made between the two during the Assembly election campaign and after the elections..
He said that there was a time when he maintained very close relationship with Mr. Satheesan and said that he would welcome the Chief Minister heartily if he were to visit Kanichukulangara.
It is natural for differences to arise within an alliance, Mr. Natesan said, adding that those in power should be respected and that disputes within the Congress were nothing new.
Mr. Natesan’s remarks mark a softening of his position towards Mr. Satheesan, whom he had repeatedly targeted during the run-up to the Assembly elections. At the time, he had questioned the Congress leader’s political stature, criticised his style of functioning and had also argued that senior Congress leader K.C. Venugopal was better placed for the Chief Ministerial post. He had also voiced concerns over the Indian Union Muslim League’s influence within the United Democratic Front (UDF).
However, Mr. Natesan’s shift in stance had begun to be apparent soon after Mr. Satheesan assumed Chief Ministership, when his son and SNDP Yogam vice-president Thushar Vellappally had visited Mr. Satheesan at his residence in Aluva, accompanied by SNDP office-bearers, an indication that the SNDP leadership was willing to engage with the UDF government.
Mr. Natesan’s efforts at rapprochement had gained momentum recently, when he chose to play down the absence of Mr. Satheesan at the R. Sankar memorial day celebrations on November 6, where the Chief Minister had been invited to inaugurate the event
The timing of Mr. Natesan’s bid to mend fences with the Chief Minister is noteworthy, for the Nair Service Society (NSS) general secretary G. Sukumaran Nair had recently reached out to Mr. Satheesan, in an effort to smooth over the strained relationship he had had with Mr. Satheesan, since 2021, when the latter assumed office as the Leader of the Opposition
Mr. Nair had invited the Chief Minister for the 150th birth anniversary of NSS founder Mannathu Padmanabhan, which the Chief Minister had accepted. Mr. Nair had also stated that his earlier misunderstandings with Mr. Satheesan had been resolved following their interaction.
On Thursday, Mr. Natesan also defended his association with former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and that there was nothing wrong in him sharing a ride with Mr. Vijayan in the latter’s official vehicle, something that had become a political controversy in the State at the time
He alleged that he had been subjected to harassment in his public and private life for three decades and accused those seeking to target him of attempting to undermine the SNDP Yogam and the SN Trust.
Published - November 26, 2026 03:41 pm IST

title: 25K government jobs will be filled soon, taking total beyond one lakh: Revanth Reddy
description: Congress CM Revanth Reddy pledges 25k more jobs, claims 1 lakh total, pledges Achampet model development, and attacks KCR on irrigation neglect.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy announced that the recruitment process for another 25,000 government jobs would be completed soon, taking the total number of government jobs filled by the Congress government to one lakh. He also promised to do his utmost to develop the Achampet constituency and make it a model for the rest of the State.
Addressing a public meeting in the Achampet Assembly constituency of Nagarkurnool district on Thursday, the Chief Minister said his government had already filled more than 75,000 government jobs, providing employment opportunities to the unemployed youth.
Mr. Reddy launched the distribution of Indiramma saris and released funds for 4.74 lakh newly sanctioned Cheyutha social security pensions. The pension amounts would be credited directly to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries. Continuing his attack on former Chief Minister and Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) president K. Chandrasekhar Rao, Mr. Reddy accused him of neglecting irrigation projects in the erstwhile Mahabubnagar district during his 10-year rule.
“Though the previous BRS government spent ₹1.80 lakh crore on irrigation projects, it did not spend even ₹10,000 crore on projects in Palamuru,” he alleged, adding that, as a son of the soil, it was his responsibility to complete the pending projects.
The Chief Minister accused Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao of compromising Telangana’s interests in the sharing of Krishna waters with Andhra Pradesh during the tenure of former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy. He alleged that Andhra Pradesh was illegally diverting thousand million cubic feet (tmcft) of Krishna waters a day to Rayalaseema and had increased the discharge capacity of the Pothireddypadu head regulator.
“Had the irrigation projects in the erstwhile Mahabubnagar district been completed during the BRS rule, Telangana would have been in a position to lift Krishna waters,” he said, accusing the previous BRS government of doing injustice to Telangana by agreeing to a share of 299 tmcft of Krishna waters. Mr. Reddy promised to develop Achampet into a model constituency for the State.
Slamming KCR for confining himself to his farmhouse after losing power, the Chief Minister questioned why the BRS president was not coming out in public and raising issues on behalf of the people.
Published - November 26, 2026 09:30 pm IST

title: SIT’s chargesheet gives clean chit to Nagendra in Valmiki Corporation scam
description: SIT clears Nagendra in Valmiki scam, naming him a witness; CBI and ED continue separate investigations.
author: The Hindu Bureau
content:
Former minister and ex-corporation chairman Basavaraj Daddal named as witnesses in final chargesheet filed before Lokayukta Special Court
In a major departure from the findings of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Directorate of Enforcement (ED), the Karnataka Special Investigation Team (SIT) has found no evidence linking former Minister B. Nagendra to the alleged misappropriation of ₹89.62 crore from the Valmiki Corporation, and has named him as a witness, and not an accused, in its final chargesheet.
The chargesheet, filed before the Lokayukta Special Court on November 25, under the Prevention of Corruption Act, also names former corporation chairman Basavaraj Daddal as a witness.
The SIT’s findings effectively give Nagendra a clean chit in the alleged fund diversion, in contrast to the separate investigations by the CBI and the ED, both of which have implicated him. The CBI has described him as prime accused in the scam, while the ED has also accused him of involvement in the financial irregularities.
Mr. Nagendra was Minister for Scheduled Tribes Welfare when the alleged scam came to light. He resigned from the Cabinet following the controversy and was subsequently arrested by the ED. After being re-inducted into the Cabinet, he resigned again in August this year.
Reacting to the SIT’s findings, Home Minister Priyank Kharge said the investigation was based on evidence and that no money trail linking Nagendra to the alleged misappropriation had been established.
The alleged scam came to light following the suicide of Chandrashekar P, the corporation’s accounts superintendent, at his residence in Shivamogga on May 26, 2024. His death brought to light the alleged diversion of ₹89.62 crore from the corporation.
The SIT was constituted to investigate both the alleged financial irregularities and Chandrashekar’s death. In its first chargesheet, filed in August 2024, the SIT did not name Nagendra as an accused in the alleged fund diversion. It charged several others, including Padmanabha, Parashuram Durgannanavar, a former accounts officer of the corporation, Sathyanarayana Etakari, Nekkunte Nagaraj, Nageshwar Rao, M Chandramohan and several others from Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
The accused also included Satyanarayana Varma and Saiteja from Hyderabad, G.K. Jagadish from Shivamogga, Teja Thammaiah from Bengaluru, and Pittala Srinivasa and Khaki Srinivasa Rao from Andhra Pradesh.
In a second chargesheet, the SIT invoked abetment of suicide and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) charges against two others in connection with Chandrashekar’s death, but concluded that Chandrashekar had died by suicide.
Despite clean chit, Mr. Nagendra continue to be in the dock as the CBI and ED are continuing their separate investigations into the alleged scam.
Published - November 26, 2026 09:30 pm IST

title: Mamata Banerjee's brother seeks case against Abhishek over remarks on courts, EC
description: Swapan Banerjee accused the Diamond Harbour MP of criminal intimidation insulting public servants and inciting the public against constitutional institutions
author: Tapas Sengupta
content:
Mamata Banerjee's brother seeks case against Abhishek over remarks on courts, EC
Swapan Banerjee accused the Diamond Harbour MP of criminal intimidation, insulting public servants and inciting the public against constitutional institutions.
Swapan Banerjee, younger brother of former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, has approached the Kalighat police station seeking registration of an FIR against his nephew and Trinamool Congress (TMC) national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee. Swapan, also known as Babun, accused Abhishek of making allegedly defamatory and inflammatory remarks against constitutional institutions, including the judiciary and the Election Commission.
In a seven-page complaint submitted on Thursday afternoon, Swapan accused the Diamond Harbour MP of criminal intimidation, insulting public servants and inciting the public against constitutional institutions.
He cited Abhishek's November 7 Facebook video, recent statements to the media and a September 24 post on X (@abhishekaitc) as the basis for his allegations.
According to the complaint, Abhishek had repeatedly targeted the Calcutta High Court, the Supreme Court and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, allegedly suggesting that the judiciary was "biased" and "sold to the BJP".
Babun has sought police action over the remarks, contending that they amounted to an attack on institutions that form the foundation of the country's constitutional framework.
The complaint marks a fresh escalation in the ongoing differences between the two sides of the Banerjee family. There was no immediate response from Abhishek Banerjee to the allegations.
This is not the first time Babun has approached the police against his nephew. He had earlier alleged intimidation and obstruction of a blood donation camp, seeking registration of an FIR against Abhishek in connection with the incident.
Speaking to reporters after visiting the Kalighat police station, Babun had claimed that a culture of threats and intimidation had taken root during the TMC's 15-year rule in West Bengal and continued even after the BJP came to power in May this year. He said he had witnessed such incidents since 2024.
"Many things happened during the TMC regime. This has been going on since 2024 and continues even today. There have been instances of obstruction of government work, forcible takeover of clubs and intimidation. How much can I say? I have endured a lot," news agency PTI had quoted him as saying.
The latest complaint also comes against the backdrop of a prolonged estrangement between Babun and his elder sister, Mamata Banerjee, who had publicly distanced herself from him at one point and even declared that she had severed ties with him.
The family discord has taken on an additional political dimension following the BJP's victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, ending the TMC's uninterrupted 15-year rule in the state.
Since the change of government, Babun has increasingly been seen moving closer to the BJP leadership and has repeatedly expressed admiration for Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.
He recently invited Adhikari to inaugurate a community Durga Puja in his neighbourhood and was seen touching the chief minister's feet as a mark of respect.
His public gestures have fuelled speculation about a possible political shift towards the BJP. However, Babun has not formally announced any decision to join the party.
With the latest complaint bringing Abhishek's remarks on constitutional institutions into focus, attention will now be on the police response and whether an FIR is registered.
Any response from Abhishek or the TMC is also likely to add another dimension to the escalating political and family feud.

title: Telangana man suffocates daughter to death over affair, passes it off as murder
description: The accused allegedly cremated her body in haste on the same morning without waiting for relatives to arrive raising suspicions
author: Abdul Basheer
content:
Telangana man suffocates daughter to death over affair, passes it off as murder
The accused allegedly cremated her body in haste on the same morning, without waiting for relatives to arrive, raising suspicions.
A man was arrested in Telangana's Adilabad district for allegedly suffocating his daughter to death with a pillow and subsequently staging the murder as suicide by hanging her body from a ceiling beam, after he reportedly objected to her relationship with another man, police said.
The accused allegedly cremated her body in haste on the same morning, without waiting for relatives to arrive, raising suspicions over the circumstances surrounding her death and eventually leading to a police investigation.
The accused, identified as Ade Kailash, allegedly killed his daughter, Ade Kalyani, at their home in Umri village under Narnur Police Station limits in the early hours of November 24.
According to police, Kalyani's marriage had already been arranged by her family, and her engagement was scheduled to take place just two days after her death.
However, Kailash was reportedly unhappy after discovering that his daughter was in love with another man.
Preliminary findings of the police investigation suggest that he was angered by the relationship and feared it would bring disrepute to the family. He allegedly decided to kill her rather than allow the relationship to continue.
According to Utnoor ASP Ruthvik Sai Kotte, Kailash allegedly pressed a pillow against Kalyani's face, suffocating her to death. He then used her dupatta to hang her body from a ceiling beam in an attempt to make the incident appear to be a case of suicide, the cops added.
The respective ages of the accused and the victim were not immediately known.
The incident initially came to light as a suspected death by hanging. However, the father's decision to cremate his daughter's body hurriedly on the morning of November 24, without waiting for other family members and relatives to arrive, raised suspicions.
Subsequently, the village Panchayat Secretary lodged a formal complaint, following which Narnur Police registered a case and initiated an investigation.
The case was registered under Sections 103(1) and 238 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), pertaining to murder and causing the disappearance of evidence of an offence, respectively.
Addressing a press conference on Thursday, ASP Ruthvik Sai Kotte said the investigation had revealed that the accused murdered his daughter and attempted to conceal the crime by portraying it as suicide and hurriedly cremating her body.
Kailash was subsequently arrested by Narnur Police and produced before the court before being sent to judicial remand.
Police said further investigation was underway to gather additional evidence and establish all aspects of the crime.
The case has brought renewed attention to the issue of honour-based violence, with the preliminary findings pointing to the alleged murder being driven by the father's opposition to his daughter's relationship.

title: Plates tossed, sabzi looted, meal on cardboard: Anant Singh's grand feast takes ugly turn
description: The wedding of Mokama MLA Anant Singh039s daughter was billed as one of Bihar039s grandest celebrations with arrangements to feed four lakh people But the visuals emerging from the grand feast showed plates flying in the air guests grabbing food from the ground lathis being used to control guests and people eating off cardboards
author: Sushim Mukul
content:
Plates tossed, sabzi looted, meal on cardboard: Anant Singh's grand feast takes ugly turn
The wedding of Mokama MLA Anant Singh's daughter was billed as one of Bihar's grandest celebrations, with arrangements to feed four lakh people. But the visuals emerging from the grand feast showed plates flying in the air, guests grabbing food from the ground, lathis being used to control guests and people eating off cardboards.
Plates were tossed into the crowd as if it were a game of catch-catch. A sea of guests jostled to get hold of one. Those who couldn't, grabbed food directly from serving vessels. Others resorted to eating puri-matar paneer off pieces of cardboard. Numerous videos from Bihar strongman and Mokama MLA Anant Singh's daughter's wedding feast painted a picture of chaos. Singh had, after all, invited the whole wide world to the wedding. And going by the visuals of a sea of people, 10-km-long traffic jams and guests pushing and jostling for food, it seemed the whole world had descended on Nadwan, the expelled JD(U) MLA's ancestral village in Patna district.
Newspapers, too, doubled up as plates as the food counters struggled to cope with the massive rush. It was meant to be a grand feast for everyone, and it turned into a scramble for food for many.
The wedding of Anant Singh's daughter, Shivangi, at Nadwan village in Bihar's Patna district on November 25 saw several political heavyweights in attendance. Such was the rush that even VIPs travelling by road were stuck in traffic for hours. Ask Bihar Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar or Danapur MLA Ram Kripal Yadav. The much-hyped horse race, too, had to be postponed after three rounds as the crowd became difficult to manage.
The visuals triggered outrage on social media, with several people questioning the manner in which the guests were treated. Journalist Gargi Rawat took to X and questioned the need for such a display of grandeur. Others argued that feeding people should be an act of generosity and not a spectacle of power and wealth.
PLATES IN THE AIR, PURI-SABZI ON CARDBOARD IN ANANT SINGH'S GRAND FEAST
Such was the rush at the food counters that disposable plates (pattal) were tossed into the air, with guests scrambling to catch them. In one of the viral videos, lathis could be seen being used to control the crowd at the food counters.
In a video shared by Chapra Zila handle on X, a guest could be seen carrying some puris and sabzi on a piece of cardboard (with Sudha branding) after reportedly failing to get a plate. Sudha is a popular dairy brand in Bihar and Jharkhand, run by the Bihar State Milk Co-operative Federation (COMFED).
Another video showed people climbing over one another to get hold of disposable plates. Some guests used whatever they could find to carry their food.
"Getting food here is like winning a war. Your brother managed to get food, which means I have won the war. The rasgullas were looted, and we didn't get any," a guest said in a viral video.
In another unusual visual, people could be seen picking pieces of paneer directly from a vessel containing matar paneer curry.
A separate video purportedly showed a man falling into a large vessel containing sabzi amid the rush.
The massive traffic jams also forced some wedding-bound guests to turn back without even reaching Nadwan, according to BBC Hindi News.
FOOD FOR FOUR LAKH, BUT HOW MANY TURNED UP?
According to Anant Singh, arrangements had been made to feed over four lakh people. Around 500 cooks and workers were engaged, with more than 300 cooking stations set up for the grand bhoj.
The elaborate vegetarian spread included eight varieties of sweets, four types of sabzi, litti-chokha, dosa and Kashmiri pulao.
However, the rush at Nadwan overwhelmed the food counters. While arrangements had reportedly been made to feed four lakh people, the actual turnout appeared to have exceeded expectations, according to reports. News agency AFP put the wedding turnout at around four lakh, with a lakh people turning up for the horse race alone.
While some people on social media questioned the civic sense of those scrambling for food, others questioned the organisers' responsibility towards the people they had invited.
"If you have the resources to invite thousands of people, you must also have the responsibility to feed them with dignity. Feeding people should be an act of generosity, not a spectacle of power and wealth," an X-handle named talkmaze posted.
India Today TV journalist Preeti Choudhry said the wedding visuals exposed the chasm between two Indias, "One of extraordinary abundance and the other of acute deprivation that even the leftovers from a celebration become worth fighting for." Linking the scenes to electoral politics and the popularity of cash transfers, she added, "The politics of poverty cuts across ideological divides."
While Anant Singh's open invitation was among the biggest talking points in India ahead of the wedding, it is the scramble for a plate of food that has now become the subject of discussion.

title: Driven out of forests, 56 displaced elephants run into politics in Karnataka
description: Karnataka’s plan to move 56 elephants from Hassan’s coffee estates to Bhadra has stalled after protests by legislators and residents in Chikkamagaluru. | India News
author: Arun Dev
content:
Arun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.
Driven out of forests, 56 displaced elephants run into politics in Karnataka
Karnataka’s plan to move 56 elephants from Hassan’s coffee estates to Bhadra has stalled after protests by legislators and residents in Chikkamagaluru.
The movement of 56 elephants out of Hassan’s coffee estates in Karnataka has run into a political roadblock, with the forest department temporarily suspending the operation after protests by legislators and residents in neighbouring Chikkamagaluru.
The herd, meanwhile, has scattered across three districts, with 39 elephants in Mudigere, 13 back in Belur and four tuskers moving towards Kodagu as of November 26. For the elephants, finding a safe home is proving almost as difficult as escaping one: forests are fragmented by plantations, roads and fences, while the prospect of moving them elsewhere has run into resistance from communities worried about inheriting the conflict.
The operation, launched after two people were killed in elephant attacks in Belur, began on November 21, following the capture of two tuskers on November 18 and 19. One was shifted to the Mathigodu elephant camp in Nagarahole Tiger Reserve, while the other was released into the wild in Bandipur after being fitted with a radio collar. The forest department then began guiding the remaining 56 elephants from Belur towards the Bhadra forests.
Although the operation has been suspended, officials are continuing to monitor the herd and guide the elephants in Mudigere towards the Tatakola forest area, which adjoins reserve forests. Forest minister Ramalinga Reddy is scheduled to meet legislators from the affected districts on November 30 to discuss the issue.
The dispute has raised a difficult question: moving elephants away from one set of villages may simply shift the risk to another, particularly as the habitats and traditional routes connecting forests become increasingly fragmented.
Political resistance across districts
Hassan district in-charge minister K M Shivalinge Gowda has defended the operation, arguing that Belur has barely 100 acres of forest and cannot provide adequate habitat for the elephants.
However, Congress MLAs Nayana Motamma, T D Rajegowda and H D Thammaiah have opposed moving the herd towards Chikkamagaluru, which also faces frequent human-elephant conflict.
Motamma, who represents Mudigere, submitted her resignation to the Assembly speaker on November 23, protesting against the movement of elephants into her constituency without consulting local elected representatives. She withdrew it after chief minister D K Shivakumar and senior Congress leaders intervened, but continued to demand assurances on public safety.
“I have to answer the people who elected me. I am not answerable merely to the government. If we cannot protect the people who elected us, what is the purpose of holding public office?” she said.
Reddy, meanwhile, said elephants belonged in forests rather than coffee estates and cautioned legislators against politicising the issue.
“These elephants belong to the forest and not to the coffee estates. Do not indulge in politics,” he said.
Fences, roads and shrinking habitats
Research from the Hassan landscape helps explain why moving elephants from one area to another may offer only temporary relief.
A study published in August in the Journal of Wildlife Science, titled Navigating the coffee fields: elephants’ use of habitat mosaics and the impacts of barriers on their spatial use of villages in a fragmented landscape of South India, examined elephant movement across 466 villages spread over approximately 1,180 sq km between 2023 and 2025.
Researchers from the Nature Conservation Foundation mapped 277 solar-powered fences erected around coffee plantations between 2010 and 2025. Together, these fences stretched 382 km and covered approximately 32 sq km, nearly 5% of the study area.
Nearly 20% of the identified refuge habitat fragments shared a boundary with a solar fence, while another 30% had fences within 300 metres.
“The proximity of fences to habitat refugia limited elephants’ access to resources, pushing them into new areas,” the researchers found.
The study also identified the expansion of National Highway 75 from two lanes to four as a barrier to elephant movement. Elephant activity hotspots recorded on both sides of the highway in 2023 shifted predominantly to its northern side in 2024 and remained concentrated there in 2025. The researchers linked the shift to the highway expansion, completed in 2023.
They recommended protecting refuge habitats, redesigning fences to allow elephant movement, discouraging new fencing near natural forests and constructing highway overpasses or underpasses at critical crossing points.
Corridors exist, connectivity doesn’t
Karnataka has nine identified elephant corridors, but the Union government had reported securing only two through private land purchases, according to a Rajya Sabha reply in March 2023.
The state acquired 25.37 acres for the Edayahalli-Doddasampige corridor in 2017 and another 16.30 acres at Muddahalli for the Chamarajanagar-Talamalai corridor in 2021-22.
The Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26 estimated the state’s elephant population at 6,395, based on the 2023 assessment. It also reported that the state had installed 428 km of railway barricades, 1,360.87 km of solar fencing and 1,775.41 km of elephant-proof trenches to reduce human-elephant conflict.
While these barriers can protect farms and settlements, their placement can also restrict elephants’ access to habitats and traditional movement routes.
Joseph Hoover, president of the United Conservation Movement and a former member of the Karnataka State Wildlife Board, said the conflict was being viewed too narrowly.
“We are blaming elephants for a crisis largely created by human intervention. Their habitats have been fragmented, food sources depleted and traditional corridors blocked. When elephants are forced out of forests into agricultural land, we cannot treat them as the problem. We have to address what drove them there,” he said.
“Capturing elephants and driving them back into forests will only provide temporary relief. Unless we restore habitats and protect corridors, we will continue to see more human deaths and more elephant deaths,” he added.
The human cost of conflict
For farmers in Hassan, the conflict has also meant repeated crop losses. Union government data show that the district recorded 4,285 cases of crop damage by elephants in 2022-23, for which ₹2.97 crore was paid in compensation.
The number of cases fell to 3,641 in 2023-24, but compensation rose to ₹4.07 crore. In 2024-25, the district recorded 3,015 cases, with ₹3.80 crore paid in compensation.
The same data recorded 24 human deaths in elephant attacks in Hassan between 2020-21 and 2024-25.
For the forest department, the immediate challenge is to manage the 56 elephants dispersed across Belur, Mudigere and towards Kodagu without exposing more communities to danger.
The November 30 meeting may resolve the immediate political dispute, but not the underlying conflict. Driven out of one landscape because of the threat they pose to people, the elephants face resistance in another. Shrinking habitats, plantations, roads and fences lie at the heart of the problem. Relocating the herd may shift the conflict, but will not address its causes.

title: 164 Indonesian, Malaysian nationals rescued from ‘cyber slavery’ racket in Delhi
description: According to police, the network specifically targeted people in Indonesia and Malaysia by offering them employment opportunities in India.  | India News
author: PTI
content:
164 Indonesian, Malaysian nationals rescued from ‘cyber slavery’ racket in Delhi
According to police, the network specifically targeted people in Indonesia and Malaysia by offering them employment opportunities in India.
Lured to India with promises of lucrative jobs, 164 foreign nationals from Indonesia and Malaysia allegedly found themselves trapped in a network of cyber slavery, with their passports seized upon arrival, movement restricted, and lives reduced to making fraudulent calls to people back home, the Delhi Police said on Thursday.
Kept in paying guest (PG) accommodations, allegedly served substandard food and subjected to physical assault if they refused to work, the foreign nationals were forced to follow written scripts to cheat unsuspecting people in their own countries through fraudulent investment platforms, police said.
Also read: CBI nabs Hisar man for ‘cyber slavery’, trafficking of Indians to Southeast Asia
In a major crackdown in southwest Delhi's Dwarka on an alleged international human trafficking and cyber fraud network, the Crime Branch of the Delhi Police has rescued 164 foreign nationals, including 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians, from premises allegedly being used to operate the racket. A 25-year-old Malaysian national, identified as Tan Guan Wei, has been arrested in connection with the case.
According to police, the network specifically targeted people in Indonesia and Malaysia by offering them employment opportunities in India, promising attractive salaries and better career prospects. However, their ordeal allegedly began soon after they landed in the country.
Their passports were taken away upon arrival, leaving them without control over their identity documents and restricting their ability to leave, police said. They were subsequently shifted to PG accommodations and allegedly forced to work as cyber slaves.
Those who resisted or refused to participate in the fraudulent activities were allegedly thrashed by members of the network to ensure compliance, a senior police officer said, adding that so far they have learned that around two people were thrashed.
The living conditions at the accommodations were also allegedly poor, with the foreign nationals being provided substandard food. Despite a fleet of around 40 cabs being used to ferry them between the PG accommodations and the cyber fraud call centre, they were not allowed to venture out independently or move around as they wished, the officer said.
Also read: Baghpat man trafficked to Cambodia for cyber fraud repatriated safely
"The cabs were allegedly deployed to transport them to the call centre and bring them back to their accommodations, ensuring that their movement remained under the control of the handlers," the officer said.
The foreign nationals were not merely made to operate computers and mobile phones but were allegedly trained to execute a specific pattern of cyber fraud. They were provided written scripts containing conversations that they had to follow while approaching prospective victims.
The targets were primarily people in Malaysia and Indonesia. The operators allegedly created fictitious female identities and social media profiles to establish contact with unsuspecting individuals.
Also read: ₹5 lakh via Facebook ad">Mohali: Haryana govt employee duped of ₹5 lakh via Facebook ad
"Using these profiles, the foreign nationals were instructed to initiate conversations, develop online relationships and gradually gain the confidence of their targets. Once trust was established, the victims were persuaded to invest money through fraudulent trading and investment platforms," the officer added.
The syndicate allegedly used websites and APK-based applications to lure people with promises of high returns. The victims were made to believe that they were investing in legitimate financial opportunities, while the money was allegedly siphoned off through the fraudulent network.
"We got to know about the fraud after the crime branch received an email alert about the alleged cyber slavery racket around a week ago, following which its officers began developing intelligence about the network," the officer said.
Initial information suggested that around 60 to 70 foreign nationals were being held and forced to work in the cyber fraud operation. However, when the police team conducted the operation at the suspected premises, the actual number turned out to be significantly higher. The operation led to the rescue of 164 foreign nationals, exposing the scale of the alleged racket.
The police are now investigating how the foreign nationals were recruited, who facilitated their travel to India, and how their passports were taken away. "During the entire investigation, two names -- Sunil Kumar and Sushil Bhati -- cropped up. Bhati used to arrange the PG accommodations and transportation facilities. Both are absconding, both will be arrested soon," the officer said.
Certain bank accounts allegedly maintained by Kumar and Bhati have been identified as being used to meet rental and other operational expenses of the network. The financial trail is being examined to establish the flow of money, identify the beneficiaries and trace the proceeds generated through the alleged cyber fraud. The arrested Malaysian national, Tan Guan Wei, a resident of Negeri Sembilan, is being questioned about his alleged role in the network, his association with other members and the extent of his involvement in operating the fraudulent platforms.
The police have seized a substantial digital infrastructure allegedly used to run the operation. The recoveries include 355 mobile phones, 168 desktop computers, 26 laptops, 53 SIM cards and 174 passports. Of the 355 mobile phones, 335 were old or used handsets, and 20 were new phones in sealed packaging. The 53 SIM cards include 31 international and 22 Indian connections. The recovered passports comprise 95 Indonesian and 79 Malaysian documents.
Servers and other electronic material have also been seized. Investigators are examining the devices to identify the victims, establish the communication channels used by the syndicate and trace financial transactions linked to the fraudulent platforms.
Also read: ₹25 crore">Gurugram: 2 arrested in PayU's cloud servers breach, siphoning over ₹25 crore
A case has been registered at the Crime Branch police station under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Further investigation is underway to identify other members of the international network and establish the extent of the alleged human trafficking and cyber fraud operation.

title: Abhijeet Dipke launches nationwide ‘Save Democracy’ movement at Constitution Day rally in Nagpur
description: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced a nationwide campaign at a Nagpur rally, while actor Prakash Raj backed calls to protect democracy and constitutional rights. | India News
author: Pradip Kumar Maitra
content:
Abhijeet Dipke launches nationwide ‘Save Democracy’ movement at Constitution Day rally in Nagpur
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced a nationwide campaign at a Nagpur rally, while actor Prakash Raj backed calls to protect democracy and constitutional rights.
Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday announced a nationwide movement to “Save Democracy and Save Constitution”, urging citizens to unite against what he alleged were threats to democratic rights, electoral freedoms and constitutional values. Actor Prakash Raj, who joined a rally in Nagpur to mark Constitution Day, also called for greater protection of dissent and freedom of expression.
Addressing the gathering in Nagpur on Thursday evening, Dipke urged people to uphold constitutional values, protect democracy and follow the ideals of Babasaheb Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Constitution. Appealing to young people to take the lead, he raised concerns about electoral processes, social media moderation and the protection of democratic safeguards.
Speaking in Hindi and Marathi, Dipke said the earlier protest at Jantar Mantar had given young people a platform to voice their concerns. “You have power. We have the Constitution,” he said, questioning the government over alleged electoral irregularities, including discrepancies in vote counts during the last hour of polling and the deletion of names from voter lists.
He also questioned the Maharashtra government’s reported move to overturn the outcome of the Gokul dairy election through an ordinance, asking what such interventions could mean for larger electoral contests.
Referring to what he described as a lookout notice issued by Mumbai police, Dipke said he was in Nagpur and would continue protesting. He urged supporters to remain united and continue peaceful demonstrations even if they were detained.
Dipke also called for 50% representation for women in cabinets and in the distribution of election tickets by political parties. Citing Ambedkar’s work on women’s rights and labour protections, he said his legacy should be recognised across communities.
He said the Constitution had enabled people from humble backgrounds to reach the highest public offices, citing Prime Minister Narendra Modi as an example. Recalling a visit to the tribal district of Gadchiroli, Dipke alleged that he had seen classrooms without benches and bathing facilities for tribal girls without roofs or doors. He questioned how long children in such schools would have to wait for basic infrastructure.
Dipke, who had been in Nagpur since Wednesday to organise the rally, described Constitution Day as a significant occasion and urged citizens to defend democratic and voting rights.
Earlier in the day, Dipke paid floral tributes to Ambedkar at Nagpur’s historic Deekshabhoomi, where the latter and his followers embraced Buddhism in 1956, underscoring the symbolic significance of the location for the campaign.
Prakash Raj, meanwhile, criticised the government over what he alleged were attempts to silence dissent, warning that suppressing the voices of students and young people would only make them louder.
He said protecting the rights and freedoms guaranteed by the Constitution was a collective responsibility and called on citizens to come together to defend democratic freedoms. He alleged that young people raising questions about education, healthcare and employment were increasingly being silenced instead of receiving answers from the government.
“Attempts to suppress voices will only make them louder,” Raj said, stressing that young people’s freedom of expression must be respected and their questions addressed.
He also expressed concern over reports of citizens being prevented from travelling abroad even after boarding flights. Referring to a recent case involving YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, Raj questioned the restrictions on citizens’ freedoms and alleged that people carrying the national flag were also being jailed.
Raj said the campaign aimed to remove the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) from power, adding that any political party taking steps against the Constitution would face opposition. He maintained that the movement was not about conventional politics but about defending constitutional values and democratic rights.
On Jantar Mantar being denied as a protest site, Raj said that protest spaces would emerge across the country, including in neighbourhoods and on streets.
Dipke also raised concerns about the visibility of political content on social media platforms. He alleged that posts about Prime Minister Narendra Modi were being promoted, while content critical of other political leaders and parties was being restricted. He alleged that more than 50 lakh Instagram posts had been taken down between January and June, although the figure and his allegation of political bias in content moderation have not been independently verified.
Dipke further alleged that the government had prevented 27-year-old CJP co-convenor Saurav Das from travelling to the London School of Economics and Oxford University out of “jealousy” over invitations he had received from the institutions.
Dipke said CJP co-convenors Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, along with him, had been invited to the UK. They had decided that Das would travel to London, while he and Ranka would visit parts of Maharashtra to assess drought conditions. However, Das was stopped at the airport, he alleged.
“The move stemmed from jealousy,” Dipke added.
He said the three had been invited to speak about how the Jantar Mantar protest, guided by the ideals of Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi, had garnered widespread support. “But this individual is a narcissist, he wants not just the country, but the entire world to revolve around him. He believes that he alone should travel across the world,” he added.
Das approached the Delhi high court on Wednesday challenging the action. The Ministry of External Affairs, meanwhile, said he had been issued a show-cause notice seeking an explanation for discrepancies concerning his place of birth in his passport..

title: 'Wish Akhilesh Had Spent 6 Months In Jail': Azam Khan Recalls Prison Ordeal, SP Chief Reacts
description: Reacting to Khan's account after the manifesto launch, Yadav said he understood the senior leader's suffering and had felt his pain over the years.
author: Yimkumla Longkumer
content:
'Wish Akhilesh Had Spent 6 Months In Jail': Azam Khan Recalls Prison Ordeal, SP Chief Reacts
Reacting to Khan's account after the manifesto launch, Yadav said he understood the senior leader's suffering and had felt his pain over the years.
Senior Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan on Thursday recalled his difficult time in prison and said he sometimes wished party chief Akhilesh Yadav had spent six months behind bars to understand the hardships faced by inmates.
Speaking at the launch of the Samajwadi Party’s manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in Lucknow, Khan said he had often shared this thought with his son Abdullah and others during his imprisonment.
- ‘Azam Khan Should Fear An Encounter’: BJP's Sangeet Som Says SP Leader Was Behind Muzaffarnagar Riots
- 'Hyderabadi Biryani Is Not Preferred Here': Azam Khan's Swipe At Owaisi As UP Poll Battle Heats Up
- ‘Hyderabadi Biryani Aur Pulao Sad Gaye Hain’: Azam Khan Dismisses Owaisi-Chandrashekhar Tie-Up For UP Polls | Exclusive
- Akhilesh Yadav vs Keshav Maurya: 'Radhe Radhe' Slogan Sparks UP Political Row | News18
“My heart wished Akhilesh ji, too, could come to jail for six months, so he could know how the days and nights pass and what one goes through," Khan said.
His remarks came with Yadav sitting on the stage during the event.
Akhilesh Yadav Says He Felt Khan’s Pain
Reacting to Khan’s account after the manifesto launch, Yadav said he understood the senior leader’s suffering and had felt his pain over the years.
“He is a member of our party and our family. I have felt his pain from time to time," the SP chief told reporters.
Khan also spoke about the emotional trauma of being separated from his son Abdullah during a prison transfer. He said the experience left him uncertain about whether they would ever meet again.
The senior SP leader said his imprisonment involved severe mental and physical distress. He also recalled the difficulties of having his son remain in jail alongside him for years.
Earlier, Yadav had assured Khan that the party would do whatever was needed to fulfil the promises made in its manifesto.
Azam Khan’s Imprisonment And Political Career
Khan, a 10-time MLA from Rampur, served as a cabinet minister in the Akhilesh Yadav-led Uttar Pradesh government from 2012 to 2017.
He was released from Ghaziabad’s Dasna jail on November 18 after the Allahabad High Court granted him interim bail in a money laundering case linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur.
The Enforcement Directorate had arrested him on October 31, shortly after his release from Rampur jail in another case. He had spent nearly 11 months in prison during that earlier stint.

title: Ujjwala Scheme Helps Prevent 15% Of Household PM2.5 Emissions In North India, But Solid Fuels Persist
description: While the access to LPG has expanded, people continue to use firewood, and other solid fuels for cooking, heating and lighting, which adds to the winter pollution
author: Pathikrit Sen Gupta, Srishti Choudhary
content:
Ujjwala Scheme Helps Prevent 15% Of Household PM2.5 Emissions In North India, But Solid Fuels Persist
While the access to LPG has expanded, people continue to use firewood, and other solid fuels for cooking, heating and lighting, which adds to the winter pollution
Got Question about the News?
Burning solid fuels for cooking and heating remains one of the largest contributors to primary PM2.5 emissions in the Indo-Gangetic plains, even though the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) has helped prevent at least 15 per cent residential PM2.5 emissions and 4 per cent black carbon emissions in 2025 alone, according to a new study.
Since its launch in May, 2016, the scheme has provided free LPG connections to 105 million women from economically weaker households. The latest study compared a decade of actual LPG sales with a scenario in which PMUY was never launched, and estimated that additional LPG use under PMUY avoided 4,963 kilotonnes of PM2.5 and 132 kilotonnes of black carbon from 2016 to 2026, including 834 kilotonnes of PM2.5 in FY25-26 alone.
- Are Punjab, Haryana Farm Fires Being Hidden? Satellite Data May Be Missing The Real Picture | News18
- Electric Idli Maker vs Traditional Stovetop Pot: Which Is Convenient, Makes Soft, Fluffy Idlis?
- WHO Congratulates India On 1 Crore HPV Vaccine Doses; 6 States Achieve 100% Target Coverage
- School Holidays: Delhi, UP, Bihar Schools Closed Tomorrow Due To Guru Nanak Jayanti
While that is some progress, the study done by New Delhi-based Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW), found that at least 36 per cent of primary PM2.5 emissions in the most-polluted airsheds of the Indo-Gangetic plains can still be traced to cooking. Home to 40% of India’s population, the Indo-Gangetic plains is one of India’s most polluted regions, which remains under a toxic smog for most of the winter season.
A WINTER TOP-UP FOR CLEAN AIR?
The study found that while access to LPG has expanded, it has not translated into sustained use in households. People continue to use firewood and other solid fuels for cooking, heating and lighting, worsening the pollution, especially during winter. PMUY beneficiaries use an average of 4.8 cylinders a year, against the 7-8 cylinders a household needs to cook exclusively on LPG. “Many families still cook with firewood alongside LPG because the next refill is hard to afford," said co-author Abhishek Kar, Fellow, CEEW, adding that residential combustion is often overlooked as a major pollution source, but it burns year-round and spikes every winter.
As per government survey data for 2023-24, LPG is the primary cooking fuel for 90 per cent of households in Punjab, but only 61 per cent in Uttar Pradesh, 47 per cent in Bihar and 40 per cent in Jharkhand. CEEW’s own survey of rural households in Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand found that 44 per cent and 66 per cent, respectively, still cooked only on solid fuels. “The households we surveyed most often told us the high cost of the next refill keeps them burning firewood alongside LPG. A winter top-up would ease that, but only for those already enrolled, and only while LPG is available. Enrolment drives and a second clean option, such as electric cooktops in the kitchen, matter just as much," said lead author Rahul Das, Programme Associate, CEEW.
The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana scheme has provided free LPG connections to 105 million women since May 2016.
The CEEW study estimated that additional LPG use under PMUY avoided 4,963 kilotonnes of PM2.5 from 2016 to 2026.
PMUY beneficiaries use an average of 4.8 cylinders a year compared to the 7-8 cylinders needed to cook exclusively on LPG.
LPG serves as the primary cooking fuel for 90 per cent of households in Punjab, 61 per cent in Uttar Pradesh, 47 per cent in Bihar, and 40 per cent in Jharkhand based on 2023-24 government data.
PMUY households pay about Rs 642 for a cylinder in Delhi, after a subsidy of Rs 300 that has covered up to four cylinders a year since June 2026. Refill costs were cited as the main barrier, followed by patchy home delivery. The study recommended a winter top-up on LPG refills — an extra Rs 200 for four cylinders between October and March, when pollution levels peak across the plain, in Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal, to bring a refill down to about Rs 442 at today’s price.
“Rs 400 is the price at which four in five surveyed households said they would cook only on LPG, though those answers were self-reported. The top-up would be a fixed Rs 200 per cylinder, with refills at least 25 days apart to keep costs predictable and prevent misuse," the CEEW team said in its latest report.
Quick Answers
The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana has helped prevent at least 15 percent of residential PM2.5 emissions and 4 percent of black carbon emissions in North India's Indo-Gangetic plains during 2025 alone.
