title: Jaipur Viral Video: क्लब में चेकिंग करती रही पुलिस, पीसीआर में युवक छलकाते रहे जाम
description: राजधानी जयपुर में पांच युवकों ने पुलिस की पीसीआर को ही शराब पार्टी का ठिकाना बना लिया। जिस वक्त पुलिसकर्मी क्लब में चेकिंग कर रहे थे, उसी दौरान युवक सरकारी गाड़ी में बैठकर जाम छलका रहे थे। इतना ही नहीं, उन्होंने पुलिस वाहन के वायरलेस का तार तक तोड़ दिया।
author: Kamal Mishra
content:
Hindi News / Rajasthan / Jaipur / Jaipur Viral Video: क्लब में चेकिंग करती रही पुलिस, पीसीआर में युवक छलकाते रहे जाम
Jaipur Viral Video: क्लब में चेकिंग करती रही पुलिस, पीसीआर में युवक छलकाते रहे जाम
राजधानी जयपुर में पांच युवकों ने पुलिस की पीसीआर को ही शराब पार्टी का ठिकाना बना लिया। जिस वक्त पुलिसकर्मी क्लब में चेकिंग कर रहे थे, उसी दौरान युवक सरकारी गाड़ी में बैठकर जाम छलका रहे थे। इतना ही नहीं, उन्होंने पुलिस वाहन के वायरलेस का तार तक तोड़ दिया।
जयपुर। राजधानी जयपुर में पुलिस की कार्यप्रणाली पर सवाल खड़े करने वाला एक वीडियो सोशल मीडिया पर वायरल हुआ है। इसमें पांच युवक पुलिस की पीसीआर (चेतक) में बैठकर शराब पार्टी करते और फिल्मी गानों पर रील बनाते नजर आ रहे हैं। हैरानी की बात यह है कि जिस समय युवक पुलिस की गाड़ी में बैठकर जाम छलका रहे थे, उस समय पुलिसकर्मी कुछ ही दूरी पर स्थित क्लब में चेकिंग कर रहे थे। वीडियो सामने आने के बाद पुलिस महकमे में हलचल मच गई। पुलिस ने पांचों युवकों की पहचान कर उनके खिलाफ मामला दर्ज किया है। अब आरोपियों की गिरफ्तारी के लिए दबिश दी जा रही है।
मामला 13 सितंबर का बताया जा रहा है। डीसीपी (ईस्ट) रंजीता शर्मा के अनुसार, उस दिन एसएमएस थाना पुलिस की चेतक पर चालक कृष्ण और हेड कांस्टेबल हरिमोहन की ड्यूटी थी। दोनों नारायण सिंह सर्कल स्थित सबाना क्लब में चेकिंग के लिए पहुंचे थे। क्लब में भीड़ अधिक होने के कारण हेड कांस्टेबल ने चालक को भी अंदर बुला लिया। इसी दौरान शराब के नशे में पांच युवक क्लब से बाहर आए।
पुलिसकर्मियों की गैरमौजूदगी देखकर युवकों ने बाहर खड़ी पीसीआर को ही पार्टी का ठिकाना बना लिया। वे पुलिस की गाड़ी में बैठ गए और शराब की बोतल हाथ में लेकर फिल्मी गानों पर रील बनाने लगे। वीडियो में एक युवक सड़क पर खड़े होकर भी शराब पीता दिखाई दे रहा है। युवकों ने इस दौरान पीसीआर के वायरलेस का तार भी तोड़ दिया। इसके बाद उन्होंने वीडियो सोशल मीडिया पर अपलोड कर दिया।
वीडियो वायरल हुआ तो बंद कर लिए मोबाइल
करीब ढाई महीने पुराना यह वीडियो 26 नवंबर को सोशल मीडिया पर वायरल हुआ। इसके बाद पुलिस ने जांच शुरू की। डीसीपी के मुताबिक, क्लब संचालक की मदद से पांचों युवकों की पहचान भव्य खंडेलवाल, आशुतोष चक्रवर्ती, गोपाल, मृणाल और अमन जैन के रूप में हुई है। पांचों के खिलाफ एसएमएस अस्पताल थाने में बीएनएस, आईटी एक्ट और पीडीपीपी एक्ट के तहत मामला दर्ज किया गया है। वीडियो वायरल होने के बाद आरोपियों ने अपने मोबाइल फोन बंद कर लिए। पुलिस उनकी तलाश में संभावित ठिकानों पर दबिश दे रही है।
पुलिसकर्मियों की भूमिका भी जांच के घेरे में
इस पूरे घटनाक्रम में पुलिसकर्मियों की भूमिका भी सवालों के घेरे में है। आखिर ड्यूटी पर तैनात पुलिसकर्मियों की मौजूदगी में युवकों ने सरकारी वाहन में बैठकर शराब पार्टी कैसे की? डीसीपी रंजीता शर्मा ने बताया कि मामले की जांच की जा रही है। ड्यूटी में लापरवाही बरतने वाले पुलिसकर्मियों की भूमिका भी खंगाली जाएगी। जांच में दोषी पाए जाने पर उनके खिलाफ भी कार्रवाई की जाएगी।

title: Kota News: ‘तुम्हारी ठेकेदारी धरी रह जाएगी… लगा लेना फिर तुम जैक’, महापौर अनुसुईया गोस्वामी का चढ़ा पारा
description: कोटा में सफाई व्यवस्था का जायजा लेने निकलीं महापौर अनुसुईया गोस्वामी वार्ड 87 में अव्यवस्थाएं देखकर भड़क गईं। सफाई कर्मचारी गायब मिले और महिला श्रमिकों में नाबालिग बच्चियां भी नजर आईं। इसके बाद महापौर ने ठेकेदार को फोन लगाकर ऐसी फटकार लगाई कि बातचीत का अंदाज चर्चा में आ गया।
author: Kamal Mishra
content:
Hindi News / Rajasthan / Kota / Kota News: ‘तुम्हारी ठेकेदारी धरी रह जाएगी… लगा लेना फिर तुम जैक’, महापौर अनुसुईया गोस्वामी का चढ़ा पारा
Kota News: ‘तुम्हारी ठेकेदारी धरी रह जाएगी… लगा लेना फिर तुम जैक’, महापौर अनुसुईया गोस्वामी का चढ़ा पारा
कोटा में सफाई व्यवस्था का जायजा लेने निकलीं महापौर अनुसुईया गोस्वामी वार्ड 87 में अव्यवस्थाएं देखकर भड़क गईं। सफाई कर्मचारी गायब मिले और महिला श्रमिकों में नाबालिग बच्चियां भी नजर आईं। इसके बाद महापौर ने ठेकेदार को फोन लगाकर ऐसी फटकार लगाई कि बातचीत का अंदाज चर्चा में आ गया।
Kota: निरीक्षण के दौरान ठेकेदार को फटकार लगाती महापौर अनुसुईया गोस्वामी। (फोटो-पत्रिका)
कोटा। शहर की सफाई व्यवस्था को लेकर महापौर अनुसुईया गोस्वामी गुरुवार सुबह औचक निरीक्षण पर निकलीं तो वार्ड 87 में अव्यवस्थाएं देखकर उनका पारा चढ़ गया। मौके पर सफाई कर्मचारी नदारद मिले। वहीं, काम के लिए मौजूद महिला श्रमिकों में चार नाबालिग बच्चियां भी होने की बात सामने आई। यह देखकर महापौर ने मौके से ही ठेकेदार को फोन लगाया और जमकर फटकार लगाई। फोन पर महापौर ने दो टूक कहा- 'तुम्हारी ठेकेदारी धरी रह जाएगी… लगा लेना फिर तुम जैक।'
महापौर ने ठेकेदार अनिकेत से सवाल किया कि जब शहर में सफाई व्यवस्था की जिम्मेदारी उसे सौंपी गई है तो कर्मचारी मौके पर क्यों नहीं मिलते? न नालियों की सफाई करने वाली लेबर समय पर पहुंच रही है और न ही झाड़ू लगाने वाले कर्मचारी दिखाई दे रहे हैं। उन्होंने नाराजगी जताते हुए कहा कि ठेकेदार खुद घर पर आराम कर रहा है और महापौर सड़क पर खड़ी होकर सफाई व्यवस्था देख रही हैं।
'तुम तो राजा हो रहे हो, हम रोड पर खड़े हैं'
ठेकेदार से फोन पर बातचीत के दौरान महापौर ने कहा कि तुम तो राजा हो रहे हो, हम रोड पर खड़े हैं और तुम घर पर ऐश-आराम कर रहे हो। जब महापौर मौके पर मौजूद हैं तो ठेकेदार को भी यहां आकर व्यवस्था देखनी चाहिए। उन्होंने साफ कहा कि सफाई के नाम पर लापरवाही और कागजों में श्रमिकों की संख्या दिखाने का रवैया अब बर्दाश्त नहीं किया जाएगा।
महापौर ने ठेकेदार को निर्देश दिए कि रोजाना सुबह 8.30 बजे तक सफाई के सभी निर्धारित पॉइंट पर पूरी लेबर मौजूद होनी चाहिए। इसमें नालियों की सफाई करने वाले, झाड़ू लगाने वाले और कचरा उठाने वाले कर्मचारी शामिल हैं। उन्होंने कहा कि सफाई कार्य निर्धारित समय पर शुरू होना चाहिए, ताकि वार्ड में नियमित रूप से सफाई हो सके।
निगम अधिकारियों को भी लगाई फटकार
निरीक्षण के दौरान महापौर ने नगर निगम के अधिकारियों और कर्मचारियों को भी आड़े हाथों लिया। उन्होंने सवाल किया कि जब सफाई का समय सुबह 8 बजे निर्धारित है तो साढ़े नौ बजे तक भी श्रमिक मौके पर क्यों नहीं पहुंचते? अधिकारियों की जिम्मेदारी है कि वे सफाई कार्य की नियमित मॉनिटरिंग करें और यह सुनिश्चित करें कि ठेकेदार की ओर से पर्याप्त कर्मचारी लगाए जाएं।
वार्ड 87 के निरीक्षण में सामने आई अव्यवस्थाओं के बाद महापौर ने व्यवस्था में तत्काल सुधार के निर्देश दिए। खासतौर पर नाबालिग बच्चियों के श्रमिकों के रूप में मिलने के मामले को लेकर भी नाराजगी जताई। अब देखना होगा कि महापौर की इस सख्ती के बाद वार्ड की सफाई व्यवस्था में कितना सुधार होता है।

title: Indian Railways Wins Silver Prize For Pavilion At IITF 2026 In New Delhi
description: Indian Railways' IITF 2026 pavilion under 'Vikas aur Virasat' showcases modernisation, the Vande Bharat Sleeper train, and passenger-centric services, underscoring faster, safer rail connectivity.
author: Oneindia Staff
content:
Indian Railways Wins Silver Prize For Pavilion At IITF 2026 In New Delhi
At IITF 2026 in New Delhi, Indian Railways earned the Silver Prize for its 'Vikas aur Virasat' pavilion, highlighting a blend of heritage and modern technology. The showcase featured the Vande Bharat Sleeper train and a range of railway models illustrating infrastructure, innovation, and improved passenger experience.
New Delhi: The Ministry of Railways has won the Silver Prize for its pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The pavilion was presented under this year's theme, _'Vikas aur Virasat'_, highlighting the Indian Railways' journey of combining its rich legacy with modern technological advancements.
The Indian Railways pavilion attracted considerable attention from visitors and jury members for its presentation of the country's progress in railway infrastructure, advanced engineering and passenger-focused services. One of the major attractions at the pavilion was the newly launched **Vande Bharat Sleeper train**, which aims to transform long-distance overnight journeys with improved safety features, enhanced passenger comfort and modern onboard facilities.
AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors
The exhibition also featured an impressive collection of models representing different trains operated across the Indian Railways network, offering visitors a glimpse into the scale and diversity of the country's railway operations. The pavilion highlighted the significant transformation taking place across the Indian Railways network, with a focus on modernisation, innovation and improved passenger experience.
The Silver Prize marks an important recognition of Indian Railways' efforts to showcase its achievements while preserving its rich heritage. It also reflects the national transporter’s continued focus on developing faster, safer and more comfortable rail connectivity. Through its participation at IITF 2026, Indian Railways reaffirmed its commitment to the vision of building a modern railway network that balances India's traditional strengths with emerging technologies and world-class infrastructure.

title: 'Bundle Of Lies And Hollow Promises': BJP Attacks Akhilesh Yadav Over SP's UP Poll Manifesto
description: BJP leaders Pankaj Chaudhary, Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak attack Akhilesh Yadav's SP manifesto for the 2027 UP Assembly elections, calling it a 'dhokha patra' and questioning its promises on jobs, farmers and social justice.
author: PTI
content:
'Bundle Of Lies And Hollow Promises': BJP Attacks Akhilesh Yadav Over SP's UP Poll Manifesto
The BJP on Thursday dismissed the Samajwadi Party's manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections as a "dhokha patra", accusing party president Akhilesh Yadav of making unrealistic promises despite what it described as a poor governance record during the SP's previous tenure.
AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors
Reacting to the manifesto, BJP state president and Union Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary said people would not trust the SP's promises, alleging that its history was marked by fear, corruption, hooliganism, lawlessness and appeasement politics.
Describing the manifesto as a "loot patra, dhokha patra and bhram patra", Chaudhary said the SP came out with a bundle of misleading promises before every election. In a statement, he recalled the SP's 2012 promises and alleged that after coming to power, the party worked to fill its own coffers instead of serving people. He accused the previous SP government of pushing the state into communal riots, corruption and criminal activities.
Questioning Yadav's claims on social justice, Chaudhary alleged that Dalits, backward classes, women and youngsters faced injustice during the SP regime. He also accused the previous government of failing to protect Dalit settlements and said statues of B R Ambedkar were damaged during its tenure.
Chaudhary said Yadav should answer for these incidents before speaking about the Constitution and social justice. He also referred to SP leader Azam Khan's alleged derogatory remarks against Ambedkar and demanded an apology from the SP chief.
On employment, Chaudhary termed the SP's promise of 25 lakh government jobs in five years an "election jumla". He challenged Yadav to account for the employment opportunities created during the SP government's tenure from 2012 to 2017.
He also questioned the SP's claims on investment and industrial development, alleging that its government had failed to create an environment conducive to investors and industries. Accusing the SP of neglecting farmers when it was in power, Chaudhary said the party was now making promises in their name despite having failed to ensure fair prices and protection for them during its tenure.
He alleged that the previous SP government had failed to maintain law and order and that women faced security concerns, while criminals enjoyed political patronage. Chaudhary said the BJP would seek another mandate in UP on the basis of development, good governance, security and public welfare.
Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya also attacked the SP over its manifesto, calling it a "dhakosla patra" and accusing Yadav of making promises after neglecting governance, development and law and order while in power. In a post on X in Hindi, Maurya said the people of UP had not forgotten what he described as "goondaraj" and the protection of criminals during the SP regime.
"Yadav ji, do not get so disturbed by being out of power that you have to open a shop of false promises. The people of Uttar Pradesh know the dark history of you and your governments," Maurya said. He further claimed that the SP's electoral prospects would suffer in the 2027 assembly elections, asserting that the BJP's agenda of good governance, development and security would prevail.
Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak accused the Samajwadi Party of shielding criminals and mafias during its tenures, mistreating Dalits and failing to deliver on promises, while claiming the BJP had improved law and order and created employment opportunities.
"Samajwadi Party has issued not a manifesto but a bundle of lies and hollow promises. It should have issued an apology letter instead, seeking forgiveness from the people for its past actions," Pathak said. "BJP works on its track record, while the Samajwadi Party keeps playing the tape record of its old promises," he said, alleging that the SP had never implemented its previous manifesto.

title: Major Fire Breaks Out At Sahara Shahar In Lucknow, 15 Fire Tenders Rushed To Spot
description: A major fire broke out in the parking area of Sahara Shahar in Lucknow's Gomti Nagar, prompting the deployment of 15 fire tenders. The incident came hours after another fire at a firecracker and mattress shop in Jankipuram Extension.
author: PTI
content:
Major Fire Breaks Out At Sahara Shahar In Lucknow, 15 Fire Tenders Rushed To Spot
A major fire broke out in the parking area of Sahara Shahar in Lucknow's Gomti Nagar on Thursday evening, prompting the deployment of 15 fire tenders, officials said. The fire was reported at around 6.30 pm, following which fire personnel, led by the chief fire officer, rushed to the spot.
AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors
The blaze was brought under control, and firefighters were engaged in dousing the remaining flames, an official said.
There was no information about anyone being trapped in the incident, the official said, adding that local police personnel were also assisting in the operation.
Eyewitness accounts and visuals from the area indicated that flames rose high above the site, while a thick plume of smoke was visible from a distance, triggering panic in the neighbourhood.
Earlier in the day, another major fire broke out at a shop selling firecrackers and mattresses in Sector 3 of Jankipuram Extension in the city. The fire triggered repeated explosions of firecrackers for nearly two hours, officials said.
 VIDEO | Uttar Pradesh: A massive fire broke out inside a building at Sahara States in Gomti Nagar area of Lucknow.Fire tenders and firefighters are engaged in continuous efforts to bring the blaze under control. The exact cause of the fire is yet to be established. No casualties or injuries have been reported yet.(Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd)
— Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) November 26, 2026
Three fire tenders and local police personnel were rushed to the spot, and the blaze was brought under control after an operation lasting around two hours. No casualties were reported, police said.
A sprawling private campus with lush greenery adjoining the Gomti, Sahara Shahar was established as part of the business and real estate operations of the Sahara Group, founded by late businessman Subrata Roy Sahara.
He later faced prolonged legal proceedings over funds raised from investors, culminating in his imprisonment in 2014 following Supreme Court proceedings in the investor-refund case. He died in November 2023. The property faces legal challenges.

title: Firewood and dung cakes fuel nearly half of PM2.5 emissions in polluted Indo-Gangetic belt
description: Cooking's Contribution To PM2.5 Emissions Remains High Despite The Progress Made By The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) In Recent Years
author: PTI
content:
A new study has revealed that cooking with firewood, dung cakes and coal, among others, is the single largest source of PM2.5 emissions in the most polluted areas of the Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP).
It added that cooking through such methods contributes 36-49 per cent of the total primary PM2.5 emissions in the IGP's most polluted parts, stretching from Punjab in the west through Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar to West Bengal in the east.
The study, released by the Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW) on Thursday, comes at a time when Delhi-NCR continues to witness bad air quality, and much of the focus is on how stubble burning and Diwali firecrackers drive spikes in pollution.
Cooking's contribution to PM2.5 emissions remains high despite the progress made by the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) in recent years.
The scheme was launched in May 2016 to provide economically weaker households with free LPG connections.
According to the study, the PMUY helped avert 15 per cent of India's household PM2.5 emissions in financial year 2025-2026.
In a statement, Abhishek Kar, a fellow at the CEEW, said, "Many families still cook with firewood alongside LPG because the next refill is hard to afford, and in the Indo-Gangetic Plain's most polluted areas, cooking is the single largest source of PM2.5 emissions."
The study highlighted that residential combustion takes place year-round and increases every winter, as households also burn fuel for heating.
Cooking accounts for about 80 per cent of household energy use, so transitioning from polluting to cleaner cooking fuels is the only way to cut most of the residential emissions, according to the study.
It recommended a winter top-up under the PMUY that would make the next LPG refill affordable when pollution is at its worst.
The study also suggested that India's 25,000-plus LPG distributors sell certified induction cooktops and electric pressure cookers at a discount to households that give up two of their four subsidised cylinders.

title: Congress alleges ‘contempt’ for democracy over delay in Great Nicobar case in Calcutta HC
description: The Modi Government Came With A Clear Strategy To Further 'stall And Delay' The High Court Proceedings, Even After Assuring The Supreme Court That It Would Co-operate To Have The Hearings Completed, Says Jairam Ramesh
author: PTI
content:
The Congress on Thursday accused the Modi government of delaying the proceedings on four petitions challenging the Great Nicobar Island Project in the Calcutta High Court, saying it "suddenly discovered" the need to file new affidavits and has demonstrated "utter contempt" for democratic processes.
Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said on Wednesday, the Calcutta High Court was to finally begin hearings on four petitions challenging the Great Nicobar Island Project.
"One petition is based on violations of the Forest Rights Act, 2006. Two petitions challenge the drastic reduction in the Eco Sensitive Zone notified around Galathea and Campbell Bay National Parks. The fourth petition assails the approval of Coastal Zone Management Plan maps for Great Nicobar in which coral reefs have magically disappeared," Ramesh pointed out.
The Modi government came with a clear strategy to further "stall and delay" the High Court proceedings, even after assuring the Supreme Court that it would co-operate to have the hearings completed as scheduled and having them argued yesterday itself, he said on X.
"The hearings have now been put off to January 13, 2027, because the Modi government suddenly discovered the need to file new affidavits," Ramesh said.
Meanwhile, this ecological disaster of a project continues to get "bulldozed through", he alleged.
"Bids were invited on October 26th to demarcate the entire 166.1 sq km area earmarked for the project that includes about 122 sq km area of biodiversity-rich forest land. The boundary is itself of about 43 km. Tenders were thus invited just a month before the Calcutta High Court hearings demonstrating the utter contempt that the Modi government has for democratic processes," Ramesh said.
"Its mind is made up and can be summed up thus: 'Let the challenges meander their way through the courts but the project will go forward unhindered'. This is brazen callousness. The havoc that it will cause is foretold," he said.

title: Govt to consider E25 petrol only after 'necessary ecosystem' is in place: Hardeep Puri
description: The Union Minister Says 'Rest Assured. Our Policy Is Very Clear. We Will Conduct A Comprehensive Set Of Tests To Move Beyond E20 Petrol. Only When The Necessary Ecosystem Is Ready We Will Consider Moving To E25 Or Beyond'
author: PTI
content:
Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Thursday that necessary tests will be conducted and a "comprehensive ecosystem" will be developed before increasing the ethanol blending in petrol from the current 20 percent.
During a question-and-answer session with students at a Constitution Day celebration at Devi Ahilya University in Indore, Puri said that India has achieved the target of 20 percent ethanol blending in petrol well ahead of the original 2030 target.
"Rest assured. Our policy is very clear. We will conduct a comprehensive set of tests to move beyond E20 petrol. Only when the necessary ecosystem is ready we will consider moving to E25 or beyond," he said.
Ethanol blending in petrol -- which has drawn criticism from a section of consumers -- has saved India Rs 1.90 lakh crore in foreign exchange, of which Rs 1.40 lakh crore has gone to farmers, the minister said.
Later, while speaking to reporters, Puri said, "There is no problem with the availability of LPG cylinders in the country. However, the government is trying to encourage people to switch from LPG to Piped Natural Gas (PNG), as PNG is a more pure, economical and convenient fuel."
He also claimed that opposition parties are spreading confusion regarding petrol prices. The Union Minister said that there is currently no shortage in the global supply of petrol, and given the current situation, the prices may decrease.
Puri said that petrol prices depend on global crude prices, transportation costs, refining margins, and dealer commissions.
"Now if anyone comes and tells you that they have a magic wand that can make petrol prices rise or fall, it's not true. I've been looking for such a wand for five years, but I haven't found it yet," he quipped.
Puri, recently elected to the Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh, has been targeted by Congress for allegedly having links with American sex offender Jeffrey Epstein in the past. Congress has also cited a purported photograph of Puri and Epstein.
Asked about the same, he denied the allegations, saying the issue was being raised for political gains.
"I have already addressed a press conference on this issue. I already stated that I was not the Permanent Representative to the United Nations at that time and was a private citizen. I used to live in New York and meet important people.
"At that time, a person showed a photo in which he was sitting there and I was sitting here. What more do you want to know?" Puri said.
Regarding the re-alliance between the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Shiromani Akali Dal ahead of the Punjab Assembly elections, Puri said that this alliance would prove to be very good for Punjab and the country.

title: Was Delhi pollution data during Diwali misleading?
description: BBC Verify analysis indicates missing data led official Diwali pollution figures to be lower than they should be.
author: Shruti Menon and Barbara Metzler
content:
Was Delhi pollution data during Diwali misleading?
- Published
BBC Verify has found significant discrepancies between two Indian government datasets showing Delhi's air pollution during Diwali, indicating official figures may not have captured the full extent of the problem.
As fireworks lit up Delhi's skies on 8 November to mark one of India's biggest festivals, some monitoring stations recorded very high levels of PM2.5, a fine particulate matter which can damage people's lungs and cause other serious health problems.
But every hourly PM2.5 reading above 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre was excluded from the widely cited air quality index (AQI) published by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), even though these higher readings were present in the data from the Delhi Pollution Control Commission (DPCC).
Delhi is one of the most polluted cities in the world and often has dangerously poor air quality, so it is vital people living in India's capital can trust the official data. Firecrackers are not the only cause of pollution, which is also attributed to a mix of reasons including vehicle emissions, construction dust, farm fires and atmospheric factors. But they can worsen air quality, especially in winter.
Government critics and opposition parties have accused the government of deliberately under-reporting the pollution data. The CPCB rejected this in a statement, which said the body was "committed to transparent, scientific and reliable reporting".
The CPCB, whose figures are generally cited by Indian media, said readings above 1,000 micrograms are treated as "outside" the range for detection its equipment has been calibrated for and are excluded from calculations.
"During extreme episodes which are occasional like Diwali firecracker bursting, this may appear as a data gap at the particular station concerned, and those hours do not contribute to the 24-hour average of relevant pollutant for concerned station," the statement added.
Dr Manoj Kumar, a researcher at Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), told BBC Verify that excluding high readings risks misrepresenting actual pollution levels and could cause people to lose trust in official figures.
Our analysis found that, across the same 30 stations over 24 hours covering Diwali night, available CPCB readings averaged 240 micrograms per cubic metre - less than half the average of 551 in DPCC's data.
What does the pollution data show?
On the night of Diwali from Sunday into Monday, Delhi's already high pollution levels rose sharply as the celebrations peaked.
Three different pollution monitoring stations recorded PM2.5 hourly concentrations above 3,000 micrograms, DPCC data examined by BBC Verify shows.
Dr Kumar said that even a short-term exposure to extreme levels of particulate matter can have adverse health impacts.
The World Health Organization's air quality guidelines state that annual average concentrations should not exceed five micrograms per cubic metre.
Between 21:00 local time (15:30 GMT) on 8 November and 07:00 on 9 November, during the peak of Diwali celebrations, 217 hourly PM2.5 observations were missing across 59 CPCB monitoring stations in Delhi. Only 16 stations reported complete data during this period, while 43 had at least one missing observation.
None of the 116 readings above 1,000 micrograms from the 30 DPCC-managed stations appeared in the CPCB's published records they feed data into.
This matters because stations need at least 16 hours of valid PM2.5 measurements to calculate a daily average, according to CPCB's methodology. So a station with too many missing or invalid readings will not contribute to official pollution calculations.
One example of a station with several hours of missing data was at RK Puram in south Delhi, where pollution peaked at nearly 2,500 micrograms.
Using hourly PM2.5 readings from this station, BBC Verify calculated an average concentration of about 945 micrograms over the 24-hour period after 17:00 on 8 November.
But similar averages of CPCB's published data for 14 of those 24 hours produced a much lower figure of 299 micrograms. The missing 10 hours also meant this data was not included in daily average calculations.
The missing data across the city means that, despite a sharp overnight rise in pollution at some monitoring stations, CPCB reported Delhi's AQI at 344 at 16:00 on 9 November, down from 376 at the same time the day before.
Dr Sierra Clark, an environmental epidemiologist from City St George's, University in London, warned classifying high pollution readings as missing could leave out days which "contribute the most to short-term health events, such as asthma attacks and heart attacks".
She told BBC Verify "for transparency", Delhi's pollution reporting could show two scenarios including and excluding extreme pollution episodes.
"The latter would give a sense of typical pollution levels that are more representative of people's day-to-day experience. But it is also important to show the impact of those few days and what they contribute," Dr Clark added.
Pollution in Delhi is not limited to PM2.5 and satellite imagery shows a thick haze over the city on 8 and 9 November.
Satellite measurements of other pollutants like nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO) and fire activity in the atmosphere, rather than at ground level, showed increases on 8 November.
But their overall average for Diwali week was not very high compared with 2024 and 2025.
Graphics by Jess Carr and Tom Shiel.

title: Tamil Nadu: India investigates alleged 'AI scam' involving public library books
description: The Tamil Nadu government has ordered an internal audit of library collections across the state.
author: Xavier Selvakumar and Yazhiniyan
content:
New Indian mega library rocked by scandal over 'AI-generated books'
- Published
An Indian court has ordered an investigation into allegations that a public library in the southern state of Tamil Nadu bought hundreds of books suspected of being generated using AI.
The controversy began after Tamil novelist Perumal Murugan raised concerns about books containing false information and questionable authorship at a newly opened library in Coimbatore city.
The Madras High Court has ordered the state's anti-corruption agency to investigate the purchases and freeze bank accounts linked to a publisher accused of supplying the books.
The state government has blamed the previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party-led administration for buying the books. The DMK denies allegations.
Tamil Nadu's School Education Minister A Rajmohan has described the allegations as potentially "India's first AI scam" and said the investigation would cover purchases at other public libraries across the state.
The case has raised wider questions about the growing use of AI in publishing, where tools can generate entire books quickly and cheaply, but also produce false information and invented references.
It has also highlighted the challenges facing libraries and publishers in checking the authenticity of books as AI-generated content becomes more widespread.
The controversy centres on the Periyar Arivulagam library, built at a cost of about 3bn rupees ($34m; £26m). Named after social reformer Periyar EV Ramasamy, it was inaugurated on 16 October by Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay.
Murugan, whose novels Pyre and One Part Woman have received international recognition, raised concerns after visiting the library last month.
Writing in an online magazine, he alleged that nearly 1,800 books in its Tamil section had been supplied by a little-known publisher called Agal Vilakku Pathippagam.
He said many of the books carried unfamiliar authors' names, unusually high prices and questionable International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs).
One book cited in the controversy, Naladiyar Vaazhvin Vazhikatti (A Guide to Life through Naladiyar), was reportedly priced at 1,445 rupees for 300 pages.
It describes Naladiyar as a Tamil poet and philosopher, although Naladiyar is a classical Tamil work consisting of 400 four-line verses on morality and ethics.
Another book reportedly attributes the ancient Tamil poem Madurai Kanchi to an incorrect author. It remains unclear whether AI was used to produce any of the disputed books.
Questions have also been raised about a book found at another public library in Madurai which names renowned economist Jean Drèze as its author.
The book, Democracy and People's Rights in the Contemporary World, names renowned economist Jean Drèze as its author and was published by Phoenix Publishing House.
Drèze did not respond to BBC Tamil's request for comment but told The Hindu newspaper earlier this week that he had not written the book, raising concerns that his name may have been used without his permission.
BBC Tamil visited a Chennai address listed by Agal Vilakku and another publisher named in the controversy, Phoenix Publishing House, but found no signs identifying either business.
A woman at the address confirmed that Agal Vilakku operated there. Its proprietor, Mohan, declined to comment, saying the matter was before the courts.
The controversy has prompted writers, academics and publishers to question how the books were selected for public libraries.
More than 160 writers, researchers, artists and publishers have signed a joint statement calling for an independent inquiry, the release of procurement records and an audit of library collections across Tamil Nadu.
They have also called for the recovery of public money if the investigation finds that funds were misused.
The group questioned how the disputed books could have passed through a selection process involving expert committees, price negotiations and several levels of review.
The state government has ordered an internal audit of public library collections.
Rajmohan said 523 books had already been removed from the historic Connemara Public Library in Chennai city after preliminary checks raised concerns about their authenticity and quality.
Disputed books have also been removed from Periyar Arivulagam, while anti-corruption officials examine procurement records and inspect other libraries, he added.
The controversy also sparked a political row in Tamil Nadu. Rajmohan accused the previous DMK government of ordering the disputed books and said the state would seek to recover public money if the investigation found wrongdoing.
The DMK has rejected the allegations as politically motivated and has called for an investigation into the purchases.
Additional reporting by Rachita Prasad

title: Pyre: Indian film on elderly couple's love and loneliness won 18 awards - now it's wowing audiences
description: Extraordinary scenes of audiences crying leaving theatres after watching the film have been shared on social media.
author: Geeta Pandey
content:
An Indian film that nobody would release is finally a hit - 18 awards later
- Published
A film about the tender love and quiet loneliness of an elderly couple, which took two years to reach cinemas after it was completed, is wowing critics and audiences across India.
The 111-minute Pyre, directed by television journalist-turned-filmmaker Vinod Kapri, also explores the pressing issue of outmigration which has left hundreds of picturesque Himalayan hamlets abandoned and turned them into ghost villages. It further reflects on the impact of climate change, which has made the region's weather increasingly harsh.
On social media, many Indians have shared videos showing audiences leaving theatres with tears in their eyes. Others have posted that they have not been so moved by a film in a long time.
The film's lead actors, ordinary villagers who had never faced a camera before, have also won praise from some of Bollywood's most respected figures, including Naseeruddin Shah and Anupam Kher.
Pyre's protagonists - Padam Singh (played by Kapri's uncle, Padam Singh) and Tulsi (played by Heera Devi) - are Bubu and Aama, local terms for grandfather and grandmother. The couple live in a small home in the mountains of the northern state of Uttarakhand .
It's a place where age is measured against momentous events. Singh was born two years before the outbreak of World War II. Tulsi was born in the year atomic bombs were dropped on Japan.
There are no roads and no electricity. Whenever the couple need help – which is often as Tulsi frequently has to be carried to hospital – Padam Singh uses a traditional long-horn instrument to summon neighbours. In return for their kindness, he pays them with goats.
"There's nothing here – just mountains," as one character puts it. So the young leave in search of greener pastures, and those who depart this beautiful, but blighted, land rarely return.
Kapri says his film remains focused on the "soulful love story of the ageing couple in their last days".
"They have shared a life together for 65 years and, for the last 28 years, they've been waiting for their son, Hariya, who's gone to Mumbai in search of work, to come back," Kapri tells the BBC. "It's a story of companionship, of loneliness and of waiting."
Their wait takes on a new urgency when suddenly, after all these years, a letter arrives from Hariya setting a date for his visit.
As Padam Singh and Tulsi count down the days, the handful of villagers around them leave one by one, until the couple find themselves alone in the vast mountain landscape.
"You and Tulsi should also leave as soon as possible. Otherwise, you won't even have four people to carry your body down the mountain to the funeral pyre when you or Tulsi die," one departing villager advises Padam Singh. "Or die before we leave," he adds in jest.
With no one left to call for help, Padam Singh builds two funeral pyres side by side right outside his door – one for his wife and one for himself.
"How will I carry you down the mountain if you die?" he tells Tulsi when she questions the decision.
Despite the bleak setting and the weight of the topics covered, Pyre is suffused with humour. The central couple are delightful. Like many long-married spouses, they seem to treat bickering as a love language.
Kapri, who is from Uttarakhand, got the idea for the film in 2018 after meeting an 84-year-old man in Munsiyari, a scenic hill town in the state.
"I visited him after seeing his photo in a Facebook post. The wrinkles on his face really fascinated me. His face was unique."
Kapri said he asked him and his wife what their biggest worry was.
"He said, 'My biggest worry is, if I die first, who is going to take care of her?' And she said, 'He doesn't know how to cook. So if I die first, I don't know who is going to cook food for him.' That was so heartwarming for me."
Kapri says he initially tried to make his film with "the real couple", but abandoned the idea after a week of shooting, when it became clear it was not working. He then approached actors Naseeruddin Shah and Ratna Pathak - a couple themselves - for the lead roles.
Shah loved the script, Kapri says, but felt that he and Pathak did not belong to the region and would struggle to do justice to the characters.
Kapri finally found his Padam Singh within his own family – his father's younger brother, a retired army soldier who expressed an interest in acting. He found his Tulsi in another village. Heera Devi, an elderly widow, had raised her children through years of farming, cutting grass and tending to her buffalo.
Over the years, Padam Singh and Heera Devi tell the BBC, they have watched stories of ghost villages, of children migrating for work, abandoning the elderly, play out all around them. They say today they are overwhelmed by the attention Pyre has got.
Since 2024, the film has been screened at some of the world's biggest festivals. It has won 18 awards, Kapri says, including three for best feature and 12 audience-choice best film prizes.
Despite its success at festivals, Kapri says, Pyre spent two years without a distributor. Even OTT platforms passed on the film and it finally reached cinemas only when a producer friend of his stepped in to fund a theatrical release.
But, he says, the modest 70-screen release on 30 October sparked favourable word-of-mouth reviews and with the demand for tickets going up, there was an increase in overall screenings too.
Meanwhile, the misgivings that both Padam Singh and Heera Devi say they initially had about stepping in front of the camera and forgetting their lines are gone now.
Heera Devi says she was even concerned about what her children would think - and what would society say?
Today she and Padam Singh are basking in the positive reviews of film critics and the affection of their audiences.
They have met teary-eyed people at multiple screenings - many wanting to touch their feet and hug them, many who said the film reminded them of their own parents and grandparents who are waiting in villages, towns and cities that they had come from.
"We felt immense joy and happiness. We've received so much love and inspiration - something we had never imagined," says Padam Singh.
But the best moment for him came when he met Naseeruddin Shah in Mumbai. "He watched the entire movie and had tears in his eyes. He hugged me. He said, 'Bubu, the role you have performed, I wouldn't be able to pull off even in seven lifetimes.'"
The film's appeal, Heera Devi says, is because "in reality, our village is just like this".
"Across villages in India, the elderly are left alone. No one's children stay at home anymore and it's the same situation for all parents. They keep waiting for their son and daughter-in-law, hoping that their grandchildren would visit and spend a few days with them. The loneliness is simply unbearable."
Padam Singh says he has a message for the younger generation in Uttarakhand and the rest of India.
"I want to tell them they must not abandon their motherland, the land where they were born," he says. "I also appeal to the government to bring education and employment to where people are - so that they don't have to wander away. When that happens, the parents who are being left behind will also be cared for."

title: Akhilesh’s UP manifesto goes big on GenZ outreach, from 25 lakh govt jobs to unemployment allowance
description: SP manifesto also focuses on women, PDA communities and farmers. Zero tolerance for crime and deadline to fill govt vacancies among key poll promises for UP.
author: Prashant Srivastava
content:
Lucknow: The Samajwadi Party (SP) has promised 25 lakh government jobs over five years and employment opportunities for 2-3 crore youth in the private sector as part of its manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, with a focus on reaching out to GenZ voters.
The party has also promised a monthly unemployment allowance of Rs 5,000 to young people until they find a job, farm loan waivers and 300 units of free electricity.
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav unveiled the manifesto on Thursday along with senior leaders Azam Khan and Awadhesh Pasi, outlining a roadmap focused on employment, women’s welfare, farmers and law and order.
The party plans to release three separate manifestos, a PDA (Pichda, Dalit & Alpsankyak) manifesto (which was the main one released Thursday), a women-centric manifesto, and a third outlining its vision for technology and startups.
Akhilesh promised that the first Cabinet meeting after the party comes to power would initiate the recruitment process for 10 lakh government vacancies. He also pledged to streamline recruitment, completing processes involving a single examination within three months and those requiring two examinations within six months.
The manifesto also proposes a state education policy, job-oriented skill development programmes and an Urban Employment Guarantee Act to provide employment opportunities to people in cities.
Rs 40,000 annual pension for women
During the manifesto launch, the SP chief also promised an annual pension of Rs 40,000 for women, particularly elderly women, as part of efforts to strengthen their financial security and independence.
For farmers, the SP has promised a loan waiver and a legal guarantee of Minimum Support Price (MSP) for all crops grown in Uttar Pradesh. It has also proposed a compensation mechanism in case of crop losses.
The party has promised to create a Rs 15,000 crore corpus fund for sugarcane farmers to ensure that payments are made within 24 hours.
The manifesto also addresses the demands of Shikshamitras, instructors and other contractual employees.
Akhilesh promised to work towards providing Shikshamitras and instructors salaries equivalent to those of regular teachers. The party has also pledged respectable wages and adjustments for ASHA workers, Anganwadi workers, contractual and outsourced employees.
The SP has also promised to work towards restoring the Old Pension Scheme.
‘Zero tolerance towards crime’
Significantly, Akhilesh aggressively emphasised on law and order, promising a zero-tolerance policy towards crime and criminals if the party comes to power. During the press conference, he repeated crime control promises thrice.
He promised strict action against organised crime and hate crimes targeting women, backward communities, Dalits and minorities. In the manifesto, SP also pledges to prevent riots based on caste or religion and take effective action against crimes targeting women and Scheduled Castes.
The party has vowed to prevent mafias and criminals from flourishing in the state and ensure swift action against them.
To address land disputes and prevent powerful individuals and mafias from grabbing land belonging to the poor, backward communities, Dalits and other vulnerable groups, the SP has proposed a special task force.
Similar to the Dial 100 emergency response system, the task force would operate vehicles of a different colour and conduct regular patrols to prevent land grabbing.
The manifesto also proposes deploying Dial 100 vehicles in major markets to protect traders, shopkeepers and entrepreneurs from harassment by mafias and strongmen. District officials would be held accountable for ensuring their safety.
Women’s safety has been given priority, with the SP proposing a dedicated women’s police structure under the control of the Director General of Police (DGP), with its reach extending to villages.
The proposed system aims to prevent crimes against women and ensure immediate and stringent action whenever such incidents occur.
The party has also promised to strengthen the 1090 women’s helpline and the Dial 100 emergency response system to ensure police reach the scene as quickly as possible and provide security to citizens, particularly women.
Akhilesh has also promised to set up Samajwadi Canteens across Uttar Pradesh, where people would be provided meals for Rs 5 per plate. The manifesto also mentions a 50 percent reservation for PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankyak) communities in government contracts worth up to Rs 50 crore to ensure greater representation of these communities in government-funded projects.
(Edited by Gitanjali Das)

title: Mumbai protest FIR led to lookout against CJP’s Saurav Das, was issued hours before UK trip
description: Das was stopped from travelling to the UK at Delhi airport on 23 November. Courts have, in the past, held that an LOC cannot be issued mechanically merely because a person is accused in a criminal case.
author: Ananya Bhardwaj
content:
New Delhi: The lookout circular (LOC) against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das was issued in connection with an FIR related to the CJP’s protest at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park on 2 October. The LOC came to light Thursday when the Centre disclosed its existence before the Delhi High Court, where Das is seeking permission to travel to the UK.
The FIR was registered on 3 October under Sections 189 (unlawful assembly) and 223 (disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS); read with Sections 37(1)(3) (power to prohibit certain acts to prevent disorder) and 135 (violation of prohibitory orders) of the Maharashtra Police Act.
The LOC was opened seven weeks after the protest, on the night of 22 November, just hours before Saurav Das was scheduled to travel to the UK.
Speaking to ThePrint, senior advocate Maninder Singh said the “basis on which this LOC has been opened is flawed,” while senior advocate Tanveer Ahmed called the opening of LOC in this case “a joke”.
According to a senior police officer, the FIR was registered against organisers of the protest and 400-500 unidentified supporters. The FIR names CJP functionaries Abhijeet Dipke, Pranav Ahire, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde, Saurav Das, Afreen Nawaz, Saumya Korde, Ankit Bharadwaj, Vijay Malangi and Yogesh Ingle, along with more than 400 supporters, for allegedly assembling unlawfully and raising slogans in Dadar.
Das was stopped from travelling to the UK at Delhi airport on 23 November. According to the source, the Regional Passport Office (RPO) in Chennai issued a show-cause notice to Das Monday, asking him to explain discrepancies in his identity documents, including an alleged mismatch between the dates and place of birth on his Aadhaar card, school certificate and passport. The notice also said Das must not use his passport for travel until the discrepancies were resolved. He, however, did not respond to it, the source said.
A lookout circular (LOC) is an alert issued to immigration authorities at the request of law enforcement or other authorised agencies to monitor or restrict a person’s movement across international borders. An LOC is typically opened in connection with a cognisable offence when a person is evading arrest or legal proceedings, has non-bailable warrants pending against them or is considered a flight risk.
Courts have, in the past, held that an LOC cannot be issued mechanically merely because a person is accused in a criminal case, emphasising the need to establish deliberate evasion of legal proceedings and the likelihood of the accused leaving the country to evade the process of law. Courts have also recognised an individual’s right to challenge an LOC.
The CJP’s 2 October protest, titled ‘Chalo Mumbai’, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, saw more than 4,000 people gather at Shivaji Park in Dadar. Mumbai Police had not officially granted permission for the protest.
Also Read: Abhijeet Dipke tests Meta — Does praising Modi help your Instagram reach?
‘Violation of law, a cruel joke’
Senior advocate Maninder Singh said the opening of an LOC in connection with an FIR registered in Mumbai, that too seven weeks later, was in violation of the law when none of the requirements to open the LOC were satisfied.
“As per my knowledge, there were no summons issued to Saurav Das to join investigation, he was not evading arrest, nor was he served a notice under Section 41A (now Section 35(3) of BNSS, which provides for a notice to appear before the police) in connection with this FIR. Opening an LOC straight away on the basis of this FIR is a violation of the law and the law laid down in various judgments of the High Court of Delhi and Supreme Court,” he said.
Singh added that the circumstances under which an LOC can be opened are clearly laid down. These typically involve a cognisable offence, a person refusing to join the probe or absconding or evading from the process of law, or is considered a flight risk.
According to Singh, had it merely been a case of a show-cause notice seeking an explanation for discrepancies in Das’s documents/passport, it would still have been understandable, although the timing of the notice too was questionable, given that it was served just hours before Das was scheduled to leave for the UK.
The opening of an LOC, however, made little sense, he said, as there was no allegation of Saurav Das absconding, being a flight risk or failing to join the investigation.
“There is an established procedure for opening an LOC, which has been violated and not followed,” he said. “Also, the moment an LOC is issued, the person needs to be informed so that he or she can seek legal remedies as per the settled law.”
Senior advocate Tanveer Ahmed said that an LOC cannot be initiated by the police or a law enforcement agency unless there is a non-bailable warrant against the accused.
If the accused is an Indian citizen, is cooperating with the probe, and there are no such coercive measures in the field against him, the LOC becomes arbitrary on this count and is liable to be struck down, he said.
Adding, “An LOC impinges directly and unequivocally on the fundamental right to travel. The Supreme Court has always said that an LOC cannot be the first option and has to be the last option.”
He also said that whenever an LOC is opened and there is a direction to the Bureau of Immigration to mark the LOC at airports and ports, the authorities have to supply detailed reasons in the application against the subject. “Those have to entail details of the case, but also why you consider the person to be a flight risk. You also have to state whether any coercive measures were taken against the subject upon his making himself scarce and not coming forward,” he said.
Ahmed explained that BNS Section 189, under which the FIR has been registered, on the face of it, makes the opening of an LOC a “cruel joke, not only on Das and other cockroaches, but also puts the entire country to colossal shame”.
“Normally, LOCs attained vigour after economic offenders like Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi, Mehul Choksi and others fled India after causing immense economic damage and loss to the public exchequer. Das and others are by no stretch of imagination terrorists, economic offenders or narco-terrorists, nor is their exit or free movement prejudicial to the sovereignty, territorial integrity and economic stability of the country,” he said.
He added that it is “beyond pathetic” when an LOC is opened in a case of public nuisance or disobeying government orders in light of the fundamental right to protest peacefully. “Das and the Cockroach Janta Party, by no stretch of imagination, are a threat to India’s affinity and friendly relations with other foreign countries. This is a cruel joke,” he said.
(Edited by Amrtansh Arora)

title: Should accreditation determine protection for journalists? SC to probe amid plea born from CJP protests
description: The top court said it would lay down SOPs on how to deal with journalists during public demonstrations, if it found grey areas or a vacuum.
author: Bhadra Sinha
content:
New Delhi: The Supreme Court Thursday posed four questions while hearing a petition regarding the alleged detention and forced removal of journalists while covering protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.
– Who qualifies as a journalist?
– Should professional accreditation or institutional affiliation determine the protection available to journalists?
– Do journalists enjoy any special privilege vis-à-vis law enforcement agencies while covering protests?
– Does forcible removal of a journalist from a protest site amount to custody? What are its constitutional consequences?
A bench led by Chief Justice Suryakant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana disposed of the petition, asking the petitioner to approach the court-monitored enquiry panel, looking into the allegations of violence and police atrocities during the protests.
The bench did not express any opinion on merits, but said it would examine larger constitutional questions to maintain a balance between journalistic freedom and maintenance of public order. The committee, it clarified, will examine individual allegations of police excesses.
However, Justice Bagchi said there were gaps in the existing framework governing police interaction with journalists.
He pointed out that self-proclaimed journalists might not necessarily enjoy the same level of protection as accredited ones.
To elaborate his point, he said: “Status (as a journalist) is not self-conferred. If you are a journalist from a newspaper/print media, you’re under [Press Council] accredited journalist. If you are a TV channel of that newspaper, you are accredited accordingly. You can also be an online journalist, and you can also have registration. These things we have to…we are in the realm of atomised individuals claiming to be journalists. Self-proclaimed journalists may not have the same protection as accredited journalists.”
The petition was filed by Kerala Union of Working Journalists (KUWJ).
A fortnight ago, the Delhi Police made a similar submission before the court in their affidavit, filed in response to a batch of petitions, accusing the force of atrocities. The police claimed social media influencers, content creators and reel makers would not get the same protection as accredited journalists.
It was maintained that the police did not knowingly obstruct any journalist from carrying out their duties.
“The Delhi Police has, at no point, sought to obstruct, impede or interfere with the bona fide discharge of journalistic duties, whether during the protests in question or otherwise,” the affidavit said.
It denied breach of the top court order that directed the police from exempting the media from restrictions imposed by the Delhi Police to regulate the movement of those present at the protest sites. It said content creators cannot seek benefit of this directive.
During the hearing Thursday, the top court said it would lay down a Standard Operating Procedure (SOPs) on how to deal with journalists during public demonstrations, if it found grey areas or a vacuum.
Justice Bagchi said: “First we have to define a journalist. Is it a journalist in the category where someone is registered under the Press Council? Or is employed with a registered newspaper/TV channel? Or a person who seeks to be a (spokesman) to the citizens, like on social media, who are making reels.”
Responding to a lawyer’s claim that categorisation of persons into “journalists” and “reel-makers” was an after thought cannot be done on the spot during a demonstration, the judge said: “Even if we lay down an SOP, the SOP’s graded stance of law enforcement agencies would also depend upon the status and character of the person claiming to be a journalist.”
He said the court would first address the issues on principle of how far a journalist in a situation where there is an assemblage or demonstration can go; whether a journalist has a special privilege in such a situation with respect to law enforcement agencies.
He also said that a crucial question that needs a determination is do “journalists have a superior or a different species of treatment in a situation where a demonstration is going.” This, he explained, has to be decided based on their right to pursue their profession, while making sure that law and order is maintained.
(Edited by Anupama Yadav)

title: CEC Gyanesh Kumar Makes an Appearance at a Wedding After Long Silence Over SIR Protests - The Wire
description: Going by a photograph posted on social media, apparently by a BJP leader, Kumar attended a wedding in Bhopal a few days back.
author: The Wire Staff
content: New Delhi: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar has remained out of public view and has not addressed the media ever since mass protests began over the Election Commission’s handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). He has now resurfaced at a private wedding reception in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh.A photograph of Kumar at the reception, hosted by senior police officer Upendra Jain for his son, showed him standing with senior Congress leader Ajay Singh and MP Assembly Speaker Narendra Singh Tomar.The Wire had noted in a report published on October 24 that Kumar had not appeared in public or addressed the allegations since the Indian Express reported on September 23 that Election Commissioners Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu had raised 14 objections to the SIR process over 10 months.Prior to the demands for his resignation, Kumar had presided over a press conferences where he had aggressively sought affidavits from opposition leaders after they alleged there had been vote theft and questioned the SIR process.Several opposition parties and student groups have over the last roughly three months demanded his resignation, and protests – as well as crackdowns on protesters – have taken place across the country. None of it broke the silence of the CEC, including mass arrests.Also read: Delhi Police Manhandle, Detain Protesters Asking for CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s Removal at Jantar MantarThe Election Commission has issued press notes announcing changes to the SIR process, including revisions to Form 6, special drives to include left-out voters and provisions for hearings for those affected. However, Kumar has not personally addressed the controversy.His scheduled voter outreach programmes in Meerut and Varanasi in September, as well as a two-day visit to Chhattisgarh in October, were postponed.Ajay Singh said his encounter with Kumar at the Bhopal reception was incidental and denied having spoken to him. He said he had attended the function as a guest and was unaware of Kumar’s presence and that he could not recognise him.“Whether he was Gynesh Kumar or Amit Shah, I wouldn’t know. I was not talking to him either – why would I? We want him [Kumar] to resign – we have said it repeatedly, he must go. That has been our slogan, so the question of talking to him does not arise,” Singh told the media on Thursday (November 26). The picture appears to be from a few days ago.Singh was tagged in the photograph on Facebook by a third person, Bharti Pratyush, who describes himself as a BJP leader and a member of former MP chief minister Shivraj Singh Chauhan’s team. A sarcastic post about the Congress party accompanies the photograph. Pratyush also writes in his bio that he is a property dealer and says: “Bhagwan hain mere Narendra Modi ji (Prime Minister Narendra Modi is my god).”The Congress organised a symbolic protest against Kumar in Bhopal, but demonstrators reached the hotel and airport after the CEC had already left. The protest ended with his effigy set on fire outside the MP Congress office.Kumar has not commented on the photograph or the controversy around it.For our full coverage on the SIR and the issues it has brought to citizens, click here.

title: Siang Dam Project Faces Village-Level Resistance Despite Union Govt's Outreach - The Wire
description: Village heads have rejected the idea of being displaced from their historical regions and the Union government's assurances regarding rehabilitation. They demand the withdrawal of security forces and release of detained protesters.
author: The Wire Staff
content: New Delhi: The Union government’s bid to break the deadlock over the proposed 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh has not worked. At the village, district and state levels, the project continues to face stiff resistance, say reports.This is despite two recent meetings held by state and Union government representatives at Boleng, the Siang district headquarters, and another at Yingkiong, the Upper Siang district headquarters. The residents of Geku, boycotted the second meeting, held on Wednesday (November 25), said a report in the Times of India.The proposed reservoir for the dam is reportedly planned near Geku, around 35 km downstream of Yingkiong, said ToI. Assurances for the project displaced made by Union home minister Amit Shah have also not worked.Consultations were held between the residents of the specific villages where NTPC wishes to conduct pre-feasibility studies and the government representatives, reports ToI. However, village heads, known as gaon burahs, have refused to accept displacement as the cost of the project and rejected the argument that it has security implications.“But if people get evicted, for whom such security will be needed?” said Adi Bane Kebang United (ABKU) spokesperson Datik Ratan at a press conference on Wednesday (November 26), ToI separately reported on Thursday (November 26). Datik echoed the views of Tanyo Lipir, Gaon Burah, Simong village in Siang district, whose rejection of the government’s security claims and rehabilitation offers has been widely circulated on social media.“You can cut us into pieces and throw us,” Tanyo Lipir reportedly said at a meeting with senior state government officials and Union power ministry representatives held on Tuesday. He said the Adi communities would not allow the construction of this project.The residents of affected areas had also previously rejected the government’s offer, as The Wire reported, with a number of local organisations standing firmly against the dam. The BJP has been facing resistance from locals since the pre-fesibility studies for the project began.“We have rejected the government’s offer to hold talks. Day by day, more people protesting against the proposed dam are being arrested. We want to talk but how can we talk in such a situation. For that, there has to be a conducive situation,” Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum spokesperson Tagori Mize told The Wire on November 6.Also read: Journalists Covering Anti-Dam Protests in Arunachal Talk of State Repression, Restrictions as CM Distances Himself From Police ActionEarlier this month, the Arunachal Pradesh government released four of the protesters and reinstated some of the village heads whom it had suspended due to their opposition to the dam.Union home minister Amit Shah has backed the Siang dam on strategic and energy security grounds and promised that those displaced by it would get India’s “most attractive” rehabilitation package. On November 21, during a two-day visit to Arunachal Pradesh, Shah cited China’s proposed 60,000 MW hydropower project while speaking at the Police Training Academy in Banderdewa near Itanagar.Shah also said the government would hold “positive discussions” with Siang Valley residents. His offer for talks followed a joint memorandum submitted by the ABKU and the Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum on November 20, seeking a halt to pre-feasibility work, the release of detained protesters and the withdrawal of security forces.Ratan, too, said there could be no dialogue until Central Armed Police Forces personnel were withdrawn from the region and all detained and arrested protesters had been released.

title: Self-Proclaimed Journalists May Not Have the Same Protection as Accredited Journalists: SC - The Wire
description: The top court also posed the question that does forcible removal of a journalist from a protest site amount to custody, and what are its constitutional consequences.
author: The Wire Staff
content: New Delhi: While hearing petitions filed by Kerala Union of Working Journalists (KUWJ) over Delhi police’s crackdown on journalists covering the recent protests in the national capital, the Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26) remarked that “self-proclaimed journalists may not have the same protection as accredited journalists,” reported Bar and Bench.The remark was made by Justice Joymalya Bagchi, who was part of a bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and also comprising Justice V. Mohana.Senior advocate P.V. Dinesh and others represented the KUWJ over the Delhi Police’s alleged detention and forcible removal of journalists who were covering protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.The top court said on Thursday that it would examine questions about protection afforded to journalists covering protests.During the hearing, the court also posed a number of questions on the issue, including: Who qualifies as a journalist, should professional accreditation or institutional affiliation determine the protection available to journalists and do journalists
